Las letras pueden imprimirse de varias formas, aunque recomiendo imprimirlas en posición vertical. De esta manera se conserva mejor el efecto volumétrico del diseño y se obtiene una superficie más limpia. Para garantizar una buena adhesión a la base, especialmente si se imprimen varias letras a la vez, es recomendable utilizar un brim amplio. Las letras mostradas en las fotografías se han impreso con filamento tricolor. Si utilizas este tipo de material, conviene prestar atención a la orientación de cada pieza, ya que el ángulo de impresión influirá directamente en la distribución de los colores y en el resultado final. Para obtener el mejor acabado posible, recomiendo utilizar una altura de capa reducida o, preferiblemente, altura de capa variable. El efecto globo se basa en superficies curvas y transiciones suaves que pierden definición cuando se utilizan capas demasiado gruesas. También es posible imprimir las letras en horizontal, pero en ese caso es especialmente importante utilizar una altura de capa muy fina o altura de capa variable para mantener el aspecto redondeado y evitar que se pierda parte del efecto característico del diseño. description: Xenomorph (Alien) Ultra Detailed Display This one is by far one of my largest, and definitely the most detailed model that I've worked on to date.. This is an Ultra Detailed Xenomorph statue that stands 19 inches (48cm) tall in the largest form! This statue pulls inspiration from the unbelievably awesome Sideshow Collectibles Vinyl model, which if you are familiar with their models, are next level in detail.. but next to impossible to get! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 19" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 19" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 19" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. I had 4 machines running test prints none stop. I promise though, it is worth it at the end. **Please also be aware that the model images you see are 100% real, with 0 use of AI, but they have been post-process colored using some Rub'n Buff waxes, along with some gloss clear coat layer application at the end. ASSEMBLY REQUIRED ** The 19" tall, multipiece print will require some glue. I have used both super glue, as well as hot glue. Hot glue was my preference. With all the parts printed, and supports cleaned up (TAKE YOUR TIME REMOVING THE SUPPORTS AS THE PARTS ARE HIGHLY DETAILED AND FRAGILE ) do a dry-fit of all the parts to ensure proper fitment. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. Assembly is very straightfoward, with the exception of the tail. DO NOT mount the tail to the model until the Xenomoprh is placed onto the base display. The tail loops around the display and needs to be installed afterwards. Install the tail by turning is 90 degrees and carefully looping the tip around the back of the base and then gently rotating it up into the reciever cutout on he back of the xenomorph (Yes, it looks like a butt ). With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process, you can assemble everything together, just leave the tail to the end. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting peg as well as some glue to the toes of the left foot (there is no peg here) and firmly place the model on to the base. Proceed with snaking the tail into position, and then apply some glue onto the peg of the base of the tail. There is a small mounting support for the tail at the back of the base that also requires a small application of glue to help it from bouncing around with the model fully assembled. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff Antique Gold wax for the Xenomorph, and Brass color for the base. Wear gloves and apply the wax to a towel and gently go over the details. Avoid pressing really hard so that the void remain black/dark, this helps with final contrast of the model. As you can tell from these two photos the difference between the plain model and the colored one is pretty phenomenal and I HIGHLY recommend going through the effort!

Este diseño de mariposa está pensado para ser una pieza versátil que puede servir como una delicada decoración o como un marcapáginas único. El modelo está diseñado específicamente para ser impreso directamente sobre tela de tul, lo que le otorga un fondo transparente y una textura muy especial. Instrucciones de Impresión (Técnica sobre tela) Para lograr que la mariposa quede adherida a la tela, es necesario seguir un proceso de impresión con pausa. Aquí están los pasos clave: Pausa programada: El archivo de impresión debe configurarse en el laminador (slicer) para que genere una pausa automática exactamente al terminar la primera capa . Colocación de la tela: Durante esta pausa, el cabezal se apartará. Es el momento de colocar la tela de tul estirada sobre la cama de impresión, justo por encima de la capa base que se acaba de imprimir. Fijación con imanes: Para evitar que el cabezal arrastre la tela o se formen arrugas, utiliza imanes en los bordes para fijar el tul firmemente a la base metálica de la impresora. Asegúrate de que los imanes queden fuera de la trayectoria del extrusor. Reanudación de la impresión: Una vez que la tela esté tensa y asegurada, reanuda la impresión. El plástico de las siguientes capas se fundirá a través de los agujeros de la malla del tul, encapsulando la tela y uniendo el diseño de forma permanente.

EDIT 2026/07/10 Please note that this is not your everyday casual 3D print! If interested in printing, read everything below! It requires some experience and I advise everyone to think everything through before blindly starting to print. Post-processing is needed after assembling. Read through my description below! It will take roughly 12-15kg of filament and probably several months of work including post-processing, painting and adding details. The parts are without infill and without top- and bottom layers. 6 wall loops. Adjust the parameters to your liking, also depending on your choice of post-processing! With this update, I tweaked the print profiles by adding a few more modifiers. They are placed in rather flat areas and have the top layers re-enabled so these areas turn out more smooth. - - - - - Yes, I’m insane. Regular-sized figures and statues just aren’t my thing - So I modelled Batman from scratch and printed him…life sized. After printing, assembling and painting, I gave him a batcape, glass eyes, metal screwhead details and a glossy surface finish for his metal parts. I modelled him after the design in the arkham origins game because I think this is one of the sickest batsuit designs. Who agrees? If you happen to be equally crazy as I am and to actually download and print your own life-sized statue, here’s a few additional information: Print overview Batman himself consists of 40 parts which can be printed on every Bambu printer except for the A1 mini. His accessories on the belt as well as the batarang add another 11 parts making it a total of 51 parts. To identify each part, I created a general overview below. You can identify each part in the print profiles too - I named the print bed labels and the parts on it according to the overview. Because Bambu Studio won’t let me create more than 36 plates, I divided the parts into “Lower body”, “Torso & Head” and “Shoulders, arms & Accessories”. Each print profile has its own overview with the parts it contains. Assembling, Post-processing For assembling, there’s no connectors, screw holes or anything like that - Like a typical cosplay prop, the print itself just serves as the base and is then further refined, making the seams invisible and giving it a nice finish which will also hold everything together properly. I used a heated sculpting tool called Modifi3D to melt the seams together, which added a lot of strength already while also making the seams barely noticeable. And from this point on, it’s entirely up to you how far you want to take the surface finishing process. I coated everything in fiberglass which was a sh!tload of work but it really paid off in terms of both durability and appearance. And because there’s so many different ways, techniques and methods for the entire post-process, there’s no right or wrong when it comes to slicing and printing. I printed everything without infill and without top- or bottom surface (with a few exceptions), leaving the parts hollow, made of 6 wall loops. Sort of a vase mode. Adjust the parameters to your liking. Really curious to see if there’s ANYONE who will actually go for this project. And if so, I need pictures! model_name: Mecha Pokémon Statue Series — Mecha Lugia statue
description: Mecha Pokémon Statue Series — Mecha Lugia Hyper-Real Steel Sculpture 1. Concept & Design Following our tradition of heavy mechanical re-forging (Mecha Reforge) applied to iconic anime characters, we turn our focus to the legendary Guardian of the Seas from the Johto region— Lugia . This creation reimagines Lugia’s streamlined biological form through the lens of heavy industrial and military cyberpunk aesthetics. Moving away from low-detail smooth surfaces, the majesty of the diving sea god is materialized here as a dense, armored exoskeleton statue. Its roaring headline pose, the intricate neck cables alongside exposed hydraulic pistons, and the layered plating of the heavy chest armor exude an organic living-alloy tension and pure mechanical menace. Its iconic hands-like wings are re-engineered into heavy military-grade thruster wings, complete with articulated mechanical joints and individual aerodynamic slats. In this static stance, the signature dorsal plates running down to the tail are transformed into rigid external cooling fins, conveying a supreme sense of compressed energy beneath the armor. model_name: Mecha Pokemon Series — Beedrill Hyper-Real Statue
description: Mecha Pokémon Statue Series — Mecha Beedrill Hyper-Real Steel Sculpture 1. Concept & Design This sculpture reinterprets the iconic, lethal airborne assassin through the lens of heavy mechanical re-forging (Mecha Reforge). As the newest chapter of our "Mecha Pokémon Series," we turn our focus to the legendary high-speed apex predator of the Kanto region— Beedrill . This creation reimagines Beedrill’s aggressive biological silhouette into a heavy armored exoskeleton statue brimming with industrial rigidity. The design transforms its naturally lightweight abdomen and segments into layered, curved armor plates packed with dense mechanical panel lines, exuding immense physical mass and weaponized tension within a static warrior pose. Structurally, due to Beedrill's defining biological trait of having extremely small feet , achieving balance in large-scale monolithic FDM printing posed a significant challenge. To counter this, we engineered the right arm to drive its massive lance directly into the ground , establishing a rock-solid triangular base. However, this required a compromise: visually, it looks as though half of Beedrill's iconic twin stingers are missing. To fix this, we included an extra loose lance accessory just for you guys ! This bonus lance gives you complete display freedom—you can hang it on the raised left hand to create a gripping effect, holding it facing forward or backward. (Note: If you wish to completely lift it overhead, you will need to utilize an aftermarket action figure display stand for support). Of course, you can also get creative and print multiple extra lances to scatter around him, replicating an epic "infinite weapon arsenal" scene from certain anime series (lol). 2. Engineering & Printability The statue is highly optimized for large-scale FDM stability, prioritizing ballast physics and center-of-gravity compensation over part articulation: Support Removal & Structural Integrity: The primary printing hurdle with this model is that the supports beneath both arms are somewhat tricky to remove , requiring patience. On the flip side, the supports for the wings detach very easily. However, because the joint area connecting the wings to the main body is quite small , please handle them with care during cleanup so you don't accidentally snap the entire wing section off. The remaining parts should be smooth sailing for experienced makers. Minor Artifact Correction: If your print suffers from a slightly warped or misaligned pinky finger on the left hand , there's no need to scrap the print. Simply use a heat gun to gently soften the plastic, realign it, and secure it with a drop of glue. Geometric Shadow Readability: At 0.2 mm layer heights, the mechanical compound eyes, the layered armor on the torso, and the sweeping taper of the giant lances catch ambient light perfectly, throwing deep dual-density shadows that eliminate the absolute need for immediate painting. 3. Display & Customization With its sweeping, aggressive wingspan, Mecha Beedrill naturally commands a premium presence when staged inside industrial mecha bays, barren desert ruins, or post-apocalyptic military outposts. For advanced miniature painters and makers, the model offers limitless creative room for custom finishing: The expansive metal surfaces are perfectly suited for heavy weathering, grease-staining, and metallic edge dry-brushing. The deep recesses between the armor plates and the main lances are ideal for dropping high-contrast vivid hive-amber or neon toxic-green paints to simulate a lethal weapon system charging up. By printing several extra copies of the lance and staking them into a custom clay or foam terrain base, you can flawlessly recreate a "Gate of Babylon" styled boundless armory effect that dramatically elevates the visual impact. Whether positioned as a standalone desk centerpiece or integrated into a sci-fi diorama, its silhouette delivers superb stylized plausibility from every angle. 4. Conclusion The Hyper-Real Mecha Beedrill statue stands as a definitive showcase piece, proving that high collectible impact isn't born from moving parts, but from raw sculptural presence. It transforms a childhood memory into tangible awe—blending menace, mass, and sharp industrial geometry into an essential collector’s centerpiece that completely dominates the space it commands. Quick Tips: Avoid using photography/timelapse travel modes for this print to minimize stringing or failure risks around the delicate antennae and sweeping wing overhangs. Crucial Warning: If you plan on using a mini-torch or a heat gun to clear stringing and print residue from the wings, remember that the wings are extremely thin—please exercise extreme caution ! To prevent the thin geometry from softening and warping instantly upon heating, it is highly recommended to steady the wing with one hand while keeping the heat source moving rapidly. My absolute go-to filament for reading these industrial mechanical details remains the Bambu Lab gray series . When removing tight supports from beneath the arms, needle-nose pliers combined with Bambu’s FAC002-N scraper will be your ultimate soulmates.

Inspired by one of the world's most iconic street art motifs, this model is part of my Modern Art Collection —a series of 3D printable models inspired by famous works of art. After designing Balloon Girl and Floating Balloon Girl , I wanted to continue the collection with another iconic Banksy-inspired piece. Instead of creating a traditional multi-color print, I split the model into separate parts. The figure, bouquet wrapper and flowers are printed individually and assembled afterwards. This keeps print time and filament waste low while preserving the striking black, white and red color scheme (or any colors you choose). The flowers are intentionally simplified. My first version looked more realistic, but it proved difficult to print reliably. This stylized low-poly bouquet turned out to be a much better balance between appearance, printability and durability. Included Parts Figure Bouquet wrapper Flower bouquet Optional frame The frame is printed separately, so you can choose whether to display the model on its own or as framed wall art. I really enjoy turning iconic artworks into printable display pieces, and I hope this model fits nicely alongside my Balloon Girl and Floating Balloon Girl designs. Printing Notes No AMS required Figure requires supports Bouquet and wrapper print without supports The bouquet slides into the wrapper and can be glued if desired I hope you enjoy printing it! If you do, I'd love to see your make.

description: This is a 150 mm standing Catholic crucifix designed as a cleaner, easier print. The model separates the crucifix body from the base so the main cross section can be printed more efficiently with fewer major supports and less cleanup. The finished piece has a traditional devotional look with a sculpted corpus, INRI plaque, rectangular cross, and a stable display base. It works well as a home altar piece, prayer corner display, desk crucifix, shelf decoration, or Catholic gift. The two piece design makes the model easier to print than a single upright crucifix because the base and cross can be handled separately. After printing, the cross section fits into the base. A small amount of glue can be used if you want a permanent fit. Prints in a single material (PLA) — no multi-color or exotic filament needed. The included profile is tuned for the Bambu Lab X2D at 0.16mm for fine surface detail. Tree supports are pre-placed for the figure's overhangs and pop off cleanly thanks to a one-layer support gap. A stone, marble, or matte PLA gives a carved-statue look. Remove supports gently from the figure with flush cutters; a quick pass with a soft brush cleans up the interface marks. Print the stand in the same or a contrasting color. Optional: even easier support removal (AMS / multi-material If you have an AMS or a second filament, you can make the supports practically fall off. PETG doesn't bond to PLA, so using it only for the support interface gives a clean break with a smooth surface underneath: In Bambu Studio, open the Support tab. Set Interface filament to a slot loaded with PETG (keep the rest of the supports/body as PLA). Make sure there's a small support gap (the included profile already uses 0.16mm) and re-slice. Print as normal — the PLA body lifts right off the PETG interface. This is fully optional. The default single-PLA profile already releases cleanly; the PETG trick just makes cleanup even nicer if you have the filament on hand. If you make one, please share a photo and leave a like — it really helps!

description: Final Form Cooler – Multi-Part Display Statue ( NO AMS ) Bring one of Dragon Ball's most iconic villains to life with this multi-part display statue of Cooler . Designed with FDM printing in mind, this model combines a dynamic battle stance, clean anatomical proportions, and carefully separated parts to create a collectible that is both enjoyable to print and satisfying to assemble. Unlike traditional multi-colour prints, this model is divided into individual components, allowing you to achieve a clean, multi-colour finish without requiring an AMS. Each section can be printed separately using your filament colour of choice, making the project accessible to anyone with a standard single-extruder printer. The model has been engineered with generous assembly tolerances to accommodate minor differences between printers. For the strongest and cleanest finish, I recommend assembling the parts using CA (super glue) after a quick dry fit. Recommended Print Settings 0.4 mm nozzle ( 0.2 nozzle for 23 cm version NON ams version eyes ) Variable layer height for the best quality Tree supports where required, painted some extra ( used PETG support interface layer for H2D profile for a cleaner look ) Use profile orientation for best quality set your own support setting that work best for your printer for easy removal Tips The names of the parts have been added on the support layer for the caps. These fit nicely, so if it feels wrong check the position. For the 23 version or smaller, i would suggest to print the eyes in one set. I have added the part for that, or print it with a 0.2 nozzle. Left and right parts have different connection measurement, they will fit nicely one 1 side. Use a brim or my preferred profile to make sure that the prints stay on your plate :) On the large profile the eyes are made from 2 pieces. first glue the red eyes on the black base. then push them far inside the head. Get some good tools to remove the supports, cut the tree's into pieces before removing everything. Whether you prefer printing in accurate character colours or creating your own custom version, this model is a fantastic display piece for any Dragon Ball collection. If you decide to print it, I'd love to see your results! Please consider uploading a photo, leaving a rating, or sharing your painted version with the community. description: 🌴 Grand Theft Auto VI - Premium Lightbox 🌴 Hello everyone, makers! I know very well that there are already several GTA 6 theme lightboxes on MakerWorld, but I really wanted to give my personal contribution. I chose to redesign this model line by line , taking care of every single detail to make it truly flawless, clean, and easy to print. I hope you will appreciate the work behind it! The model you see in the photo was printed at the maximum size allowed on the build plate of my Bambu Lab A2L , but I have great news for everyone: I will soon upload the optimized version for 256x256 plates (P1S, X1C, A1, etc.) , so that anyone can have the opportunity to make this splendid lightbox! 🛠️ Print & Assembly Details: Separated Central Logo (Rear Insertion): To guarantee perfect definition and avoid any kind of imperfection or bleeding on the front side, the central "Grand Theft Auto" text is printed separately. It must be inserted directly from the inside of the main body , fitting perfectly into the slot. Then, you just need to secure it firmly with just 2 drops of glue (such as cyanoacrylate/superglue). The front result will be absolutely clean and flawless. Customizable LED Cable Pass-Through: I purposely DID NOT include a fixed hole for the USB LED cable in the base model. This way, each of you is free to create the hole directly in Bambu Studio (using the "Negative Part" tool), positioning it exactly where it is most convenient for you based on where you will place the lamp. Placement & Mounting: On the back, I integrated a convenient wall-mounting system with screw slots. However, thanks to the thickness and balance of the design, the lightbox stands up very well on its own on a shelf or on your gaming desk. If you appreciate the care I took in rethinking this project from scratch, please support the project by leaving a Boost and a Follow! description: Stormwing – Windswept Owl Sculpture The idea behind Stormwing came from my fascination with driftwood sculptures and how nature and time shape everything they touch. I wanted a model that looks like raw power and motion, which lead to this windswept owl—an animal pushing forward while almost getting torn apart. The current height of the sculpture is ~ 16 cm (~6.3 in) in height. I would not print it smaller as the thin edges would become rather thin and increase the risk of not forming as it should. For the easiest support removal, keep the model in the provided vertical position. This helps reduce the amount of support required and makes the supports as manageable as possible to remove. Printing Use a clean print plate with some glue (unless you are using a super tack plate) Use dried out filament (Different filament and printers impacts the print differently, please adjust your settings accordingly.) Keep the model in the provided vertical position Support Removal Instructions Allow the print to cool completely before removing it from the build plate. Use small flush cutters, needle-nose pliers, and tweezers to remove the support branches in smaller pieces. Support removal will take a little bit of time. Patience and careful handling are important for protecting the thin driftwood details. Be especially careful around the talons of the owl. Start by removing the larger support sections around the base and outside edges. Break the smaller branches into smaller sections and alternate around each supported section as needed. I needed to alternate between the front and backside as some of the support was built up from both sides for the same section. After removing the supports, clean up potential rough contact points with a precision knife, small file, or fine-grit sandpaper if needed. Light sanding and gentle, controlled heat may be needed to clean up areas where the supports were attached. I used a handheld mini torch, but apply heat carefully to avoid warping or damaging the print. Wood PLA is very sensitive to heat! Cookie Monster Godzilla "Cookie Blast" Edition "Cookie...zilla breathes cookies!" What happens when Cookie Monster Godzilla unleashes his ultimate attack? You get the Cookie Monster Godzilla "Cookie Blast" Edition! Instead of a traditional monster breath attack, this version features Cookie Monster Godzilla standing on a detailed base while blasting a stream of cookie dough from his mouth. Some might call it a cookie-powered attack... others might say it looks like he's having a bit of a cookie-related incident. Either way, it's a hilarious and unique addition to any monster, cookie, or 3D printing collection. The model includes a custom base designed to add stability, along with a detailed flowing "cookie flame" effect that gives this version a completely different look from the original Cookie Monster Godzilla Duck. Design Process This model was created using a hybrid workflow of AI-assisted generation and traditional 3D modeling. I began with an original mashup concept, then used AI-assisted tools to explore different forms and proportions. After selecting the strongest base design, I refined the model to improve the details, clean up geometry, and optimize it for reliable FDM printing. Print Settings Layer Height: 0.20 mm Infill: 15% Gyroid Supports: Tree Supports (required) AMS Required: Yes Base Modifier A modifier is included that increases part of the base to 30% infill . This adds extra weight to the bottom of the print and helps prevent the model from becoming top-heavy and tipping over. Color Changes This print uses 6 colors and requires two pauses for filament swaps . The pauses are already in the file, but be sure to check that after slicing. If you change the size for a larger or smaller printer, you'll need to change the pauses. Layer 350: Swap Gray for Light Brown Layer 949: Swap Black for Dark Brown Filaments Used Anycubic PLA+ Black Anycubic PLA+ White Kingroon Blue PLA Kingroon Light Brown PLA Elegoo PLA+ Gray Sunlu PLA+ Coffee Brown Post-Processing Notes Support removal on this model can be a little challenging. The area underneath the tail can be difficult to access when removing supports, so take your time and be careful. The cookie drips at the very top of the "cookie fire" effect are also extremely delicate and can break during cleanup. I broke a few of mine during testing, but thankfully they were fairly easy to repair. Small pieces can usually be reattached with glue or bonded back together by carefully heating the plastic. If one of the cookie drips breaks off and you don't want to repair it, remember... it's a melting cookie! You can carefully heat the broken end slightly to soften it and let it resolidify into a natural-looking melted edge. The entire cookie flame effect is fairly fragile, so handle it carefully after printing. Notes for Future Versions I may create a larger version of this model in the future that separates at least part of the cookie flame effect into an assembly piece. This would make the effect more durable while also allowing for an even larger and more detailed version. Print Testing I always print my models before releasing them so I can make sure they actually work and look good in real life. Most of the time, I start with a simple single-color test print first. That lets me check the overall geometry, supports, and printability without burning a ton of filament. If everything comes out clean, I'll move on to the full multicolor AMS version. My prototyping and testing setup includes two Bambu Lab P1S printers and two Snapmaker U1 printers , which lets me quickly iterate between test prints and full-color versions depending on what I'm working on. That said, if I'm already confident in the design—usually from similar prints or earlier versions—I might skip straight to the multicolor print. description: 🏔️ Japanische Schattenbox – Fuji, Sakura & Pagode (Kein AMS benötigt!) Bring ein Stück traditionelle japanische Ästhetik in dein Zuhause! Diese wunderschöne, mehrlagige Schattenbox zeigt den majestätischen Berg Fuji, umrahmt von blühenden Kirschblüten (Sakura), einer klassischen Pagode und einem strahlenden Vollmond, der sich im Wasser spiegelt. Das fertige Modell eignet sich perfekt als dekorativer Hingucker für dein Bücherregal oder den Schreibtisch. Das Beste daran? Du benötigst absolut kein AMS (Automatic Material System) für dieses Modell! Jede Schicht wird komplett einzeln auf einer eigenen Druckplatte gedruckt. Dadurch kannst du ganz einfach mit verschiedenen Filamentresten und Farben experimentieren, um deinen eigenen, einzigartigen Look zu kreieren. 🛠️ Projektdetails & Aufbau Das gesamte Projekt besteht aus insgesamt 16 separaten Druckplatten : 14 Design-Platten: Jede Platte steuert eine präzise Ebene und Farbe zum plastischen 3D-Effekt bei. Die einzelnen Segmente sind besonders filigran ausgeschnitten. 1 Rückplatte: Ausgestattet mit kleinen Haltestiften, um den Stapel perfekt auszurichten. 1 Front-Rahmen: Ein schlichter, eleganter Rahmen, der das gesamte Kunstwerk umschließt. Zusammenbau: Drucke alle 14 Design-Platten in deinen Wunschfarben aus. Staple die Platten einfach nacheinander auf die Rückplatte auf. Setze den vorderen Rahmen auf – je nach Passform deiner Drucke kannst du die Schichten und den Rahmen mit ein paar Tropfen Kleber fixieren. 🖨️ Druck-Empfehlungen (Print Settings) Layer Height (Schichthöhe): 0.2 mm (oder feiner für noch sauberere Kurven bei den Blüten) Infill: 15% – 20% (Gyroid empfohlen) Support: Nicht erforderlich! Alle Platten sind so konstruiert, dass sie flach und ohne Stützstrukturen gedruckt werden können. Filament-Tipp: Matte Filamente (z. B. Matte White für den Rahmen, Matte Navy Blue für den Berg) eignen sich hervorragend, um Reflexionen zu minimieren und den typischen "Paper-Cutout"-Look zu verstärken. 📢 Ich freue mich über dein Feedback! Hello Everyone! I created a few 3D printed convention badge ribbons for Convergence 2026. I figured with Dragoncon coming up, as well as other fan conventions with a badge ribbon trading culture, others may want to print these as well. They have a pleasing thickness but are not too thick or heavy. Perfect for pairing with other traditional ribbons. These match the standard 4" x 1 5/8" or 3.5" x 1 5/8" Badge Ribbons. (See the print profiles for each size) These work best printed flat on the bed. The model comes with text “change me” included, simply change the font and text size as necessary. Do not adjust the embedded depth or thickness for best printing results. I find that rotating these 180 degrees to be face up while you're working on them is helpful, then re-flip when you're ready to print. You could add SVG graphics, just match the embedded depth and thickness to the text for best results. You should be able to fit 14 copies on a P1/P2/X1/X2/A1 bed, however makerworld is fussy about Prime Tower placement and the print profiles I've provided have 11 copies. The minimized prime tower settings in the profile should get you there, if you get a “g-code conflict” just move the prime tower around until it's happy. Print on a holographic bed for an even better effect! I recommend switching to a “smooth high temp plate” setting if you're going to do this and remember to run a bed level every time you switch plates. If using a 0.4mm nozzle, fonts with large spacing and bold details print better than fonts with minute details. Dry filament is important, any first/second layer issues will cause these to not look very good. Clean your plate with dish soap and water and dry thoroughly. Make sure to wash the plate if you accidentally touch it trying to get these off between batches. This should work with either PETG or PLA, but I find the most visually pleasing results with PLA, PETG can be too shiny. description: Gothic Revival Desk: VEF-DSK-0044 1:12 Dollhouse How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale (and you can do it too) The image above is an example showing how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for the Dollhouse models I upload. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image, (the item I want to scale), into a Victorian room reference image, (the wall with the fireplace, window and door). Most important is to set the wall image to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image at the bottom of this description, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Download & Scale your Models to 1:12 Bambu Settings for this Model

description: 《软绒星瞳》是一枚以“治愈系萌宠”为灵感的雕塑戒指，它将猫咪的软萌与戒指的佩戴性完美结合，打造出一款兼具艺术感与治愈感的独特饰品。戒指同样采用奶白色哑光材质打造，质感温润细腻，自带柔和的柔光效果，仿佛被赋予了温度，上手后自带温柔的氛围感。 戒指的核心设计，是一只从戒环中探出脑袋的软萌猫咪。猫咪的造型采用了全立体雕刻，从毛茸茸的脸颊、尖俏的耳朵，到圆溜溜的眼睛、粉嫩的小鼻子，再到探出戒环的两只小肉垫，每一处细节都刻画得栩栩如生。猫咪的毛发纹理细腻逼真，层层叠叠的绒毛雕刻，让它看起来软乎乎的，仿佛伸手就能摸到它蓬松的毛；圆溜溜的眼睛温润透亮，没有多余的装饰，却自带无辜又灵动的眼神，像藏着星光一样，自带治愈感；两只肉垫搭在戒环上，肉垫的弧度与纹理都被精心还原，仿佛猫咪正乖乖趴在你的指尖撒娇，可爱感拉满。戒环的内侧同样打磨光滑，佩戴时贴合指腹，圆润的边缘不会硌手，兼顾了可爱造型与佩戴的舒适感。 这枚戒指的设计，藏着关于陪伴与治愈的温柔寓意。猫咪象征着陪伴与治愈，而这枚戒指就像一只永远趴在你指尖的小猫咪，无论何时何地，都能给你带来温柔的慰藉。它打破了传统饰品的刻板印象，将萌宠元素与雕塑艺术结合，打造出独一无二的风格，无论是日常通勤搭配休闲装，还是搭配甜酷风、温柔风的穿搭，都能轻松适配，让你的指尖自带一份软萌又高级的氛围感。 English: "Starry-Eyed Kitten" is a sculptural ring inspired by the "healing charm of pets". It perfectly blends the cuteness of a kitten with the wearability of a ring, creating a unique piece that is both artistic and comforting. Crafted from the same creamy-white matte material, it has a smooth, warm texture with a gentle sheen, almost as if imbued with a comforting warmth that translates into a soft, elegant aura when worn. The centerpiece is an adorable kitten peeking over the band. The form is fully sculpted in three dimensions, with every detail brought to life: the fuzzy cheeks, pointed ears, round eyes, pink nose, and two tiny paws resting on the ring. The fur texture is intricately carved, layer upon layer, giving it a plush, soft appearance that makes you want to reach out and pet it. The round eyes are smooth and luminous, free of extra decoration yet brimming with innocent, lively expression, as if they hold a piece of starlight. The two paws are perfectly shaped, their contours and pads meticulously recreated, making it look like the kitten is playfully perched on your finger. The inner band is polished to a smooth finish, sitting comfortably against the skin without any sharp edges, balancing its charming design with wearability. The design carries a gentle message of companionship and comfort. Cats symbolize companionship and healing, and this ring acts as a forever kitten perched on your finger, offering gentle solace wherever you go. Breaking away from traditional jewelry tropes, it combines cute elements with sculptural art for a truly unique style. Versatile enough for everyday casual wear, sweet-and-cool looks, or soft feminine styles, it adds a touch of whimsical luxury to any outfit.

Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

I've been really wanting to try out iron-on t-shirt printing since the first time I saw it on Bambu. I decided on this fun design that I saw on Temu a while back. This was printed onto parchment paper that was secured to the plate with magnets and tape (on the back side), with Elmer's glue for additional adhesion (it washes off after). Please read the recommendations and instructions below carefully - they are crucial for a great print. It was a few iterations to find the right way to print this, so here are my recommendations: Only Ever Use TPU Filament: Do not attempt this with PLA or PETG. TPU (Thermoplastic Polyurethane) is a flexible rubber that acts exactly like a hot-melt adhesive when ironed, allowing it to permanently fuse into the fabric fibers. Rigid plastics will not bond correctly and will shatter or peel right off the shirt Go with Exactly 1 Layer: Scale your model's Z-height to 0.3mm and match your initial layer height to it. ( prevents the nozzle from dragging and it won't be heavy on the T-shirt ) Crawl the Speeds: Parchment paper has zero traction. You must restrict all slicer speed settings to force a slow, consistent crawl. Cap your Initial Layer Infill , Gap Infill , Outer/Inner Walls , and Top Surface all down to 20–30 mm/s . Dial in Retractions & Z-Hop: Enable a Normal Z-Hop (0.4mm) so the toolhead lifts straight up like an elevator between letters instead of dragging strings. Increase your retraction length to 1.2mm–1.5mm to stop TPU ooze. Use a Washable Glue Stick: Apply a thin, even layer of standard Elmer’s washable glue stick to the parchment paper before printing. It provides just enough tackiness to anchor fine details (like text and icons). Any leftover residue on the fabric completely dissolves on the shirt's very first wash cycle! Bed Temp: Drop the bed to 45°C and secure the paper tightly with strong magnets around the perimeter to keep it perfectly flat. Ironing: Place the print design-side-down on the shirt, press firmly with a dry iron (Medium/Wool setting) for 15 seconds without sliding it around, and let it cool completely before peeling! Enjoy printing this, and make sure to post your makes below—I'd love to see what designs you create! Happy printing!

Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: 🛍️ Trash Bag – L'eleganza nasce dove nessuno se l'aspetta Chi ha detto che il lusso debba seguire sempre le stesse regole? Trash Bag nasce proprio da questa provocazione: prendere qualcosa di estremamente semplice e quotidiano e trasformarlo in un accessorio capace di attirare ogni sguardo. È una borsa che gioca con i contrasti, mescolando ironia, design contemporaneo e raffinatezza in un oggetto unico. Le sue superfici sfaccettate ricordano un tessuto morbido che si è cristallizzato nel tempo, creando una geometria elegante e dinamica che cambia aspetto a seconda della luce. Il grande fiocco che funge da manico non è solo un dettaglio decorativo, ma il simbolo della sua personalità: romantica, femminile e audace allo stesso tempo. L'ispirazione arriva dalle linee sinuose del Liberty e dell' Art Nouveau , reinterpretate in chiave moderna attraverso la stampa 3D. Il risultato è una borsa dal carattere deciso, capace di sembrare una piccola opera d'arte più che un semplice accessorio. Che venga stampata in colori pastello delicati, in finiture opache, seta o perlati, Trash Bag cambia completamente personalità, diventando ogni volta un pezzo esclusivo. È perfetta per chi ama il design, la moda alternativa e gli oggetti che raccontano una storia. ✨ Design originale e fuori dagli schemi 🎀 Grande manico a forma di fiocco, elegante e scenografico ✨ Superficie geometrica ispirata agli origami e ai drappeggi della stoffa 💎 Perfetta come accessorio fashion, pezzo da collezione o elemento d'arredo moderno 🖨️ Progettata per valorizzare al massimo la stampa 3D con dettagli puliti e una finitura impeccabile Divertiti a personalizzarla con i tuoi filamenti preferiti: ogni colore le regalerà un'anima diversa. Dal rosa cipria al nero satinato, dal bianco perlato ai colori più vivaci... ogni Trash Bag sarà davvero unica. 📸 Hai stampato la tua versione? Pubblicala su MakerWorld ! Sono curioso di vedere le vostre combinazioni di colori, finiture e interpretazioni personali. 📖 La storia di Trash Bag La leggenda racconta che il primo prototipo nacque quasi per gioco. Un designer osservava un semplice sacchetto appoggiato sul tavolo del suo studio. Era stropicciato, imperfetto, destinato a essere buttato. Eppure, tra quelle pieghe casuali, vide qualcosa che nessun altro aveva notato: eleganza. Da quell'idea nacque una sfida. E se ciò che normalmente viene considerato banale potesse diventare qualcosa di prezioso? Così, piega dopo piega, curva dopo curva, quel concetto prese forma fino a trasformarsi in una borsa dal carattere inconfondibile. Il grande fiocco rappresenta il gesto finale: il momento in cui l'ordinario si veste di straordinario. Per questo Trash Bag non è solo una borsa. È un piccolo manifesto di creatività, un invito a guardare il mondo con occhi diversi e a trovare bellezza dove gli altri vedono soltanto normalità.

Versión B — Cara visible contra la placa La pieza se imprime con la cara frontal apoyada directamente sobre la placa , lo que hace que adopte la textura de la superficie de impresión. Esta versión no requiere soportes y ofrece un acabado limpio, ideal para quienes buscan una apariencia pulida sin posprocesado adicional. En este caso, la parte inferior debe quedar así. 🎯 Recomendación de uso Versión A : ideal si prefieres una superficie con relieve, aceptando el trabajo extra de retirar soportes. description: 水果主题便携折扇 安装说明视频： 配色说明： 创作灵感：复刻童年折扇回忆 作品取材于儿时经典层叠圆形纸折扇，依托3D打印技术重塑怀旧物件，赋予老折扇现代设计形态。 以水果横截面作为扇面核心视觉，结合扇子消暑的使用属性，借助热带水果清新甜美的气质，强化清爽氛围感，兼具实用性与创意趣味。 系列包含八款独立水果造型，自带专属图案，色彩搭配丰富，可匹配不同家居风格。 无AMS多色打印机也能制作单色版本 ，仅外观存在差异，功能性能完全相同。 手柄依照对应 水果特质定制专属纹理 ，每款握持手感各不相同； 指尖大小的开关按钮也采用水果造型 ，细节设计呼应整体主题。 机身尺寸适配大人与孩童握持，体积迷你可收纳进裤袋、包包。成品重量约50g，耗材仅60g，长时间手持不易疲惫。 扇体坚固耐用，开合手感顺滑，打印精度出众，参数经过优化，操作简单易上手。 整体全卡扣结构拼装，不用胶水与额外配件。 设计过程分享： 一开始做这把折扇，我以为弄懂结构就很容易成型，结果实操处处碰壁。 想要做出童年那种超小巧的扇子，可 FDM 机器精度有限，没法一味缩小尺寸。只能反复改模型，兼顾小巧体积、免胶卡扣组装和结构牢固度。 受打印平台限制放弃了方形扇面，改用圆形设计。加上水果图案后，打印纹路复杂，折叠很容易开裂，放射纹理的款式更是改了好几版才修好。 原本计划只做三款水果样式，越设计越觉得多款切面都很好看，一路追加到八款。全部利用下班业余时间，整整花了一个月才做完，难度远超预想。 期间还试了很多配色、不同品牌耗材，材质差异带来不少突发打印问题，都逐一调试解决。 这把小扇子耗费了不少心血反复打磨，喜欢的朋友不妨自行打印支持一下。谢谢！

Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. This is an ultra-thin, flexible emblem specifically designed to be heat-transferred onto t-shirts, hoodies, or canvas bags using your 3D printer. Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: I bring to you a glasses/sunglasses case that features a magnetic latch mechanism, allowing one-hand operation. It uses 3 12x3mm magnets to enable a tight locking/unlocking mechanism depending on the position of the latch. Make sure to insert the magnets using the right polarity, such that one of them will attract the magnet in the latch—securing the case in the closed position—, while the other will repel it—pushing it away and, hence, opening the case. In the print profile you will find two plates with one version each: “Independent_parts”. This plate prints the bottom and top parts independently, so you can print them in different colors. You will have to put them together to enable the hinge mechanism. Be aware that it might require some strength to insert the hinge in place. “Print_in_place”. This second plate features a print-in-place version. You won't have to put the top and bottom parts together, since they will be already printed together, with the hinge in place after printing. It might require a slight "breaking" by turning the hinge, just in case that the clearance is to tight for your printer resolution, but the parts should be apart enough to avoid melting and still providing the hinge natural rotating motion. There is a lot of room for improvement/enhancing, and I will continue working on this model to provide more sizes, as well as softer inserts to keep the glasses even more secure inside the case. Happy printing/protecting/transporting!

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

Bring a touch of nature and elegance to your wrist with this Orchid Lace Bracelet . This design combines the precision of 3D printing with a simple and fun post-processing technique (thermoforming) to create a perfectly curved, comfortable piece of wearable art. It features a delicate, lace-like pattern inspired by the beautiful silhouettes of orchids, making it a perfect accessory or a unique gift. 💡 The Concept & Credit This model is designed to be printed completely flat on your print bed and then shaped using hot water. While this is an original design made from scratch, the brilliant concept of using flat-printed patterns to thermoform bracelets was inspired by the work of @ G-ODA and their excellent Organic Wave Bracelet . I highly recommend checking out their work, which taught me this wonderful technique! 🛠️ How to Make It (Post-Processing Guide) Shaping the bracelet is incredibly easy and takes less than 2 minutes. Follow these simple steps: Print the file completely flat. Prepare hot water: Fill a mug or container with hot water. It doesn't need to be boiling, just hot enough to soften the plastic. Shape it: Carefully wrap the bracelet around the outside of the mug. 🖨️ Recommended Print Settings Material: PLA works perfectly for this technique as it softens at accessible temperatures. (The one in the photos is printed in Matte Olive Green). Layer Height: 0.16mm or 0.20mm for clean details. Bed Adhesion: A clean bed is recommended due to the detailed first layer. No brim needed. If you like this design, please share your makes! I'd love to see the colors you choose for your orchid bracelets.

description: A functional, aesthetic charging and display stand based around the Pebble Time 2! Includes an indent for the heart rate sensor and a non-slip TPU 95A foot. HARDWARE This project requires a couple things: Your Pebble magnetic charger. If you don't want to use the one that came with your watch, I have had luck with this one from Amazon . There are a few like this, but if you buy one without the USB C port make sure it has a thin (preferably flat), flexible cable. Right-angle USB-C adapter. If you don't use a charger with an attached cable, you will need one of these. Make sure it is slim. The fitment was modeled after one similar to these from Ugreen . USB-C cable, if you aren't using a charger with one attached. Just use one of the hundreds you have laying around at this point! 4x M3x25mm self-tapping screws. Mine came from this set . These are optional, but I like the look of screws instead of using glue and it's easier to take apart. PRINTING TIPS I have carefully painted supports, infill & walls on the included print profiles. There should be no need to tweak them. Ironing is enabled on the Pebble logo to look nice and smooth. This can be tweaked or disabled to your preference. If printing from the step files, note the following: The stand is best printed on its side so that the curves are smooth and the inset on the bottom is accurate. Ensure that your bridging is calibrated and well-tuned Ensure that the widest part of the stand at least is supported; tree supports can angle into the cavity about 10mm while remaining on the build plate and I found that to be sufficient Ensure that the inset at the bottom of the stand for the foot is supported; I had to paint on supports manually since the slicer kept wanting to print that as an overhang. The inlay side (pebble logo) of the watch holder should be printed face down and should not need supports - they're hard to remove. However, the cantilever for the heart rate sensor does need support. Print the stand and foot at 100% infill (or 1000 walls, your preference). This is to ensure they are weighty enough to offset the high weight when the watch is on the stand. Print the foot on a textured PEI plate if using TPU. I recommend 95A TPU or SEBS. The texture on the plate, when applied to the foot, greatly enhances grip. Assembly Print and Gather your parts Insert the charger (with right angle connector if applicable) into the cavity. There is an indent for the lanyard if you do not want to remove it. The lanyard can also be used to add some friction by sliding it underneath the magnetic charger. Plug the cord in and feed it through the cavity in the stand. Slide the stand onto the watch holder. Fitment is tight, so a small amount of force may be necessary. It may be easiest to slide the watch holder onto the stand, feeding the charger into the cavity as you do so. Secure 4x M3x25mm self-tapping screws into the four holes on the side of the stand. Screw them all the way in so their heads are flush to ensure that they have secured the holder to the stand. Click the logo inlay into place. It should not require glue, but a little dab does not hurt. Insert the foot into the inset in the bottom. The small peg should align to the small hole next to the cord cutout. Do not glue this in or the cord will be impossible to remove later. Fill your coffee!

Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: Say Goodbye to the Claw-Clip Head Bump! We’ve all been there: you clip your hair up, get into the car, and immediately realize you can’t lean your head back comfortably against the headrest. My wife was looking for a viral magnetic hair clip that solved this problem, but it was sold out everywhere. So, I decided to design my own! This Flat Magnetic Hair Clip is a modular, low-profile system. Instead of one bulky claw, this design uses two separate pieces held in each hand. They gather your hair in the center and snap securely together using four strong neodymium magnets. The result is a secure, flat hold that sits flush against the back of your head. Key Features: Travel & Car Friendly: Designed specifically to allow you to lean your head back comfortably on car headrests or airplane seats. Modular Design: I designed this in Autodesk Fusion with every part separated. This means ZERO SUPPORTS are required for printing! Secure Hold: Uses 4 strong magnets to lock the hair securely in place. Customizable: Because the pieces are separate, you can easily mix and match filament colors for the top caps and the base clips! Check out my YouTube Short showing how I designed and tested this: [Insert link to your YouTube Short here] 🛠️ Print Instructions & Assembly Print Settings: Material: PETG or ABS/ASA is highly recommended for durability and flexibility, but tough PLA will also work. Layer Height: 0.12mm works perfectly. Infill: 15% - 20% (Gyroid recommended). Wall Loops: 3 or 4 walls for extra strength on the clip teeth. Supports: NONE! All parts are designed to print flat on the build plate. Hardware Required: 4x Neodymium Magnets (Size: 8x5mm ). Cyanoacrylate Glue (Superglue). Assembly Guide: Print all the individual parts. Check the polarity of your magnets before gluing! Ensure the magnets on the Left Clip will attract the magnets on the Right Clip. Apply a small drop of superglue into the magnet recesses on the base clips and press the magnets firmly into place. Apply a thin layer of superglue to the top surface of the base clips. Align and press the decorative Top Caps onto the base clips, sandwiching the magnets inside. Let the glue cure completely before testing. Snap them together and enjoy comfortable travel!

description: I designed these for my daughter who wanted multiple sets to wear on her trip to Disneyland. Instead I created a single set with inserts that could be changed out easily. This is done with the magic of magnets holding a front ear frame with an insert to the back part of the ear housing on the headband. For the desings its as simple as changing the color of the ear plate and/or adding a design. I used Maker Lab’s Image to Keychain and glued them on the front, or you can even embed it with the blank earpiece for a flat printed look. Along with this I also created carring case for ear inserts, which can be found here . Additional Items used: Battery operated lights from Amazon: Fairy Battery Operated Lights Magnet set from Amazon: 400 Piece 8 Sizes Magnet Set (12 - 5*3mm & 2 - 12*3mm Magnets from set used) Hot Glue: To hold lights in place and to secure magnet holder to the bow Super Glue: To secure the magnets in place. I use Gorrila Glue Super Glue Gel Assembly: Lights: Insert the light’s battery pack, wire side to the bottom, into the battery box on the headband. The battery pack should fit snuggly in the battery box, but if desired a small dot of hot glue could be used to hold it in place. Test to see that the battery box cover slides down and you feel it ‘lock’ into place once closed. Now take the wire and dry run it (not glueing yet) to the right ear and string half the lights (10) around the ear, assuring when you complete you can run blank wire across to the other side. String the lights around the left ear and once you are sure about how they are strung, glue them in place with a small dot of hot glue. You can also place a small dot of glue on the wire crossing between the ears to bottom center of where the battery box connects to the headband. *Note: the wire on the that crosses from ear to ear will be covered by the bow. Magnets: Place a small drop of super glue into each recessed spot before inserting the magnets. 6 of the 5*3mm are used for each ear on the headband. Assure you are placing the magnets in place with the same polarity facing out. Repeat the process with the other 6 of the 5*3mm magnets for the front ear frames, assuring that the outside facing magnet polarity is attracted to the headband ears. For the bow, place a drop of super glue in the recessed spot on the cover of the battery holder and instert a 12*3mm magnet. Repeat this for the magnet holder that would go on the bow with the other 12*3mm magnet. *Note more bow magnet holders and 12*3mm magnets would be required if you want to add/change out your bows. Ears: Insert the ear plate of your choice into the front ear frame. Notches on the ear frame and plact should match up and should snap into place with slight force around the edges. Attach the front frame to the headband and repeat for the other side. To remove or change the place reverse the process appling slight force near one of the notches from the front side. Bow: The magnet cover while small is important to assure the bow does not slide off from the battery box magnet. The cover is designed to only allow pulling vs sliding of the magnets to remove the bow. To attach the magnet cover to the bow, use a small dollop of hot glue on the back of the bow near the center and attach the magnet cover. *Note it is easier to insert the magnet into the bow magnet cover prior to attaching the cover to the bow.

description: One customizable OpenSCAD generator for everyday personalized tags: keychains, luggage tags, fridge magnets, screw plates, bin labels, door signs, and desk nameplates. Universal Personalized Tag Generator Pro expands a simple winning keychain label into a broader personal-label generator. Choose a mode, type your text, and generate a practical tag for keys, bags, storage bins, fridge notes, tool panels, doors, desks, and workshop organization. The first build includes seven fast MakerWorld-ready modes: `keychain` , `luggage_tag` , `fridge_magnet` , `screw_plate` , `bin_label` , `door_sign` , and `desk_nameplate` . Each mode has sensible default size, shape, text layout, and mounting, while manual overrides let you tune the width, height, thickness, shape, mount type, and text style. Mounting options include single ring hole, double ring holes, strap slot, blind magnet pockets, screw holes with counterbores, adhesive tape recess, and no-mount plates. The default text style uses raised lettering so color changes near the top layers are easy on a standard FDM printer. Optional text styles include engraved, recessed, and inlay-ready lettering for paint, resin, or filament-fill workflows. The desk nameplate mode prints as a simple support-free wedge with text on the sloped face. Customization Notes - Use `tag_mode` first, then leave `size_preset` , `mount_type` , `text_layout` , and `shape_style` on `mode_default` for a quick printable result. - Leave `color_style` on `raised` for the easiest two-color print with a filament swap near the top layers. - Use `inlay_ready` for deeper lettering pockets that can be filled after printing. - Use `fridge_magnet` or `magnet_pockets` for blind underside magnet pockets; glue magnets in after printing. - Use `screw_plate` or `door_sign` for screw holes with counterbores. - Use `back_side` for simple underside ID text such as phone number, serial number, property label, or emergency info. - Keep very long labels short or reduce the font size for narrow tags.

How It's Made (PLA+ Method): For this specific shirt, PLA+ was used. Since this filament is tougher to melt, it requires a specific technique combining high heat and immediate pressure: Setup: Lay the t-shirt perfectly flat on a smooth, heat-resistant surface (like floor tiles). Placement: Position the main Haaland design, then carefully place the 2 or 3 small detached pieces that aren't connected to the rest. Protection: Cover the entire design with tightly stretched baking paper. Heating: Use a heat gun to melt the filament onto the fabric through the baking paper. Pressing (The key step): Immediately after heating, firmly press a wooden cutting board directly onto the hot baking paper to force the melted filament into the fabric mesh for a solid bond. ⚠️ Warning: Do not stay in one spot for too long with the heat gun! Heat evenly and keep moving, then press immediately to avoid deforming the plastic. 💡 Pro Tip: Which filament should you use? Standard PLA with a household iron (Possible, but not recommended): You can technically try using regular PLA with a standard iron (no steam) and baking paper, but the result isn't great. The plastic doesn't bond well to the fabric and tends to peel off easily. TPU Filament (The absolute best option): For the best results, we highly recommend using TPU (flexible filament) instead. It works beautifully with a regular household iron (no steam) . When heated, the TPU melts right into the fabric mesh, blending with the textile. This gives you maximum flexibility, a softer feel, and incredible longevity. 🧼 Care Instructions: To ensure your design lasts as long as possible, always wash the t-shirt at a low temperature and inside out .
