description: This is a Tweak Station used to help you remove tweak from your RC 1/28th scale chassis. There are a lot of tweak videos on youtube to show you what tweak is and how to remove it from your chassis, every chassis is slightly differnt in the way this can be achieved. This design was influenced buy a few other designs already out there and by my previous setup board also available here https://makerworld.com/en/models/2449239-1-28-mini-z-setup-board#profileId-2688656 . Usage : Adjust the leveling screws to make the bubble levels in the middle centered which should mean the platform is level, then place the car with the front axel on the pivoting section at the front or the rear depending on your preference, or what you are adjusting, then adjust the car until the front bubble level is centered, which should make the car de tweaked. Required Hardware: 3 x Bubble level inserts 29x10x10mm (I'm using these: https://www.amazon.com.au/dp/B01L4PUVHQ?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title ) 5 x Flanged bearings 4x8x3mm (I'm using these: https://www.amazon.com.au/dp/B0CGXF888Y?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title&th=1 ) 1 x Carbon fibre rod 57.5-58x4mm Or a 60x4mm steel dowel pin and file it down to size, Amazon stock it but expensive probably cheaper in local hobby shop. As many as needed 4x6mm shims of various thicknesses to space out the floating plate so it wont bind or flop around to much, can be had on Amazon but might be cheaper in local hobbyshop. Assembly: 1. Start by installing the 5 flanged bearings once installed they should sit flush into the face of the print, the fit should be snug but easy to push in or with slight persuation from the back end of a set of tweezers or something else flat pushing on the flanged side of the bearing, try to keep it parallel with the face of the print. 1.1 Push both of the bearings in the main plate in from the back side. 1.2 On the flaoting plate at the back push the bearing in from the back side. 1.3 On the front of the floating plate push both bearings in from the front. 2. To assembled both parts you can line it up as shown below then push the main plate forward and it should just fall into each other, to unassembled requires a similar process in reverse, just be careful it will pull appart with no force just have to line it up, forcing can break the bearing carrier part of the main plate at the front. Thats a bad day. 3. Once the bearings are all in place and the main parts assembled you can slide the shaft in fron the front, just take it easy and use a pair of tweezers to insert the shims if you are using them as you feed the shaft through, the shaft will be captured on both ends by the bubble level inserts so the shaft must fit flush with both bearings it cannot stick out beyond the bearings or the bubble level inserts will not fit. 4. Once the shaft is installed make sure the floating plate can pivot left to right freely and inserts the bubble level inserts very carefully, they need to be lined up perfecly flat at the top of the slots and then pushed in evenly into the slots, if they start going in at an angle they wont fit and could cause damage, better to pop them out again and slide them in flat. The photo below shows the location of the shims if used via the bown arrows, they go in between the floating plate main body and the main plate body. The last step is to screw in the leveling screws, they are designed to be slightly tight the first time you insert them but will free up after that. Don't force it and make sure they are starting on a thread and will go in nicely. Thats it, enjoy.

Warning This is a beta project . That means things will break, some geometry is still being refined, and the documentation, while thorough, is still a work in progress. Don’t expect a plug-and-play kit that works perfectly out of the box. Do not build this project unless you: Enjoy Hobby RC Enjoy 3D Printing Have built RC kits before Have a drawer (or two) of spare RC parts lying around Are comfortable with reprinting parts, tweaking parts, and troubleshooting What is Oscar SCT? Oscar is my attempt at creating a hobby-grade style 1:10 Scale, 2WD Short Course Truck. It is compatible with most off-the-shelf Short Course Truck bodies and wheels. It is designed to use standard RC electronics for the motor, battery, and steering servo. What you’ll need Various hardware (screws, nuts, bearings, etc.) - please consult the User Manual for a complete list. Electronics: Motor (540/3650/3665 size): I used: HobbyWing EZRUN 3665 3200kv brushless motor. ESC (appropriate for your motor): I used: HobbyWing EZRUN MAX10 G2. Battery (appropriate for your motor and ESC): I used: CNHL 2s Shorty Lipo Battery 4900mAh Servo: I used: a generic 30KG digital servo from Amazon. RX/TX: I used: Radiolink RC4GS V3 Shocks (~80mm): I used: 1/10 80mm RC Oil filled Shock Absorbers kit for Tamiya TRX4 Axial SCX10 Short Course Truck Body: I used: JConcepts Illuzion Ford Raptor SVT SCT-R Short Course Truck Wheel/Tires (12mm hex drive): I used: generic 2.2" SCT wheels and tires from Amazon. Body Clips Double-sided tape or Velcro for mounting electronics Velcro straps for securing battery to battery tray: I used: Apex 16mm x 300mm Straps Filament Choices I used a combination of PLA, PETG, and “TPU for AMS” for this model. CC3D 72D Flexible TPU Filament is a good alternative to “TPU for AMS”. DO NOT use a soft TPU filament . In all of my photos: Light Grey is PLA, Dark Grey is PETG, and White is TPU. Diese modulare Halterung ist die professionelle Lösung für das saubere Trocknen Ihrer bemalten oder mit Airbrush besprühten Modellteile. Das System basiert auf quadratischen und rechteckigen Platten, die mit speziellen, im Lieferumfang enthaltenen Verbindern (Connectors) beliebig erweitert werden können. Ob Sie eine lange Linie, eine T-Form oder sogar um die Ecke bauen möchten – diese Station passt sich Ihrem Arbeitsplatz und Ihren Projekten an. Ein weiterer großer Pluspunkt: Wenn die Halterung gerade nicht benötigt wird, lässt sie sich mit wenigen Handgriffen komplett auseinanderbauen. Die flachen Platten und kleinen Verbinder nehmen im Gegensatz zu klobigen Styroporblöcken so gut wie keinen Platz im Regal oder der Schublade weg. Ein wesentlicher Vorteil ist zudem die Doppelfunktion der Verbinder: 1. Platten verbinden: Um die Station beliebig zu erweitern. 2. Stabilisieren: Wenn keine weitere Platte angeschlossen wird, können die Verbinder als seitliche "Stützbeine" eingesteckt werden. Dies verhindert effektiv, dass die Platte kippt, falls Sie sehr schwere oder große Teile an der gegenüberliegenden Seite zum Trocknen platzieren. Haupteigenschaften: Maximale Modularität: Kombinieren Sie Platten und erweitern Sie diese in absolut jede Richtung. Kompakt & Platzsparend: Nach dem Projekt einfach zerlegen und mühelos verstauen. 4mm System: Kompatibel mit weit verbreiteten 4mm-Stäben (z.B. mit Alligator-Clip-Aufsätzen) oder einfachen Holzspießen. Dichte Lochmatrix: Für maximale Kapazität auf kleinem Raum. Clevere Stabilität: Integrierte Stabilisierungsfunktion durch Connectoren verhindert das Umkippen bei ungleicher Gewichtsverteilung. Druckanweisungen: Material: PLA oder PETG (PETG empfiehlt sich für etwas mehr Flexibilität bei den Verbindern). Infill: min. 8% (Ein höheres Infill sorgt für mehr Eigengewicht und somit für einen noch sichereren Stand). Düsendurchmesser: 0,4mm (Standard). Schichthöhe: 0,2mm. Support: JA, erforderlich. description: A ribbed push-in plug that caps off any round tube - bike bar-ends, furniture and chair legs, railings, fence posts, or any open pipe. Features Push-in fit : flexible barbs grip the inner wall, no glue or screws Clean finish : flange seats flush against the tube end as a visible cap Even ribs : barb spacing stays uniform for any fin count One part : works as a bar-end plug, furniture foot, or pipe cap Default Dimensions The default settings fit standard road bike handlebar ends with thick bar tape (~3 mm) wrapped into the bar end. Using thinner tape or no tape? Increase fin outer diameter so the barbs still press firmly - the plug is what locks your tape in place. Customizable Parameters This is a parametric model - every dimension is adjustable, each parameter has a description in the customizer. The key rule for a good fit: set the fin outer diameter ~0.3–0.5 mm over your tube's inner Ø, and the flange diameter larger than the tube outer Ø so the cap seats as a stop.

Hallo an alle die den EduColon Kapselautomaten gedruckt haben oder drucken wollen, (übrigens die Fensterteile findet ihr hier: https://makerworld.com/de/models/3020347-3d-window-parts-for-the-educolon-vending-machine#profileId-3393353 ) Mein Upgrade ist passend für: https://makerworld.com/de/models/1646388-remixed-full-vending-machine-200-scale#profileId-1740186 von Naddou oder https://makerworld.com/de/models/1258546-remixed-capsule-holder-for-200-scale-educolon?from=search#profileId-1282437 von Amenthyst3D. Ich habe ihn auch voller Freude gedruckt und musste schnell feststellen, dass ein paar Verbesserungen nötig sind um den Funktionsbereich zu erweitern, die Haltbarkeit des Materials zu verlängern und mehr Coins einwerfen zu können. Als erstes stellte ich fest, dass das innen liegende Fach, welches die Coins auffängt, ein sehr kleines Volumen hat. Die Coins an sich sind ja schon mit fast 5cm im Durchmesser und 6mm dicke recht klobig und groß. So kam es bei uns nahezu immer vor, dass schon nach etwa 5 Münzeinwürfen, der Münzausgang versperrt war. Die Münze blieb dann einfach unten stecken und es verklemmte sich entweder das Drehrad, oder die Münze blieb stecken und drehte einfach durch und fuhr noch einmal mit. Das sah dann so aus: Eine sehr ungünstige Situation, gerade weil ich es für Kinder gedruckt habe und das Drehen immer leichtgängig sein muss. Dreht man dennoch mit Gewalt weiter, so bricht die Mechanik die vom Drehrad gesteuert wird und man muss den Automaten wieder mühevoll auseinander nehmen und das Teil ersetzen. Die andere Option, wenn der Coin mehrfach seine Runden in der Mechanik dreht, ist das ebenfalls blöd, denn jedes Kind möchte ja seine eigene Freude am Münzeinwurf finden. Abgesehen davon, fand ich es auch blöd, dass ich etwa 20-25 Kugeln (5cm) effektiv in den Kugelbehälter einfüllen kann (bei mehr mischt und bewegt es nicht mehr so gut) aber nur etwa 5 Münzen einwerfen kann bevor das System ins stocken gerät. Ich wollte es nicht immer nach 5 Münzen schütteln oder ausleeren. Das macht keinen Spaß. Also öffnete ich den Automaten wieder und überlegte wie ich es Verbessern kann. Dann setzte ich mich an Fusion 360 und fing an meine Gedanken in einen Volumenkörper zu verwandeln. Mein Upgrade löst diese Probleme zuverlässig und beinhaltet: 1) Eine größere Münzauffangschale als Unterbau. Der fertig gedruckte Automat kann einfach auf das zusätzliche Fach drauf gestellt werden. Der Deckel an der Unterseite des Automaten muss geöffnet werden, er wird für diesen Unterbau nicht benötigt und kann bei Seite gelegt werden. In Verbindung mit der größeren Rutsche aus 2) fallen die Coins direkt durchs Loch nach unten in die große Auffangschale. Wie ein Abfluss. So können unendlich viele Coins gesammelt werden, das Volumen ist riesig. 2) Eine größere Rutsche zum nachträglichen Einkleben (doppelseitiges Klebeband reicht schon, oder Sekundenkleber) die einen zuverlässigen und schwungvollen Abgang der Coins gewährleistet und den Ausgang vor dem Steckenbleiben schützt. Die Coins bleiben also nicht mehr am Ausgang liegen und türmen sich dort, sondern bekommen mehr Schwung, um weiter nach hinten direkt durch die Öffnung im Boden zu verschwinden und von der Auffangschale aus 1) aufgefangen zu werden. Die Rutsche ist später von außen nicht mehr sichtbar, die Farbe ist daher unwichtig. 3) Eine Transport- und Ordnungsbox mit Deckel, passend für 20 Coins. Wer mehr Coins verstauen will, kann die Box in der Höhe skalieren. Berechnungsgrundlage ist, dass 1 Coin eine Höhe von 6mm hat. Meine Coins haben einen Durchmesser von 49mm. Sie passieren die Mechanik des Automaten perfekt und passen perfekt in die Box hinein. Jedes Fach kann, dank eines integrierten Schlitzes Coin für Coin geleert werden. Man muss nicht alle zusammen ausschütten. Die Aussparungen für die Coins haben einen Durchmesser von 52mm falls ihr etwas größere Coins habt, passen diese auch. 3 kurze Hinweise zum Drucken: - der Unterbaubehälter besteht aus 2 Teilen, die mit 4 Verbindern zusammengesteckt und an den Kanten geklebt werden müssen. Die Verbinder ermöglichen eine passgenaue Ausrichtung. Der Druck benötigt keine Stützen. - Ihr könnt auch die Füllung reduzieren, damit es schneller druckt (z.B. 5% Infill mit Gyroid, das ist stabil genug) - wartet bis das Druckbett abgekühlt ist, sonst reißt ihr euch die Oberfläche runter. Hier ein direkter Vorher und Nachher Vergleich als GIF: Mit und ohne mein Upgrade: Likes, Kommentare und Bewertungen werden täglich gelesen und beantwortet. Teilt gerne Fotos eurer Drucke. Ich sehe gerne wenn meine Profile zum Leben erweckt werden.

SmartLid - Smart Sourdough Starter Lid for WECK-jars is a wireless, battery-powered smart sensor lid for monitoring sourdough starter rise, temperature, humidity, and battery status. It is a complete DIY solution designed to monitor the most important parameters of your starter, helping you identify the perfect time for feeding, baking, or refrigeration. Take the guesswork out of your baking and leverage peak yeast activity for consistently better bread! The device operates fully wireless, powered by a rechargeable LiPo battery, and transmits measurements via Wi-Fi using MQTT to your smart home setup. Features Growth Tracking : Measure and understand the rise of your starter (in mm and %). Climate Monitoring : Track temperature and humidity inside the jar environment. Battery Powered : Fully wireless operation with battery voltage logging and status monitoring. Smart Home Integration : Data transmission via Wi-Fi (MQTT) for easy tracking over time. Low-Power Design : Utilizes ESP32 deep sleep to maximize battery life. Required Components Printed Parts Main Sensor Body (Lid) Upper Electronics Cover Upper & Lower Mounting Rings Electronics Microcontroller: DFRobot Beetle ESP32-C6 Mini (DFR1117) Climate Sensor: Compact 4-pin BME280 Distance Sensor: VL53L1X ToF (Time-of-Flight) sensor Battery: 3.7 V LiPo battery (Type 503040) Power/Charging: USB-C female breakout board + USB-C plug Switch: SS-12F15 slide switch (handle length: min. 3 mm) (as there are several variants of some parts, ensure that you chose the correct parts. Please see github for detailed information) Fasteners 5 x M2.5 x 6 mm screws 6 × M2.5 × 16 mm screws Compatible Glass Jars The design is specifically tailored for WECK Rundrand 100 (RR100) jars, including: WECK tapered jar 500/580 ml (WECK 742) WECK tapered jar 750/850 ml (WECK 743) WECK tulip jar 950/1062 ml (WECK 745) WECK tapered jar 900/1000 ml (WECK 908) Using a different jar? Let me know in the comments! (including inner and outer diameter at the top of the jar) If there is enough demand, I will design and upload matching adapter rings. Note: Other WECK jars using the RR100 lid size should fit as well. A sufficiently tall jar is highly recommended so the starter never touches the lid or electronics, even at peak rise! Software & Integration The complete firmware and setup documentation are available on GitHub: sourdough-smartlid The firmware is optimized for the DFRobot Beetle ESP32-C6 and publishes all sensor data natively via MQTT. Data Collection & Visualization To use this project, an MQTT broker is required. Popular solutions include: Brokers: Home Assistant + Mosquitto, ioBroker, Node-RED, OpenHAB, or standalone Mosquitto on a Raspberry Pi/NAS. Dashboards: Home Assistant Dashboards, ioBroker VIS, InfluxDB + Grafana, or custom MQTT dashboards. example of measurement graph (with grafana): How It Works & Configuration The SmartLid replaces the standard glass lid of your WECK jar. The VL53L1X Time-of-Flight sensor measures the exact distance to the starter's surface to calculate the growth percentage. Simultaneously, the BME280 tracks the microclimate. To save power, the ESP32 remains in deep sleep, wakes up at your defined interval, reads the sensors, transmits the data via Wi-Fi, and instantly goes back to sleep. Fully Configurable: Via the firmware, you can easily adjust the measuring intervals, jar height, sensor calibration offsets, and Wi-Fi/MQTT credentials. Battery-Powered Operation The device is designed to operate wirelessly from a rechargeable LiPo battery. During normal use, the ESP32 wakes up only for a short time, reads all sensors, publishes the data via MQTT, and then returns to deep sleep. This greatly reduces power consumption compared to continuous operation. Estimated runtime with 10-minute measurement intervals: at least one week. Printing & Assembly Notes Print Profile: It is highly recommended to use the provided print profile. Material Recommendation: PLA or PETG is recommended. Supports: The two rings should be printed without supports. The main sensor body and upper cover require supports. Make sure to completely clean all support remnants, especially along the continuous outer rim where the parts seal. Tolerances: Screw holes are designed to fit standard calibrations. However, since printers vary, feel free to leave a comment if you run into fitment issues! Assembly: The stack order is: Lower Ring ➔ Main Sensor Body ➔ Upper Electronics Cover ➔ Upper Ring. Detailed step-by-step assembly instructions can be found on GitHub Disclaimer Food Safety Depending on printer type, material, print settings and post-processing, the printed parts cannot be considered food-safe. Avoid direct contact between the Sourdough Monitor and your starter. Use sufficiently tall jars so that the starter cannot reach the electronics. This project is intended as a monitoring lid, not as a food-contact container surface. LiPo Batteries Lithium polymer batteries can present a fire hazard if damaged, short-circuited, improperly charged, or misused. Build and use this project at your own risk. Always use appropriate charging electronics, avoid mechanical damage to the battery, and never leave charging batteries unattended. Do not use damaged, swollen, punctured, or overheated LiPo batteries. General Disclaimer This project is provided as-is without warranty. Assembly and operation are entirely at the user's own risk. A simple and efficient tray system for organizing 12GA rounds inside a standard M2A1 .50‑cal ammo can. Capacity may vary depending on cartridge length and arrangement. The tray supports two primary loading directions, indicated by arrow markings. When filling a row, if there is not enough space to continue in the same orientation near the end, the remaining space can often be used by inserting one or more cartridges perpendicular to the original direction. This allows for more efficient use of available space and can increase the total number of rounds per tray. An M2A1 .50‑cal ammo can fits up to 7 trays. The trays are designed for easy handling. All but the top tray feature small integrated handles, making it quick to grab and remove them from the box. The top tray is handle-free to avoid interference with the lid. Since most ammo boxes have a raised or uneven base, a spacer is included to provide a stable platform for the bottom tray. Printed in PETG, these trays are durable enough for regular use. If you plan to store ammo in a car trunk or in direct sunlight, ASA is recommended for improved heat resistance. model_name: Kumihimo the friendship braclet / keychain maker
description: This is a kumihimo wheel, a thing to help weave friendship braclets, regular braclets or keychains. Works best printed in TPU, but works in PLA too. How to weave? First, grab 4 strings about the same lenght and tie a knot in the middle as shown, then you will have 8 strings in total. Pull the knot through the middle of the wheel, through the biggest hole. Then, put the strings on the wheel in a cross pattern, as shown in the picture below. Now, the weaving begins. put the top left string to the bottom left. Next, put the bottom right string to the top right. Rotate the entire wheel 90 degrees counter-clockwise. Do the same thing to the other set of strings. Rotate 90 degrees, and repeat until you are happy with your keychain's length. Remove from the wheel and tie a knot at the top. Thank you for reading. Happy printing and making!

Dopo aver stampato il bellissimo modello della Arcadia Verde, volevo stampare anche l'Arcadia Blu. Il modello 3D si trova facilmente in commercio ed è molto bello ma, dal momento che non ho AMS, avrei dovuto lavorare tanto per poterlo stampare e, avendo quel modello una licenza commerciale, non avrei poi potuto condividere il mio lavoro. Allora sono partito da un modello abbastanza buono trovato in rete con licenza CCO (per uso pubblico) e ho tagliato, modificato e aggiunto per 2 mesi. Ho usato per il 95% del lavoro lo slicer Bambu Studio e solo per alcune superfici complesse ho usato Meshmixer. Non ho usato strumenti CAD e questo impatta sul risultato finale. Il risultato non è una replica perfetta dell'Arcadia originale, ma è molto simile. La punta dovrebbe essere più piccola e le ali più lunghe sulla parte posteriore, ma mi ritengo soddisfatto. Il modello stampato al 100% è lungo 60 cm (precisamente 25x25x60) Ho inserito anche un piedistallo per esposizione provvisorio, ne realizzerò uno migliore. La cosa che mi soddisfa di meno è la mia scelta dei colori. Secondo me serve un blu più scuro di quello che ho usato io ma non lo avevo. Lo ho comprato e proverò a stampare una versione più piccola (60%) ottimizzando sia i pezzi sia il colore finale. CONSIGLI PER LA STAMPA: in generale i pezzi grandi vanno stampati con layer da 0,2 e quelli piccoli con layer da 0,16. Ma ci sono molti casi in cui stampare pezzi grandi con layer da 0,16 aiuta a diminuire il numero di supporti e quindi migliora molto la qualità della stampa finale. Fare molta attenzione alle ali posteriori e alla lama anteriore. CONSIGLI PER IL MONTAGGIO: molta colla e pochi inserti. Alcune parti sono complicate da montare (es. le ali posteriori). Ho allegato le istruzioni di montaggio. Il problema più grosso? Le ossa dei teschi. NOTA: chiedo ai primi che stamperanno questo modello di avere un po' di pazienza perché, a causa dell'alto numero di pezzi (100), potrebbero esserci errori o dimenticanze.

Pottery Tip 1 - You can get a deeper plate/bowl by pressing into thicker foam. When making a deeper press, flip your piece upside down with the inner press plate still in place and set it on top of a glaze bottle or something to keep it raised until the clay has a chance to get more solid. If you’re making multiple deep plates at one time, print multiple copies of just the inner plate so you can continue making while your finished pieces rest! more sizes will be available soon / if demand is good :) After looking at normal paintbrushes and thinking, “surely a 3D printer could make one of these,” I ended up making this fully 3D printed working paintbrush. The full brush can print in under 40 minutes , and the best part is that the bristles are replaceable. So if they get too worn, bent, clogged up, or abused during a project, you can just print a fresh set of bristles instead of binning the whole brush. The bristle section is designed to be folded at the 43 mm point so it fits snugly into the brush head. Once fitted, the bristles stick out around 60 mm , but this is very customizable. You can cut them shorter, trim them into shape, or stiffen/soften the feel depending on what you want to use it for. The full brush is around 150 mm long , with the red handle section being roughly 75 mm , making it a short, comfortable, quick-use brush rather than a big chunky tool. This started as a fun “can this be done?” 3D printing idea, but it is actually useful. It could be used as: A quick emergency paintbrush A dusting brush A delicate cleaning brush A model-making brush A small archaeology/excavation-style brush A workshop brush for loose dust or debris Or whatever random use you find for it check oit the pics for assembly help The idea is simple: imagine being somewhere with a 3D printer but no brush. A workshop, research facility, maker space, garage, classroom, campsite, or just your house at midnight when you suddenly need to paint something. Print this, fold the bristles, slot them in, and you have a working brush. No AMS is needed. It can be printed as separate colour parts, or all in one colour if you just want the fastest functional version. Print / Assembly Notes Bristle fold point: 43 mm Bristle length sticking out: around 60 mm Full brush length: around 150 mm Handle grip length: around 75 mm Print time: under 40 minutes AMS: not required To assemble, fold the bristle part at the 43 mm point and fit it snugly into the brush head. Spirograph This collection of templates represents a comprehensive set of spirographs useful for drawing curves of all kinds. What is a spirograph and how does it work? A spirograph is an instrument used to draw curves called hypotrochoids. It is based on a simple concept: a circumference that rotates in a bigger circumference in a specified ratio. In fact what is important to understand how it works is to know the number of teeth of the bigger wheel, which we call R and the number of teeth of the smaller wheel, which we call r . The nominator of fraction reduced to its lowest terms between R and r tells us the number of petals that our hypotrochoids will have while the denominator, the number of revolutions the smaller wheel will do in the bigger one. The higher the numerator and denominator, the denser hypotrochoids will be, this is likely to happen when the denominator is high and a prime number since it will not be possible to reduce the fraction. How to draw? To draw, you must select and position the large circle (the one with teeth facing inward) in the center of the sheet. Then, choose a small circle (the one with teeth facing outward) and place it inside the large circle so that the teeth mesh. Finally, insert the pen into the desired hole and begin making elliptical movements, trying to follow the path of the small circle while ensuring it never separates from the large one. How to print the model? Each print profile features a wheel R —named after the profile itself—along with smaller wheels r designed to produce a particularly interesting result when combined with that R wheel. You can therefore print the large wheel and any or all of the small wheels included in the print profile. There is nothing to stop you from using small wheels "r" from other print profiles to achieve endless variations. Documentation Before printing, you can view a preview of the designs that can be created using various combinations of large wheels (R) and small wheels (r). This is an example of what you will find in the preview; this way, you can identify a design you like and know exactly which wheel size and which wheel hole to use.

model_name: Drone Launching Platform - Compact Folding Plate
description: This is a compact folding drone platform to give your drone a flat surface to take off from or land on. They can also be used for marking for surveys or even as a simple fold-able tray. It can be customized for the exact size you want/need it to be. Using the Makerworld Parametric Model Maker Click the “Customize” button above then click “Customize” again and it will bring you to the Makerworld Parametric Model Maker. To customize this model for you: Change the “Plate Width” to the width you want the plate to be. If you are fitting this into a case use the space you have available minus about 2mm so if you have 170mm available make it 168mm. Remember this is for each individual plate which is the size when folded. The actual plate size unfolded will be double this. Change the “Plate Length” to the length you want the plate to be. This needs a little extra space for the hinges so minus 2mm and the plate height below. So if have 130mm available subtract plate height (4.5mm) + 2mm buffer gets you to 123.5mm. Change the "Plate Height" if needed. Try to stay to a 4.5mm minimum. This one shouldn't need much extra clearance as the plate folds pretty flat but add a 1mm - 2mm buffer just in case. So if your space is 20mm the height can go up to 4.75mm (4.75mm x 4 main plates = 19mm + 1mm buffer). For standard pieces of filament used for the hinges leave the bore as 1.05mm. All the hinges are offset plate to plate by 0.1mm like a slight zigzag so at 1.05mm radius the effective diameter is actually 2.0mm even (1.05mm * 2mm = 2.1mm minus the 0.1mm offset). This seems to be the best value for this where the bores aren't to tight to get filament in but also not too loose where it falls out. The drop down for “Which Part” you want to create will default to “Everything” which is usually what you want. If you changed the sizes above click “Generate” to refresh the model. Click “Download” then select your printer and click “Confirm”. Click “Download” again and select a 3MF file then when prompted save the file. Open the file in Bambu Studio, right click the model, and select “Split → To Objects”. Add some additional print plates to your model then move each folding plate to its own with Plate 5 (the thin one) on a plate with the clips. Make sure to right click and “Auto Rotate” each plate which will put everything into the best orientations with the hinges up and the face of the plate down. Turn on support, set your default profile (I recommend 0.20 High Quality), for a bit of extra sturdiness set the walls to 3 or 4, and print. Download a Premade Model There are currently three different types of premade models if you don't want to use the generator. They are all 320mm x 260mm x 4mm when expanded and 160x135x16.5mm when folded up and were sized to fit this drone case: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2516787-dji-mini-3-4-5-pro-fly-more-case#profileId-2768315 Integrated Hinge & Sliders : This is the model that is fully parametric (above) and you can generate any size you want. Only download this if you don't want to mess with customizing and this size works for you. It has a total of 5 plates as one is a intermediate plate used for hinges. Because of this there is a small notch cut out of plates 1 and 2 to make room for it. It has sliding locks on the edges that nest out of the way but because of that it needs supports. However this is the most sturdy version and with the generator you can make any size plates you want. This is the recommended model . Dedicated support material is also highly recommended. In the pictures this model is the first one printed in Bambu White ABS and the default example photos. Raised Hinge : This raises the one hinge higher so it can sit on the bottom like the other hinges but because of this there is a small notch cut out of plates 1 and 2. A wider sliding lock is then added to gap that spot. This allows all the plates to be printed on their face. It is the fastest to print and requires no supports. This is the recommended model if you don't want supports . In the pictures this model is the last one printed in Bambu White ABS. Standard : This is the simplest design but to make the folds work one hinge is on the top with the other two on the bottom. Since plates 3 and 4 have hinges on two edges going opposite directions they need to either be printed vertically (not recommended but works) or horizontally with support material under them (this is how the print profile is set). Dedicated support material is highly recommended. In the pictures this model is printed using Bambu Orange ABS. Custom Sizes I have included the FreeCAD source files for the two models that are not parametric. I have also included the FreeCAD Macro for creating custom sizes of the standard and integrated hinge types (same as the generator but you don't have to use credits). With that said if you need another size and are unable to use the generator send me a message. I can get one made in a couple minutes and then post it for everyone else that might use the same container/case as you.

EcoFlow Wave 2 Wall Vent Adapter / Wanddurchführung Die EcoFlow Wave 2 ist eine fantastische mobile Klimaanlage, aber die Abluftschläuche lose aus einem Spalt im Fenster zu hängen, ist oft unpraktisch und ineffizient. Mit diesem maßgeschneiderten Wandanschluss-Set schaffst du eine saubere, permanente und professionelle Lösung – perfekt für Gartenhäuser, Werkstätten, Camper oder Tiny Houses! Das System sorgt für einen perfekten Luftaustausch durch die Wand und ersetzt provisorische Lösungen durch ein robustes, verschraubbares Design, das innen wie außen hervorragend aussieht. ✨ Design-Highlights Maßgeschneiderte Passform: Exakt auf die Abluft- und Zuluftschläuche der EcoFlow Wave 2 abgestimmt. Die Schläuche sitzen fest und sicher. Zweiteiliges System: Das Design umfasst den inneren Befestigungsring für die Schläuche sowie eine schicke Lamellenblende für die Außenwand. Integrierter Wetterschutz: Die nach unten abgewinkelten Lamellen der Außenblende verhindern zuverlässig, dass Regenwasser, Laub oder Schmutz in den Raum eindringen. Sicherer Halt: Durch die integrierten Schraublöcher lässt sich das System bombenfest im Holz oder in Gehäusewänden verankern. 🖨️ Druck-Empfehlungen Wichtiger Hinweis zur Hitze: Die Abluft der Klimaanlage wird im Betrieb sehr heiß. PLA ist für dieses Projekt ungeeignet, da es sich schnell verformen würde. Material: ABS ist für dieses Modell die absolute Top-Wahl. Es ist extrem hitzebeständig, UV-resistent (für die Außenseite) und sehr robust. Durch einen geschlossenen Bauraum lässt es sich verzugsfrei drucken. Alternativ funktioniert PETG ebenfalls hervorragend. Schichthöhe: 0.20 mm bietet die beste Balance aus Stabilität und einer sauberen Optik für die Lamellen. Wandlinien (Wall Loops): Verwende mindestens 4 bis 5 Wandlinien. Das gibt dem Adapterring die nötige Festigkeit, wenn die dicken Schläuche bewegt werden, und verhindert, dass die Schraublöcher ausreißen. Infill: 15–20% (Gyroid) sind optimal. Tipp für perfekte Überhänge: Gerade bei den Lamellen der Außenblende und den Anschlüssen ist trockenes Filament entscheidend. Frisch aus dem Filamenttrockner gedruckt, werden die Überhänge und Kanten absolut sauber, was die spätere Montage der Schläuche extrem erleichtert. 🔧 Zubehör & Montage Du benötigst: Holz- oder Blechschrauben (je nach Wandbeschaffenheit) Ich persönlich habe M-Schraubgewinde eingeschmolzen, ist aber kein muss. Optional: Etwas Silikon oder Dichtband, um die äußere Blende komplett wetterfest gegen die Wand abzudichten. Die Montage ist unkompliziert: Kreisrunde Ausschnitte an der gewünschten Stelle in die Wand sägen (z. B. mit einer Lochsäge oder Stichsäge). Die äußere Lamellenblende von außen in die Öffnung setzen und verschrauben. Den inneren Adapterring von innen fluchtend ansetzen und ebenfalls festschrauben. description: HALO GP — MotoGP Desktop Companion Case Always know when the next session starts. No apps, no aggressive ads, no searching. Born from the foundations of Halo F1 . What is Halo GP? Halo GP is a sleek, always-on desktop companion for MotoGP fans. Built around the JC4827W543 , an ESP32 all-in-one board from Guition with a 4.3" capacitive touch display. It sits on your desk and gives you everything you need about the current MotoGP season at a glance: 🏁 Session times for the next race weekend, automatically converted to your local timezone 🏆 Drivers' championship standings , updated live 📋 Session results: qualifying, race and sprint at the moment they're published 📰 Latest MotoGP news headlines , fetched directly from the web (experimental, only english for now) 🌙 Night mode with configurable time window and brightness 🌍 Many languages : English, Italian, Spanish, French, Dutch, German and counting… No subscription. No app. No aggressive ads. Just plug it in and glance at it. About this case This is the official case for the Halo GP project. It's designed to be simple to print, simple to assemble, and good-looking on a desk. The case is a two-piece snap fit : the front and back halves slide-in together and hold the board securely with no screws, no glue, and no inserts. Disassembly takes seconds if you ever need to reflash or tinker. Designed specifically for the JC4827W543 board with its integrated 4.3" capacitive touch TFT display. Print settings Setting Recommendation Material PLA or PETG Layer height 0.2 mm Infill 15–20% gyroid Supports Yes Brim Not necessary Print time is approximately 3 hours on a typical FDM printer. No post-processing needed beyond removing the supports. Getting started with Halo GP Print this case Flash the free firmware directly from your browser (no drivers, no software) at halof1.com (select Halo GP FW) On first boot, connect to the Halo-MotoGP Wi-Fi hotspot from your phone or PC and enter your home Wi-Fi credentials Snap the case shut and put it on your desk That's it. The whole setup takes under 5 minutes. Hardware you'll need 1× JC4827W543 board with capacitive touch ( you can buy it from Aliexpress from this link ) 1× USB-C cable and a phone charger to power it Important Before You Assembly: This is the items you should receive when ordering the board. The black thing on the left is a WiFi antenna with an Ipex connector. It is very important you connect it on the back of the board, otherwise it will not get a stable connection on the WiFi. If you don't receive an antenna with your board, you can buy any Ipex Antenna from Aliexpress, Amazon, Temu, … To install the antenna, simply align it on the connector on the corner of the main chip, then press firmly. It should slot into place and stay attached. Once you place the screen into the case, simply bend the antenna to fit it in the free space at the top. Common Troubleshooting: Connect to the PC via a USB A → USB C cable, USB C → USB C cables usually don't work. Check that your cable is a data cable, otherwise you won't be able to upload the firmware. Once the firmware is uploaded you can use a power only cable to power it, if you prefer. To flash the firmware connect to halof1.com and connect your board to the PC. Go to the “Install Firmware” section and press “Connect”, then select your device's COM port from the dialog and proceed with the installation wizard. WLED Remote+ - WLED Remote & HomeKit Bridge A standalone ESP32-S3 controller for WLED that combines a physical remote UI with a HomeKit bridge on a LilyGo T-Display S3. The project provides local hardware controls, WLED discovery and control over the network, and Apple Home integration in a single device. Features Physical remote interface with the built-in display, left/right buttons, and rotary encoder on the LilyGo T-Display S3 hardware. WLED discovery on the local network using mDNS plus direct control through the WLED JSON API. HomeKit bridge support via HomeSpan, exposing WLED as a light plus preset switches for Apple Home. Captive-portal Wi-Fi onboarding with fallback configuration flow and persistent settings stored in NVS. Embedded local configuration web UI served on port 8080 for setup, discovery, status, and reset actions. Built with PlatformIO for the lilygo-t-display-s3 environment and Arduino framework on ESP32. Hardware The target device is a LilyGo T-Display S3 with ESP32-S3, PSRAM, a 170x320 ST7789 display, two front buttons, and a rotary encoder used for navigation and control. The display stack is driven with LovyanGFX, and the project also depends on WiFiManager, HomeSpan, and ArduinoJson. Setup Flash the firmware to the board and boot it. Connect the device to Wi-Fi using the built-in WiFiManager flow; if saved credentials fail, it falls back to a captive portal for setup. Discover a WLED instance on the local network or configure the WLED host manually through the local config UI. Open the configuration page on port 8080 to review status, scan for devices, save settings, or reset configuration. Pair the device with Apple Home using the HomeKit QR flow shown by the UI when HomeKit is enabled. HomeKit behavior The HomeKit bridge exposes one light bulb accessory with On, Brightness, Hue, and Saturation characteristics, plus up to eight switch accessories that trigger WLED presets.[cite:2] The project overview also notes a default HomeKit setup code of 46637726, and the firmware can generate an X-HM:// pairing URI for QR-based setup. WLED integration The firmware talks to WLED over HTTP using endpoints such as /json/state, /json/effects, and /json/presets, and it posts state updates back to /json/state for actions like power, brightness, color, effect, and preset selection. WLED instances are discovered over mDNS using the _wled._tcp service, which keeps first-time configuration simple on a local network. AI assistance This project was developed with the help of AI-assisted tooling for planning, code generation, refactoring, and documentation support. Depending on the Task, different Technologies whre used. Mostly QWEN and GEMMA Models through ollama, but also cloud Models like Claude Opus were used. There are quite some files in this repository to guide AI Agents into writing better code and not making too many mistakes. You can use them as a guideline for your own project. Conçu initialement pour le standard 40 mm (entraxe 65 mm) des carburateurs légendaires comme les Weber DCOE, Dell'Orto DHLA ou Solex ADDHE (ex: BX Sport, Alfa Romeo, etc.), ce modèle est entièrement modifiable via l'outil de personnalisation MakerLab pour s'adapter à n'importe quel projet . Que vous cherchiez un simple cornet droit pour votre boîte à air ou un design expérimental pour optimiser le flux d'air, tout est à portée de clic. ✨ Fonctionnalités Uniques et Personnalisables Grâce au générateur paramétrique, vous pouvez ajuster absolument toutes les cotes de la pièce sans logiciel de CAO complexe : 📏 Dimensions sur mesure : Modifiez la hauteur totale, le diamètre d'entrée (l'évasement), le diamètre intérieur de la base et l'épaisseur de la paroi. 🔧 Platine adaptable : Ajustez l'entraxe des goujons, le diamètre des trous et l'épaisseur de la platine pour correspondre à vos carburateurs ou corps papillon (ITB). 🌪️ Option "Vortex" (Style TMAX) : Cochez une simple case pour générer des ailettes internes torsadées ! Le générateur sculpte des pales parfaitement plaquées contre la paroi courbe de la trompette pour créer un flux d'air tourbillonnaire. Vous pouvez régler le nombre d'ailettes, leur épaisseur, leur profondeur et leur angle de torsion. ⛳ Option "Dimples" (Effet Balle de Golf) : Activez cette option pour creuser un motif de petites sphères en quinconce sur toute la surface interne. Cet effet aérodynamique est pensé pour perturber la couche limite et améliorer la vitesse des gaz (comme sur une balle de golf !). ⚙️ Paramètres d'Impression Recommandés Pour une utilisation dans le compartiment moteur, le choix du matériau et des paramètres est crucial pour résister à la chaleur et aux hydrocarbures. Matériau : ASA, ABS, PETG ou Nylon-Carbone (PA-CF). Évitez absolument le PLA , qui se déformerait rapidement avec la chaleur du moteur. Orientation : Imprimez la pièce à plat sur sa platine de fixation (côté moteur vers le bas). Hauteur de couche : 0.12 mm ou 0.16 mm maximum pour garantir une surface interne la plus lisse possible (crucial pour le flux d'air). Supports : Normalement inutiles si l'évasement (courbure) n'est pas trop extrême. Si vous activez l'option "Dimples", une ventilation adéquate est recommandée. Remplissage (Infill) : 100% ou un nombre important de murs (Wall loops : 4 à 6) pour garantir la solidité au niveau de la fixation. 🛠️ Assemblage Ce modèle (dans ses dimensions par défaut de 40mm) utilise la visserie M6 standard des carburateurs concernés. N'hésitez pas à partager vos réalisations, vos réglages de Vortex/Dimples, et les véhicules sur lesquels vous avez monté ces cornets dans les commentaires ! Avertissement : Pièce destinée à un usage sur circuit, compétition ou prototypage expérimental. La modification de l'admission peut nécessiter un nouveau réglage de la carburation (gicleurs) ou de la cartographie.

AI-generated images are provided only to illustrate possible use cases and are not intended to represent the exact product. Overview The Modular Dive Marker is a fully 3D printable diving marker designed for pools, swimming practice and underwater games. The system consists of a weighted anchor and a floating buoy connected by a rope. Once placed in the water, the anchor sinks to the bottom while the buoy remains visible at the surface, creating a fixed underwater reference point. The anchor can also be used without the buoy as a simple diving target. The design is intentionally modular and easy to customize. An editable STEP file is included, allowing you to modify the model in your preferred CAD software. Features Fully 3D printable Editable STEP file included Modular design User-fillable anchor User-fillable buoy Adjustable rope length (simply tie a new knot) No special hardware required Easy to customize Designed for remixing Anchor The anchor consists of two printed parts. The rope is inserted through the top opening and secured inside the housing with a simple knot that can be accessed through the side opening. The bottom cap unscrews and can be filled with almost any ballast material, for example: Gravel Small stones Stainless steel nuts Screws Fishing weights Aquarium gravel Adjust the ballast amount to match your pool depth and desired stability. The anchor can also be used without the buoy as a standalone diving target for swimming practice and underwater games. Floating Buoy The buoy consists of three printed parts. Its geometry provides enough buoyancy to float on the water surface without requiring any additional foam or flotation material . Simply print the three parts, assemble them and attach the rope. The design is lightweight, durable and easy to customize. Printing Notes ⚠️ Please do not modify the recommended print settings. The anchor body has been intentionally designed without top and bottom solid layers . This allows water to quickly enter the exposed infill structure, preventing trapped air and significantly improving the sinking performance. The visible infill on the top and bottom surfaces is part of the design and not a printing defect . Changing these settings may reduce the anchor's performance and prevent it from sinking as intended. Designed for Customization This project was intentionally designed to be modified. Feel free to create your own versions. Future Buoy Ideas The included buoy is only one possible design. Possible alternatives: Classic buoy Star Heart Diamond Fish Shark fin Turtle Octopus Pirate barrel Treasure chest Lifebuoy Flag Balloon Pumpkin Christmas ornament Ghost Skull Crown Rocket UFO Game Ideas One marker already offers plenty of possibilities: Dive around the marker Retrieve the anchor Underwater navigation Swimming practice Diving challenges Time trials Using multiple markers opens up even more ideas: Obstacle courses Treasure hunts Team relay races Underwater slalom Orientation training Marker collection games Custom diving games Printing Recommended Material PLA PETG (recommended for outdoor use) Supports No supports required. Layer Height 0.20 mm Infill 15–20% Assembly Print all parts. Insert the rope through the anchor. Tie the rope inside the anchor. Fill the anchor with ballast. Screw on the bottom cap. Feed the rope through the bottom part of the buoy . Secure the rope with a knot inside the buoy. Assemble the buoy. Adjust the rope length by tying a new knot inside the anchor if necessary. Included Files Editable STEP file Safety This model is a diving game accessory . It is not a lifesaving or flotation device. Always supervise children around water. Use only in safe swimming environments. Remix This project was designed with customization in mind. Feel free to modify, improve and remix the design. Use this material for best results. Do NOT use PLA Matte, especially for the wing parts. Printed parts may deform after removal from the Plate due to internal material strains after cooling. Use recommended print settings. Note: The print profile for A1 mini use slightly higher material flow coefficient (1.03 instead of 0.98). For reliable printing: Clean the printing Plate before printing. After printing, remove the Plate and let it cool for 3-4 minutes Do not remove parts while the Plate is hot. 4 - Model Assembly The model consists of 20 parts, as shown in the figure. 1 – Nose, 2 – PCB Mount, 3 – A-Beam (3pcs), 4 – B-Beam, 5 – Strut (2pcs), 6 – Sting, 7 – Tail, 8 – Fin, 9 – Central Bracket, 10 – Dual-pin, 11 – Right Wing, 12 – Left Wing , 13 – Right Big Rib, 14 – Left Big Rib, 15 – Small Rib (2pcs), 16 – Gear mount, 17 – Gear Strut (2pcs), 18 – Wheel (2pcs), 19 – Pin (2pcs), 20 – BHCS Screw M2 x 4 mm (4 pcs). Note : RC Receiver, Engines, props are not shown. The following assembly steps are shown without the electronic components installed. It is recommended to review them before installing the motors and electronics. Use cyanoacrylate glue where specifically indicated. Assemble the tail unit and fuselage as shown. Assemble the wing as shown in the figure. Use Dual-pin to fix wings. After installing and fixing the wing surfaces, install Big Ribs (13, 14) on both sides. Finally, install the Ribs (15) on both sides. Wing assembly completed. To install the wing on the fuselage, pull the fuselage beam through predefined guide points on the wing Central Bracket, as shown in the picture. A slight pushing force may be gently applied if needed. Assemble landing gear unit as shown on Figure. Install landing gear on Fuselage. To fix finally the wing and landing gear position the M2x4 screws to be installed. Do not fix wing and gear assembly finally on this step! 4.1 - Electronic Components Installation Install RC transmitter PCB on bracket (2). Finally, connect the motors to the receiver board as shown in the illustration. Before final assembly, make sure the motors rotate in opposite directions. For easier assembly and adjustment, the wires should be approximately 130 mm long. The wires are preferable to route through the rib. Install the ribs with the motors onto the wing as shown in the illustration. The motors must be positioned on the outer side of each rib. Install the wing onto the lower beam, approximately at the middle of the span. Then route the motor wires behind the lower beam and around the upper beam in a figure-eight pattern, as shown in the illustration. This routing keeps the wires secure while still allowing the wing position to be adjusted. Only after routing the wires, install the landing gear, followed by the receiver bracket (2). Install the nose part (1) and secure it with screw (20). As a final step, apply a strip of clear adhesive tape to each motor, or secure it with a small drop of glue, to prevent it from rotating during operation. Install the battery and hold it in place with a suitable rubber band. The model assembly is now complete. 4.2 - Balancing Perform the pre-flight balancing check with the battery installed. Place the model on a balancing stand using the designated balance points on the wing. The model should remain level or tip slightly nose-down. Fix finally the screws (20) of wing assembly and gear bracket. 5 - Model Flight Launch the model outdoors in calm weather or slight breeze conditions. Recommended wind speed: up to 5 km/h (≈1.4 m/s, ≈2.7 knots) . Always launch the model directly into the wind . Model initially pre-balanced during assembly. Launch the model applying full throttle with a gentle horizontal push. If the model dives strongly, then: Move the wing slightly forward, OR bend the elevator slightly upward. If the model pitches up or stalls, first try reducing the flight speed. If flight speed reduction does not help, then: Move the wing slightly backward, OR bend the elevator slightly downward. Happy Flights and Smooth Landings!

description: fix for subaru crosstrek / subaru impreza cup holder. Cup holder insert that secures drinks better. I have had my car for many years, and for all that time I have disliked the cup holder design. for some reason it isnt complete circles, and has a bunch of extra room that leads to most beverage containers to be so loose, that as you turn, start, and stop, its got a high chance of tipping. Finally I had one spill to many and started looking for commercially available solutions. I decided that with a little bit of work, I could design my own cup holder insert that fixes my issues and fits great. Took me longer than I would have liked, but im excited to share the result of this work. A bit about my solution: So for starters, This model was designed for use with PETG or other material that will not warp or degrade from the sun and heat its surely to be constantly subjected to. The insert fits great in my cup holder, a 2020 Subaru Crosstrek. I'm certain it fits the 2018-2021 models for sure, you'll have to confirm for sure if it fits in other years. I'm sure it fits in the Impreza as well, as the interiors are the same. The insert is held in just by the taper of the cup holder, and it seems to secure it great, yet allow easy removal for when you do need the larger size opening. I designed it to start a bit above the bottom of the cup holder, to allow for cup holder inserts you might be using, and the small gap at the bottom makes it easy to remove by grabbing it in the gap at the bottom. The top of the insert falls just below the divider in between cup holders, and includes the opening for handles. I kept it at a height to roll into the radius of the cup holder, and the rim of the insert matches up to just below the trim of the cars cup holder opening. The holder can be used in the front or back position and fits the same in either. Personally I like to use it in only my back cup holder, leaving the larger front to place items or larger drinks like Gatoraid bottles. I tested and made many revisions in the sizing to get to the current design that im sharing. It will easily keep any normal sized can secure, yet not to tight as to stay stuck on the can when you take it out. it also fits fast food and coffee cups great. I haven't had any issues with sizing of the most common drink containers so far. I'm including a few print profiles. my personal favourite is PETG 100% infill for a nice solid piece. for those that dont want to commit as much print time or material, I have a PETG 15% infill version. I do not recommend it for long term use, but I know some will want it, so i have included a PLA 15% infill print profile as well. If it warps from heat in your car, please don't come back and complain as I have warned that its not the ideal material..

Meet Wheely , probably the cutest little starter robot you'll print this week. It’s designed to be super beginner-friendly, making it a perfect weekend project to get into robotics without the usual wiring headaches. This project is a mashup of a few designs I love. It’s a remix that combines the modularity and style of CUBY , the fun community spirit of Otto DIY , and some clever mechanical ideas from Winchy . Weekend project You won't need to waste days of printing time or a whole spool of filament for this one. It's an incredibly optimized print that only uses 82 grams of filament! In just 3 hours and 44 minutes you will be building the robot ready to start playing. Servos For the wheels you will need 2x 9g Continuous Rotation Digital Servo-360°. Instead of using standard DC motors I decided to build Wheely around servo motors. Servos are way easier to wire up, plug in, and program. If you are just starting out or building this with kids, this setup will save you a lot of frustration. The Remote Control: The controller layout is very intuitive. Each joystick directly controls one servo, giving you easy, tank-like steering control. Speed & Power: In the default code, I have programmed the servos to run at 50% power. This keeps the movements smooth, quiet, and perfect for driving around a desk. However, if you want more speed, you can easily modify the code to unleash 100% of their power. Controller and control scheme At this moment you can use the CyberBrick Official Standard Remote or other controller that uses the same wiring.

I created an all‑direction practice protector for TinyWhoop. It is available in two sizes: a 130 mm type and a 160 mm type. By mounting this 360° protector parallel and level to the aircraft’s center axis, acro‑mode flight becomes possible. Because the weight increases, the operating difficulty becomes slightly higher, but since the guard is installed, I believe the likelihood of damage is reduced. The structure has moderate flexibility, helping protect the FC and the frame. It can also run along the ground. The weight is approximately 16 g for the 130 mm type and about 20 g for the 160 mm type, so it is recommended for use with 0802 motors or larger. Print Parts 1–3 in PETG, and Parts 4–5 in TPU. For assembly, 3 mm acrylic rods are required, which can be purchased inexpensively at home improvement stores. For the 130 mm type, use six rods cut to about 75–80 mm and one rod cut to about 130 mm. For the 160 mm type, use six rods cut to 100 mm and one rod cut to 160 mm. Adjust the lengths as needed depending on the six rods placed around the circumference. Please make sure the six rods around the circumference are all the same length. After forming the circular shape with these six rods, determine the final length of the center acrylic rod. Cut the center rod slightly longer at first, then trim off the excess after test‑fitting to avoid mistakes. model_name: Eclipse Putter - Low Torque / Modular / High MOI
description: Eclipse - A Modular High-MOI 3D Printed Putter Looking for a customizable putter without the price tag of today's premium designs? This project combines the flexibility of 3D printing with design features inspired by modern high-performance putters. The putter head is designed to incorporate removable weights, allowing the majority of the mass to be positioned around the perimeter. This increases the moment of inertia (MOI), helping improve stability on off-center strikes while reducing twisting through impact. One of the key features of this design is its modular construction. The shaft insert is a separate component that bolts into the main putter head, allowing different putter head designs to be swapped without needing to remove or reinstall the shaft. Simply remove a few screws, install a new head, and you're ready to go. The shaft insert has a lie angle of 74 degrees and a static loft angle of 3 degrees to match the feel of many center-shafted putters. The design of the head of the putter has been carefully made to ensure that the center of mass is aligned with both the center of the face and the shaft when all weights are inserted. Therefore, the design of this putter naturally eliminates the majority of the torque produced when swinging. This can make it significantly easier to keep the face square at impact. To improve feel, the striking face is printed from TPU, providing a soft but responsive impact that closely resembles the insert faces found on many premium putters. Including the printed parts, added weights, screws, and epoxy, the total mass of the head of the putter is right around 320g. Features High-MOI perimeter-weighted design Center of Mass positioned to produce Low Torque when swinging Modular construction with interchangeable putter heads TPU face insert for a soft, responsive feel Removable shaft adapter secured with screws Designed for commonly available hardware and weights Inexpensive and creative alternative to traditional putters Hope you can have as much fun with this project as I did and get to give it a try out on course! For instructions, materials, and a list of parts to purchase/use, see the information below! Happy printing! Modular Design: Find other compatible putter heads here! Tempest Putter - Low-Torque / Modular / High MOI Material Selection Body / Shaft Insert - PETG is recommended for outdoor use and to withstand higher temperatures while being relatively easy to print. Face Insert - TPU provides a soft yet confident feel when striking the ball. Assembly Be sure to read all the following steps before beginning assembly of your putter! The order in which some of these steps are taken is very important! Print all required components in your favorite colors. Be sure to print each component in its recommended material. Support removal. This step can be rather difficult due to the way the model must be printed, so my recommendation is to work from the outside inwards. I've used normal supports for the flat-bottomed sections to allow for each of the gaps for the weights to be cleared in a singular piece. Press the TPU face into the putter body. Secure it by using super glue or epoxy. Install the weights. All weights should sit flat within the head of the putter when installed correctly. See the image below for the proper layout of weights. A total of 30 individual 0.25oz weights are to be inserted, with 4 stacked near the face and 2 stacked in all other locations. While removing the film on the weights (making them stick) is recommended, it is not required for the putter to work great. Doing so may reduce noises heard when making contact with the ball slightly but will make it more difficult to remove the weights if interchanging putter heads. Install the bottom plate to the putter head at the 5 holes around the perimeter. Ensure that the side which features cutouts matching the position of the weights is facing the inserted weights. Use 5x M3 x 3/8" wood screws (link provided below for the ones used). Screws should only be hand tight, and do not over-tighten them! Cut down the putter shaft to your desired length (I cut mine down to 36in for my height). For a great step-by-step process to complete this, check out this YouTube video: How to Shorten a Putter with a Steel Shaft . Install the grip to your putter shaft. I recommend completing this step before installing the shaft adapter and putter head as there is less time to work and straighten out the grip in comparison. For a great guide to doing this, check out this other YouTube tutorial: How to Install a Putter Grip (jump to 3:00 in the video). Bolt the shaft adapter/insert into the putter head after sliding the shaft adapter into place from the top. Using 3x M3 x 3/8" wood screws, secure the bottom plate, main body, and adapter together through the bottom in the three central holes. Then, complete the installation by using one more screw in the hole near the top of the putter towards the back. Screws should only be hand tight, and do not over-tighten them! Epoxy the shaft into the adapter by applying epoxy to the shaft and sliding it in from the top. The epoxy which is suggested has a long working time which allows you to rotate the putter shaft so the the grip precisely lines up with its correct orientation. My recommendation for alignment of the grip is as follows: look down the shaft and line up the flat part of the grip with the line on top of the putter which is parallel to the direction of your stroke. Once aligned properly, wipe away any excess epoxy from the top of the putter. Let the putter sit overnight so that the epoxy can fully cure. Next step, rolling putts! Hardware & Non-Printed Parts Required Purchased Components: I've added direct links here so you can source everything needed. Shaft: 0.370in Tip Diameter Straight Stepless Putter Shaft ( Amazon Link ) - $29.95 Grip: Any putter grip should do, but the one seen in all images here is a SuperStroke Zenergy Tour 3.0 ( Amazon Link ) - $34.39 Weights: Important to uses these weights due to their exact size and 1/4oz weight ( Amazon Link ) - $6.99 Screws: M3 x 3/8" Wood Screws ( Amazon Link ) - $6.79 Required Tools/Adhesives: Links are provided in case you may need to get these. If you don't already have some of these, they are also great to have in general for a variety of projects. Epoxy: Simple JB Weld 2-Part Epoxy ( Amazon Link ) - $5.93 Steel Tube Cutter: I used a copper pipe cutter (although it worked, not recommended), but using a proper steel pipe cutter is advised if possible ( Amazon Link ) - $13.99 Total (For Required Components and Printed Parts): ~$80 USD Future Plans This modular platform was designed with expansion in mind. I plan to release additional interchangeable putter head designs that will all use the same shaft adapter, allowing you to experiment with different shapes and weight distributions without building an entirely new putter. If you build one, I'd love to see your make! Feel free to leave feedback or suggestions for future head designs. Happy printing, and good luck on the greens!

description: This is my interpretation of the Panzer DC tank made by @Kugelblatz Since this is a fake tank, I thought I would make a backstory for it! After 1945, the German industrial complex was still able to churn out more machines of war; the Panzer IX was but one of them. In 1946, a replacement for the Maus was requested. Most allied tanks struggled against the armor geometry of the Maus, so it was used as the basis for the Panzer 9. The Turret of the Maus was scaled up to fit the new 200mm Kwk cannon and a 100mm coaxial cannon. The main turret was raised in order to fit the engine bay underneath it. A modified King Tiger turret was placed in the front section to deal with more lightly armored enemies. The Panther tanks were deemed a success, and an enlarged turret design was requested to be used with the 88mm gun and to be mounted on the midsection of the tank. A larger design in general was developed to make it more difficult for the newly unleashed T95 TD, and T29/T34 Heavy tanks to penetrate the side armor. The Panzer IX is roughly the size of two Maus tanks, so it was seen as a more feasible production option compared to the P.1000 Ratte. A squadron of Anti-air vehicles would be at the Panzer IX's side at all times to deter bombing attacks from the Allies. (Note the second Panzer IX was destroyed by an American F-80 about two weeks into deployment.) This is a fake tank, but I hope you like the lore I thought of! Enjoy!

Ösen-Fitting fürs Wochenende, Haken-Fitting im Alltag). --- ## 🚗 Passend für folgende Fahrzeuge Alle VW T5, T6 und T6.1 in sämtlichen Ausbaustufen: `California` · `California Beach` · `California Ocean` · `California Coast` · `Multivan` · `Multivan PanAmericana` · `Multivan Highline / Comfortline / Trendline / Startline` · `Caravelle` · `Transporter / Kombi / Kasten` · `Shuttle` ⚠️ **Wichtig – zwei Griff-Sub-Typen im T5/T6/T6.1:** - **Version A (dieses Modell):** Passt auf den serienmäßigen Standard-Haltegriff **ohne** bereits integrierten Kleiderhaken (meist im vorderen Fahrzeugbereich verbaut). - **Version B (kommt bei entsprechender Nachfrage separat):** Für den Haltegriff **mit** werkseitig integriertem Kleiderhaken (typischerweise im hinteren Fahrzeugbereich). 👉 Bitte vor dem Druck einen Blick auf euren eigenen Griff werfen. --- ## ⚠️ Materialwahl – bitte unbedingt lesen Dieses Teil wird **im KFZ-Innenraum verbaut** und muss unter zwei Bedingungen zuverlässig funktionieren, die viele Standard-Filamente überfordern: **1. Temperatur im Fahrzeug-Innenraum** Ein VW Bus wird im Sommer hinter der Windschutzscheibe und im Dachhimmel schnell **60 °C und mehr**, in praller Sonne auch deutlich darüber. Filamente, die in diesem Bereich weich werden, verlieren unter Zuglast schlagartig ihre Formstabilität. **2. Mechanische Zugbelastung** Eine nasse Jacke, eine quer gespannte Wäscheleine mit Handtüchern oder ein Karabiner mit dranhängendem Rucksack erzeugen dauerhaft Zugkräfte – genau dort, wo das Filament am heißesten Punkt sitzt. Deshalb bitte **nur folgende Filamente** verwenden: | Filament | Empfehlung | Warum | |---|---|---| | ✅ **ASA** | **empfohlen** | UV-, temperatur- und schlagfest – Standardmaterial für Automotive-Interior | | ✅ **ABS** | empfohlen | Wärmeformbeständig bis ~95 °C, zäh | | ✅ **PA-CF / PET-CF / PAHT-CF / ASA-CF** | Premium-Wahl | Maximale Steifigkeit und Temperaturstabilität, ideal bei dauerhaft eingestecktem Airline-Fitting mit Zuglast | | ⚠️ **PETG** | **nicht empfohlen** | Wird ab ca. 70–80 °C weich (Glasübergang) – im Sommer im Bus grenzwertig, unter Zuglast riskant | | ❌ **PLA / PLA+** | **nicht verwenden** | Wird ab ca. 55–60 °C weich – im geparkten Bus im Sommer garantiert kritisch, Bauteil kann kriechen und versagen | Wer keinen gehärteten Nozzle für CF-Filamente hat: reines ASA reicht für den normalen Camping-Einsatz vollkommen aus. --- ## 🔩 Montage (3 Minuten) 1. Die beiden Torx-Schrauben des Originalgriffs herausdrehen 2. Druckteil **unter den Originalgriff** setzen – die Aussparungen im Druckteil legen sich exakt um die Original-Schraubpunkte 3. Original-Schrauben wieder eindrehen und mit Gefühl anziehen (nicht in den Dachhimmel würgen) 4. Bei Bedarf Airline-Fitting oder Karabiner einstecken – fertig 💡 **Schrauben-Hinweis:** Bei mir haben die **Originalschrauben mit Standard-Länge** einwandfrei gereicht. Sollte durch Fertigungstoleranzen oder Farbabweichung bei euch die Klemmlänge knapp werden: zwei minimal längere Torx-Schrauben mit demselben Gewinde und Kopf aus dem Baumarkt besorgen (typischerweise ~5 mm länger als Original genügt). **Sicherheitshinweis:** Während der Fahrt eingesteckte Airline-Fittings oder Karabiner entfernen – bei einem Unfall besteht sonst Verletzungsgefahr für Insassen. Das gedruckte Teil ist Zubehör für den stehenden Betrieb (Camping, Übernachten, Rangieren im Stand), keine sicherheitsrelevante Komponente. --- ## 📦 Optional erweiterbar mit - **Airline-Fitting deiner Wahl** (25-mm-Raster, EU-Standard): - **Ösen-Fitting** → für Karabiner, Seile, Wäscheleine - **Haken-Fitting** → für schwere Jacken, Handtaschen - **Ring-Fitting** → für Wäscheleine und Gurte gleichzeitig Bezugsquellen: Camper- und Bootsausrüster (Suchbegriff: „Airline Fitting", „Airline Zurrmulde", „Airline Bodenschiene Fitting"). Preis meist 3–8 € pro Stück. - **Karabinerhaken 6–8 mm** direkt für die Fitting-Öse - **Wäscheleine 3–4 mm mit zwei Karabinern** – klassisch quer durch den Bus gespannt zum Handtuchtrocknen Werkzeug für Montage: Torx (T20 oder T25, je nach VW-Baujahr). --- ## 💛 Wenn dir das Modell gefällt Ich freue mich riesig über **Make-Fotos**, ehrliche Rückmeldung und einen 👍 – und wenn dir das Modell wirklich weitergeholfen hat, würde ich mich extrem über einen **Boost** freuen. Das kostet dich nichts außer einem Klick, hilft aber enorm dabei, dass ich weiter neue Camper-Teile veröffentlichen kann. 🚀 Konstruktive Kritik, Verbesserungsvorschläge oder Fitment-Rückmeldungen zu speziellen Sub-Varianten: jederzeit gerne in die Kommentare – ich iteriere aktiv weiter. Happy printing & safe travels!

model_name: RC Trailer for WPL 1:16. scale model
description: I made this trailer to tow behind my WPL-C24 RC car. It started as a hot glued mess of random prints, and a different failed trailer. I decided I wanted to make my own design, and so this was born. I didn't go with functioning suspension for simplicity sake. That way you don't need to worry about printing fiddly leaf springs, or having to buy extra parts, and if you don't care 100% about scale accuracy, it's a lot more straight forward I've used a pin style hitch again for simplicity, you can just use a long screw or piece of wire to hold it on to the cars hitch. To attach it to a vehicle, it will need a hitch similar to the one I've provided on my rear bumper bar design for the WPL-C24 This version of the trailer uses quite a few m3 screws to hold it together. It was a trade off between ease of printing, and assembly. Depending on the response from this trailer, I'm contemplating redesigning the model to print in fewer parts, so it uses fewer screws, but I might need to think how it goes together. Printing: The model is pretty straight forward to print. PLA has been fine for my versions. Some parts will need supports, like the suspension mount, and around the lip of the trailer tray, but they are minor, and mostly any support scarring is hidden from view. You have the option of printing the tray & fenders from one colour, while printing the chassis & suspensions from a secondary colour. I've separated them onto two seperate plates Parts / BOM As well as the printed parts, you need a couple of other things. A bunch of M3 screws, and some wheels. M3 Button head screws: 4x m3x6mm for fenders 15x m3x8mm for everything else 2x 5mm hex drive wheels with a max diameter of 65mmfrom the likes of a WPL C24 kit, or replacements. 2x m2 screws to hold the wheels on. Assembly: The main assembly is pretty straight forward, screw everything together as pictured. One thing I recommend doing is attaching the hitch swivel first with the screw in the back of the cap. It is easier to do it before you attach the trailer neck to the chassis / tray. The 4 m3x6mm screws are for the fenders. If you use 6mm screws, they will fit perfectly, and not protrude into the model's tray. It's best for clearance to use button head screws for these. The rest of the screws will be the m3x8mm screws. You can get away with using up to 10mm screws for most joints if you have them, apart from the 4x holding the tray to the chassis. These screws also don't need to be button head screws, but for the sake of consistency, that is what I've used. I hope you can enjoy this model. As always, feel free to get in touch if you have suggestions to improve it, or run into issues with printing or assembling it.
