description: ☢️ 🐶Thermonuclear Reactor Pet-Feeder Module 😺☢️ The Thermonuclear Pet-Feeder Module is a premium sci-fi-inspired automatic pet feeding station that transforms an everyday necessity into a cinematic centerpiece. Designed to resemble a miniature industrial reactor, it combines bold engineering aesthetics with practical functionality, making it equally at home in modern living spaces, gaming setups, workshops, and offices. Standing approximately 15 inches (381 mm) tall and 12 inches (305 mm) wide , the module offers generous food storage while maintaining a compact footprint. Its modest weight makes it easy to relocate anywhere around your home, while the customizable front name plate allows you to personalize the feeder with your cat's or dog's name, giving every unit a unique identity. Featuring an illuminated food chamber (especially useful for older blind/ weak eyesighted pets), a bubbling "radioactive coolant" column, high-detail industrial armor panels, a gravity-fed water system, and mechanical detailing throughout, every element has been designed to create the illusion of a fully operational futuristic reactor. Despite its highly detailed appearance, the model has been engineered for reliable FDM printing without requiring an AMS system for people with all levels of printing experience! Whether you're feeding a curious cat or a loyal dog, the Thermonuclear Pet-Feeder Module is built to be a functional everyday feeder while doubling as a statement piece that is guaranteed to become the focal point of any room. Key Features Large-capacity dry food storage chamber Illuminated front viewing window Pump-assisted "radioactive coolant" display tube Gravity-fed water reservoir (optional) Adjustable food dispensing system Airtight storage lids for easy refilling Sliding rear utility storage compartment Removable food tray for easy cleaning Transparent front inspection panel Customizable front name plate Modular construction for easy printing and assembly Hardware Required Assembly requires only a few inexpensive components. Required Hardware: 1 × Clear acrylic sheet (front viewing window) 8 × M4 × 12 mm machine screws Super glue (CA glue) Optional Upgrades: For an even more immersive reactor effect, the following upgrades are recommended but completely optional. Mini Aquarium Pump: A small aquarium pump can be installed to circulate the green coolant inside the reactor tube, creating a continuous bubbling effect. Example: LINK . If activating the water chamber, use silicone like this: LINK to ensure there is no leak in the piping joints with the Plastic. The silicone will help seal all the gaps. If you are afraid of leakage or your printer is not properly calibrated, I recommend using an epoxy coat inside the water chamber to avoid any future leakage. Add some food color to make the liquid pop out! Interior Lighting: The food chamber can be illuminated by mounting an LED light source to the inside ceiling of the chamber. This dramatically enhances the industrial reactor appearance, especially in low-light environments. Also useful for old pets. You may use: A small battery-powered puck light An LED strip light Any similar compact lighting solution that fits inside the chamber All compatible lighting options, along with the acrylic sheet and machine screws, are listed in the model's Bill of Materials (BOM). Customization: How to Customize? The front name plate is fully customizable, allowing you to personalize the module with your pet's name, warning labels, fictional reactor names, or your own branding. The design also lends itself well to custom paint jobs, weathering, metallic finishes, LEDs, or additional sci-fi detailing if desired. Step 1: Click and select the piece. Step 2: While selected, click on the ‘text tool’ on the top ribbon. Step 3: Add text to the surface you want and adjust the orientation and depth according to your liking. Step 4: Change the color of the text and slice and print! Print Profiles Included Three optimized print profiles are included to suit different printer sizes and user preferences. Use the given profiles for best results. They are highly modified for best fit. Standard Profile Designed to fit almost all common FDM printers. The model has been divided into smaller sections for maximum printer compatibility while maintaining excellent structural strength. Assembly is straightforward using the included alignment dowels. Simply insert the dowels into their corresponding holes and apply a generous amount of super glue during assembly to create a strong, rigid structure. Large Format Profile Designed for large-format printers, such as the Bambu Lab H2D series and other printers with similarly large build volumes. This version contains significantly fewer cuts, resulting in larger printed sections, reduced assembly time, and a cleaner overall appearance with fewer visible seams. While both versions produce virtually the same finished product, the reduced part count gives this profile a slightly more premium look. If your printer can accommodate the larger components, this is the preferred version. Optional Gravity-Refill Water Bowl An additional print profile is included for the Gravity-Refill Water Bowl Attachment. This optional accessory allows the water bowl to be connected to an inverted water bottle, automatically replenishing the bowl as your pet drinks. It's an excellent upgrade for users who want to reduce the frequency of manual water refills while keeping fresh water available throughout the day. Assembly The model has been designed as a modular build and is straightforward to assemble. Print all required parts using your preferred print profile. Dry-fit the components before applying adhesive. Use the provided alignment dowels to accurately position each section. Once satisfied with the fit, apply super glue liberally along all mating surfaces and assemble the parts. Trace the front panel on the sheet and cut the borders and the hole locations for the 4 screws. Install the acrylic viewing window. Secure the structural components using the 4 × M4 × 12 mm machine screws where indicated. Install the food and water components, along with any optional lighting or aquarium pump if desired. If you have any questions during assembly, you can refer to the following build video for guidance. Feel free to pause, rewind, and follow along at your own pace: Assembly Reference Video: https://www.instagram.com/p/Daon67yMfkF/?hl=en * Food-Safe Filament Option: If you intend to use the feeder with food-contact components, you may also print the food-contact parts using Bambu Lab PLA Pure (listed in BOM) , which is manufactured using food-contact-approved raw materials. As with any 3D-printed food container, proper printing practices, clean nozzles, and post-processing should be considered to maintain hygiene. You can also combine PLA Pure with different filament colors for the non-food-contact components to create your own unique reactor theme while keeping the food storage chamber printed in food-contact-approved material. description: Hello everyone! 👋 I bring you the Toy Story Space Crane again, but this time, it's the version adapted for the Bambu Lab Magnetic Levitation Kit ! ✨ If you are looking for the standard version, you can find it » [HERE] « Both AMS and NON-AMS print profiles are available! 🎨 The AMS profile is quite similar to the non-AMS one, but parts like the Space Crane walls, the alien floor, the UFO, and the joystick background feature enhanced quality and more colors. However, I’ve done my best to make the non-AMS version look as close to the AMS version as possible. 🖌️ 🫤 Since I'll be away for a week and short on time, I wanted to upload this magnetic levitation version right now to celebrate the Toy Story movies! 🎬 I would have loved to include a promotional video and a full assembly guide, but for now, I've prepared a short written tutorial with photos so you won't have any issues. I'll make sure to create those videos as soon as I can! ^^ 📹 🛸 About the UFO: To ensure it fits inside the rocket, doesn't hit the claw when a figure is placed on top, and still allows light to shine through, I had to keep the design quite simple with thin walls. This will remain as V1 , and I will likely release an improved V2 later on. Please note that the structural grip in this V1 isn't perfect, precisely because the thin walls required for illumination make it tricky to design robust joints at this scale. 🛠️ Assembly Instructions Before starting: If you feel you need glue, use it! If you don't plan on taking the rocket apart, gluing is the best option. 🧴 Joystick: Assemble the joystick background together with its buttons. 🕹️ Wiring: Remove the power cable from the levitation kit's motherboard, but leave the mini-board (touch button) connected. ⚡ Power plug: Insert the power plug into the back cover (as shown in the photo) and route it upwards through the internal hole. Once connected, route the button cable downwards and place the magnetic base in its slot (it has four alignment points). 🧲 Touch button: Slide the mini-board/button down the back of the door, alongside the power plug, and snap the door onto the rocket with a bit of pressure. If you swipe your finger on the outside of that area, the button will activate when the UFO is levitating on the base! 👆💡 Base: Assemble the walls to the base of the rocket (glue is recommended). 🏗️ Floor: Next, cover the magnetic base with the floor piece you decided to print ( DO NOT GLUE THIS PART! ). 🚫🧴 Claw: If the tolerance is too loose, you can glue the claw to the top of the rocket; otherwise, just snap it into place. I recommend placing the open claws facing forward, as seen in the photo. 🦞 Top section: Join the top part with the walls (glue recommended). 🚀 🛸 Let's build the UFO! (It's very simple) Place the copper piece at the bottom, followed by the spacer, and then the metal piece with the magnet. Leave the light on top and cover it with the cap so it doesn't move. 💡 Drop the top shell onto the bottom one, adjust it slightly, and you're done! As mentioned before, it's designed this way to allow the light to shine through. I’ll try to create an improved V2 later. 🔄 FOR NON-AMS ONLY: You will need a tiny drop of glue for both the floor and the windows. Be careful, I know it can be a bit tricky! 🤏 🎯 Final Setup Once everything is assembled, carefully lower the UFO right in the center, as close to the claw as possible. You'll hear a characteristic sound when it locks into the levitation point. Then, just place your favorite mini-figure on top!!! 🤠👾 I have created quite a few of them » HERE « , take a look and print whichever ones you like! 🖨️ ✨I hope you all like it! 🦖 Best regards. 🟢Don't forget you can follow me on Instagram as @Jotas3D ^^ 📸 ⚠️ » HERE « for Toy Story Logo ⚠️

description: 🖨️ TypeRoll - Vintage Typewriter Paper Towel Holder Tired of having a standard, vertical paper towel roll sitting on your living room coffee table or workshop bench, slowly unrolling itself over time? Modeled after a vintage mechanical typewriter, it completely encloses a standard paper towel roll, feeding it perfectly through the top slot. Load the Paper: Insert a fresh paper towel roll into the main rear chamber, feeding the first sheet up through the horizontal platen slot. Secure the Roll: Thread the two side platen knobs through the chassis walls and into the center core of the paper towel roll to lock it securely in place. description: A Small Project Made with Big Love for Pets This liquid treat bowl started as a simple idea at home: How can I make liquid treats more fun? Instead of letting broth or yogurt disappear in seconds, I wanted to create something that encourages pets to slow down, explore, and enjoy every last lick. Designed by an amateur maker, refined through countless test prints, and shared with fellow pet lovers, this is a project made for the joy of creating—and hopefully, for bringing a little extra happiness to the animals we love. Whether you have a playful puppy, a curious kitten, a senior companion, or simply a pet that loves tasty treats, this bowl is designed to turn everyday snacks into an engaging enrichment activity. Designed for 3D Printing The bowl is designed to print easily on most consumer 3D printers and consists of five printable parts : Base Bowl Lid Two Ball Halves Thread that joins the two ball halves together No complicated assembly or special hardware is required—just print, assemble, and enjoy. Why Your Pet Will Love It The ball rolls in the liquid as your pet licks, creating a constant reward for being engaged. Instead of quickly gulping down treats, it forces snack time to last longer while providing gentle mental stimulation. My dog kept going for 25 minutes until it was empty. Perfect for serving: Bone broth Plain yogurt Goat's milk Diluted wet food Homemade liquid treats Pet-safe nutritional supplements Suitable for both dogs and cats of all sizes. More Than a Bowl This isn't meant to be another plastic gadget. It's a small DIY project created by someone who simply enjoys designing things that make pets happy. If printing and sharing this bowl gives your dog a wagging tail or your cat a few extra minutes of curious entertainment, then the project has done exactly what it was made to do. description: 🌿 Alocasia Maharani Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Wer schon einmal dekorative Pflanzentöpfe mit aufwendigen Blattmotiven skaliert hat, kennt das Problem: Wandstärken verändern sich, Details werden unsauber und das Design verliert an Wirkung. Deshalb erhältst du hier vier separat angepasste Größen, die jeweils speziell für ihre Größe optimiert wurden. Jeder Topf trägt ein plastisch ausgearbeitetes **Alocasia Maharani Blatt**, das besonders bei einfarbigen Drucken hervorragend zur Geltung kommt und den Töpfen ihren charakteristischen Look verleiht. --- # 💧 Selbstbewässerungssystem Alle Größen wurden für die Nutzung als Selbstbewässerungstopf ausgelegt. Der eigentliche Pflanztopf sitzt im oberen Bereich. Darunter befindet sich ein separates Wasserreservoir. Über einen Kapillardocht, der durch die Bodenöffnungen des Orchideen- oder Aroid-Topfes geführt wird, kann die Pflanze selbstständig Wasser aus dem Reservoir aufnehmen. Dadurch wird eine gleichmäßige Wasserversorgung ermöglicht und die Gießintervalle können deutlich verlängert werden. Bei allen Größen wurde darauf geachtet, dass die Innentöpfe bequem von oben entnommen werden können, ohne im Topfinneren hantieren zu müssen. --- # 👀 Sichtfenster (optional) Auf der Rückseite befindet sich ein Sichtfenster, durch das sich Wasserstand und Wurzelentwicklung bequem kontrollieren lassen, ohne den Innentopf herausnehmen zu müssen. Hi, ich habe eine neue Lampe mit Korbstruktur gezeichnet. Das Gute an der Korbstruktur ist aber, dass man auch dunklere Farben verwenden kann und trotzdem immer etwas Licht durch die kleinen Öffnungen scheint. Auch cool an Lampe ist, dass ein Bajonettverschluss am Schirmboden eingebaut ist so, dass Lampenschirm oder Lampenfuß mit allen anderen Lampenteilen des Systems ausgetauscht werden können. Jetzt NEU! model_name: Trampa para Avispas - Respetuosa con las Abejas
description: RECOMIENDO LEER LA DESCRIPCION Constantemente hay riego en mi terraza y se forman diferentes charquitos los cuales les encantan a las avispas, por desgracia se hace imposible estar en ella durante las horas del día, por ello me he visto obligado a diseñar esta trampa para avispas y poder disfrutar de mis tardes en la terraza. El modelo esta diseñado específicamente para que la entrada a la trampa sea muy sencilla y parezca segura para las avispas, pero siendo imposible su salida… la entrada desde la parte superior hace que sea muy sencillo bajar ya que la propia inercia ayuda pero una vez abajo, la falta de luz y el pequeño diámetro de su salida, lo vuelve imposible… Utilizando la mezcla correspondiente, la trampa es totalmente inútil contra abejas, convirtiéndola en una trampa respetuosa para ellas, ya que no se sienten atraídas por el aroma. RECETA MUY EFICAZ: En un frasco verter 200ml de cerveza + 100ml de zumo de manzana o melocotón + una cucharadita de azúcar + una o dos gotas de lavavajillas. RECETA EFICAZ: Si no dispones de los elementos nombrados en la receta muy eficaz, también puedes utilizar: 150ml de vinagre de manzana + 100ml de agua + 2-3 cucharadas de azúcar + unas gotas de lavavajillas. Una vez hecha la mezcla, verter en la parte inferior de la trampa hasta la mitad del recipiente (Sobrara mas liquido para próximas ocasiones) El liquido de lavavajillas es necesario ya que rompe la tensión del agua evitando que puedan posarse encima. Indicar que los soportes son un pelín costosos de quitar pero eran necesarios para la correcta impresión del modelo , nada que 2-3 minutos no puedan solucionar.

I tre pannelli affiancati creano un'unica composizione floreale fluida quando affiancati. Ogni pannello presenta piccoli fori agli angoli per essere appeso facilmente tramite viti o chiodini. Istruzioni di stampa: Stampato in PLA Nero Bambulab. La stampa è facilissima e consuma solo 54 grammi di filamento in totale (spessore 2 millimetri). I colori si possono cambiare dallo slicer al momento della stampa, il modello può essere ingrandito o rimpicciolito a piacimento. Solitamente 2 mm di spessore sono abbondantemente sufficienti. Quindi se lo ingrandite sugli assi x e y tenete attiva la funzione “Scala uniforme”, dopodiché per variare lo spessore, togliete il flag da “Scala uniforme” ed agite solo sul valore dell’asse z che imposterete ai millimetri desiderati (io ho messo 2 mm e va benissimo). CONSIGLI GENERALI Un consiglio che dispenso sempre è quello di pulire preliminarmente il piatto di stampa con detersivo per piatti ed una spugnetta risciacquando con acqua calda, dopodiché asciugarlo con aria compressa evitando di toccare la superficie con le mani. Inoltre consiglio di fare le calibrazioni del flusso dinamico e del flaw rate previste in bambu studio. Personalmente prima delle stampe asciugo il PLA con AMS 2 PRO per circa 1 oretta. Sono questi piccoli accorgimenti, insieme a tanti altri, che determinano la riuscita di una bella stampa . Prima di mettere giudizi negativi, cortesemente regolate questi parametri. Se avete difficoltà o continuate a riscontrare problemi non esitate a contattarmi, cerchiamo insieme le soluzioni in un perfetto clima collaborativo. Ho fatto diverse stampe di questo oggetto e sono venute tutte perfette come in foto: se avete parametri sballati, nozzle sporchi o intasati, macchine calibrate male, filamenti umidi o di cattiva qualità non ve la prendete con me. I've been growing herbs and strawberries in hydroponic towers at home for a long time. But classic tower models had many drawbacks: they were too noisy due to the sound of falling water, poorly irrigated the upper tiers of plants due to their imperfect design, have no lights and took up a lot of space. So I decided to develop my own design that eliminated these drawbacks. I combined NFT hydroponics and a traditional tower to create a spiral plant nutrition system. I also designed the tower for corner installation so it would take up a quarter of the space of a traditional circular tower. I also added many improvements, which I detailed in my YouTube video: For assembly, you will need: 1) a water tank. I used a plastic bucket from a local marketplace with a diameter of 295 mm and a capacity of 18 liters https://ozon.ru/t/yCqJQjw. 2) a pump with a capacity of 800 liters per hour and a water lift of 160 cm https://ali.click/jlwlg1u. 3) a silicone hose with an internal diameter of 12 mm and a length of 150 cm https://ali.click/z0xlg1z. 4) two 45-watt grow lights 105 x 40 x 35 cm, or four 55cm length with metal buckles https://ali.click/1sxlg16. 5) a 1-meter cable for connecting the lights and a 3-pin timer https://ali.click/pfylg19 https://ali.click/8sylg1v. 6) 45 x 45 mm agrowool plugs for green seeds, or foam glass for strawberries. You'll need total 3 kg of PETG plastic for printing, and I recommend using Bambu Lab PETG HF. I'm not sure why, but the locks on the parts work better with it than with PETG Basic. For now, all the tower parts are designed for printing on H2 series printers. But you can support my project using the link in my profile, and I'll make a model for printing on standard Bambu Lab A1/P/X series printers.

description: Check out my newly released models: Product Description Meet the Self-Locking Towel Holder — a minimalist, wall-mounted accessory that keeps your towel exactly where you want it, using nothing but gravity and a clever internal ball mechanism. No hooks to snag on, no clips to fiddle with, no adhesives on the fabric. Just push the towel in, and it holds itself. How It Works Inside the arched body sits a free-rolling ball housed in a tapered channel. The mechanism works in three intuitive steps: Insert — Push the edge of the towel upward into the slot from below. The ball lifts out of the way, letting the fabric pass through easily. Lock — As soon as you let go, the towel naturally pulls downward. The ball rolls down with it and wedges the fabric against the tapered wall of the channel, gripping it firmly. The harder the towel pulls, the tighter the hold. Release — To remove the towel, simply pull it sideways (horizontally) instead of down. This motion disengages the ball from the wedge zone, instantly releasing the fabric with zero effort. It's a purely mechanical, gravity-driven design — no springs, no magnets, no moving parts to wear out beyond a single ball. Key Features 🪝 One-handed operation — insert and release with a single motion 🎨 Warm brown finish — pairs beautifully with neutral, Japandi, or earth-tone bathroom interiors 🧺 Universal fit — works with hand towels, tea towels, dish cloths, and thin bath towels 🌊 Bathroom & kitchen ready — great next to the sink, shower, or by the stove 🔩 Minimal footprint — the compact arched profile takes up almost no wall space 🛠️ Easy install — double-sided tape Why You'll Love It No more towels sliding off hooks or bunching up on bars. This holder embraces the beauty of simple physics — the more your towel wants to fall, the more securely it stays. A tiny piece of engineering that quietly does its job, every single day.

description: Hey everyone! We always read about epic battles with dragons, or watch them breathing fire and tearing down cities in movies. description: Beschreibung Die meisten selbstbewässernden Drucktöpfe scheitern an denselben zwei Dingen: zu flach (die Pflanze kümmert nach ein paar Wochen) und Baumwolldochte, die in 2–3 Wochen verrotten und Krankheitserreger einschleppen. Dieser Topf löst beides. Das Prinzip: Im Boden des Außentopfs sitzt ein großes Wasserreservoir. Der Innentopf steht darüber; sein Boden hat Belüftungs- und Drainagelöcher. Drei Erdsäulen reichen vom Innentopf in den Wasserspeicher – die Erde in ihnen dochtet selbst, ganz ohne Zusatzmaterial, das faulen kann. Ein Überlauf hält den Wasserstand knapp unter dem Innentopf-Boden: Das Reservoir kann nicht in die Erde überlaufen, überschüssiges Gießwasser läuft ab. Ergebnis: konstant feucht, nie nass, Wurzeln bekommen Sauerstoff. Genau die Bedingungen, unter denen Basilikum zum Busch wird statt einzugehen. Praxistest bestanden: Ein handelsüblicher Supermarkt-Basilikum ist darin innerhalb weniger Wochen zum kompletten Busch herangewachsen (siehe Vorher/Nachher-Foto). Features Echtes SIP-Prinzip – Wasser und Erde getrennt, Wasseraufnahme nur über die Erdsäulen; kein Wurzelfäule-Risiko durch Staunässe Selbst-dochtende Erdsäulen – kein Baumwolldocht, nichts, was verrottet Überlaufschutz – hält den Wasserstand knapp unter dem Innentopf-Boden, kann nicht überlaufen; überschüssiges Gießwasser läuft ab Füll-Kerbe am Rand zum sauberen Nachgießen ins Reservoir Belüftungs-/Drainagelöcher im Innenboden für Sauerstoff an den Wurzeln Großes 2L-Reservoir – Standzeit gut eine Woche ~130 mm Erdtiefe – echtes Wurzelvolumen für Basilikum, Minze, Petersilie & Co. Facettiertes Design – modern, druckt sauber Technische Daten Außendurchmesser 202 mm (facettiert, rund) plus einseitig 17mm für die Eingießtülle Innendurchmesser 183 mm Gesamthöhe: 206 mm Erdtiefe: ca. 130 mm Überlauf: 66 mm ab Innenboden Reservoir (nutzbar bis Überlauf): ca. 2L → Standzeit gut 1 Woche, je nach Pflanzengröße und Standort Teile Außentopf – Reservoir + facettierte Wand Innentopf – Erde, Belüftungslöcher, Aufnahmen für die Erdsäulen Erdsäulen (3 Stück) – separate Dochtsäulen, werden in den Innentopf eingesetzt (können eingeklebt werden, müssen aber nicht – siehe Montage) Montage Erdsäulen in die vorgesehenen Aufnahmen des Innentopfs einsetzen. Einkleben ist optional – wenn der Innentopf im zusammengesetzten Zustand (im Außentopf sitzend) mit Erde befüllt wird, hält der Erddruck die Säulen von selbst an Ort und Stelle. Innentopf in den Außentopf setzen – der Flansch liegt auf dem Rand des Außentopfs auf. Erde einfüllen, dabei die Erdsäulen mit Erde füllen (nicht hohl lassen – sie sind der Docht ins Reservoir). Erste Bewässerung von oben angießen, damit sich die Erdsäulen vollsaugen. Danach übers Reservoir über die Füll-Kerbe nachfüllen. Pflege-Tipps Etwa wöchentlich über die Füll-Kerbe nachfüllen, bis Wasser am Überlauf austritt – der Überlauf verhindert Überfüllen von selbst. Kurze Trockenphasen sind gesund, das Reservoir nicht dauerhaft randvoll halten. Für buschigen Wuchs die Haupttriebe über einem Blattpaar auskneifen. Blütenstände früh abknipsen – blühender Basilikum wird bitter.

🇩🇪 Einstellbarer Chlortabletten-Dosierer für Pool-Skimmer Dieser Dosierer wurde für handelsübliche 200-g-Chlortabletten entwickelt und wird direkt im vorhandenen Skimmerkorb eingesetzt. Die Chlortablette befindet sich dadurch im Wasserstrom des Skimmers und wird nur während der Pumpenlaufzeit umspült. Die Dosierung lässt sich durch einfaches Verdrehen des Gehäuses individuell an den eigenen Pool anpassen. Warum ein Skimmer-Dosierer? Im Gegensatz zu schwimmenden Dosierern erfolgt die Chlorabgabe nur während der Filterlaufzeit. Dadurch kann die Auflösung der Chlortablette kontrollierter erfolgen und die Dosierung lässt sich einfach an den Bedarf des Pools anpassen. Offenes Design für eine optimale Oberflächenreinigung Im Gegensatz zu einigen Skimmereinsätzen, die den gesamten Skimmerquerschnitt als zusätzlicher Korb abdecken, sitzt dieser Dosierer im vorhandenen Skimmerkorb . Dadurch bleibt der Ansaugbereich des Skimmers weitgehend frei und die Oberflächenströmung wird kaum beeinflusst. description: This storage bowl and lid started with a request for a cute desk storage that could still be suitable at work. The idea was to blend in a tiny dragon among the succulents, which lead to the “potted plant lid” which hides the storage of small items like Chapstick, hair ties, eyeglass wipes, and other small desk essentials. Current Size: Bowl: ~10cm wide, ~5cm High Lid: ~ 10 cm wide, ~5.5 High Printing Use a clean print plate with some glue (unless you are using a super tack plate) Keep the support setting as is for the lid. Do NOT move the items to the same build plate as they don't share the same settings. (Do not activate “on build plate only”, leave it un-checked for plate 2/object 2) the support is needed to be formed on the model bottom to be able to reach all needed sections: Use dried out filament Different filament and printers impacts the print differently, please adjust your settings accordingly. If printing with silk PLA, then I recommend to adjust the Speed Outer wall setting to 40mm/s and Tope Surface to 40mm/s. Verify that “Variable layer height” is still enabled - this increases the smoothness of the round shapes. You will find it at the top bar looking like stacked layers: Support Removal & Clean up: Gently break the support off starting at the middle by breaking (crushing) the support in the middle. Avoid pulling firmly on the delicate cutout sections. Work slowly and remove the supports in small pieces. Move to the top and remove the support. Remove the remaining support from the bottom. There might be some thin “Webb strands" - those will disappear if you apply gentle heat. Light sanding and gentle, controlled heat may be needed to clean up areas where the supports were attached. I used a handheld mini torch, but apply heat carefully to avoid warping or damaging the print. description: # 🌿 Alocasia Nobilis Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Deshalb erhältst du hier vier separat angepasste Größen, die jeweils speziell für ihre Größe optimiert wurden. Aus diesem Grunde gibt es in der Datei den Skalierungstest-Druck, da ich bei meinen Testdrucken festgestellt habe, dass je nach Filament und verwendeten Klötzchen diese mal strammer, mal lockerer in den Ausschnitten sitzen. Dafür ist das Verkleben der Klötzchen mit den geschlossenen Seitenteilen einfacher und m. M. nach stabiler und sauberer verarbeitet. description: 🔧 3D Layered Custom Name with Shape - Customizable Name Display This model is a fully parametric desk sign generator that combines two stacked text lines, an optional emoji accent, and a three‑layer color structure for crisp multi‑color prints. description: Credit: @luluanaki I love Pokémon figures — both the detailed 3D printed versions and the vibrant Hueforge style. 🌐 Internet Connection Monitor 24H The project that finally proved my Internet provider was wrong. Have you ever had random Internet dropouts that magically disappeared every time the technician arrived? I did. For almost three weeks my Internet connection kept randomly disconnecting. Video calls froze, downloads stopped, smart home devices went offline... but every time I called my ISP the answer was always the same: "Everything looks perfect from our side." And of course... When the technician came to my house... The connection was perfect. So I decided to build something that could monitor my Internet connection 24 hours a day , collect real data, and prove what was really happening. That is how this project was born. After a few days of continuous monitoring, the graphs clearly showed that the connection randomly died for short periods before automatically recovering. Those historical logs finally convinced the provider to investigate further. The real culprit? A faulty modem/router that randomly crashed and reconnected. Three weeks of frustration... Solved thanks to a tiny ESP32. What does it do? This standalone monitor continuously checks your Internet connection without requiring a PC. It periodically performs: ✅ HTTP connectivity tests ✅ Ping / Latency measurements ✅ Wi-Fi RSSI monitoring ✅ Connection Health calculation ✅ 24-hour historical logging Everything is displayed on a beautiful touchscreen interface. HOME Screen The main page always shows: Internet status (UP / UNSTABLE / DOWN) Connection Health (%) HTTP Connectivity Network Latency (Ping) Wi-Fi Signal Strength (RSSI) IP Address Immediate RGB status indication 24-Hour History Touch the display to open the historical graphs. You can instantly see: Internet quality over the last 24 hours Ping history Connection stability Drops and recovery events Sometimes a connection that "looks fine" at the exact moment you're checking it tells a completely different story over an entire day. And that's exactly the purpose of this project. Recommended Print Settings For the best performance and a watertight tray, the following print settings are recommended: Material: PLA Layer Height: 0.20 mm Walls / Perimeters: 3–5 (recommended) Bottom Layers: 5–8 Supports: Not required Using 3–5 wall perimeters creates a strong, durable shell and greatly improves the tray's waterproof performance , minimizing the chance of leaks. Overview This kinetic sculpture has linkages that cause the ball to be always centered in the exact same position. Due to each hinge axis passing through the center, no matter how each link is moved, it will cause the entire structure to articulate around a stationary center. It features a print-in-place and thread-together design that requires no glue or additional hardware. It requires no supports and is extremely fascinating and satisfying. The base can also be filled with sand or other materials to provide a more premium feel. I have also created a soccer version that is completely compatible with all of these parts. You can find the soccer version here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2977052-soccer-football-fixed-center-kinetic-sculpture#profileId-3339654 For printing Standard setting can be used for printing. No AMS is required and no supports are needed. For the print profiles, there is one with all parts on separate plates for different colors for each part and two that have all the parts on a single plate (one includes the funnel and the other does not). All materials should work; however, for the ball to stay more centered, avoid flexible materials like TPU. Features The model prints in three pieces: the ball, the base, and the print-in-place linkages. Additionally, a funnel can be printed to more easily fill the base with sand or another material. The hole for filling the base is the same hole that the linkage structure threads into. The entire structure is about 95 mm in diameter and about 105 mm tall. All parts are compatible with the other versions. Assembly Assembling this model is very simple. Optionally, the funnel can be threaded into the hole in the base and the base filled. After the funnel is removed, the linkage structure can be threaded into that same hole until it stops. The location of where the threads stop should position the linkage structure properly. Lastly, the ball can be threaded onto the rod at the center of the ring. The links may be slightly stiff and not want to move after printing, but with some slight pressure, the links can be broken free. Versions with Themes I currently plan on making more variations of this model with specific themes. I have already created a soccer version that you can find here. https://makerworld.com/en/models/2977052-soccer-football-fixed-center-kinetic-sculpture#profileId-3339654 Other versions may include but not be limited to: A space theme with the ball being a planet or the moon. An outdoor activity-themed version that could have a surfboard, skateboard, or fishing bobber or lure. A larger version that had a light using the led light kit. There are many possible versions that I could create. Let me know which ones you want to see, and let me know of any other ideas that you have. description: The Great Pyramid Cross-Section Explore the secrets of the Great Pyramid of Giza with this detailed cross-section display, revealing the intricate chambers that have fascinated humanity for millennia. What Lies Within? While traditionally understood as a grand tomb for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid remains an enigma. Beyond the famous King’s Chamber —home to the enigmatic red granite sarcophagus—and the Queen’s Chamber , the pyramid contains the breathtaking, corbelled-roof Grand Gallery . Hidden shafts, mysterious voids discovered via muon tomography, and an unfinished Subterranean Chamber carved deep into the bedrock all point to a level of engineering sophistication that continues to challenge our understanding of the Old Kingdom. Are these voids hidden burial sites, or part of a larger, lost architectural plan? A New Discovery Beneath the Sands Recent, cutting-edge research using satellite imaging and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has suggested the existence of an extensive, deeper subterranean complex beneath the Giza Plateau. Reports indicate potential anomalies, including vertical shafts and structured, geometric patterns reaching deep into the bedrock beneath the major pyramids. While these findings have sparked intense debate among archaeologists regarding their nature and origin, they offer a tantalizing glimpse into what may still be hidden beneath our feet. Inspired by these findings, I have designed a model of the subterranean structures that some researchers believe may be part of this deep network, featuring complex pillars with coiled sections and block-like bases. TrailMark3D Turn Your Trail Into a Trophy TrailMark3D is a web application that generates 3D printable terrain models from GPX files. Upload any GPX track from Strava, Garmin, Komoot, or other tracking apps and get a detailed topographic model ready for 3D printing, zero setup, no software to install, no CAD skills required. Whether it's the summit you finally bagged, a century ride, a multi-day thru-hike, or your local loop, TrailMark3D turns the route you recorded into a physical object you can hold, display, or gift. Who It's For Hikers & trail runners who want a tangible keepsake of a route or summit Cyclists commemorating a big climb, gran fondo, or tour Gift-givers looking for something personal for the outdoor enthusiast in their life, or organizers and gift shops producing them in small batches for events and races. 3D printing hobbyists who want real-world terrain data without wrangling GIS tools How it Works Upload your GPX file to TrailMark3D.com Choose your preferred model shape, size , rotation, map features, printing style Generate your 3D terrain model (processing takes minutes depending on features, size, and resolution) Download the STL/3MF file for 3D printing Core Features Web application - No installation or boilerplate setup needed. Just upload, tweak, and generate. Shape options - Square, Circle, Hexagon Map features - Terrain, Buildings, Roads, Water Bodies, Trail (from GPX) Separated objects - Map features are separate objects inside the 3MF file, so objects can be printed separately. NO AMS NEEDED. Multi-day adventure workflow - Upload up to 5 GPX files to combine your multi-day hike, ride, or any recorded adventure. Job storage - Your latest generated 3D mesh is always stored in the database under your account, so you can always come back to redownload or modify your model. Persistent 3D mesh generation - 3D mesh generation can take time. This feature lets you close your browser and come back anytime to download the generated 3D model. Interactive 2D map view - Resize, rotate, or drag your choice of shape on a 2D map view. Selective water body removal - You may or may not want to print some of the fetched water bodies. This tool lets you exclude water body segments from being generated. Extension tiles - A single GPX is a single tile by default. You can extend the tiles by adding new tiles in the Interactive 2D Map View. Jigsaw puzzle - Generate up to a 20×20 jigsaw terrain puzzle with full control over the jigsaw shape parameters and randomness. Preset (Experimental) - Skip the tweaking by selecting the type of adventure for your GPX. Free & Pro Tiers The core features of TrailMark3D are completely free - no credit card, no expiry. With the free tier you get up to 10 downloads per month, grid resolution up to 200, all three shape options (Square, Circle, Hexagon), water features (Seas, Lakes, Rivers), through-hole water slots, water preview, tree line, activity presets, 3D trail animation, 3MF export, and custom colors. The free tier limits are set around what the server can sustainably handle - 10 downloads/month and a resolution cap of 200 keep things running smoothly for everyone without blowing past my hosting budget. Pro upgrades go directly toward the server capacity that makes higher limits possible. Upgrading to Pro unlocks everything in the free tier plus: unlimited downloads, grid resolution up to 500, shelf mode and water exclusion, shrink-below-trail, buildings and roads, multi-day trips (up to 5 days), priority processing, and early access to upcoming features. Why TrailMark3D From data to object - Your recorded route becomes a real, printable model with accurate terrain. Full control - Tune shape and which map features to include before you generate. Print-friendly - Separated objects mean clean multi-part prints without needing an AMS. Come back anytime - Generation runs server-side, and your jobs are saved to your account. Free to start - The core features are completely free, with Pro available when you need more power. Zero setup - No software to install, no CAD skills required. Prepare for the most fun ultimate mechanism assembly project! This took years of perfecting the design and making it repeatable, with multiple units built to iron out quality issues that arose from the nature of the challenge of making precision mechanisms with 3d printed parts. Summary: A fully mechanical clock with a completely original design for all mechanism components. Uniquely engineered with a background of aerospace engineering approaches to design philosophy, it includes a simple precision pendulum escapement and custom involute gear train with separate hour, minute, and second hand faces designed to fully display the mechanical beauty of the mechanism that makes it function. Depending on the height at which it is mounted on your wall, it will run for 3 to 4 days before needing a rewinding, easily done in seconds with the included crank and embedded ratcheting mechanism. description: Hold a medically accurate piece of human anatomy right in your hands! (Read the last sentence for a curiosity question!) 🩻 Overview 🩻 This advanced 3D model is a highly detailed representation of the human shoulder (glenohumeral) joint, developed through a hybrid medical and digital workflow. The skeletal framework was extracted directly from real CT scans to ensure an anatomically correct bone morphology. The surrounding soft tissues were subsequently hand-modeled in Blender, carefully crafted based on anatomical studies and medical literature. To ensure the best possible 3D printing experience and educational clarity, this model focuses on the primary structures. Some minor or overlapping anatomical elements were intentionally omitted, providing a clean, understandable, and highly printable display piece without overwhelming the slicer or the viewer. 🦴 Included Anatomical Structures The model highlights the key bony landmarks and major soft tissues crucial for understanding shoulder biomechanics: Skeletal Framework (CT Extracted): Scapula (Shoulder Blade), Clavicle (Collarbone), and Humerus (Upper arm bone), featuring accurate articular surfaces and bone topography. 💪 Muscular System (Blender Modeled): Key musculature, including major components of the rotator cuff and biceps, which are essential for shoulder stability and movement. 🔗 Ligaments & Connective Tissue (Blender Modeled): Essential stabilizing ligaments and capsular elements highlighting the articulation points. 🎯 Intended Use Education & Study: A brilliant hands-on visual aid for medical students, anatomy classes, and healthcare professionals. Clinical Communication: Perfect for physical therapists and orthopedic specialists to easily explain shoulder mechanics, impingements, or rotator cuff injuries to their patients. Advanced 3D Printing Showcase: A fantastic display piece that highlights the precision of your printer on complex organic shapes. 💡 Print Settings & Recommendations Material: This model has been fully designed and optimized for standard PLA . No flexible or exotic filaments are required. Versatile Print Profiles: To make this model accessible to everyone, I will be uploading dedicated print profiles for both AMS and non-AMS setups . The multicolor profile is organized to maximize visual contrast and educational value. Based on the provided images, the recommended color mapping is: Bone White: Skeletal structures (Scapula, Clavicle, Humerus) and tendons. Red: Musculature (Rotator cuff and supporting muscles). Blue: Ligaments, and capsular structures. Different colors are presented in the non-AMS setup for printing reasons. SIMPLY INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE NO-AMS PROFILE ⚠️ Disclaimer: This model is intended strictly for educational, illustrative, and hobbyist purposes. It is not a clinical tool and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. For the most interested ones, a bit of anatomy! 🤓🫀🔬 The shoulder, or shoulder girdle, is a complex system designed to give the upper limb a very wide range of motion, with bones, muscles, tendons, and ligaments working together. In my model, the labeled parts show both the supporting framework and the soft tissues that stabilize movement. Bones 🦴 The scapula is a flat triangular bone at the back of the thorax, and it provides attachment for many shoulder muscles. The humerus is the upper arm bone, and its rounded head articulates with the scapula to form the glenohumeral joint, which is the main shoulder joint. The clavicle acts like a strut between the sternum and the scapula, helping keep the shoulder positioned away from the chest wall so the arm can move freely. Soft tissues 💪 The rotator cuff is made of four muscles and their tendons, and its main job is to keep the head of the humerus centered while the arm moves and rotates. The tendons connect muscle to bone, and the long head of the biceps tendon also contributes to shoulder stability as it passes near the joint. The ligaments connect bone to bone and reinforce the joint capsule, helping prevent excessive movement and instability. The subacromial bursa is a small fluid-filled sac that reduces friction between the acromion and the rotator cuff tendons during arm elevation. A question for the more curious viewer: Why does the biceps tendon anchor to the scapula instead of attaching directly to the humerus? Let me know in the comments!

description: A fully 3D-printable Push-to-Open mechanism with 4 tactile click stages and a completely new rotating locking wheel concept. Snap-fit assembly No supports required No additional hardware No tools required 4 parts 1 printing plate Approx. 3 hours print time Approx. 110 g filament Tested with PLA, standard print settings and the printer X1E and X1C I designed a completely new Push-to-Open (Push-to-Lock / Push-Push) mechanism. This model is intended as a functional demonstration of the working principle and can be assembled quickly using snap-fit connections. I plan to use this Push-to-Open principle in future projects. Unlike other 3D-printed Push-to-Open mechanisms, this new concept is based on a wheel with movable print-in-place contact pins. To make the mechanism easier to understand, I added viewing windows to the model so every movement step can be observed clearly. The mechanism creates 4 distinct click sounds that provide both tactile and audible feedback during every cycle🔔: The first click indicates that the button can be released The second click confirms that the mechanism is locked Pressing again creates the third click, indicating that the button can be released. The fourth click confirms that the mechanism is open and the cycle can start again Additionally, the spring elements inside the mechanism are not permanently loaded in the locked or unlocked position, which increases durability (This does not apply to the spring that retracts the sliding latch). The locking wheel rotates 90° during each open-close cycle. Suitable Applications This functional model is suitable for: Educational and demonstration purposes Mechanical concept studies DIY projects Prototype development for Push-to-Open systems Just to have fun with the mechanism 😉 I believe this mechanism has potential for many different applications and further development. For example: Different spring forces for opening and closing could be implemented Different actions could be triggered after each 90° rotation The mechanism could be activated from all four sides I am open to application ideas, improvement suggestions, and remixes.👐 Print Settings and Material The mechanism can be printed without any special print settings. I tested the mechanism using PLA for all parts. Other materials may require adjustments and were not tested. In my tests, the spring elements of the locking wheel were stiffer when printed in standard PLA, which made the click sounds more noticeable. PLA Tough+ for the locking wheel was more flexible and allowed the mechanism to run slightly smoother, but the click sounds were less pronounced. Assembly The functional model consists of four parts: Housing ① Base plate ② Locking wheel ③ Spring-loaded sliding latch ④ Do not heavily load the spring elements immediately after printing. Allow the parts to cool down completely first. Check if the spring elements inside the locking wheel can move freely. Sometimes a small amount of plastic may fuse inside the gap during printing. This can usually be separated easily. Press each pin toward the center as shown in the image. 2. Insert the spring-loaded sliding latch into the housing as shown in the image. Make sure the guide rails are aligned correctly. 3. Place the locking wheel into the housing. The locking wheel must sit flush inside the housing as shown in the image. 4. Slightly press down the spring-loaded sliding latch at the push point while inserting the base plate from the top until the snap-fits lock into place. 5. Finished!🥳 Do not store the spring of the sliding latch in a permanently preloaded position, as this may reduce the spring force over time. From my experience, the mechanism runs smoother after several cycles. It is important that the locking wheel can rotate freely. Too much friction may cause the mechanism to malfunction. This was a problem in my first prototypes, but the newer versions worked reliably. If you experience any issues, feel free to leave feedback.🤔 Detailed Function Description (Now things start getting a bit more technical😉) I marked the most important elements with colors: The housing contains: First locking position (pink) Second locking position (purple) The locking wheel contains: First contact pin (red) Second contact pin (yellow) These pins can move toward the center and spring back afterward. The locking wheel also contains: Spring-loaded locking sliders (blue) Rotation stops (green) The following section explains the closing and opening sequence of the mechanism. The circled numbers correspond to the images shown below. Closing Process During closing, the spring-loaded sliding latch is inserted from the top by hand and presses against the first contact pin, causing the locking wheel to rotate clockwise ①. At the same time, the second contact pin is pushed toward the center by the side wall of the sliding latch and becomes preloaded, creating enough space for the sliding latch to move to the end position②. As soon as the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the first locking position ③. This prevents the locking wheel from rotating backward. The spring-loaded sliding latch can now move backward slightly using the spring force (spring not shown). Due to the previous rotation of the locking wheel, the return path of the sliding latch is blocked by the rotation stop ④. Because of this, the sliding latch can only move back to the rotation stop position and the mechanism is now locked ⑤. In this position, the preloaded second contact pin can move back into the matching recess of the sliding latch ⑥. Once this happens, the Push-to-Open mechanism can be opened again. Opening Process Opening is performed by pressing the sliding latch a second time by hand. The sliding latch pushes the second contact pin downward until the end stop is reached ⑦. The required travel distance is only 5 mm. During this movement, the first contact pin is preloaded against the side wall of the sliding latch ⑧. When the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the second locking position to again prevent the locking wheel from rotating backward ⑨. The sliding latch can now be fully pulled out of the mechanism by the spring force (spring not shown) ⑩. Since the first contact pin is no longer pressed against the side wall of the sliding latch, it can spring back into its original position ⑪. The system is now back in its starting position and the cycle can begin again. Thanks for checking out the project! 😁

description: The project This life-size 3D model is a realistic human hand skeleton. It was created starting from a real CT scan to keep the true shape of the bones. After cleaning up the scan, custom joints were added directly into the design. The result is a highly accurate model that prints in one single piece and moves just like a real hand. ⚙️ Print-in-Place Kinematics & Anatomy Unlike standard static models or complex multi-part assemblies, this hand is designed to be printed as a single, continuous piece: Zero Assembly Required: The complex mechanical joints are built directly into the geometry. Once the print is finished, the fingers and thumb are immediately ready to flex, extend, and move. Bio-realistic Movement: The internal joint constraints were specifically calibrated to respect the natural limits and range of motion found in a real human hand. Medical-Grade Accuracy: Features true-to-life representations of the carpal bones, metacarpals, and phalanges, preserving the organic textures and shapes of the original scan. 🎓 Perfect For: Clinical & Academic Study: A fantastic, hands-on visual aid for medical students, physical therapists, and anatomy teachers. Biomechanical Demonstration: Easily explains how the skeletal framework behaves during grasping, finger articulation, and thumb opposition. 3D Printing Showcase: An incredibly impressive project to demonstrate your printer's dimensional accuracy, bridging capabilities, and print-in-place tolerances. Artistic Reference: A great physical tool for artists and animators studying lifelike hand poses. 💡 Print Guidelines Format: 100% Print-in-Place. Material: Optimized for standard PLA. Rigid materials work perfectly to demonstrate the skeletal kinematics—no TPU or flexible filament is needed. Scale: Pre-scaled to match the proportions of an average adult human hand (1:1 scale). Disclaimer: While highly accurate and derived from real medical data, this model is designed strictly for educational, demonstration, and hobbyist purposes. It is not intended for clinical diagnostics or to replace professional medical advice.

The tactile design gives students a simple, hands on way to pause, regulate, and reset. For younger students, an adult can guide the rhythm by saying: Trace up, breathe in. Trace down, breathe out. description: Modular Articulated DNA Educational Model Let your students build, connect, and explore the DNA with this colourful modular model designed for hands-on learning. Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases, while the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone. This model is great for classrooms, STEM projects, biology demonstrations, or anyone who wants a fun physical way to understand nucleotide pairing and DNA structure. I also plan on extending this model with a couple of more pieces for better demonstration of topics like Transcription and Translation . Feel free to leave a like and follow if you'd like to stay updated. Parts You can print as many of the individual parts as you like and connect them with each other! Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases and the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone: Cytosine Guanine Adenine Thymine Uracil Assembly & Colouring The backbone pieces can be clicked together with a little bit of force. It is recommended to use 5x2 (dxh) magnets for both the backbone pieces and nucleotides, to better hold them in place. Place the magnets into the slot (make sure you have them oriented all in the same way!) and use a paper clip, a scredriver, or something similar to push the magnet all the way into the slot. You can also remove the magnets if needed using a paper clip from the other side. Feel free to adjust the colouring of the pieces to your needs. My file uses the colours according to the Wikipedia nucleic acid image: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid#/media/File:Difference_DNA_RNA-EN.svg Versions There are two Versions of nucleotides: Standard Set (recommended!) nucleotides have no chamfer/fillet on the connection pin. This makes them harder to separate from their counterparts, but results in a more stable double strand. Rounded Nucleotide Set contains nucleotide pieces with a rounded down connection pin. This makes them easier to separate, e.g. when demonstrating something, but obviously also reduces the stability of the entire double strand in terms of base pairs disconnecting when you move the double strand around. After many months of developing, it’s finally here! This is an Inline 2 Vacuum Engine, a model of an inline 2 internal combustion engine, that runs off a vacuum. I have spent months working out every little detail and mainly trying to get every tolerance perfect. I also go through a lot of work on all of my models to ensure that they are easy to print, and with minimal supports. This model is completely press-fit, no glue, no tape, no magnets, just plain old PLA, modeled with the intent of being easy and fun to assemble and mess with, for experts to beginners to people who just enjoy messing around with cool contraptions. Additionally, those who have previous experience with vacuum engines can attempt to performance tune it, by changing the offset the camshaft has on the crankshaft. Simply print out all the parts (don't forget to boost with that free boost token ;), assemble with the easy assembly instructions, and enjoy! Note: You will need six 608 bearings, either 3D printed versions from Makerworld, or the metal versions which I have included in the Bill of Materials from Makersupply. Also note that the tolerances are very good for a Bambu Lab A1, but I cannot guarantee perfect fits with other printers, although they should be pretty close. Operation Instructions: Operation is easy, simply stick a vacuum up to the cone on the exhaust manifold, and watch it rip! You may need to give it a rotate or two to help it get started. Tips for success: Be sure that the camshaft if offset by a quarter turn from the crankshaft (explained in the instructions). Try lubing all of the areas where there is filament on filament contact, to reduce friction and increase speed and power. Clean out your vacuum's filter, or remove it entirely to improve your vacuum performance. Be sure there is little friction inside the crank case, as in make sure there are tiny gaps between all of the moving parts to ensure they move freely. Updates: I have many updates planned, from gaskets cutouts, to new exhaust manifolds for different vacuums. I will include links to them here as they are developed. I just finished a throttle body for this engine, and you can find it here Thank you for checking this model out, and if you enjoyed, please share with your friends and family! I love designing models like this, and yall's support keeps me going. It takes a lot of time and trial runs to design new models. This model was no exception! Instructions: This model can be a bit complicated, as there are many pieces, but personally I found it very fun to assemble, and very satisfying. Step One: Connect the piston heads to the connecting rods with the two pins. Next assemble the crankshaft. This can be a bit tricky, with all the pieces looking identical, but pay attention to the photo, and you'll do fine. Note, the the position of the two cranks should be opposite, but I accidently had them the same in the first photo. The parts include are the five crankshaft pieces, three 608 bearings, the two piston assemblies, the flywheel, and one of the two gears with a hexagon cutout. Step Two: Connect the two valves to the connecting rods with the two pins. Now assemble the camshaft, this can also be a bit tricky, since there are so many pieces that make up the camshaft. Again, just pay careful attention to the photos and you'll do great. Note: If you get the crankshaft and camshaft pieces mixed up just remember the camshaft has a shorter stroke than the crankshaft, meaning the pieces are smaller. The pieces used here are the five camshaft pieces, three 608 bearings, the two valve assemblies, and one of the two gears with a hexagonal cut out. Step Three: Attach the cylinder heads to the block. There are a different amount of each size of screw included in the file, and throughout the rest of these instructions I will refer to each screw by the amount of them that are included. The set of three screws go in the three holes in a line in the head, and the single screw goes in the single hole on the other side of the head. VERY IMPORTANT: The screws included with this file are FRAGILE and cannot take very much twisting force at all. To avoid breaking off screws inside of the engine block or oil pan, finger tighten or lightly tighten with a flat-head screwdriver until its not easy and then STOP SCREWING. Note that the screwheads are also 10mm, and you may be able to fit a socket on them, but you must still be very careful to not over tighten the screws. Step Four: Now it is time to lay the crankshaft, the camshaft, and the middle gear into the engine block. This step can be tricky, and must be done correctly or the engine will not function. The secret to vacuum engines is to have the camshaft a one quarter (0.25, 90 degrees) turn AHEAD of the crankshaft, in the direction you want it to rotate. In a simpler sense, this means that while the valve is completely open (Top Dead Center) the piston must be halfway up. When the piston reaches Top Dead Center, the valve with already be half closed. Additionally, since this engine has two cylinders, the pistons and valves must be in opposite positions to be most efficient. Finally, if you would like to mess around with tuning the engine for higher speeds, try changing the amount that the camshaft leads the crankshaft. Basically, try a lead of maybe a sixth of a turn or a third of a turn, instead of a quarter turn. Step Five: Once you've got those in place, you can carefully screw the oil pan to the engine block with the set of four screws included in the file. Be sure the quarter turn amount does not change while you set the engine block and the oil pan together. Step Six: Finally, attach the exhaust manifold to the heads with the set of two screws, and the nuts. This may take some finagling to get them on. Once again remember to not overtighten, I advise only finger tightening. Congrats! Your finished! Don't forget to share a comment with a photo about your experience, I love to hear about it, whether success or failure. Also don't forget to boost!

Please handle all parts with care during and after printing. Improper assembly may require reprinting of certain small parts. Take your time during gluing steps — rushing is the most common cause of mistakes on this build. Update 1 – Scaling, Lettering, and Bearing Options I tested the model at multiple scales with only minimal modifications needed, mainly to the bearing holder. Overall, the engine can be scaled from 100% down to 60% with little to no issues. The main exception is the dowels, which may fit too tightly when scaled proportionally. I recommend printing the dowels 1 percentage point smaller than the rest of the model . For example, if the engine is printed at 60% scale , print the dowels at 59% . I have also uploaded a new print profile with everything prepared and ready to print, so no additional modifications should be necessary. Additionally, I added a version of the engine with the lettering integrated directly into the body In “alternate Parts” profile. This version is especially useful for dual-nozzle printers for improved detail and overall print quality. I also created a bearing support compatible with the common 608ZZ bearing (8 × 22 × 7 mm) . However, for the scaled-down versions, I recommend using the fully 3D-printed, bearingless configuration. At smaller scales, the printed bearing system generally rotates more smoothly because it produces less friction than a standard 608ZZ bearing. A traditional bearing may still work well if a high-quality, low-friction bearing is used. Sections Story & Background Engine Info Printing Tips & My Modifications Assembly Instructions Final Notes 1) Story & Background This model was originally designed for a special MTU event in the DFW area — a tribute to the engineers and technicians who work on and around one of the most advanced jet engines flying today. It was built for a friend who works there, and for the incredible team around them. Building this model meant diving deep into the real engineering behind the LEAP-1B, and coming out the other side with an even deeper respect for what CFM International has achieved. It was a labor of love from first sketch to final print, and sharing it with the maker community feels like the right next step. 2) Engine Info The CFM International LEAP-1B is the exclusive powerplant for the Boeing 737 MAX , designed and produced by CFM International — a 50/50 joint venture between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines , established in 1974. It represents a massive leap forward in efficiency and sustainability over its predecessor, the CFM56. MTU & the LEAP-1B This model was created for an MTU event — and MTU's connection to this engine runs deep. MTU Aero Engines is directly involved in MRO (Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul) services for both the LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B, helping keep this massive global fleet airworthy and operational. 3) Printing Tips & Modifications I made targeted modifications on a per-component basis rather than applying global settings — for example, on the engine body I adjusted print speeds for better surface quality and used support enforcers and blockers on specific areas to avoid unnecessary supports elsewhere. If you use your own print profile, you will still get a good result. However, if you have a Bambu A1 like mine, you'll get the best results using my specific print profile. Since the A1 is a Cartesian (bed-slinger) printer , outer surface quality can sometimes suffer — my speed adjustments help mitigate this, though it may not be perfect. Alternate Parts & Customization I have also uploaded an alternate parts profile for those who want additional options or a cleaner look. This includes: Clean engine variant — a version free of decals for a sleek, minimal finish Alternate display stands — additional stand styles as shown in the figures below Blank logo plates — fully blank plates that you can customize by importing SVGs directly in Bambu Studio or your preferred CAD software Bearing Options The shaft supports are designed to accommodate several bearing configurations. Choose whichever works best for you: Option Specs Notes Bambu-sourced bearing (6000ZZ) ID/OD/W: 10 × 26 × 8 mm Recommended Common Amazon bearing ID/OD/W: 8 × 22 × 7 mm Easy to source 3D printed bearing — Works, but not ideal Custom / your own bearing — Blank shaft support included Bearingless option Surprisingly works well A blank shaft support is included if you'd like to fit your own bearing or design a custom solution. All alternate parts and bearing profiles are included in the alternate parts profile attached to this upload. If you use a bearing, the shafts are pressure fit where the blade shaft diameter is 12 mm. Nozzle recommendation: I have uploaded multiple print profiles ( 0.2mm and 0.4mm). A 0.2mm nozzle will give you the best results for the lettering and logo details. 4) Assembly Instructions Step 1 — Fan Core Sub-Assembly (Shaft + Flywheel + Fan Support) Start by assembling the three core components: the blade support shaft , the flywheel , and the fan holder . Orient the shaft correctly — the flat side faces a specific direction as shown in the photo. ⚠️ If installed backwards, the fan blades will not seat in the correct position. Apply a small amount of glue into the alignment hole only — do not over-apply. Applying glue here (rather than on the shaft body) prevents glue from migrating to the shaft collar, which must remain free to spin. The completed fan core must be able to rotate freely — confirm this before the glue sets. Step 2 — Install Fan Core into Engine Body Apply glue to the designated glue area on the engine body interior as shown in the photo. Insert the fan core sub-assembly into the body. Align the notches on the shaft holder with the corresponding notches inside the engine body — this is critical for correct positioning. Do not proceed until the notches are fully seated and glue has cured. Step 3 — Fan Blades & Dowels Once the engine body assembly is fully cured, apply glue to the alignment hole of the fan blades and install them. Insert the dowels into their holes around the face ring — these may require a small amount of glue depending on fit tolerance from your printer. Step 4 — Remaining Assembly The rest of the assembly is largely self-explanatory — components are designed to fit together intuitively. Take your time and dry-fit each part before committing to glue. Step 5 — Seam Alignment (Aesthetics) For the best finished look, align the seam lines of the outer cowling sections with one another at the bottom of the engine. This small detail makes a big visual difference in the final display piece — as shown in the photo. 5) Final Notes Several customization options are included to personalize your build: Display stands — multiple styles to show off the engine Logo variants — alternate branding plates and logo options This model is shared for personal, non-commercial use only . description: Help students pause, breathe, and reset with this simple Box Breathing Pause Card from 3DprintEDU. This 3D printable calm corner tool gives children a tactile path to follow with their finger while practising a simple breathing routine. Students can trace the square, moving from corner to corner as they breathe in, hold, breathe out, and pause. Each Pause Card uses a raised O as the starting point, making the collection consistent and easy for students to use independently. This post includes 2 card variations , so you can choose the version that works best for your classroom, calm corner, counselling space, or sensory toolkit. Place your finger on the O and slowly trace along the square path. Use equal 4 second intervals for each part of the breathing cycle: Inhale for 4 seconds as you move from the O to the next raised circle. description: This is a bevel gear drive intended for demonstration and teaching purposes. As I am not personally involved in gear design and lack professional expertise in this area, the construction of this gearbox is not fully compliant with standards or industry practices in all aspects. What this model illustrates: Adjusted mounting of Tapered Roller Bearings (in X and O arrangement) Adjustment of bearing clearance using shims and a shaft nut Assembly sequence and process utilizing housing covers What this model does not depict: Realistic, industry-standard design parameters (shaft diameters, module, screw sizes) Fit precision of components (clearance, transition, and interference fits) Realistic cast housing geometries Assembly Preparation of the Model: Embedding all Heat-Set threaded inserts into both covers and the housing. Gluing the magnets into the three machine keys and the shafts (Caution: ensure correct polarity!). Assembly Sequence: Mount the inner ring of the tapered roller bearing onto the pinion shaft. Insert the corresponding bearing outer ring into the housing bore. Insert the pinion shaft through the housing opening. Slide the inner ring of the second tapered roller bearing onto the pinion shaft. Screw the shaft nut down to secure and adjust the bearing clearance. Pre-assemble the 30mm shaft: Slide on the bevel gear and both bearing inner rings. Loosely position the pre-assembled shaft into the housing. Fasten the large housing cover. Insert the bearing outer ring on the gear side. Mount the bearing cover on the gear side (without a shim). CAUTION: This cover has a longer projection of 3 mm. Insert the second bearing outer ring on the opposite side. Insert the shim. Bearing arrangement is typically adjusted via shims of varying thickness (only realized with one shim in this model). Fasten the corresponding bearing cover. Mount the front pinion shaft cover and the end cap for the pinion shaft on the opposite side. Insert all shaft seals (optionally, these can also be glued in before mounting the covers). Insert the machine keys.

The key itself functions both as to make the chuck work, by being the driving force behind the whole mechanism. And it also a hex key allowing you to tighten the bolts, though not too hard, since they are printed, and cant wihstand that much pressure without snapping. VERY IMPORTANT !!! When assembling the lathe chuck you have to ake sure you do it in the right order, or else the chuck will not grip around the center. You have to put claw 1 in slot 1 and so forth. When the claws sit in their respective slots, you need to turn the key, until they all get gripped by the spiral. You NEED to make sure that claw one grips first, then claw two, and lastly claw 3. This will make sure that the self centering mechanism works. When the claws have gotten grip, you simply turn it until the claws slowly move inwards. You will very likely need a bit of force to get the claws moving inwards. I recommend sliding the claws back and forth in their respective slots, when the spiral isnt in. This will help break in the slots, and make sure they move more smoothly. Video Of Assembly I hope you like the model, and have a fun time printing and using it. -Sincerely Capspam3D.

description: Help students pause, breathe, and reset with this tactile Loop Breathing Pause Card from 3DprintEDU. This 3D printable SEL tool gives children a calming finger tracing path to follow while practising mindful breathing, focus, and emotional regulation. Students begin at the raised O , then slowly trace the loop path as they breathe in and out. The included 3MF file contains both versions , so you can choose the style that works best for your students, classroom, or sensory space: Raised Path Version An embossed tactile path that students can feel clearly as they trace. Indented Path Version An engraved tactile path that gives students a smooth recessed channel to follow with their finger. Both versions are no AMS , quick to print, and use less than 20 g of filament, making them easy and quick to print for classrooms, calm corners, counselling spaces, occupational therapy rooms, and home regulation kits. How to Use Begin at the raised O , which is designed to be the consistent starting point across the SEL Pause Cards collection. Place your finger on the O and slowly follow the loop path. Students can breathe in as they trace up and around the first loops, then breathe out as they continue along the path. The goal is not perfection, it is slow, steady breathing and gentle focus. Repeat the path a few times, moving calmly and noticing each loop. The tactile design gives students a simple, hands on way to pause, regulate, and reset. For younger students, an adult can guide the rhythm by saying: Trace slowly. Breathe in. Keep tracing. Breathe out. Reset. My Educational Mechanical Examples Series This model is one of my educational mechanical mechanism examples on 80mm x 80mm base plates. You can find all models of the series in this collection => [Mechanical Mechanism Examples] The present model This is an educational model of a Hart's A-frame, which is one of the exact straight-line linkages. Brief Description The approximate straight-line mechanisms introduced so far — Watt's linkage, the Chebyshev linkage, and the Grasshopper linkage — are all based on four-bar linkages. The coupler point need not lie at a joint between two links; it may sit at the midpoint of a link or on its extension. Even so, these simple linkages confine the coupler point to a path that is only approximately straight — and they do so without any linear guide or prismatic pair. A four-bar linkage, however, cannot trace an exactly straight line. Hart's A-frame achieves exact straight-line motion by raising the number of links to six. Five of them move; the sixth is the base plate itself, which serves as the hidden ground link. Laid out as the capital letter A, each slanted side is built from a long link and a short link half its length, joined end to end, and the two short links meet at the apex. The lower end of each long link is pinned to the base plate, and these two fixed pivots are spaced apart by twice the length of the crossbar. The crossbar — the horizontal stroke of the A — joins the two long links at the points that divide them in a 3:1 ratio, with the longer portion toward the fixed pivot. Only these two lower pivots are anchored; every other joint is free to move. Under this arrangement the apex of the A, which is the coupler point, is constrained to travel along a perfectly straight line: the vertical line engraved on the base plate, which is the perpendicular bisector of the two fixed pivots. Move the coupler point by hand and you can feel it being held to this line. As you play with the model, though, you will find that this is not the only path open to the coupler point: the motion branches at the midpoint between the two pivots. There, the coupler point can leave the straight line for a second, skewed path that traces a distorted triangle, also engraved on the plate. Pushing on the coupler point alone will not carry it past the corners of that triangle; there you must also control how the links fold in order to pass through. To keep the motion well-behaved, confine the coupler point to either the upper or the lower half of the straight line, or guide it through the midpoint so that it does not slip onto the other branch. Reference https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hart%27s_inversors Related Models Case This model is compatible with the case included in my first set . Printing Use the models named ???-printable.stl for printing . The models named ???-assembled.stl are provided just to show how they should be assembled. Use well-dried PETG to have better dimensional accuracy. Use 0.1 mm or 0.08 mm layer height to have smoother surfaces. Use slow printing speed for overhangs. Select “Random” seam position to have smoother rotation. Randomly distributed seam should be easily worn out after some wearing.Printing Sanding and Filing Note that, in this model, the rotation of the bases for bearings is intentionally made not too smooth. Sometimes, the gears suffer from the stringing effect and/or elephant foot effect, resulting in a too tight fit to the shafts (they are designed with a 0.15 mm radial clearance). If you see rough surface on the shafts due to stringing, sand off the roughness with a small piece of sand paper. If you feel the gears do not rotate smoothly due to an elephant effect, widen the hole slightly by using a thin round bar file. Without those issues, the parts should rotate very smoothly with minimal friction. Assembly Secure the links onto the shafts with the retaining rings. Find them in this collection: https://makerworld.com/collections/15048577-my-educational-mechanism-models Happy printing!
