I've gotten some lovely feedback and compliments on the armchair model, which really helped me stay motivated through the creation and testing process for this one. I hope you enjoy this project if you decide to give it a try, and I look forward to seeing your creations! Let me know if you have any struggles and I will try to help (I check in here a couple times a week most of the time). What to gather up once you've printed the files: Tools: Sharp scissors, craft knife, tweezers (Optional: pinking shears, applique or nail scissors with a curved blade) Glues: glue stick, preferred structural/assembly glue, preferred fabric/craft glue Textile materials: something for batting (i prefer cotton), something for upholstery material (still prefer cotton) Other handy stuff if you have it already: A piece of photo paper to put under templates while gluesticking them, rubber brayer to smooth fabric on templates, Fray Check. More detailed remarks on materials: Quilting cotton or muslin in a small print. I recommend this for beginners particularly as it's much easier to glue than synthetics, both for sticking purposes, and for not making the fabric look stupid and jacked up. You don't need a lot of fabric. I didn't even have an eighth yard left of that pink flowered fabric I used. Batting/padding. I use Warm & Natural cotton batting usually, and it's my favorite since it's easy to shape and kind of smoosh into position even if it's not perfect at first. I've also upholstered with synthetic felt or fleece, or even untextured paper towels for very small scale work. If you don't mind doing more layers, you'll be fine using a thinner batting. You could also make the cushions less dramatically stuffed. Probably the most important thing is choosing a batting material you like working with, that won't look lumpy or show through the fabric in a way you don't like. Glue. For this project I used an Elmers Craft Bond extra strength glue stick, Gorilla brand wood glue, because it sets up pretty quick and sticks to PLA better than you'd expect, and Bearly Art craft glue. Bearly Art is a bit pricey in my opinion, so I don't necessarily love to recommend it to others. Suggested alternate adhesives: Most of the Aleene's product line. Beacon FabriTac. The main things you want to accomplish adhesive-wise are listed below by use case: For the thin plastic panels use a glue stick to attach the fabric, because it's an easy way to get good enough coverage to keep the fabric from wrinkling. Suggestions: most glue sticks are probably fine. For structural gluing of PLA panels to PLA, or for gluing raw fabric edges to PLA where it'll be covered later , use something that grabs well and cures firm. Suggestions: most of the Aleene's product line but especially turbo tacky. Beacon FabriTac. Gorilla wood glue. For gluing fabric to fabric , use something that won't dry stiff in a place you want the fabric to look plush or flat. Wood glue will dry hard and you want a more flexible hold. It's smart to test the glue on your particular fabric to make sure it cooperates and doesn't bleed through and look awful. Suggestions: Bearly Art if you got the bucks, Beacon FabriTac, Aleene's.

If the dragon dies, any portals near the lair close immediately. Customizing Dragons FTD p33 You can customize any dragon's stat block to reflect the dragon's unique character. Minor changes such as those below are easy to make and have no impact on a dragon's challenge rating. Languages. Most dragons prefer to speak Draconic but learn Common for dealing with allies and minions. But given their high Intelligence and long life span, dragons can easily learn additional languages. You can add languages to a dragon's stat block. Skills. Most dragons are proficient in the Perception and Stealth skills, and many dragons have additional skill proficiencies. As with languages, you can customize a dragon's skill list (even doubling their proficiency bonus with certain skills) to reflect particular interests and activities. You can also give a dragon tool proficiencies, particularly if the dragon spends time in Humanoid form. Other Traits and Actions. About Models: These models are designed to represent real animals as naturally as possible, with focus on accurate size, shapes, proportions, colors, fine details, and natural movement or pose. Some models include articulated, hinge, or flexi parts for motion and flexibility, while others are non-articulated and focus on realistic appearance. Some parts, such as legs, can be carefully adjusted with gentle heat for a more natural pose, but too much heat can damage or deform the model. Print: All settings are pre-configured and optimized for a balance between detail, print time, strength, functionality, and easy support removal. I recommend printing the models at their original scale. Scaling down may cause issues such as fused moving parts, small hinges not working correctly, or fine details not printing properly. Difficulty Guide: The difficulty icon is a general overall guide and may vary depending on your printer, filament, slicer settings, calibration, and experience. It mainly reflects print complexity, filament changes, possible waste, fine details, support use, and support removal. Multicolor prints may create more waste on single-nozzle AMS or AMS Lite systems, such as A1 with AMS Lite, compared to dual-nozzle or lower-waste systems like X2D or H2C. Level 3 / Supports: For higher difficulty models, especially Level 3, I recommend using Support Material for PLA. It can make support removal much easier, cleaner, and safer for delicate parts. This is especially helpful when the model has many supports, thin details, legs, antennas, or other fragile areas. Note / Handling: Some models may have very small hinge parts or delicate thin areas, such as legs, antennas, tails, or other small details. On some models, these parts may disconnect or break more easily if handled roughly. Please handle the models with care. They are not intended for aggressive play, but rather as educational models, display pieces, or gentle collectible toys. Durability may vary from model to model. Some models are stronger and may be suitable for careful play, while others are more delicate and better suited for display on a shelf. Articulated / Hinge Versions: For models with moving parts, hinges, or flexi sections, please open the included 3MF file, ideally in Bambu Studio. Exporting to another slicer may cause hinge problems. My hinges are created and tested by me, usually designed to print without supports, and are added this way so they can be moved, adjusted, customized, or removed when scaling the model down. STL / 3MF Note: STL files are usually provided without moving parts. The prepared articulated or hinge version is inside the 3MF file. This helps avoid problems with small scaled-down models, where moving parts, gaps, or hinges may fuse or fail. If needed, you can remove the hinges and print the model as a solid version. Safety Notice: Some models may have sharp edges or small parts. Avoid printing them too small and do not leave children unattended with them, as there is a choking risk. If you adjust parts with heat, always proceed carefully and use heat gently. Support / Links: I truly appreciate every comment, rating, or photo of your print it really motivates me to keep creating. The Pacific Halibut ( Hippoglossus stenolepis) is one weird looking fish. It's completely flat, it's 2 eyes are on the same side of it's head, and it's underside is completely white despite it's top side being a dark olive or brown color. Believe it or not each of these strange adaptations help this fish become an apex predator. Their flat shapes and eye placement allow them to hug the ocean floor and look for prey. Their color scheme (known as countershading) makes it easy for them to hide from predators and prey. If viewed from below their white bellies blend in with the light from above and if viewed from above they blend in with the sand and sediment of the ocean floor. While countershading is common in nature, halibut take it to the extreme with completely blank white undersides. They live in the cold (3-8C) waters of the North Pacific at depths of 180-450 ft. During the spawning season the fish dive to depths of 600 ft and females lay 500,000-4,000,000 eggs per year. The eggs hatch after 15 days and the fry circulate with current for hundreds of miles. Halibut are a prized species for sport fisherman in Alaska due to their high quality meat and massive size. While most anglers catch fish weighing 20 lbs or less, 150 lb fish are not uncommon. The state record specimen weighed a staggering 459 lbs and a replica hangs in the Anchorage airport. For thousands of years, native Alaskans used special hand-carved V-shaped hooks when fishing for halibut, designed to catch medium sized fish, but spare larger ones. This was because they wanted to spare the spawning females to protect the species, but also because hooking a monster without modern watercraft or gear could be a life-threatening experience. Today, to catch these fish, rods are secured to the side of the boat and outfitted with a 5lb lead weight, a hook, and bait. The weight pulls the bait all the way down and then bounces along the bottom with the motion of the waves. When a fish bites, the fisherman then has to retrieve the weight and the fish up through hundreds of feet of water, a few inches at a time. I've been fortunate enough to fish for halibut twice and its a ton of fun, even catching the small ones. This model uses interlocking scale units that allow the model to “swim” just like my other articulated fish models. This model prints in one piece and doesn't need any glue or a registration pin. It also uses only 4 colors and fits on an A1-mini. I printed one in brown and dark green, but if you have a dark olive colored filament, that would be the best match. Happy printing (and fishing)!

Some are anadromous meaning they swim out to sea to spend most of their lives, returning only to spawn. During spawning season, males develop a kype, or hooked bottom jaw to help them fight other males for breeding territory. While this characteristic is not unique to this species, it's something I wanted to include in the model to capture the appearance of trophy brown trout caught by anglers. Large specimens can reach 40 lbs and 31 inches. Brown trout are generalist predators meaning they'll eat a wide array of bugs, invertebrates, frogs, and even mice. description: 🐾 Vizsla The Vizsla is an elegant, athletic breed celebrated for its striking golden-rust coat, affectionate nature, and exceptional versatility. Originating in Hungary, the Vizsla was developed centuries ago as a hunting companion, prized for its ability to point and retrieve game across fields, forests, and wetlands with speed, endurance, and precision. Graceful yet powerful, the Vizsla combines remarkable athleticism with a deeply loyal and people-oriented temperament. Often called the "Velcro dog" because of its desire to stay close to its family, this breed thrives on companionship and human interaction. Today, Vizslas are cherished as devoted family dogs, energetic sporting partners, and loving companions who excel in both active lifestyles and affectionate homes. 🐶 Appearance & Personality Coat: Short, smooth, and dense coat with a beautiful golden-rust color that is unique to the breed. Their coat is low-maintenance and naturally glossy. Build: Medium-sized, lean, and muscular with an elegant yet athletic frame. Built for speed, stamina, and agility rather than bulk. Expression: Warm, intelligent, and gentle. Their expressive amber eyes reflect the breed's affectionate and eager-to-please personality. Ears: Long, silky ears that hang close to the cheeks, contributing to their refined appearance. Tail: Traditionally docked in some countries, though naturally long where docking is prohibited. Carried with a slight curve and used actively during movement. Temperament: Affectionate, energetic, and highly intelligent. Vizslas are exceptionally loyal and form deep bonds with their families. They are friendly, sensitive, and thrive on positive interaction, making them wonderful companions for active households. 🎾 Activity & Companionship Vizslas are high-energy dogs that require plenty of daily exercise and mental stimulation. They excel in activities such as running, hiking, agility, scent work, obedience, field sports, and retrieving games. Originally bred as versatile hunting dogs, they enjoy having a job to do and flourish when given regular challenges and training. Vizslas crave human companionship and are happiest when included in family activities. They generally do not enjoy being left alone for extended periods and thrive in homes where they receive plenty of attention and interaction. 💪 Health & Care Exercise: High — Vizslas need substantial daily physical activity combined with mental enrichment to remain healthy and well-balanced. Coat care: Low — their short coat requires only occasional brushing to remove loose hair and maintain its natural shine. Diet: A balanced, high-quality diet supports their active lifestyle, lean muscle development, and overall health. Health: Vizslas typically live 12–15 years. They may be predisposed to hip dysplasia, epilepsy, certain eye conditions, and some forms of cancer. Regular veterinary care, responsible breeding, and maintaining a healthy weight contribute to their long-term well-being. 🌍 Fun Facts 🏹 The Vizsla is one of Hungary's oldest sporting breeds, with a history dating back several centuries. 🧡 They are often nicknamed the "Velcro dog" because they love staying close to their owners. 🏃 Their speed, endurance, and agility make them excellent companions for runners, hikers, and outdoor enthusiasts. 🐦 Vizslas were bred as versatile hunting dogs capable of pointing, retrieving, and working on both land and water. 👨👩👧👦 Friendly, affectionate, and eager to please, Vizslas thrive in active families where they receive plenty of exercise, training, and companionship.

⛰️ Dao Miniature – Earth Genie Matriarch of Stone and Sovereignty This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Dao are the proud and merciless genies of the Elemental Plane of Earth, rulers of vast subterranean empires where wealth is measured in mountains of gemstones and kingdoms are carved directly into living stone. To a Dao, power is not earned through kindness, it is seized, possessed, and defended forever. Everything beneath the earth belongs to someone. And the Dao believe that someone is them. This miniature depicts a formidable female Dao standing with unwavering confidence upon a crystal-strewn outcrop, every detail reinforcing her status as an elemental noble whose authority is as enduring as the mountains themselves. Her powerful physique is sculpted from living stone, with layered rock textures, natural fractures, and mineral-like surfaces covering her body. Unlike mortal flesh, every muscle appears carved from ancient bedrock, conveying immense strength without sacrificing elegance. description: The Breach Gate Ruins is a dark fantasy terrain set designed for 28–32mm heroic scale tabletop games, RPG encounters, skirmish games and ruined city battlefields. description: Bring flexible defensive terrain to your grimdark sci-fi battlefield with this detailed Modular Imperial Bunker Tower terrain piece. This model is designed as a modular ruined bunker building with a plug-in connection system, allowing it to be used in two different configurations. Build it as a tall multi-level tower for a strong vertical battlefield silhouette, or separate the parts into a fortified bunker section and an additional ruined wall piece for more flexible table layouts. The modular design makes it easy to adapt the model to different battlefield setups. Use the full tower as a line-of-sight blocking centerpiece, or split it into two separate terrain pieces to create more cover, movement options and variation on your tabletop. All my models are real test prints, not just digital renders. I always try to find the best balance between print time, level of detail and filament usage, so the terrain looks impressive on the table without becoming unnecessarily difficult or wasteful to print. I also put a lot of effort into optimizing the files, removing print issues and making the models as user-friendly as possible. My goal is to offer terrain that prints cleanly, feels solid, and can be used straight from the printer or painted with simple drybrushing techniques. Designed with FDM printing in mind, the piece is suitable for PLA filament printing and looks great in simple grey material without any color changes. Description : This is a 3D printed model of a 4 cylinder DOHC engine. The engine is of the Ibishu Miramar from BeamNG.drive, equipped with racing parts for the carburetor and exhaust manifold. I exported the model and made some modifications to it ( I divided the model into 3 parts : gearbox, engine block and exhaust manifold) in order to make easier to print, remove supports and paint. I resized the model to 1/18 and 1/24 scale. The model from the pictures is painted. For the engine block I used metallic grey ( Tamiya XF-56), the valve cover is painted in flat red ( Italieri 4606AP), the racing parts are in chrome silver ( Tamiya X-11), the gearbox is in flat aluminum ( Tamiya XF-16) ,the other parts are in flat black ( Tamiya XF-1) and the gold accents and blue filter are in gold leaf ( Tamiya X-12) and gloss french blue ( Italieri 4659AP). Notes : I suggest printing it in white, that way painting is easier and no second coat is required. Some supports may be harder to remove, but not impossible ( if some supports are stubborn you can use a craft knife). Be careful when removing supports from the alternator because it is prone to breaking off. In order to assemble the 3 parts glue is required ( I used Tamiya cement). When assembling the gearbox, some supports may still be attached to the connector from the engine block ( just break them off). Happy printing :)

This model generates a real two-part buckle: male part with flexible snap arms and rigid center guide; female part with side-release windows. Main features 7 attachment styles, independently selectable for each side Choose a different tail style for the male and female parts: sewn slot belt pass-through adjustable tri-glide paracord holes, 2 or 4 holes closed loop / D-ring style single cord hole solid flat tab The tail shape automatically adapts to the selected attachment type: narrow rounded shape for cord use, full-width body for webbing, shaped tails for loops, paracord and flat mounting. Wide size range Designed for webbing widths from 10 mm to 60 mm , with adjustable overall thickness from 5 mm to 14 mm . Rigid center guide tongue — V2 The male part includes a rigid central guide tongue that helps insertion, reduces lateral wobble and protects the flexible arms from over-bending. On very narrow buckles, the guide is automatically disabled if there is not enough physical space. Improved snap-fit durability V2 includes several geometry improvements: rounded arm roots to reduce stress concentration; chamfered and rounded entry mouth for smoother insertion; side windows sized so the arms can relax when locked; adjustable latch geometry and arm stiffness. One-parameter fit tuning The most important parameter is clearance. Recommended starting point: default: 0.35 tighter fit: 0.25 – 0.30 looser fit: 0.40 – 0.45 Print, test, then fine-tune only this value first. Safe parametric sliders Critical parameters are internally limited to keep the geometry printable. If a limit is reached, OpenSCAD shows a NOTE in the console. Multilingual customizer labels The customizer labels are shown in 5 languages : Italian / English / French / German / Chinese IT / EN / FR / DE / 中文 Set part = "guide" to display a translated parameter legend directly in the 3D preview. Modern printable design V2 has a smoother commercial look with: rounded top edges; slightly barreled female body sides; shaped attachment tails; flat bottom for reliable bed adhesion. Printing instructions Print the parts flat on the bed , exactly as generated in the both layout. This is important because the snap arms flex in the XY plane , so the stress stays within the printed layers. Do not print the buckle upright, otherwise the arms may break along the layer lines. Recommended settings: no supports required; PETG or PLA+ recommended; ABS / ASA for outdoor or hotter environments; 0.2 mm layer height; 3 perimeters; 25–40% infill. For this model, perimeters matter more than infill . Included files Full parametric OpenSCAD source file; ready-to-print STL pair for 25 mm webbing : male part with sewn slot; female part with tri-glide attachment. V2 changelog Compared to the previous version, V2 adds: rigid center guide tongue; improved side-release fit; rounded arm roots; smoother chamfered mouth; shaped tails for different attachment styles; description: Make your own text stamp for clay, soap, leather, play dough, fondant, and normal ink-pad stamping. Up to three lines of custom text, round or rectangular head, emboss or deboss, optional border, and a comfortable twist-lock handle. Prints support-free. Type your text and print a personal stamp. The rigid PETG/PLA version presses crisp, readable impressions into polymer clay, air-dry clay, soap, soft leather, play dough, fondant, and similar soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping, a tested option is to split the stamp face in the slicer and print the actual raised letters/rim in TPU, with the base and handle in PETG, so the letters flex slightly like a softer stamp face. Features: - Up to three lines of text, automatically centered. - Mirrored text by default, so the stamped impression reads correctly. Turn mirroring off to print a readable display plaque instead. - Two impression styles: "raised" presses your text INTO the material (debossed impression), "recessed" leaves your text standing proud (embossed impression). - Round or rectangular head with adjustable size and optional border ring - the border stamps a clean frame around your text. - Adjustable text depth (0.8-3 mm) for shallow or deep impressions. - Comfortable mushroom handle with a bayonet twist-lock: insert into the head back and twist clockwise to a firm stop. The locked handle cannot pull off, even when lifting the stamp out of sticky clay. Print one handle and many heads: name stamps, date stamps, logo text, gift tags. - Tested TPU-face workflow: print the raised letters/rim in TPU and the base + handle in PETG for a softer face that also works better as a normal ink-pad stamp. - Console warning if your text is too wide for the chosen head size. - Both parts print flat with no supports. The model checks your text width against the head size and prints a note in the customizer console if a line will not fit. Note: rigid PLA/PETG stamp faces are best for clay, soap, leather, dough, and other soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping on paper, the tested TPU-face workflow gives a more forgiving contact surface than a hard FDM face. Results still depend on ink pad, paper, layer height, and surface finish, so test first. Custom Fonts: You can use any font MakerWorld has installed , type it into font_name as "Family:style=Style". Examples: Liberation Sans:style=Bold (default) Liberation Serif:style=Bold (bookplate look) Liberation Mono:style=Bold (typewriter) Liberation Sans Narrow:style=Bold (fits longer text) DejaVu Sans:style=Bold DejaVu Serif:style=Bold Stick to Bold styles thin strokes don't stamp well and can be fragile. Customization Notes - line_1 / line_2 / line_3: your text; leave lines empty to use fewer lines. - font_name: keep the default Liberation Sans Bold for reliable width warnings; other bold fonts work, but check the preview. - mirror_text: leave ON for stamping. Turn off only for display plaques. - text_style: "raised" = pressed-in (debossed) impression, "recessed" = raised (embossed) impression. - text_depth: 1.5 mm default; use 2-3 mm for soft doughs, 1-1.5 mm for firm clay and leather. - head_shape / head_diameter / head_width / head_height: face size. Bigger faces fit longer text. - border_enabled / border_width / border_inset: frame ring around the text. - border_depth: rim height, independent of text_depth. Match text_depth for a classic one-level stamp, or make the rim taller than the text so it contains the material and controls impression depth like a cookie-cutter frame - useful for wax-seal-style stamps and uniform clay medallions. - fit_clearance: twist-lock clearance. Increase by 0.05-0.1 if the handle is hard to insert or twist; decrease toward 0.05 for a tighter lock. - part: "all" prints both pieces; "head" alone for extra stamp faces for a handle you already printed; "fit_preview" is preview-only - do not print. description: Windproof Heavy Duty Sand Pegs Stakes Engineered for Extreme Beach Camping Stop watching your tent fly away in coastal gales! Built out of pure necessity, these heavy-duty screw-in sand pegs were designed to withstand the brutal realities of off-grid wild beach camping. When you are exposed to relentless 70–80 km/h winds , standard tent stakes just won't cut it. These aggressive, deep-threaded spiral anchors bite hard into loose ground to keep your shelter, tarp, or beach umbrella firmly rooted. Smart, Optimized 3D Print Design As a maker and avid camper, I designed these pegs from scratch to solve two major problems: weak ground holding and wasteful printing. The geometry has been carefully tuned for the 3D printing process: Zero Supports: Engineered to print completely support-free, saving post-processing time. Fast & Efficient: Optimized design drastically cuts down on print time and filament waste without sacrificing structural integrity or toughness. 3 Included Models & Sizes To ensure you have the perfect anchor for any beach topography, the package includes 3 distinct variations: 1x Medium Size: Great for compact packing, firmer damp sand, and standard setups. 1x XL Standard: Extended length for deep penetration into shifting, loose sand to provide massive pull resistance. 1x XL Wide-Thread: Features a significantly wider screw thread configuration. This is engineered specifically for extra strength and maximum surface area bite if you are dealing with ultra-fine, super dry, or powdery sand. Print Settings & Material Recommendations ⚠️ For Best Results: Print with high infill (minimum 40-50%) and at least 4-5 perimeters/walls to ensure maximum torsional strength when screwing them into the ground. ASA (Highly Recommended): If your stakes are going to sit in the blistering direct sun all day, ASA is the top choice . It offers excellent UV resistance and high thermal stability, ensuring the pegs won't soften, warp, or deform under intense beach heat. PETG (Budget/Alternative Option): PETG works perfectly fine with a simple trick! If you use PETG, dig a hole in the sand until you reach the damp, harder layer, screw the pegs in there, and then bury them back up with sand. As long as they are buried away from direct sunlight, PETG will stay cool enough to maintain its strength and hold your gear secure. Pro-Tip for Maximum Hold in Loose Sand: To get the absolute best anchorage on windy beaches, don't just screw them into the dry, powdery top layer. Dig a small hole until you reach the dense, wet sand underneath. Screw the anchor directly into that wet layer so the wide threads can lock into the compacted sand. If the sand is completely dry or you can't dig deep enough, pour a bottle of sea water over the area after screwing it in to tighten and pack the sand around the threads. Fill the hole back up and stomp it down!

description: This one was quite the task! I originally did my clicker bar using these transparent bead storage cases which worked perfectly fine while making the odd one at home but I ran into a bit of an issue when we took it to our events. The first was they were quite small in height meaning I couldn't put a lot of keycaps in them, it also caused overflow into the other containers when people were digging around for the colour they wanted so I had random letters mixed in with each other. 😩 They were also a pain to put out on display because they came with an attached lid so I had to keep them closed after people left or use double the space to keep them open. Not great when you're already busy enough building the actual clickers and limited on table space! That got me motivated to upgrade the display - I looked around for a while but couldn't find anything that really matched what I needed so I set myself to work. The main issues I needed to resolve were: It had to be modular so I can always add extras for new keycaps if needed. Had to be held together somehow during the events so it doesn't get pushed over easily by people but needs to be able to accommodate for different sized bins and layouts due to table restrictions. A slot to show the letters/symbols as people often got lost trying to find letters if keycaps were flipped upside down in the box, worse if letters got mixed around already. Ideally stackable so I can just stack them together after events and pack it away in a box for ease of use. A lid preferably so they don't accidentally fall out or have other small objects fall into them. Features of the storage bins: Fully modular. x1, x4 and x9 bins. Bins are stackable. Please note x9 bin requires 256mm x 256mm build plates but you can print a x4 with x1 and combine to make a x9 for A1 Mini users. Two coupler versions for joining displays. Bins can be attached with the row or the quad coupler. There are both snug and loose fits so print the one best for your printers/filament calibration. Quad couplers are for holding 4 bins together or for joining large 9 bins with 4 bins. The row coupler is if you wanted to build horizontally/vertically only. Display slot version and one without. Slots are slide in and can be removed after event completion by placing it inside the bin with the keycaps for easy storage. Personally I like the slot version but I included one without in case others wanted to use these for other purposes. Stackable. Please note there is a small gap where they are stacked - this finger gap is INTENTIONAL so you can actually separate them easier without them getting stuck. (Mishaps have happened during testing...) Various lid options. x1 lids have handles and coupler holes, x4 lids have coupler holes, x9 lid have no holes. If using the handle versions for x1, please secure handles using GLUE. I could add more variations but I feel like for most people these versions should suffice. For handles I have a short and a taller version as well. There are two sizes to these in case you find them too tight to fit into the hole on the lids. Recommended Print Settings: Layer Height: 0.2mm Nozzle: 0.4mm Wall Generator: Classic Infill: 15-20% Gyroid Supports: Not required Speed: 20-50mm/s for layer 1, then 150-200 for the rest. description: A wall mount system for the Lightweight Infinite Skadis panels that keeps every peg-hole free. No drilling into the wall required. The panels attach to the mounts using the existing mounting holes, so your full pegboard surface stays available for accessories. Compatible with Lightweight Infinite Skadis panels without standoffs: 160x160mm, 200x200mm, and 240x240mm (links below). How it works Attach the mounts to your wall or surface using double-sided tape. Then insert 4x20mm wood/chipboard screws through the mounting holes in the panel and screw them into the pegs. The panel is clamped securely between the screw head and the peg, with no peg-holes occupied. The set covers any panel configuration 1 panel: 4x Single 2 panels horizontal: 4x Single, 2x Double Horizontal 2 panels vertical: 4x Single, 2x Double Vertical 2x2 grid: 4x Single, 2x Double Horizontal, 2x Double Vertical, 1x Quad You can mix and match elements based on your layout: Component Purpose Quad Mount Connects 4 panels together into one stable hub Double Horizontal Connects 2 panels side-by-side horizontally, useful in the top row and bottom row and it is essentially the bottom part of the quad. Double Vertical Connects 2 panels stacked vertically, will be required on the far left and far right columns and it corresponds to the vertical half of the quad. Single Mount For a single panel endpoint or areas without adjacent connections, single with a through hole are needed on the corners. Use the strongest double-sided tape you can find. Load capacity depends entirely on the tape used. Compatible only with Lightweight Infinite Skadis panels without standoffs by zomb (links below) . Update 05/07/2026 : Fixed the Quad Mount orientation. The connector was mirrored along the X axis, which caused misalignment when connecting 4 panels at corners. For easy alignment just check: Infinite skadis Alignment Tool Prefer a no-screw solution instead? The Lightweight Infinite Skadis Wall Mount - No Screws lets you mount panels with tape only, no screws needed. New to Lightweight Infinite Skadis? description: Parametric Storage Box - Custom Lid & Base A fully customizable storage box with a separate lid and base. This design is a new version of my original Parametric Storage Box . Where the original design does not let you adjust the heights of the lid and base separately, this design does! This design uses a simple but strong filament hinge to join the lid and base. The model is fully parametric. Click Customize to open MakerWorld’s Parametric Model Maker to adjust the dimensions. See below for more details. Please DO NOT use Bambu Studio's Scale option , this will probably lead to failure… To get the most out of this design, please read the following instructions carefully! UPDATE 03 July 2026 I noticed the tolerances of the hinges were a bit too tight, so I slightly increased them to improve smoothness of the operation. The original version still works, but that needs some ‘wearing in’ for it to function smoothly. Additionally, I tweaked the print profile a bit so that the seam is now less prominent (backside) Features Fully parametric and customizable Independently adjustable lid and base heights Separate lid and base (not print-in-place) Bigger boxes on smaller printers (only 1 part per build plate instead of the entire box) Reliable filament hinge No supports required Snap-fit locking mechanism Suitable for PLA, PETG and other common filaments Dimensions The model uses external dimensions as input parameters. All dimensions can be adjusted between 13 and 350 mm where applicable . Maximum dimensions are mainly limited by your printer size. External dimensions (customizable) In order to customize the design to your specific needs, hit the ‘customize’ button under the print profiles: The Parametric Model Maker will open in a new tab, where you can adjust the following settings: boxWidth : 95–350 mm boxDepth : 25–350 mm baseHeight : 17–350 mm. lidHeight : 13–350 mm Internal dimensions The usable internal dimensions are: Width : boxWidth − 8 mm Depth : boxDepth− 9 mm Base height : baseHeight − 4 mm Lid height : lidHeight − 4 mm Example (box in attached print profile): An external size of 125 × 80 × 70 mm (W × D × total height) could be configured with a 13 mm high lid and a 57 mm high base. This results in internal dimensions of 117 × 71 mm, with 9 mm usable height in the lid and 53 mm usable height in the base. After downloading, the model in Bambu Studio is 1 object. If you want to print the 2 parts separately (if they don't fit on 1 plate), you can use the ‘Cut’ menu in Bambu Studio to separate the parts. See image below for the settings to use: Filament hinge The hinge uses a short piece of filament as the hinge pin. A piece (30 mm) of standard (1.75 mm) filament can be used as the hinge pin. For assembly, I suggest the following: First, you take a piece of filament and test fit all the holes BEFORE assembly. As the tolerances are tight (intentional) a small printing artefact can cause headaches during assembly. By test fitting first, you smoothen the holes for the next step. Then, you fit the parts together and then slide in the filament pieces from the side. . . Locking mechanism The box uses a snap-fit latch to keep the lid securely closed while still allowing easy opening. Customization ideas This box can be used for many purposes, including: Hardware storage Workshop organization Electronics components Desk organization Small parts storage Custom travel containers You can also create your own inserts or dividers to match your specific needs. I am working on custom inserts for this box, which I will release soon. Printing The design is optimized for 3D printing. No supports required Print settings depend on your printer and filament PLA and PETG both work well If you create a custom size, I would love to see your print! 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: Square Kumihimo disc for flat bracelets This is a square Kumihimo disc to make flat bracelets using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The disc has ten (10) horizontal and vertical notches to hold the strings in place and a rounded slot in the center for the weaving pattern to form. The top and bottom horizontal rows are labelled 1-10 and the left and right side vertical columns are labelled A-J to make it easier to stay oriented while making your Kumihimo weaving bracelet. The labels are printed flat on the bed, so the disc is rotated upside down. If using an AMS, the labels are pre-colored and will be printed using a color for the disc and a second for the labels. Without an AMS, the labels will still be visible through the trick of the labels being recessed by one layer height (0.2mm), this embeds the outline of the labels even without color as shown below. If desired, you could trace the etching using a permanent marker after the print. Instructions No assembly is required for the print. Simply print it, get some strings of silk, yarn or rope and you're ready to go. Patterns and instructions on how to use a Kumihimo disc to make rope/bracelets can be found online with several websites dedicated to it and many instructional videos. 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: 本模型仅供个人下载使用，您不得以任何形式出售此模型的数字及物理打印版本。 项目背景 在过去很长一段时间里，每次准备焊接，我都需要把电烙铁、PCB 夹具、焊锡丝、烟雾净化器等工具一个个搬到桌面。 焊接结束后，又要逐一收回。 随着焊接工作越来越频繁，我发现真正浪费时间的并不是焊接本身，而是 准备焊接和整理桌面 。工具越来越多，桌面越来越拥挤，不仅影响工作效率，也让整个工作环境显得杂乱无序。 另一方面，我一直使用空气净化器作为临时方案处理焊接烟雾。随着焊接时间增加，我希望增加专业的焊烟过滤器，但市面上的产品大多是独立设备，这意味着桌面上又会增加一个新的设备，进一步加剧原本就混乱的焊接环境。 我开始意识到，我真正需要解决的问题，并不是增加一个新的工具，而是 重新组织整个焊接环境。 愿景 于是，我开始构思一个新的概念—— 焊接坞（SolderDock） 。 它不仅仅是一台焊烟过滤器，更应该成为焊接工作中所有常用工具的”停靠点”。 我希望它能够同时承担以下几个角色： 焊烟过滤 常用工具挂载 焊接工具收纳 模块化扩展平台 更重要的是，希望焊接结束后，我只需要移动一个设备，就能快速完成整个焊接环境的收纳，让工作台能够迅速从 焊接模式 切换到 装配、拼接、测量 等其它工作模式。 设计思考 既然希望所有工具最终都能围绕同一个主体展开，那么首先需要确定整个系统的核心。 观察整个焊接环境后，我发现焊烟过滤器本身就是体积最大的设备，也是所有工具中位置最固定的一部分，因此决定以焊烟过滤器作为整个”焊接坞”的核心。 随后，我开始寻找市面上的现成方案。 经过一段时间的调研后，我基本放弃了现有产品，原因主要有三个： 1. 体积与成本 过滤效果较好的产品通常体积较大，价格也相对较高，不适合作为桌面长期使用的中心设备。 2. 滤芯成本与维护 很多产品使用专用滤芯，不仅需要重新验证过滤效果，后期更换时也难以保证长期稳定购买，维护成本较高。 3. 扩展能力不足 市面上的焊烟过滤器几乎都是独立产品，并没有预留安装其它工具的可能，更无法作为整个焊接环境的中心。 因此，我希望最终的方案能够满足几个目标： 使用价格低廉且容易获得的标准滤芯； 成本尽可能低； 能够方便集成其它焊接工具； 保留后续模块化扩展能力。 实现方案 基础选型 整个设计首先从滤芯选型开始。 我希望直接采用已经成熟、供应稳定的标准滤芯，这样不仅能够降低成本，也方便后期长期更换。 最终，我选择了小米车载空气净化器所使用的滤芯。 原因很简单： 市场保有量大； 原厂、副厂滤芯供应充足； 更换成本低； 后续维护几乎没有压力。 确定滤芯之后，我曾考虑直接改造小米车载空气净化器。 不过很快发现两个问题。 第一，原机采用多面进风设计，作为焊烟过滤器时，无法将吸力集中到焊接区域。 第二，原机出风方向与理想结构并不一致，同时也没有预留任何工具挂载空间。 相比继续修改原机，重新设计整个外壳显然更加合理。 随后，我开始研究风扇和驱动方案。 最初计划单独购买离心风扇和驱动板，再重新设计整体结构。 但在比较价格时，我突然意识到： 直接购买二手小米车载空气净化器，反而比单独购买风扇和驱动电路更便宜。 于是最终选择拆解整机，仅保留： 风扇 驱动板 电源系统 除此之外，这块驱动板还带来了意外收获： 它不仅支持三档风速调节，还可以连接米家 App，通过蓝牙查看简单的空气质量信息，为整个产品增加了一些不错的交互体验。 结构设计 确定核心硬件后，整个设计开始围绕”焊接坞”这一理念展开。 优化风道 重新设计外壳，使进风口与出风口保持相对方向，让烟雾能够沿着更合理的路径流动，提高吸烟效率。 精准反向工程 由于原厂风扇安装孔位和接口均为异形结构，为保证装配精度，我通过 3D 扫描获取原始模型，并进行反向工程设计，使电机卡扣准确入位。 模块化扩展 外壳预留了大量标准 M3 安装孔，方便后续增加新的功能模块，也方便用户根据自己的需求进行扩展。 焊锡支架 顶部增加挡风罩，并将标准焊锡丝线轮集成其中，在保证风道效果的同时，也方便焊接过程中直接取锡。 焊锡分装收纳盒 整卷焊锡丝负责储存，分装盒负责使用。 通过可挂载的焊锡分装盒，让焊锡丝在 储存、收纳与焊接 之间自由切换。 PCB 夹具 通过金属万向软管安装 PCB 夹具，使夹具能够直接固定在焊接坞主体上，进一步减少桌面设备数量。 铜丝球清洁挂载 在侧面预留铜丝清洁球盒的挂载位置，将烙铁头清洁功能集成到焊接坞中，减少桌面独立设备。 电烙铁挂架 右侧设计了倾斜式电烙铁挂架。 这样的设计不仅符合日常使用习惯，还能够让烙铁余烟继续被吸入过滤器，同时降低误碰烫伤的风险。（这个设计来自一次真实的教训。） 图：电烙铁挂载图 快拆维护 采用快拆卡扣结构，更换滤芯无需拆卸整机。 同时，滤芯还能定期旋转角度，使滤材利用更加均匀，进一步延长使用寿命。 成品验证 最终，这套”焊接坞”基本实现了最初设定的目标。 电烙铁、PCB 夹具、焊锡等常用工具全部集中到一个主体上，现在只需一只手即可移动整个焊接环境，大幅降低了部署和收纳成本。 实际测试中，在关闭空调和风扇的室内环境下，焊烟能够在距离进风口约 12 cm 的位置被稳定吸入，满足日常焊接需求。 后续优化 目前，电烙铁和焊烟过滤器仍然采用独立供电。 下一阶段，我希望进一步整合供电系统，使整个焊接坞只需要一根电源线即可完成部署。 同时，也计划增加顶部辅助照明、更多可扩展模块以及统一的供电接口，让整个系统真正成为一个可持续扩展的模块化焊接平台。 本模型仅供个人下载使用，您不得以任何形式出售此模型的数字及物理打印版本。

You tell it what you carry and it builds the box around you: a **bento-style grid** interior, a **personalised two-colour lid**, a **click-stop hinge** that holds itself open, and an **ergonomic thumb latch** — all auto-sized, all support-free. > 👉 **Press the “Customize” button** to open it in MakerWorld’s parametric editor and dial in your own box right in the browser — no software to install. Then download your `.3mf`/`.stl` and print. --- ## ✨ Highlights - 🧩 **Bento-grid interior** — drop vials, syringes, or wipe slots into a Row × Column grid; the box **auto-sizes** around your loadout. - 💉 **Holds your whole kit** — 3 / 5 / 10 ml vials (standing *or* laid on their side), open syringe bins, and vertical wipe slots. - 🏷️ **Personalised lid** — flush **two-colour text + graphics** (great with Bambu AMS), 40+ fonts including bold, aggressive display faces. - 🔗 **Click-stop hinge** — the lid **holds open** at set angles instead of flopping, and is engineered to survive **thousands of open/close cycles** in PLA. - 👍 **Ergonomic latch** — a smooth thumb-pry lip pops the lid with one finger; still snaps shut securely. - 🖨️ **Prints clean** — watertight and **support-free**; tuned for Bambu Lab and every FDM printer. --- ## 🧩 The Bento Grid (how the interior works) The inside is a grid of **`grid_rows × grid_cols`** quadrants. You drop a **component** into each cell, and the box grows to fit: | Component | What it is | Footprint | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | **vial1 / vial2** | pockets of your two chosen vial sizes | `cols × rows` | **auto-fills** the compartment; each can stand up **or lay flat** | | **syringe** | an **open deep bin** for U100 syringes | `count×20 × 130 mm` | floor→ceiling, no wasted solid; syringes lie in & stack | | **wipe** | a **vertical slot** for 50×50 mm wipe packets on edge | `(count×5) × 50 mm` | ~5 mm ≈ 10 wipes; +5 mm per count | | **empty** | a solid spacer | — | for gaps / future use | **How the sizing works (so it always fits):** - **Column widths** grow to the widest cell in that column; **row lengths** grow to the longest cell in that row — a clean table layout. So a 130 mm syringe makes its whole row 130 mm long, and the vial cell next to it **auto-fills** that length with more vials. - **Box height = your tallest item** (a standing 10 ml is 54 mm; a standing wipe is 50 mm — whichever is tallest sets the height so the lid still closes). - **Partition walls** turn each cell into a real compartment. `partition_level` sets their height: **0 = none, 1 = 25 %, 2 = 50 %, 3 = 75 %, 4 = full**. ``` grid_cols ───────────────► Example default 2×2: ┌──────────────┬───────────────┐ │ vial1 (3 ml) │ syringe bin │ r1c1 = vial1 (3 ml) r1c2 = syringe ×2 │ auto-filled │ ▭▭ open/deep │ r2c1 = vial2 (10 ml) r2c2 = wipe ×3 ├──────────────┼───────────────┤ │ vial2 (10 ml)│ wipe slot ▮▮ │ └──────────────┴───────────────┘ ``` ### 💊 Vial catalog | Vial | Size | Pocket | |---|---|---| | **3 ml** | Ø16 × 40 mm | Ø17 | | **5 ml** | Ø22 × 40 mm | Ø23 | | **10 ml** | Ø22 × 54 mm | Ø23 | Pick which two sizes you want with `vial1_type` / `vial2_type` (sizes are editable in **`[Content Catalog]`**). --- ## 🎛️ How to use the parametric controls Open **Customize** and you’ll see the settings grouped into sections. Here’s what each group does: ### `[Grid]` — the layout skeleton - **`grid_rows` / `grid_cols`** — how many quadrants (e.g. 2 × 2). - **`partition_level`** — divider-wall height, `0`–`4` (none → full). ### `[Row 1] / [Row 2] / [Row 3]` — fill each cell - **`r1c1` … `r3c3`** — the component in each cell: `vial1`, `vial2`, `syringe`, `wipe`, or `empty`. - **`r1c1_n` …** — the **count** (vials wide, syringe width, or wipe thickness). - **`r1c1_rows` …** — vial **rows deep** for *that* quadrant (`0` = use the default), so every cell can have its own R × C. ### `[Vial Types]` — vials behaviour - **`vial1_type` / `vial2_type`** — `3ml` / `5ml` / `10ml`. - **`vial1_orient` / `vial2_orient`** — `standing` or **`flat`** (lays the vials in round side cradles). - **`vial_pack`** — `fill` (maximise how many fit) or `exact` (place exactly your R × C). - **`vial_align`** — `spread` (outer vials hug the walls, evenly indexed) or `center` (centred block). - **`vial_wall_clear`** — gap kept to the walls so pockets never break out. ### `[Box Height]` - **`height_override`** — `0` = **AUTO** (sized to the tallest item). Set a value to force a total height. - **`extra_height`** — add head-room above the auto height. ### `[Output]` — what to render - **`show_bottom`** — the tray. **`show_top`** — the lid. **`show_combined`** — lid sitting on the box (preview). - **`show_contents`** — draws translucent mock vials/syringes/wipes so you can eyeball the loadout. **Turn it OFF before exporting** — it’s preview-only. - The **console report** tells you the grid, box W × L × H, what each cell holds, and warns if anything is too big for your plate. > 💡 **Tip:** export **once with `show_bottom`** and **once with `show_top`** — that’s your tray + lid. --- ## 🏷️ Personalise the Lid — flush two-colour Text & Graphics The lid top can carry a **flush, co-planar** label — *not* embossed or engraved, but a second-colour region in the same surface (perfect for **Bambu AMS / MakerWorld multi-colour**). **Text** and **Design** are independent — use either or **both**, each with its own colour and placement. **Orientation frame:** picture the closed box with the **latch toward you** (front) and the **hinge at the back**. Everything is placed in that frame — `halign` = your left/right, `valign` `top` = hinge / `bottom` = latch. ### `[Lid Text]` - **`lid_text_on`**, **`lid_text`** (+ optional **`lid_text_line2`**), **`lid_text_color`**. - **`lid_font`** — a dropdown of clean classics **plus aggressive / manly display faces**: Oswald, **Anton**, **Bebas Neue**, **Archivo Black**, **Black Ops One**, Bungee, Bangers, Teko, Russo One, Orbitron, Audiowide, Staatliches, Monoton, Permanent Marker, **Alfa Slab One**, **Ultra**, **Bevan**, **Passion One**, **Titan One**, **Squada One**, **Rajdhani**, **Chakra Petch**, **Wallpoet**, **Goldman**, **Michroma**, **Stardos Stencil**, **Special Elite**, **Rye**, **Metal Mania**, **Pirata One**, **UnifrakturCook**, **New Rocker**, **Germania One**, and more. - **`lid_font_custom`** — type **any** font name to use it instead (this is a searchable **font picker** in MakerWorld’s editor). - **`lid_text_weight`** — Regular / Bold / Black / … ⚠️ **Set this to `Regular` for single-weight display fonts** (Anton, Bebas Neue, Bangers, Black Ops One, Alfa Slab One, etc.) or they fall back to the default. - **`lid_text_size`** — a real font size in mm (`0` = no text); it **auto-shrinks to fit** so long words never run off the edge. - **Alignment + padding** — `lid_text_halign` / `lid_text_valign` **anchor the text to that edge and grow it inward** (right-align fills right→left, left-align fills left→right — never cut off). **`lid_text_pad_l/r/t/b`** inset each side in mm to nudge it perfectly. - **`lid_text_orient`** — `horizontal` or `vertical`. ### `[Lid Design]` - **`lid_design_on`**, **`lid_design`** — `molecule`, `helix`, `honeycomb`, `logo`, or full-lid tilings `helix-full` / `honeycomb-full`. - **`lid_design_orient`** — horizontal / vertical / corner-TL/TR/BL/BR, plus **`halign` / `valign` / `pad`** (same edge-anchored behaviour as the text) and **`lid_pattern_scale`** for size. - **`lid_design_color`** — the design colour. **Layering:** where text and a design overlap, the **text reads on top** (the design is relieved out from under the letters), each in its own colour. > 🎨 **To print in two colours:** render the lid (`show_top`) and **export as 3MF** — each colour region becomes its own material for the AMS. (A single-material STL is also fully watertight.) --- ## 🔗 Hinge & Latch — engineered, not guessed **Ergonomic latch pry-lip** — a smooth, rounded ridge you hook a thumb under to pop the lid. Hulled (no sharp edges), self-supporting underside, and clear of the snap bump so the **secure close is unchanged**. Set with `latch_relief` / `latch_relief_size`. **Click-stop detent hinge** — the open lid **clicks and holds** at set angles instead of flopping. A rounded nub on the lid drops into rounded dimples on the barrel ends — and because the detent lives on the **hinge end faces**, it needs **no supports at any angle**. - **`detent_angles_deg`** = `[90, 120, 140, 160, 180, 210]` (210 = full-open back-stop) — edit to taste. - **`detent_phase`** nudges the click angles; **`detent_nub_proud`** firms the click; **`detent_bore_extra`** adds local relief *only* if a test print snaps on too stiffly. - This design survived a **multi-pass adversarial stress-test** — it’s tuned to flex the long lid spring by only a few tenths of a millimetre per click (low strain) with filleted features for fatigue life. **Third (center) hinge** — on wide boxes the long barrel can sag, so a center support cradle is **added automatically** when the box `width ≥ third_hinge_width_threshold` (160 mm) or when you set `enable_third_hinge`. The lid still snaps on in one motion and prints support-free. > 🧪 **Pro tip:** print a quick **one-knuckle test coupon** first to feel the snap + click, then fine-tune `detent_phase` / `detent_nub_proud` before committing to a big box. --- ## 🖨️ Print settings & tips - **Material:** PLA is great; **PETG** is tougher for the hinge. - **Layer height:** 0.20 mm. **Supports:** ❌ none needed — everything opens upward. - **Orientation:** print the **tray on its floor**, the **lid on its rim / top-face-down** (the slicer plates them correctly from the exported files). - **Two-colour lid:** assign the text/design region a second filament in the AMS (use the **3MF**). - **Vial fit:** `vial_clearance` controls the radial gap; `vial_z_clearance` is the air gap above a vial so the lid clears a crimp/flip cap. - **Hinge stringing/snapping at layer lines?** Slow the top layers, raise min-layer-time to ~10 s, or bump temp +5 °C. --- ## 📦 What’s included - The **parametric model** (`.scad`) — the whole project, fully customizable on MakerWorld. - A set of **ready-to-print example STLs** (various grids). - The built-in **lid designs** (molecule / helix / honeycomb) and the optional logo. --- ## ❤️ About / License Designed from scratch by **Keaton Hoskins** — MakerWorld **@thehoskins**. 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: 32-slot Round Kumihimo disc for round bracelets This is a beginner friendly round Kumihimo disc to make round bracelets using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The disc has 32 marked notches to hold the strings in place and a rounded circle slot in the center for the weaving pattern to form. The notches are labelled 1-32 and the notes are marked every 8th slot with a large dot to indicate starting points for common 8-string weaves (at 8, 16, 24 and 32), as well as every 4th slot in between for 16-string weaves with a smaller circle (at 4, 12, 20 and 28). The labels are printed flat on the bed, so the disc is rotated upside down. If using an AMS, the labels are pre-colored and will be printed using a color for the disc and a second for the labels and markings. Without an AMS, the labels will still be visible through the trick of the labels being recessed by one layer height (0.2mm), this embeds the outline of the labels even without color as shown below. If desired, you could trace the etching using a permanent marker after the print. Instructions No assembly is required for the print. Simply print it, get some strings of silk, yarn or rope and you're ready to go. Patterns and instructions on how to use a Kumihimo disc to make rope/bracelets can be found online with several websites dedicated to it and many instructional videos. Therefore, I created this model which fits on the side of a BambuLab P1S or X1C. 💡Features: almost everything is 3D printable, needs only 3 M4x10 screws (even those are optional) keyed dovetail connection between the boards for strong fit significant clearance between the board and printers side panel + TPU spacers to prevent scratching mounted using printed hooks on a stock printer setup rigid and universal The SKADIS itself was generated from the parametric model by user @Line Arc Line from printables ( Parametric SKADIS Board Generator ). Kudos to the designer! Dimensions of the final SKADIS: 32 x 42 x 5.3 mm Most parts can be printed out of PLA but the mounting hooks need to be printed out of PETG, ASA or another less brittle material than PLA . The reason is, that those parts need to be flexed quite a lot to snap into place during mounting. 📜Part list and filaments: You will need the following printed parts. All are present in the submitted print profile and split into plates ( see below ). 4x SKADIS plates labelled 1-4 - PLA or any other material 6x spacers with three pins - PLA or any other material 3x spacers with a M4 hole - PLA or any other material 3x thin washers with a M4 hole (can be replaced by metal washers as well) - PLA or any other material 9x spacer caps - TPU (optional) 2x top mounting brackets - PETG, ASA or other non-brittle material ( PLA won’t work! ) 2x bottom mounting brackets - PETG, ASA or other non-brittle material ( PLA won’t work! ) Non-printed parts 3x M4x10 screws 🖨️ Print instructions: Before you print all the pieces consider printing the TEST model first (see print profile). It's a quick 20 min to check if the settings fit your printer tolerances and setup. The provided print profiles have all settings dialed in and are ready to print (Bambu Handy App friendly). Just print each plate once and you should have everything you need: Plates 1-4 (PLA, ~350g total, 2h30min each): SKADIS parts labeled 1-4. Plate 5 (PLA, ~7g, 22 min): 6x stand-offs with pins, 3x normal standoffs and 3x spacers Plate 6 (TPU, ~4g, 22 min): 9x TPU caps for the stand-offs Plate 7 (PETG/ASA, ~12g, 30 min): 3x top and 3x bottom mounting hooks ( only two needed each, the other ones are spare ) 🔩 Assembly: A picture-assisted assembly and mounting guide is provided in the description. I strongly recommend to use that. You will find the text-based instruction below. Depending on the tolerances of your printer, the SKADIS pieces may go together either quite tight or be a little bit loose. I dialed the tolerances in for my P1S and the pieces grab onto each other quite well. Glue is not required for the assembly but is strongly recommended to prevent the whole thing from disassembling if you plan to hang something heavy from it. DO NOT use cyanoacrylate-based superglue especially if you printed the parts out of black (or dark) plastic. In my experience the glue emits some kind of vapour while drying which stains the plastic white. Instead, use a little bit of dedicated PLA glue or two-component resin glue. If the pieces go in quite tight you may use a rubber hammer to jam the pieces together which would probably hold quite well even without glue. Place piece 1 on a flat surface with the number 1 facing upward Hold piece 2 with the marking facing the top and slide into piece 1 from the top Repeat steps 1 and 2 for pieces 3 and 4 respectively Connect all pieces together by sliding the 1-2 piece into the 3-4 piece Insert the spacers with 3 legs into respective holes on the back of the board. The use of glue is advised if you are certain that you assembled the pieces right. Place the small spacers at the indicated spots at the front of the board. Insert the M4x?? screw from the front through the spacer and through the SKADIS hole. Screw in the remaining long spacers onto the M4 screws Cover all spacers with the TPU caps by inserting them into the respective holes 🪜Mounting: Remove the top glass of your P1S or X1C printer Hold the top mounting bracket with the SKADIS hook facing to the left. Flex the bracket and slide the right hand latch onto the frame where the glass sits on top. Straighten the left side of the bracket so it snaps into place. Repeat the same process for the other top mounting bracket Hang the assembled SKADIS onto the top brackets as indicated. Insert the bottom brackets into the indicated holes. Flex the right side of the bracket so it passes the bottom edge of the printer chassis and snaps into place. Repeat for the second bracket Now you are done and ready to go! Have fun! If you encounter any issues, feel free to comment or write me a DM, maybe I'll be able to help you. Post your makes, I'm curious how yours will look like ;) Cheers and all the best!😉 Fun fact: I finished the project in 2024 and it has been mounted on my P1S since without any issues. I just now finally found the time to document and release it properly. I hope you find it useful ;)

🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.
