I've always had a soft spot for the SKÅDIS pegboard system — cheap, endlessly flexible, and there's an accessory for pretty much everything. But there was one thing I could never find for it: a version of one of my favorite pieces of design history, an iconic modular storage unit from the late 1960s, originally made as a single molded block of compartments and hooks. You can actually buy the original — it's a single molded block holding all the compartments at once — but it's pricey and pretty bulky for what is, at the end of the day, a desk organizer. So I decided to reinterpret it for the SKÅDIS ecosystem instead: I redesigned the whole thing from scratch as a set of separate, 3D-printable modules, each with its own hook built directly into the print, so they clip straight onto a vertical 37×56 SKÅDIS panel. The result is a family of 13 individual modules . Arrange them close together in the original grid layout and you get a look that's a clear nod to the source of inspiration — or spread them out, mix them with other SKÅDIS accessories, or use just a handful of them, however suits your desk and your workflow. Since each piece hangs independently, you're never locked into one fixed configuration the way you would be with a single molded block! You can use PLA or PETG (I actually used Pla Tough). Some modules need supports, but they're minimal and pop off cleanly with no visible marks afterward, because it's all internal. Feel free to make it colourful by printing the models in different colors, or to repaint the pegboard and make it all the same color, to remind the original vintage piece! A fully 3D-printed folding wall shelf that tucks flat against the wall when not in use and deploys a load-bearing support arm when you need it — practical, space-saving, and finished with a honeycomb underside for style. -- Why I made this - Most wall shelves are permanent fixtures. I wanted something that earns its space — a shelf that disappears when you don't need it and holds its own when you do. This design is 100% 3D printed (minus the wall screws and anchors you'll source locally) and built around a real folding mechanism rather than a novelty hinge. -- What it is - The shelf folds on a set of printed hinge knuckles: fold it up and it sits flush against the wall, fold it down and a pivoting support arm locks it into a horizontal position capable of handling real everyday loads. The underside of the shelf panel features a honeycomb pattern — so the face you see when it's folded up looks intentional, not bare plastic. All the structural work is done by the shelf panel, the support arm, and the hinge knuckles. The only hardware you need are wall screws and anchors appropriate for your wall type. -- Design details **Folding hinge knuckles** — printed-in geometry, no metal hardware at the pivot **Pivoting support arm** — braces the shelf against downward load when deployed **Honeycomb underside** — decorative and visible when the shelf is stowed -- How to print - Print in PLA+ for a lightweight indoor shelf or PETG if you want better humidity and temperature resistance. Either material works well here. ORIENTATION MATTERS, ALWAYS ORIENT IN A WAY WHERE LOADS WONT SHEAR THE Z LAYERING OF THE PRINT. - **Shelf panel** — lay flat on the bed, largest face down. - **Support arm** — lay flat on face so layer lines run along the arm's length; this puts the strongest layer orientation against bending loads, which is exactly where you need it. - **Hinge knuckles** — This is the trickier one, check overhanging geometry in your slicer before printing; orientation matters. - **20-30% infill** on all structural parts and many walls 4-5 (support arm, hinge knuckles, and cradle). ### Tips - Run a test fit of the hinge knuckles before final assembly — tolerances can vary slightly between printers; a quick pass with a small file cleans things up in seconds. - When mounting to drywall, use wall anchors rated for at least the load you plan to put on the shelf — the print will hold, so make sure the wall fastening matches. - PETG is the better choice for garages, laundry rooms, or anywhere with temperature swings or moisture. ### Assembly / Instructions 1. Print all parts: shelf panel, support arm, hinge knuckles/wall brackets and cradle. Check orientation notes before slicing. 2. Dry-fit the wall bracket onto the shelf panel. Verify smooth pivot motion; lightly sand or file any tight spots. 3. Attach the wall brackets shelf panel and place against the wall, level it out and mark the holes for each wall bracket. 4. Drill out marked holes and install anchors. 5. description: Overview A customizable Skadis holder for round stuff, where you set the diameter and it does the rest. It hangs a row of round cups on an IKEA Skadis pegboard and holds just about anything cylindrical: glue sticks, markers, highlighters, screwdriver handles, small bottles, hobby paints, spray cans and WD-40. You really only set two things, the object diameter and how many cups you want. From there the customizer sizes the cups, packs them in next to each other and puts a Skadis hook behind each one at the nearest real slot. Heavy or wide cups get a second peg on their own so they can't tip out, and everything else is optional. Measure the object itself and type that number in, the model adds the fit gap for you so you're not left guessing tolerances (the optional floor hole works the same way). One thing worth doing before a big run: print a single cup first. Printer tolerances vary, so even if you know yours it pays to slice one cup at your diameter and check the object actually drops in before you print a whole row. A two-minute test is a lot cheaper than redoing a full board that came out a hair too tight. If the fit is off, nudge the Clearance a little (0.2 is snug, 0.3 is the default, 0.4 is looser) and reprint that one cup. Set the diameter — the customizer sizes every cup to fit. Highlights Diameter 10 to 80 mm, 1 to 12 cups in a row. Mixed sizes in the same row, so a wide can sits happily next to slim glue sticks. Heavy cups get a double peg automatically, and there's a thin-profile mode for short rows. Optional hole through the floor to pass a tool or screwdriver through. Native Skadis hook that fits both real Skadis (5 mm) and printed boards. Dimensions. The default 3 cup, 21 mm row comes out around 100 x 35 x 30 mm. Yours will depend on the diameter and count you choose. Compatibility. IKEA Skadis and Skadis-compatible printed pegboards (5x15 mm slots on a 40 mm grid). Cylinders up to 80 mm outside diameter. Printing. Print it standing up, with the panel flat on the bed and the cups opening upward. Any material is fine (PLA, PETG, ABS/ASA, PC). PETG is a solid all-rounder and PLA works perfectly well. Use a 0.4 or 0.6 mm nozzle and skip 0.8, which softens the detail and the fit. A bit of support on the rear pegs, none under the cups. Full customizer guide Every setting, if you want to fine-tune. What the settings control — diameter, clearance, wall, cup height, floor. Setting Default What it does Object diameter 21 mm The object's exact body diameter, 10–80 mm (any decimal). Measure it — the model adds the fit gap for you (set by Clearance). Count 3 Number of cups in the row, 1–12. Cup height 30 mm How far the cup wraps the object, 5–100 mm. Taller = steadier for tall/heavy items. Warns if a cup is too short for its diameter. Per-cup size off (0) Optional: give one cup its own diameter and/or height (0 = use the main size). Sits right under the main size. Pegs per cup auto (0) 0 = auto: 1 peg for light items, 2 for heavy/large. Or force 1–3. Heavy threshold 40 mm A cup at/above this diameter auto-gets a second peg. Single peg row off Thin-profile mode — forces all pegs into one row for the lowest backboard (best for short, light items). Clearance 0.3 mm The fit gap added to the diameter — applied to both the cup bore and the floor hole (a 30 mm object → a 30.3 mm bore). Measure exact and let the model add it. 0.3 (default) suits most prints — snug but slides in; 0.2 is very snug (only if you trust your printer); 0.4 plays it safe (looser). Wall 2.4 mm Cup wall thickness. Gap between cups 4 mm Spacing between neighbouring cups. Floor thickness 2 mm Every cup has a closed floor; this sets it. Floor hole 0 (off) The exact diameter of a tool/device to pass through every cup's floor (or to drain) — the model adds the same clearance as the cup. Any decimal. Per-cup override available. Plate thickness / margin / radius 3 / 5 / 7 mm Back panel: thickness, border around the cups, corner rounding. Board thickness 5 mm The Skadis board the pocket fits, 4–7 mm (standard Skadis is 5). Setup tips Measure exact, leave the tolerance to the model. Enter the object's true diameter, and if you use the floor hole, the true diameter of whatever goes through it. The model adds the Clearance to both, so you don't need to pad your own measurement. 0.3 (the default) suits most prints, snug but it still slides in. 0.2 is very snug, only worth it if you trust your printer. 0.4 plays it safe. One cup, two pegs. A single cup on one peg sits snug on the board, but with only one peg it can rotate a touch and a knock can twist it. For a steady single holder, set Pegs per cup to 2 so the two stacked pegs lock the rotation. (Auto already does this for heavy cups, and a row of three or more braces itself anyway.) Heavy or tall items. Keep it on auto (or force 2 pegs) and use a taller cup. Don't put a full can in single peg row mode, because it really wants the double peg. Thin profile. Turn on Single peg row for short items, like a tray of stubby markers, to get the lowest backboard possible. The pegs snap to the 40 mm Skadis grid, so a peg can sit slightly off a cup's centre and very close cups will share a peg. That's fine for light rows. Board grip. The default 5 mm board thickness fits standard Skadis. Drop it a little for a firmer grip on a thinner or printed board. How the pegs work Each cup gets a native Skadis hook that fills a 5x15 slot and catches behind the board. Heavy or wide cups (at or above the heavy threshold) automatically get a second peg stacked one slot below the first , a vertical pair that stops a full can from tipping out. Slim cups keep a single hook. Either way, every peg drops into a real slot at the same time. Turning on Single peg row overrides all of that and forces one thin row. The native hook catches behind the board. Hooks straight onto an IKEA Skadis board. Mixed sizes in one row Every cup uses the main diameter unless you give it one of its own. Set just the cup you want bigger and a wide can will still pack in tight next to a slim glue stick, with every hook landing in a real slot. The panel sizes itself to whatever row you build. Any size in one row — a fat can beside slim cups. anno_mixed.png Floor holes (optional) Cups are closed by default. You can open a hole through the floor, on every cup or just one, for a few reasons: to pass a screwdriver or tool through (handle in the cup, shaft poking out the bottom), to let a long object stick out the bottom, or to push something up from below to pop it out. Measure the exact diameter of whatever goes through and the model adds the same fit gap as the cup (the hole comes out as your diameter plus clearance), so it's a clean, snug pass-through. Print settings Setting Value Material Any. PLA, PETG, ABS/ASA or PC. PETG is a great everyday pick (fine indoors too) and PLA is perfectly fine. There's no real material limit here. The pricier engineering filaments just add heat and strength you probably don't need. Nozzle 0.4 or 0.6 mm (both print cleanly). description: Symmetric Pattern Generator Perfect for panels & drawer faces. I recently designed 3D printed drawers with Kumiko and Hexagon faces, and all of the generator I could find online never generator what I needed: Controllable frame dimensions / thickness Controllable pattern size or quantity to fill the frame in a perfectly symmetric way Controllable border padding Editable notch (optional) This script is perfect for anyone looking for an easy and quick way to generate patterns or panels. Very useful for laser cutting or CAD as well. HOW TO USE Panel Size - Thickness Width & Height: control the size of the panel in mm Thickness: control the thickness of your frame Notch Add notch: toggle the notch function on/off Notch width / height: control the size of you notch Notch radius: Control the roundness of your notch ends Notch border: control the border thickness around your notch Border padding Border top / right / bottom / left: control the thickness of the padding around your frame Pattern style Pattern style: Select between 16 pattern styles (more to come) Size mode: this is the critical modifier: by size: the frame will be filled with repetitive patterns of the selected size. Very useful when making different panels where you want the pattern to stay consistent on different frame sizes. by count: the frame will be filled with exactly the selected “n patterns” number of the pattern. IF you select 7 “n patterns”, the frame will be filled with 7 patterns, the script will calculate the pattern size to make it fit exactly the width (working on making it height / width selectable). Use this if you want a perfectly symmetric pattern where left and right ends are identical (imagine a mirror in the middle of the frame). Pattern size: select the size of each pattern in mm (only when size mode is by size ) n patterns: select the exact amount of patterns to fill the frame width (only when size mode is by count ) Branch thickness: control the thickness of your patterns. For 3d printing, avoid going under 1.5mm Inner Thickness: control the thickness of inner branches (only currently used for the Boxes patterns) Export to SVG / DXF or more formats I designed this script to firstly export to DXF to work with Fusion360 and my laser cutting software. description: ## Short Description Generate round spacers, rectangular shims, or tall standoffs with custom dimensions, hole sizes, clearances, and copy count. ## Full Description This parametric generator creates simple workshop spacing parts for 3D printers, enclosures, jigs, furniture fixes, craft builds, mounting jobs, and everyday repairs. Choose between a round spacer/washer, a rectangular shim plate, or a taller cylindrical standoff, then set the exact dimensions you need. The default model prints a small support-free batch of round spacers with central clearance holes and no unnecessary side notch. Switch to rectangular shim mode for flat plates with 0-4 mounting holes, or tall standoff mode for longer cylindrical stand-offs. A clearance parameter lets you slightly oversize holes for real-world FDM fit, and the copy count parameter lets you print one part or a small set at once. Optional finishing controls include chamfered spacer edges, engraved or raised top labels, and a countersunk top variant for flush-fit screw applications. This is intended as a practical custom-fit utility print. It is not a certified precision, load-rated, or high-temperature hardware replacement. For functional assemblies, print one test piece first and adjust the clearance for your printer, filament, and screw/bolt size. ## Customization Notes - Use `part_style` to choose `round_spacer` , `rectangular_shim` , or `tall_standoff` . - Use `copy_count` and `copy_gap` to print one part or a small batch. - For round spacers, tune `outer_diameter` , `inner_diameter` , and `spacer_height` . - For tall standoffs, tune `outer_diameter` , `standoff_height` , and `standoff_hole_diameter` . - For rectangular shims, tune `shim_length` , `shim_width` , `shim_thickness` , `hole_count` , `shim_hole_diameter` , and `hole_spacing` . - Use `clearance_extra` to add real-world hole clearance. Start around 0.20 mm for PLA, then test and adjust. - Use `chamfer_enabled` and `chamfer_size` to soften round spacer/standoff edges. - Use `label_enabled` , `label_style` , and `label_text` for engraved or raised top labels such as `M4 5mm` . - Use `countersink_enabled` , `countersink_diameter` , and `countersink_depth` for a countersunk top variant. - `edge_marker_notch` is off by default; enable only if you want a visible orientation/counting notch.

🌬️ Tronic TLK 7000 C2 Zwei-Schlauch-Adapter | Massiver Effizienz-Boost! 🚀Hole das absolute Maximum aus deinem Tronic TLK 7000 C2 (Lidl Hausmarke) oder baugleichen mobilen Klimageräten! Dieses smarte, zweiteilige Upgrade verwandelt deine ineffiziente Einschlauch-Klimaanlage in ein hocheffizientes Zwei-Schlauch-System . Das Ergebnis: Der Raum wird deutlich schneller kalt, das Gerät verbraucht weniger Strom und du kannst spürbar größere Flächen kühlen. 💡 Warum ist dieses Design ein Gamechanger? (Die Physik dahinter) Das Problem im Originalzustand (Einschlauch): Mobile Klimageräte nutzen die mühsam gekühlte Raumluft, um den heißen Kompressor im Inneren zu kühlen, und blasen diese Luft durch den originalen Abluftschlauch nach draußen. Dadurch entsteht in der Wohnung ein massiver Unterdruck . Die Folge: Knallheiße Sommerluft (30°C+) wird permanent durch jede Türritze, jedes Schlüsselloch und jede Fensterdichtung von draußen wieder in die Wohnung gesaugt. Ein endloser, extrem ineffizienter Kampf! Die Lösung mit diesem Adapter (Zwei-Schlauch): Dieser zweiteilige Aufsatz kapselt das untere Ansauggitter (den Heißluft-Kreislauf des Kompressors) komplett ab. Über den neuen, zweiten Schlauch (Zuluft) saugt das Gerät die Luft zur Kühlung der Technik direkt von draußen an. Über den originalen Schlauch wird sie wieder nach draußen geblasen. Der Clou: In deiner Wohnung entsteht kein Unterdruck mehr! Die Raumluft wird im Inneren nur noch im Kreis gesaugt, eiskalt gefiltert und wieder abgegeben. Die Kälte bleibt im Raum, die Hitze bleibt draußen. Die Effizienz steigt um bis zu 50%! 🔩 Benötigtes Zusatzmaterial (BOM) Für den Zusammenbau und die Montage benötigst du folgendes Zubehör: 8x M3 Einschmelzgewinde (Gewindeeinsätze / Heat-Set Inserts, z.B. Ruthex) 8x M3 Zylinderkopfschrauben (M3x10mm oder M3x12mm sind ideal) Mindestens 6x Kabelbinder (um den Basisrahmen am Gitter der Klimaanlage zu fixieren) 1x Zusätzlicher flexibler Schlauch (Abluft-/Zuluftschlauch, Durchmesser passend zum gedruckten Stutzen wählen) (Zudem vielleicht ein Abdichtband für Fenster - bekommt man in jedem Baumarkt) Disclaimer: Notfalls lassen sich die zwei Teile ebenfalls mit dünnen Kabelbindern zusammenfügen OHNE die Einschmelzgewinde (ist so nur eleganter) 🛠️ Montageanleitung Das clevere, zweiteilige Design macht die Installation und spätere Wartung kinderleicht: Gewinde vorbereiten: Schmelze die 8x M3 Gewindeeinsätze mit einem Lötkolben vorsichtig in die dafür vorgesehenen Löcher des flachen Montagerahmens . Rahmen fixieren: Setze den Montagerahmen auf das untere Gitter der Klimaanlage. Nutze mindestens 6 Kabelbinder , um den Rahmen bombenfest am Kunststoffgitter zu verzurren (siehe Projektbild). Knipse die Enden der Kabelbinder sauber ab. Trichter aufschrauben: Setze den großen Trichteraufsatz auf den Rahmen und verschraube ihn mit den 8x M3 Schrauben. Vorteil: Für Filterreinigungen oder den Wintertransport kannst du den Trichter jederzeit abschrauben, ohne die Kabelbinder zu beschädigen! Schlauch anschließen: Stecke deinen neuen Zuluftschlauch auf den Stutzen und führe ihn (zusammen mit dem originalen Abluftschlauch) nach draußen – am besten durch eine feste Rollladen- oder Fensterblende. 🖨️ Empfohlene Druckeinstellungen (Print Settings) Material: PETG (ABS oder ASA) absolut empfohlen! Da die Schläuche und die Rückseite des Klimageräts im Hochsommer sehr warm werden können, ist normales PLA nicht hitzebeständig genug und könnte sich mit der Zeit verformen. Wände / Peripherie (Walls): Mindestens 3 bis 4 Wandlinien . Das Bauteil muss absolut luftdicht sein, damit keine Falschluft gezogen wird. Infill: 20% - 25% (Gyroid oder Grid) Support: Empfohlen! An open-source clamshell holder generator for openGrid , using the openConnect system. The holder can be used to mount objects either under a desk, often in combination with the Underware system, or on a wall. A common use case is holding power strips, but the dimensions and openings can be adjusted for a wide range of object shapes. Several example .stl files are included, with the parameters used to generate them in the file names. Customization guide: Measure the item. Set "item_width" , "item_height" , and "item_depth" . Adjust "item_corner_rounding" based on the item's shape. Add a little clearance if you want the item to slide in easily. For a heavy item, you may want to increase "holder_thickness" to make the holder sturdier. Set "holder_slot_position" . "Top" makes the item face forward when mounted on a wall, or downward when mounted under a desk. You can also choose "Front", which makes the item face sideways when mounted under a desk. Adjust the front opening. Use "front_opening_side_margin" and "front_opening_end_margin" . Larger margins create a smaller front opening, which may interfere with use, such as blocking the outlets of a power strip. Adjust the side openings. Use the "side_opening_x_margin" parameters. The side opening can be enabled on one side, both sides, or disabled completely. The position and size of the opening are highly customizable. Set "holder_slot_column_limit" . This value defaults to the minimum of 1, which saves filament and helps with heat dissipation. Increase it if you want the holder to cover more of the item. Set "slot_slide_direction" . "Left" and "Right" are usually used for under-desk mounting, while "Up" and "Down" are usually used for wall mounting. Choose the direction that lets the holder slide onto the openConnect slots from the accessible side. "generate_holder_part" : "Both" shows a good preview of the result, so it is recommended during customization. The "Left" and "Right" options allow different parameters for each part and automatically orient the model for 3D printing, which is convenient when exporting the result. The model is open-source under the CC-BY-SA license. Like all the OpenSCAD models I've designed for openGrid, it can be found in this GitHub repository . Feel free to use the code; feedback and suggestions are welcome.

description: Press the Customize button to customize! A fully parametric open-top mesh basket: pick a rectangle or ellipse boundary, a solid border frame, and one of five interior grid patterns. Add an optional snap-fit lid, printed as a separate piece, that clicks onto the basket with a continuous printable ridge/groove around the whole rim. Looking for a flat mesh panel or a bowed strainer/colander instead? Those are separate listings: Parametric Mesh Panel Generator and Parametric Mesh Strainer Generator . Key Features Rectangle or ellipse boundary: set overall width and depth (or diameter, for a circle) directly Five grid patterns: square, diagonal (45 degree square), hexagonal honeycomb, triangular, and staggered circular holes; every pattern tessellates edge to edge with a uniform strut width between holes Open-top basket: solid bottom panel plus mesh side walls; 4 flat walls for a rectangle, one continuous wrapped curved wall for an ellipse Solid bottom / solid sides toggles: make the bottom panel or the side walls solid (no mesh) independently of each other Snap-fit lid: an optional separate piece (switch the Customizer's view to lid) with a skirt that slides inside the basket opening and clicks into place Solid lid top toggle: make the lid's top plate solid instead of meshed 3D-printable snap ridge: the ridge/groove is a single continuous triangular bead wrapped around the entire rim, tapered to a self-supporting 45 degree slope so it prints with no supports on either the basket or the lid Auto-sized holes and struts: hole_size and strut_width default to 2.5x your nozzle diameter when left at 0, so a fresh copy prints cleanly without any tuning Pattern rotation: rotate the whole grid independently of the panel's default orientation Print Settings Setting Recommended Basket orientation Print flat, bottom panel down Lid orientation view = "lid" already outputs it flipped, plate-down on the bed Supports Not required for either piece Perimeters 2-3 Infill 15-20% Material PLA or PETG Download the optimized print profile from this page, delete the sample models off the plate, and import your STL into it. How to Use Outer Shape: set shape to rectangle or ellipse, then outer_x, outer_y, and thickness. Border: set border_width; 0 removes it entirely. Basket: set basket_height for the side wall height. Use basket_solid_bottom or basket_solid_sides if you want part of the basket solid instead of meshed. Lid (optional): turn on lid_enable, set lid_skirt_height and lid_fit_clearance to match your basket opening, and leave lid_notches_enable on for the snap fit. Switch view to lid and re-export to get the separate lid STL. Pick a pattern: choose pattern and, if you want a specific look, set hole_size and strut_width; leave both at 0 to auto-size from nozzle_diameter. Export the STL (once for view = "model", once more for view = "lid" if you enabled the lid), delete the sample models off the plate, and import your STLs into it. Customization Use the MakerWorld Customizer. All parameters are grouped and annotated. View - view: model renders the basket, lid renders the separate lid piece (only produces geometry when lid_enable is also on) Outer Shape - shape: rect for a rectangle, ellipse for an ellipse or circle - outer_x: overall width, X axis (mm) - outer_y: overall depth, Y axis (mm) - thickness: panel / wall material thickness (mm) Border Frame - border_width: solid border frame width around every face (mm); 0 = no border Basket - basket_height: height of the side wall(s), measured up from the top of the bottom panel (mm) - basket_solid_bottom: make the bottom panel solid instead of meshed - basket_solid_sides: make the side wall(s) solid instead of meshed Lid - lid_enable: add a snap-fit lid - lid_solid_top: make the lid's top plate solid instead of meshed - lid_skirt_height: depth the lid's skirt reaches down inside the basket opening (mm) - lid_fit_clearance: gap between the skirt and the inside of the basket walls, per side (mm) - lid_notches_enable: add the continuous snap ridge/groove around the rim - lid_notch_depth: how far the ridge/groove projects past the nominal skirt/wall surface (mm) - lid_notch_band: vertical height of the ridge/groove's tapered profile (mm); must be at least 2x lid_notch_depth for a printable 45 degree slope - lid_notch_offset: distance from the top of the wall/skirt down to the center of the ridge/groove (mm) Mesh Pattern - pattern: square, diagonal, hex, triangle, or circle - hole_size: hole size (mm); flat-to-flat, edge length, or diameter depending on pattern; 0 = auto (2.5x nozzle diameter) - strut_width: wall width between holes (mm); 0 = auto (2.5x nozzle diameter) - pattern_rotation: extra rotation applied to the whole pattern (degrees) Printer - nozzle_diameter: drives the auto strut/hole sizing and minimum-feature warnings (mm) Pattern Notes Every pattern is built as a continuous solid lattice rather than a punch-through grid of disconnected holes, so the remaining material always stays one connected piece. Triangular and circular holes sit on the same tightly-packed triangular lattice as the hex pattern, so every hole is equidistant from its six neighbors and the gap between any two adjacent holes is a uniform strut width. Snap-Fit Lid Notes The lid's skirt slides inside the basket's top opening, and a continuous triangular ridge on the skirt cams past the basket wall until it seats into a matching groove cut into the wall, holding the lid down with a light friction snap. Both the ridge and the groove taper at a 45 degree slope (never more), so the whole feature prints cleanly with no supports on either piece. If the fit feels too tight or too loose, adjust lid_fit_clearance; if the snap feels weak, try increasing lid_notch_depth a little (keeping lid_notch_band at least 2x that value). Sizing Tips If holes print closed or clogged, increase hole_size well above 2.5x your nozzle diameter. If struts look flimsy or go missing, increase strut_width; anything thinner than 2.5x your nozzle diameter will not print as designed.

description: ⚠️ Measure your power strip before printing! This is a parametric model. Do NOT print it using the default dimensions unless your power strip matches them. Before generating the model, carefully measure your power strip and enter its dimensions. 1. Add extra length The length of the enclosure should be slightly longer than the actual power strip. Since the power strip is inserted from the top at an angle, it needs some extra clearance during installation. If the enclosure is exactly the same length as the power strip, inserting it will be difficult or even impossible. I recommend adding at least 5 mm (typically 5–8 mm) to the measured length to ensure easy installation. Example: Measured power strip length: 250 mm Enclosure length: 255–258 mm The width and height can remain much closer to the actual dimensions, but the length should always include this additional clearance. 2. Check the cable exit position Before printing, check the distance between the top surface of the power strip and the top of the cable exit (see reference image). This check is important because the power strip is inserted from above. If the cable exits too close to the top of the power strip and your desk is thick, the cable may interfere with the underside of the tabletop during installation. You can verify the required height using this rule: Measure the distance between the top of the power strip and the top of the cable exit . Subtract your desk thickness . Subtract 6 mm (design clearance already accounted for in the model) . Available clearance = (top-to-cable-exit distance) − desk thickness − 6 mm If the result is positive or zero , the default height is sufficient. If the result is negative , increase the model height by that amount (absolute value). Example Top to cable exit: 20 mm Desk thickness: 25 mm Result: 20 − 25 − 6 = −11 mm → Increase height by 11 mm 3. Printing instructions This is a parametric model , meaning you only need to adjust three main values to fit your power strip: Length Width Height Once these values are set, the model will automatically adapt to your specific power strip dimensions. Two-part design The model is split into two separate parts : Top part Bottom part Both parts must be generated using the exact same dimensions to ensure a proper fit. Orientation for printing After exporting the models: The bottom part can be printed as-is. The top part must be rotated 180° before printing to ensure correct orientation and printability + This is necessary due to the geometry of the design. Assembly After printing, the bottom part must be permanently glued to the top part . Once glued, the two parts form a single rigid enclosure ready for installation into the desk. Important note This model was created in Fusion 360 , and while it is fully functional and parametric, this also means there are some design limitations related to the way parameters and exported bodies behave . For this reason, always double-check the exported geometry before slicing. If you follow the steps above, the model should print and assemble without issues. i may try to remodel this in open scad in the future About this model Turn any standard power strip into a clean, recessed desk power outlet. Instead of buying an expensive built-in desk power strip, this parametric model lets you install a regular power strip directly into your desk. Simply customize the dimensions to fit your own power strip, print the enclosure, cut an opening in the tabletop, and press-fit the insert into place. Why I designed this Most recessed desk power strips available online are: expensive available in only a few sizes often made by unknown brands with questionable quality Instead, I bought a high-quality standard power strip from a trusted manufacturer and designed this enclosure to create the same built-in look. The result is: lower cost better electrical quality freedom to choose the power strip you trust a clean and professional-looking installation If you build one, I'd love to see your Make!

description: 64-Slot Large Round Kumihimo disc for round bracelets This is a large round Kumihimo disc featuring 64 slots for strings to make complex high string-count round bracelets with up to 40 strings, using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. A 64-slot Kumihimo disc is typically used for weaves with more than 16 strings at a time as the complexity of keeping track of the strings increases if they are too densely packed together. The below picture shows the disc with a 24-string pattern using 12 different colors at the same time to create the large pattern. The disc has 64 marked notches to hold the strings in place and allowing to easily make high string-count weaves through the rounded circle slot in the center for the Kumihimo weaving pattern to form. The notches are labelled 1-64 and additionally the notches are marked every 16th slot with a large dot to indicate starting points for 8-string weaves (at16, 32, 48 and 64), as well as every 8th slot in between for 16-string weaves with a smaller circle (at 8,24, 40 and 56), as well as every 4th slot in between the 16- and 8-slot markers for 32-string weaves with a small diamond dot (at 4, 12, 20, 28, 36, 44, 52 and 60). The labels are printed flat on the bed, so the disc is rotated upside down. If using an AMS, the labels are pre-colored and will be printed using a color for the disc and a second for the labels and markings. Without an AMS, the labels will still be visible through the trick of the labels being recessed by one layer height (0.2mm), this embeds the outline of the labels even without color as shown below. If desired, you could trace the etching using a permanent marker after the print. Instructions No assembly is required for the print. Simply print it, get some strings of silk, yarn or rope and you're ready to go. I recommend a string diameter of up to 2mm in thickness (pictured above are a mix of 1mm an 2mm strings). Patterns and instructions on how to use a Kumihimo disc to make rope/bracelets can be found online with several websites dedicated to it and many instructional videos. Weighted Bobbins for Kumihimo braiding My latest addition to the series is a set of Weighted Bobbin for Kumihimo braiding which make it easier to make neat braids by taking the pressure off my hands and instead the weight can do the tension holding on the center strand of the braid. description: Apothecary Cabinet Generator V1.1 This is a fully parametric apothecary cabinet generator that lets you make a custom little drawer cabinet without having to model the whole thing from scratch every time. You choose the cabinet size, drawer size, number of rows, number of columns, wall thickness, clearances, top cap, base style, drawer face details, and a bunch of other options. The generator builds the cabinet around the drawer size you choose, then also generates one matching drawer that fits that cabinet. This version uses one uniform drawer size across the whole cabinet. That means every opening is the same size, and the tool generates one matching drawer that you can duplicate in your slicer. So if you make a 4x3 cabinet, you print one cabinet and duplicate the drawer 12 times. Simple, clean, and way less annoying than generating a pile of separate drawer files for no reason. The cabinet is built around the drawer size you pick. Change the drawer width, height, or depth, and the whole cabinet recalculates around it. You can make tiny parts drawers, craft storage, dice drawers, bead organizers, mini hardware cabinets, display cabinets, or whatever other small nonsense needs organized. 🧰 Display / Export Modes Setting What It Does Both Shows the cabinet and one drawer side by side. Good for previewing the full setup. Cabinet Shows only the cabinet body. Use this when exporting the cabinet STL. Drawer Shows only the matching drawer. Use this when exporting the drawer STL. Fit Test Shows one drawer placed inside the cabinet so you can check the fit before printing everything. The Fit Test mode is useful before wasting filament on a big cabinet. You can choose which row and column the test drawer appears in and how far it is pulled out. 🗄️ Cabinet Grid Settings Setting What It Controls Columns How many drawer openings go across the cabinet. Rows How many drawer openings go up the cabinet. Drawer Width The outside width of the drawer body. The cabinet openings are calculated from this. Drawer Height The outside height of the drawer body. This controls the height of each opening. Drawer Depth The depth of the drawer body. This also controls how deep the cabinet needs to be. Drawer count is: Rows x Columns Examples: Cabinet Size Drawer Count 2x2 4 drawers 3x3 9 drawers 4x3 12 drawers 5x4 20 drawers 6x5 30 drawers You only need to export one drawer, then duplicate it in the slicer until you have the right amount. 📏 Clearance Settings Setting What It Does Fit Clearance XY Clearance around the drawer on the left, right, top, and bottom. This is what lets the drawer actually slide. Fit Clearance Depth Extra space behind the drawer so it does not bottom out against the back panel. Divider Thickness Thickness of the walls between drawer openings. Back Panel Turns the cabinet back panel on or off. Back Thickness Thickness of the back panel if enabled. Important part: Fit Clearance XY is per side. So if you set: Fit Clearance XY: 0.5 mm That gives the drawer: Side Clearance Left 0.5 mm Right 0.5 mm Top 0.5 mm Bottom 0.5 mm That means the actual cabinet opening becomes: Drawer Width + 1.0 mm Drawer Height + 1.0 mm Start with 0.5 mm for most FDM printers. If your printer is super dialed in, you can try less. If the drawers are tight, bump it up. Tiny drawers are tolerance nightmares (sometimes), because apparently plastic enjoys lying to us! 🏛️ Cabinet Style Settings Setting What It Controls Cabinet Front Frame Adds a raised frame around the front outside edge of the cabinet. Cabinet Frame Width How wide that front frame is. Cabinet Frame Projection How far the front frame sticks out from the cabinet face. Top Cap Turns the top cap on or off. Top Cap Thickness How thick the top cap is. Top Cap Side Overhang How far the top cap sticks out on the left and right sides. Top Cap Front Overhang How far the top cap sticks out over the front. Top Cap Back Overhang How far the top cap sticks out in the back. Set this to 0 for a flat back. Base Plinth Adds a raised front base piece under the cabinet. Base Plinth Height How tall the base plinth is. Base Plinth Projection How far the base plinth sticks out from the front. For a cabinet that sits flat against a wall, use: Top Cap Back Overhang: 0 That keeps the back clean instead of giving it a useless little roof spoiler. 🦶 Base Foot Styles Option What It Does No Feet No extra feet added. Clean flat cabinet. Four Block Feet Adds block feet at all four corners. Front Block Feet Adds feet only on the front. Good for a more decorative front-facing cabinet. Side Runners Adds long runner-style feet along the sides. Full Raised Base Adds one full solid raised base under the cabinet. Setting What It Controls Foot Width Width of each foot or runner. Foot Depth Depth of block feet. Foot Height How tall the feet or raised base are. 📦 Drawer Body Settings Setting What It Controls Drawer Wall Thickness Thickness of the drawer side walls. Drawer Bottom Thickness Thickness of the drawer floor. Drawer Front Thickness Thickness of the visible front face of the drawer. Drawer Front Overlap How much the drawer face overlaps the cabinet opening. Drawer Face Gap Gap between neighboring drawer fronts. Helps stop drawer faces from colliding. The drawer body is hollowed automatically. The front face is slightly larger than the drawer body so it covers the opening cleanly. The overlap is automatically limited so if you make a bunch of drawers side by side, the fronts do not crash into each other like badly parked shopping carts. 🎛️ Drawer Front Detail Switches Instead of a confusing preset menu, the drawer details are controlled with simple on/off switches. Switch What It Adds Use Raised Border Adds a raised rectangular border around the drawer face. Use Round Knob Adds a simple centered round knob. Use Bar Pull Adds a horizontal handle across the drawer front. Use Label Holder Adds a raised rectangular label holder. Use Card Catalog Face Adds a card-catalog style label frame and pull lip. Use Cup Pull Face Adds a wider raised pull plate style front. For the classic apothecary/card catalog look, I recommend: Setting Value Use Raised Border True Use Card Catalog Face True Use Round Knob False Use Bar Pull False Use Label Holder False Use Cup Pull Face False That gives it the old little-label-and-pull-lip look without turning the drawer into decorative soup. 🏷️ Raised Border Settings Setting What It Controls Raised Border Width Thickness of the raised border lines. Raised Border Raise How far the border sticks out from the drawer face. Raised Border Inset How far inward the border sits from the edge of the drawer front. Use this when you want the drawer face to look more finished and less like a plain cube pretending to have a personality. 🔘 Round Knob Settings Setting What It Controls Knob Diameter Size of the round knob. Knob Projection How far the knob sticks out. Knob Height Position Vertical position of the knob on the drawer front. Good for simple drawers or old cabinet-style fronts. 🧲 Bar Pull Settings Setting What It Controls Bar Pull Width Percent Width of the bar pull as a percentage of the drawer width. Bar Pull Diameter Thickness of the bar handle. Bar Pull Projection How far the handle sticks out from the drawer front. Bar Pull Height Position Vertical position of the bar handle. This makes the drawer look more modern or industrial. 📝 Label Holder Settings Setting What It Controls Label Width Percent Width of the label holder based on drawer width. Label Height Percent Height of the label holder based on drawer height. Label Frame Thickness Thickness of the label holder border. Label Raise How far the label holder sticks out. Label Height Position Vertical position of the label holder. Good for parts drawers, craft storage, bead storage, hardware sorting, and all the other tiny organized-chaos stuff. 🗂️ Card Catalog Face Settings Setting What It Controls Card Plate Raise How far the card catalog details stick out. Card Pull Lip Diameter Thickness of the little pull lip. Card Label Width Percent Width of the card label frame. Card Label Height Percent Height of the card label frame. Card Label Height Position Vertical position of the label frame. Card Pull Width Percent Width of the pull lip. Card Pull Height Position Vertical position of the pull lip. This is the best setting group for the classic apothecary look. It gives the drawer that old card-catalog vibe without needing actual metal hardware. 🥣 Cup Pull Face Settings Setting What It Controls Cup Pull Width Percent Width of the cup pull plate. Cup Pull Height Percent Height of the cup pull plate. Cup Pull Raise How far the cup pull plate sticks out. Cup Pull Height Position Vertical position of the cup pull. This gives the drawer a chunkier pull face. It works better on larger drawers. On tiny drawers, it can get crowded fast, because tiny drawers are dramatic. 🖨️ Printing Workflow Set your rows, columns, and drawer size. Set Fit Clearance XY to around 0.5 mm . Use Fit Test mode to check one drawer in the cabinet. Export the cabinet using Cabinet mode. Export the drawer using Drawer mode. Duplicate the drawer in your slicer. Example: Cabinet What To Print 4x3 cabinet 1 cabinet + 12 drawers 5x4 cabinet 1 cabinet + 20 drawers 6x5 cabinet 1 cabinet + 30 drawers ✅ Suggested First Test Setting Value Columns 2 Rows 2 Drawer Width 42 mm Drawer Height 28 mm Drawer Depth 55 mm Fit Clearance XY 0.5 mm Fit Clearance Depth 1.0 mm Divider Thickness 2.4 mm Drawer Wall Thickness 1.6 mm Drawer Bottom Thickness 1.8 mm Print a small 2x2 first before going huge. Once the fit is good, scale it up and go nuts. ⚠️ Current Limitation This version uses one drawer size for the whole cabinet. That means all openings are the same size. A future version may add different drawer sizes per row or multiple drawer types, but this one is meant to be clean, usable, and not an OpenSCAD crime scene with knobs.

description: Comprehensive Guide to the Pocket Mechanical Switch Clicker Fidget 🕹️ Welcome to the ultimate Pocket Mechanical Switch Clicker Fidget project page! This model is specifically engineered for people who love the crisp, tactile sensation of mechanical keyboard switches. It functions as a heavy-duty, portable fidget toy that fits easily into a pocket, backpack, or pencil case. Whether you are trying to stay focused during class, brainstorming your next big project, or just looking for a satisfying way to pass the time, this 3-piece model is the perfect quick print. Key Design Features 💡 100% Support-Free: The geometry of this model utilizes careful bridging angles. You can print the entire file completely flat without generating any waste material. Ultra-Low Filament Consumption: Weighing in at less than 7 grams, you can print dozens of these using leftover filament scraps from the end of your spools. High Interlocking Tolerances: The button caps are designed with a standard cross-stem socket that snugly grabs onto your switches without slipping off during rapid clicking. Technical Print Specifications 🖨️ This model has been sliced and thoroughly tested on Bambu Lab printers to ensure perfect execution. Below is the exact configuration data used during the testing phase. Slicer Parameter Recommended Value Functional Purpose Printer Profile Bambu Lab P1S / X1C Targets standard CoreXY motion systems. Print Bed Type Textured PEI Plate Hides layer lines on the bottom face and improves bed adhesion. Filament Material PLA Basic (Green) Offers rigidity and prevents shrinking or warping. Layer Height 0.24mm Draft Optimizes print time while retaining tight tolerances. Sparse Infill Density 15% Provides a lightweight but structurally sound core. Infill Pattern Grid Ensures equal strength across the X and Y axes. Supports DISABLED (NONE) Eliminates post-processing cleanup and saves material. Wall Loops 2 Layers Keeps outer shells strong enough to withstand heavy finger pressure. Component Dimensional Data 📐 If you plan to modify or scale this project, please refer to the exact millimeter dimensions of the original source files below. Part Name Total Quantity Width (X) Length (Y) Height (Z) Base Part 1 Piece 41.21 mm 42.70 mm 9.00 mm Button Caps 2 Pieces 13.69 mm 17.99 mm 17.30 mm Required Extra Hardware & Materials 🛠️ To turn these plastic parts into a working clicker toy, you will need to source a few external items: Mechanical Keyboard Switches: This model accommodates standard Cherry MX style switches. For the loudest and most tactile click, look for Blue Mechanical Switches (such as dustproof clicky switches found online). “ https://www.amazon.com/Zhouwang-Blue-Mechanical-Switches-Dustproof/dp/B0FX2GT2XX/ref=sr_1_3?crid=3IEF9XUEI9D4Q&th=1 ” 3D Printed Alternative: If you do not have access to real keyboard hardware, you can search MakerWorld for a "3D printed mechanical switch" model and drop it right into the base. Adhesive (Super Glue): Because different brands of switches can vary by fractions of a millimeter, you may need a drop of standard plastic glue or super glue to lock the switches into the housing. Detailed Step-by-Step Assembly Guide 🧩 Follow these instructions carefully to assemble your clicker fidget safely and correctly. Clear the Build Plate: Let your heated print bed cool down entirely before removing the parts. Snapping them off while hot can warp the bottom plate. Examine the Parts: Check the inside of the square switch holes on the Base Part and the cross-shaped slots underneath the Button Caps . Remove any tiny stray plastic strings. Test Fit the Switches: Align your mechanical switches over the two square cavities in the base. Press straight down firmly until the side tabs click into place. Apply Glue If Necessary: If the switches slide out too easily when you pull on them, remove them. Place a tiny drop of super glue onto the inner side walls of the base cavity, then push the switches back in. Let it dry for 5 minutes. Attach the Button Caps: Line up the cross-shaped stem of the switch with the socket under the button cap. Press down evenly until the cap sits flush over the switch body. Frequently Asked Questions & Troubleshooting ❓ What should I do if the button caps are too loose? If your printer over-extrudes slightly, the cross socket might stretch. A tiny piece of paper placed over the switch stem before pressing the cap on will create a tighter fit. Can I print this in PETG or ABS instead of PLA? Yes! While PLA is recommended for its stiffness and ease of use, PETG will work great and offer higher impact resistance if dropped. Why won't my switches fit into the base? Ensure your first layer didn't suffer from "elephant's foot" (where the plastic squishes outward on the bottom layer). If it did, use a small craft knife to carefully scrape the inside edge of the square holes.

description: 🔧 Parametric Screw‑Lid Container with Partitions — Customizable, Practical, Support‑Free This model is a fully parametric screw‑lid container designed for organization, storage, and everyday utility. Every component — main body , threaded lid , internal partitions , and wall structure — is generated through a synchronized parametric system. Adjust any parameter and the entire model rebuilds instantly with clean geometry and reliable printability. The design is engineered for support‑free printing , smooth threading , and strong structural walls . Whether you're creating a multi‑compartment organizer, a single‑chamber container, or a custom storage solution, this generator delivers consistent, professional results. ✨ What You Can Customize 📏 Main Dimensions Outer Diameter — total width of the container including the lid. Container Height — full height of the base container (excluding the lid). 🧱 Walls & Base Can Wall Thickness — adjust outer wall strength. Lid Wall Thickness — control the lid’s rigidity. Bottom Thickness — set the floor thickness for durability. Optional Rim Height — adds an inner rim for seals, gaskets, or inner lids. 🧵 Screw Lid & Threads Thread Height & Turns — choose how tall the threads are and how many rotations they make. Blunt Thread Cut (%) — removes part of the thread edge for easy lid engagement and no cross‑threading . Smooth Sides — adds a wide band below the threads for smoother lid insertion. Chamfer — clean 45° edges on the lid and base for a professional look and better bed adhesion. 🍰 Internal Partitions (Compartments) Number of Walls — choose how many divider walls you want: 0 = empty container 1 = 2 compartments 2 = 4 compartments 3 = 6 compartments …and so on Partition Wall Thickness — adjust divider strength. 🖨️ Printing & Viewing Options Layout for Printing — place base and lid side‑by‑side or show them assembled. Sectioned View — cut the model in half to inspect wall thickness and thread profile. Part to Print — render the full assembly, base only, or lid only. Print Distance — adjust spacing between parts when laid out for printing. ⚙️ Advanced / Tolerance Parts Gap — default clearance between moving parts (lid vs. threads). Resolution (fn) — Resolution ( fn ) controls how finely curved geometry is tessellated in OpenSCAD. Higher values produce smoother, premium‑quality circular surfaces , but they also increase computational load. When set too high, the model becomes excessively dense, which can slow down rendering significantly and may even lead to render‑timeout errors during preview or export. 🎨 Multi‑Color Export Procedure (Important) When exporting a multi‑part model from OpenSCAD as a 3MF , the file may contain both parts merged into a single object. To prepare it for multi‑color printing in Bambu Studio, the model must be split into separate objects. Procedure Import the generated 3MF file into Bambu Studio. Select the model in the object list or directly on the build plate. Right‑click the model and choose Split → To Objects . Bambu Studio will separate the combined mesh into two independent objects. Assign different colors or filament types to each object, or print them separately as needed. This ensures each part of your SCAD‑generated model can be printed with its own color or material . 💡 Printing Tips Tight Lid? Increase the parts gap slightly (e.g., 0.4 → 0.5). Loose Lid? Decrease the parts gap (e.g., 0.4 → 0.3). No Supports Needed — threads and chamfers are designed for clean FDM printing. Infill — 15–20% Gyroid or Cubic is ideal. Walls — use 3–4 perimeters for extra strength. 🖨️ Print Settings 🧵 Material- PLA, PETG, Matte PLA (matte colors give a premium clean look) 🧱 Infill- 15%–20% Gyroid or Cubic 🧱 Walls- 3–4 walls for strong partitions and thread durability ❤️ Share Your Makes Every print carries a piece of your creativity. Are you in the market to building or replacing a picket fence? Well if you're building a 6' dog ear 7/8" thick cedar picket fence like I was this might save you some time and deliver a better product! The first cedar picket fence I put up used a manual spacer I trimmed off of the end of a 2x4 and I painstakinly marked the location for each set of screws. Second time around I thought there must be a better way so I sketched up a few revisions of this jig. The concept is to place 1 reference picket at the correct height and plumb, run a string line across the top, and then placing each picket working left to right goes quickly. All in one go this jig sets the picket spacing to 4.75mm, has a straight edge to reference the screw position on the previous picket and gives you hole spacing to spot with a drill. I used a small bar clamp to clamp the picket in place so I could remove the jig, use a countersink drill to finish, then sink two screws at the top and two at the bottom.

tags: air conditioner|exhaust hose adapter|window seal|portable ac|parametric|customizable|PETG
description: A replacement end piece for the exhaust hose of portable air conditioners that use a 150 mm spiral hose . Unlike most stock end pieces — which only have a couple of short ribs and tend to slip off the hose — this one has a continuous helical thread . You simply screw it on and it stays put. The flat, wide outlet is made to slide through window seal covers (the zip-up "AirLock" type) and into the gap between the open window and the frame. Because it's fully parametric , you can dial it in to your exact hose and window in the Customize panel — no CAD needed. Why you might want this It holds. A real screw thread grips the hose all the way around, so it won't pull out under the weight or movement of the hose. Fits tight windows. Set the slot depth to match your window gap; the wide flat outlet keeps the airflow cross-section up so the AC doesn't choke. Optional retainer ring that wedges the tip behind the seal's zipper so it can't slide back out. Adapts to other hoses. Expose the thread pitch, diameter and direction — works for many 150 mm-class spiral hoses, not just one brand. How to use the Customizer Measure your hose: outer diameter over the spiral ribs, and the pitch (rib-to-rib spacing — easiest is to measure across 5 ribs and divide by 5). Set Hose Outer Diameter , Thread Pitch and Tightening Direction (many AC hoses tighten left / counter-clockwise — check yours). Set Slot Width and Slot Depth to your window. Turn the Retainer Ring on if you want it to lock into the seal zipper. Print a test ring first: set Thread Turns to 1–1.5, print just the collar (a few minutes) and check it screws onto your hose cleanly and in the right direction. Then bump Thread Turns back to 3 and print the full part. Recommended print settings Material: PETG (the exhaust air is warm and the part may sit in sunlight — PLA can soften and sag). 0.2 mm layers (or 0.28 mm for a faster draft — the thread works fine at 0.28). 4–5 walls, ~20–30 % infill, no supports needed (overhangs are shallow). Brim recommended for bed adhesion. The model is already oriented print-ready (flat outlet face on the bed). Compatibility Designed and field-tested for the 150 mm spiral exhaust hose of the Proklima GPC12AN (Bauhaus). The measured hose is Ø ≈ 150.8 mm over the ribs, 16 mm pitch, left-hand. Many other portable-AC hoses in the 150 mm class are similar — measure yours and adjust the thread parameters to match.

🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: # AC Rig System 200 // Professional Dual-Sided Tackle Box Engineered for anglers, optimized for makers. Every curve, line, and tolerance has been field-tested right on the riverbank to guarantee retail-grade functionality straight off your 3D printer's build plate. --- ## ⚠️ CRITICAL SUNLIGHT & FILAMENT WARNING To protect your rig system from thermal deformation on the bank, please strictly adhere to the following material rules: * **Avoid Dark Colors:** Do not print the main shell or lid bodies in dark colors (Black, Deep Charcoal, Dark Navy). Dark filaments rapidly absorb solar radiation and overheat. * **Sunlight Exposure Limit:** Do not leave the box exposed to direct, intense sunlight for more than **one hour**. Keep it shaded under your side tray, brolly, or inside your carryall when not actively changing rigs to prevent overheating and warping. --- ## 🛠️ Required Hardware & Post-Processing BOM To fully assemble the model with maximum precision, you will need: ### 🔩 Hardware & Consumables: * **Magnets:** 22pcs of `5x2 mm` Neodymium magnets (for tight, secure snap closure and hook alignments). * **Hinge Pins:** 2pcs of `2.6 mm` smooth steel pins. *Hardware Hack:* You can easily source these by pulling the long metal mandrels/pins directly out of standard blind pop-rivets ! Cut to length (~50mm) if necessary. * **Rig Winders:** 3pcs of `67x12 mm` EVA foam winders (with a `17 mm` center hole). * **Adhesive:** Cyanoacrylate (Super Glue) is required to secure the colored accent inlay border line around the perimeter of the lid. ### ⚙️ Precision Post-Processing (Highly Recommended): For a flawless, retail-grade mechanical fit, do not rely purely on raw 3D printed holes. Use these tools to finish the hardware seats: * **For Magnet Seats:** Use a `5 mm` flat-bottom metal end mill (Концевая фреза по металлу) turned gently by hand or at low speed to clean out the magnet pockets. This ensures perfectly flat bottoms and a high-precision, flush press-fit. * **For Hinges:** Run a `2.8 mm` drill bit through the hinge channels before inserting your rivet pins to clear any minor FDM over-extrusion and ensure perfectly smooth, bind-free rotation. --- ## ⚙️ Functional Design Highlights * **Dual-Zone Utility:** Side A features precision layout geometry for immaculate hooklength storage. Side B is perfectly spaced to hold high-visibility pole winders, line setups, and floats entirely secure. * **Flawless Multi-Color Printing:** Fully optimized for AMS/MMU setups. The branding inlays are modeled at exactly **0.4mm** deep, allowing for incredibly crisp color swaps while preventing river mud or groundbait from packing into deep crevices. * **Rugged Tool Aesthetic:** Features a bold, geometric, chamfered-corner architecture that maximizes structural rigidity and completely resists warping under harsh field conditions. * **Micro-Tolerance Closure:** Designed with tight, crisp hardware mechanical tolerances for a satisfying snap closure that won't accidentally spill inside your bag. --- ## 📊 Verified Slicer Settings This profile has been meticulously dialed in to balance raw part strength with pristine aesthetic text definition: * **Material:** **PETG** or **ASA** is highly recommended for bankside thermal stability. (Printed model uses PETG Gray, Light Gray, and Wasabi Green/Orange elements). * **Layer Height:** `0.20 mm` Standard * **Wall Loops:** `2` walls. * **Sparse Infill:** `20%` density using a rugged **Grid** pattern for optimal interior crushing resistance. * **Top Shell:** `5 layers` (`1 mm` thickness) with a **Monotonic** surface pattern for a seamless top-face look. * **Bottom Shell:** `3 layers` with a **Monotonic** surface pattern. --- ## 📦 What's Included in the Profile * Fully organized plates ready for single or multi-color slicing. * Optimized orientation to minimize support material and maximize top-layer print quality. *Designed by Anglers Craft. description: Membership Subscribe if you want to support me Keep the backseat entertained with this highly adjustable, universal car headrest mount. Designed to securely hold everything from a Nintendo Switch to a large iPad/Tablet , it’s the perfect companion for road trips. Key Features Universal Compatibility: Adjustable clamp system that fits smartphones, gaming consoles (Nintendo Switch), and tablets. True Quick-Release: Drop your device in and lock it in seconds, making it effortless to take your device with you when leaving the car. Innovative Fast-Thread Nut: The locking nut only has threads on one half. This means you can slide it freely into position and tighten or loosen it with just a quarter-turn ($1/4$ turn) . Full Adjustability: Easily adjust both the height and the viewing angle for the perfect ergonomic setup. Built-in Cable Management: Features a dedicated "pocket" to hold your charging cable neatly when it’s not actively plugged into your device. Hardware Required To assemble the mount, you will need: 1x M5 x 35mm Bolt 1x M5 Nut (A locknut / nyloc nut is highly recommended to prevent it from loosening due to car vibrations). 100% 3D-Printed Option (No Metal Hardware Needed) If you don't have real hardware on hand, I have included a fully 3D-printable bolt and nut in the files. ⚠️ Important Assembly Note: The 3D-printed bolt is designed as a press-fit . Do not try to screw it into place—simply press it firmly together. Print Settings & Tips Material: Since this sits in a car, PETG, ASA, or ABS is highly recommended to withstand summer heat. Avoid standard PLA as it may deform on hot days. Orientation: Check the sliced preview or standard print profiles for the optimal printing orientation. Step-by-Step Guide Prepare the Parts: Gather the main arm, the tablet/Switch clamp components, and your hardware (or the 3D-printed press-fit bolt). Snap the Clamp Together: The main holding bracket and the adjustment nut snap directly together. No tools are needed for this part—just align them and press until they click. Orient the Fast-Thread Nut: When sliding the components onto the main threaded rod, make sure the innovative Fast-Thread Nut is positioned at the very top . Secure the Pivot: Use the M5 x 35mm bolt and nut (or the 3D-printed press-fit pin) to secure the tilt/angle mechanism. If using the 3D-printed pin: Remember to press it firmly into place rather than screwing it. Your headrest mount is now ready to be installed in the car! How to Setup & Use (Daily Operation) Once assembled, setting up your mount for the first time is incredibly easy, and daily use is lightning fast thanks to the quick-release mechanism. Initial Setup (First Time Only) Set the Height: Move the top nut (the Fast-Thread Nut) to the desired height where you want your device to sit, and twist it a quarter-turn to lock it in place. Insert Your Device: Place your iPad, Nintendo Switch, or phone into the bottom clamp. Secure the Base: Srew the bottom nut up against the device and tighten it gently. ⚠️ Note: Do not overtighten! Just tighten it enough so your device sits securely and cannot slide out. Daily Use (Quick Release) Once the bottom bracket is set to your device's size, you never have to adjust it again! Taking your device out: Simply loosen the top Fast-Thread Nut with a quarter-turn (1/4 turn) , slide it up, and take your device with you. Putting your device back in: Drop your device back into the cradle, slide the top nut down against it, and lock it with a quarter-turn . Voilà! Car Compatibility & Custom Requests This specific model is designed to fit an XPENG G6 MY24 . However, I can easily modify the design to fit other car models! If you want a version customized for your specific vehicle, I just need the following 3 measurements : Rod Diameter: The thickness/diameter of the metal headrest rods. Rod Spacing: The distance between the two headrest rods (either measured center-to-center, or the inner clearance between them). Seat Clearance: The distance from the headrest rods to the back of the car seat. Just drop a comment with these measurements, and I will gladly create a version that fits your car perfectly!

Conjunto de bandejas decorativas diseñadas para guardar joyas y pequeños accesorios. La parte más importante de este modelo es la configuración de impresión. Para conservar todos los detalles del grabado, recomiendo utilizar una altura de capa de 0,08 mm . Los dibujos están realizados con un relieve muy fino y su función es servir de guía durante el pintado. Si se utiliza una altura de capa mayor, gran parte de ese relieve desaparecerá y será mucho más difícil colorear el diseño con precisión. Como la mayor parte del detalle se encuentra únicamente en la base, también es posible utilizar un modificador de altura de capa en el laminador para imprimir esa zona a 0,08 mm y el resto del modelo con capas más gruesas. En mi caso, al tratarse de una pieza pequeña, preferí imprimir toda la bandeja con una altura de capa de 0,10 mm. El modelo está pensado para imprimirse en un único color y pintarse posteriormente a mano con rotuladores acrílicos o pintura acrílica. Una vez terminado, recomiendo aplicar un barniz transparente para proteger la pintura y mejorar la resistencia del acabado durante el uso diario. Son piezas ideales para dejar anillos, pendientes y otras joyas pequeñas, además de ofrecer un proyecto muy entretenido para quienes disfrutan del acabado manual de sus impresiones.

description: Precisely Designed, Minimal Look. I wanted a truly lightweight, adjustable way to wear the Google Fitbit Air during workouts without being restricted to just the wrist. To achieve a perfectly contoured fit without the messy surface finish that comes from printing on supports, I designed this frame to be printed completely flat and heat-formed using hot water. By leveraging the thermoforming properties of 3D-printed plastic, you get a pristine surface finish, maximum structural integrity, and an exact fit against the device's geometry. The frame is designed with continuous concentric paths to ensure the arms never snap under tension.. Support Me! Features Flat-Print / Heat-Formed Design: Prints completely flat without supports for a flawless surface finish, then easily shapes to the device using hot water. Continuous Ring Strength: Engineered to print as continuous concentric lines, maximizing structural integrity and arm flexibility. Skeleton Frame: A high-strength, ultra-lightweight design that strips away bulk while maintaining a secure hold. Universal Versatility: Can be comfortably worn on the wrist, forearm, bicep, calf, or ankle depending on your activity. Optional Tri-Glide Slide: Includes a printable tri-glide buckle if you want to make a strap from scratch. LED Status Pass-Through: Features a precision cutout so you can check your battery status at a glance without removing the tracker. Official Specification Matching: Designed using official dimensions provided by Google for a secure, exact-fit. Strap Compatibility Guide Off-the-Shelf Options: Recommended: COROS Heart Rate Sensor Replacement Band (My go to for all day comfort) (24mm) Budget Option: Replacement Heart Rate Monitor Armband Strap Wide Option: OrangeTheory Fitness Band (31mm) Additional Search Terms: Polar Loop 2025 ArmBand, VeveXiao Nylon Bicep Bands, Hume ArmBand Strap DIY / Custom Elastic Options: Silicone Gripper Elastic 25mm (1 inch) – Great for preventing slippage on skin. Elastic Sewing Bands 25mm (1 inch) Fold Over Elastic 25mm (1 inch) Specifications Compatibility : Google FitBit Air Filament Type: PLA (Recommended) Filament Required: ~2g (~3g with Tri-Glide Slide) Sizes Included: 16mm (5/8"), 20mm (3/4"), 24mm, 25mm (1"), and 31mm (1.25") Note: The printed part will look slightly longer than the tracker when printed; this extra length is required to accommodate the curve during heat forming.
