description: Floating Hull Upgrade for Cargo Ship Set 60422 This model is a 3D printed replacement/upgrade hull designed for the cargo ship from set 60422. The idea came from a simple wish: my child really wanted the ship to actually float. The original model from the set looks great, but it is not designed to be a real floating boat. So I designed a printable hull that allows the ship build to be placed on top and used as a floating version. Before printing the full hull, I strongly recommend printing the calibration plate available in the print profiles. The calibration file contains five 4x4 test plates with different stud diameters. Print the plate first, test which version fits your bricks best, and then print the matching hull profile. This helps avoid a fit that is too loose or too tight, since tolerances can vary between printers, filament types, and slicer settings. Recommended workflow: Print the calibration plate first. Test all five 4x4 plates with your bricks. Choose the best-fitting stud diameter. Print the matching hull version. Assemble the cargo ship parts on top of the printed hull. Test carefully in shallow water first. Please note: floating performance depends on print quality, material, infill, layer adhesion, and watertightness. I recommend testing the hull in shallow water. This is a fan-made compatible accessory and is not an official part of the original set.

Features: - Any name or short word up to 14 characters (spaces allowed). - Proportional letter layout: narrow letters like I sit close, wide letters like W get the room they need. Print the board in one color and the letters in one or more colors for the classic pastel look - no AMS required, just print the letter plate in your second color (or print letters one at a time in different colors). The model reports the exact board size in the console. Long names make long boards: at the default 40 mm letters, names up to about 6 letters fit a 256 mm bed. For longer names, reduce letter_size or print the letters without the board. Child safety: this is a decorative/keepsake print. FDM prints can crack into small parts under abuse. Not recommended as an unsupervised toy for children under 3 years; always supervise young children. Print letters large (40 mm or bigger), use plenty of walls, and inspect prints regularly for damage. ## Customization Notes - name: the name or word (UPPERCASE looks best and prints strongest). - font_name: keep the default Liberation Sans Bold for guaranteed spacing. Other bold sans-serif fonts work (pockets always match the letters), but letter spacing is tuned to the default font - after changing it, check the preview to confirm neighbouring letters do not touch, and avoid thin or decorative fonts. - letter_size: glyph height in mm. 40 mm default is a good toddler size. - letter_thickness: how tall the pieces are. Default 15 mm; the pieces stand about 9 mm proud of the board pockets. - letter_rounding: fattens and rounds the letter outlines for a chunkier look. - letter_gap: space between letters; the model enforces a minimum so pockets never merge. - board_style: "pocket" cuts a recess per letter, "tray" makes one open rimmed recess. - fit_clearance: gap between letter and pocket. 0.5 mm default suits most printers; increase if pieces fit too tight. - part: print "board" and "letters" separately for two-color puzzles, or "all" for everything on one plate. "fit_preview" is preview-only - do not print it.

description: How to Play Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe is a strategic version of the classic game. Instead of playing one simple match, you are playing nine mini-games at the same time to win a giant mega-board. The Goal Win three mini-boards in a row (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) on the large board. The Setup The main board is broken up into nine large squares. Each of those large squares contains its own small 3x3 tic-tac-toe grid. Player One takes the white pieces. Player Two takes the red pieces. The Core Rule (The Twist) The Opening Move: Player One places a small token in any square on any of the nine grids. Sending Your Opponent: The square you choose inside a small grid forces your opponent to play in that same relative section on the large board. Example: If you place your piece in the top-right corner of a small grid, your opponent is forced to make their next move somewhere inside the top-right mini-board. The Chain Reaction: Player Two then plays a piece in that designated mini-board. Whichever square they pick determines where Player One has to go next, and so on. Winning a Section When you get three small pieces in a row inside one grid, you win that specific board. Once a grid is won, clear it or flip it, and place one of the large X or O markers over the entire section to permanently claim it. What if a Grid is Full or Already Won? If a player's move sends you to a mini-board that has already been won and covered by a large marker, you get a free move. You can place your piece in any open slot on any other grid. The same free move rule applies if you are sent to a grid that is completely full and tied. Winning the Game The game ends the moment a player captures three mini-boards in a row to complete a 3-in-a-row line across the main mega-grid.

I'm starting a collection of models on my MakerWorld page, dedicated to Rubik's Cubes and twisty puzzles. And where to start better than the Rubik's Cube. Here is a fully-functional, reliable version of the iconic puzzle created by Ernő Rubik. It features a ball-core mechanism that ensures reliability, smooth turning and no pops while solving. The centers attach to the core with six M3x12mm screws. The print profile features the best printing orientation for all the pieces, ensuring that no “mechanism surface" ends up being too rough. To assemble the puzzle, start by screwing five of the “Center_Base” pieces. Then, start to slide the edges and corners of the puzzle, untill you arrive to the last layer, the one without a center. Then, screw the last center into place. If you screw all six centers at once, you won't be able to assemble the puzzle, or you may damage some parts. When assembled, adjust the tension of the screws to get the best turnig out of all six faces. Then, glue the “Center_Top” pieces, in top of the centers. Don't apply too much glue, for if you want to dissassemble the puzzle in the future. DON'T GLUE THE "CENTER_TOP" TO THE SCREWS!!!. Finally, glue the caps (the “stickers”) onto all six faces. I recommend sanding a little bit the rough surfaces of the pieces to ensure better turning, specially the ones that are in contact with the build plate, are top layers or in contact with the supports. Feel free to use lubricant for Rubik's cubes to improve turning. Have fun!

This 3D-printed toy key lock showcases the internal mechanics of a simple key lock. You could use it as a prop, novelty items or a interactive children's toy. The circular housing shows a core comprised entirely of matching plastic components. The lock features a guide for a physical key, a latch to secure the shackle, and a compliant zig-zag plastic spring that gives the shackle tension, a spring bar for the latch that gives it the necessary mechanical tension to hold the latch against the shackle cutout. The Lock parts are shown below Then you will install the following 3d printed parts to the base Lock Shackle is placed into the lock with the latch cutout to the left like shown. You will need to add the retainer ring and glue it on. Retainer ring for the Shackle. It is placed on the end of the shackle after you slide the shackle into the base collar provided. The retaining ring will need to be glued onto the end of the shackle. Don't be sloppy with the glue, Be careful not to get glue on the shaft of the shackle and accidently glue it to the collar in the base. One tiny drop will due. This retaining ring keeps the shackle permanently locked into the lock base. The Latch mechanism slides in from the right hand side of the latch holder. It has a keyway that it must slide into. HINT: Take a Crayon and color both sides of the latch to lubricate and help it slide better while in the latch holder, work it back and forth a few times. The compliant spring. Drop it into the channel provided in the base making sure it is placed in the orientation shown. I find a spring printed with PLA makes a better spring. Depending on what spring tension you prefer you could print the 5 loop version to give a more solid lock open The Latch spring is placed in its holder with the top end placed behind the latch to give it return tension. If you like you could add a small drop of glue to the latch spring holder clip or print the Latch spring ever so slightly thicker to make a tight fit. When all is added and complete it should look like this picture This picture shows the key bitway socket. Depending on the key you use from this fellow maker https://makerworld.com/en/@scotttheis then you can print his key and bitway and add it to the lock to get a full lock experience. Press the key bitway into its holder making sure it is fully seated down and left. you may need to adjust it slightly. If you plan to use one key per lock then you could glue the bitway into its holder. The Bitway is cut in such a way to only allow its corresponding key to work in the lock. Check 2nd picture. Now add the lid and snap it together. Take note of the keyway at the top of the lid and lock body. Match them up and snap it shut. The key comes in two halves and will need to be aligned, add glue and sandwiched together. Make sure you align it well or it could be a problem working with the Bitway. I hope you like it, it was a blast to create this learning object. It took me several prints with lots of trial and errors but this should be a great learning experience to a simple old style lock. Enjoy

Dune battle wheel Battle wheel for Dune (2019) by Gale Force Nine. This epic game is great as is, but the battle wheels were never my favorite. Inspired by what I saw on Boardgamegeek, I redesigned the battle wheel with a few advantages. Half slider Better visualization of half units with the half slider. Slide it in or out depending on if you use half units in your battle Spice dial Spice dial for advanced combat. We always play with the advanced combat and it is really annoying holding the amount of spice you need in your hand. So i made an additional wheel, where you can set the amount of spice you use in combat with no hassle. Better artwork Dune isn't the prettiest game, especially the sand/grey battle wheels. I wanted them to pop a little more, so I used the cover art on the spice dials as well and it turned out amazing! Printing In included 2 print profiles. One with one build plate and another one with multiple build plates. Use the one with multiple build plates if you want to save on filament changes (it's 20 vs 40 filament changes). The top wheel is printed upside down on the Smooth PEI Plate I have. This makes the worm look really good and the support for the leader indent is fairly easy to remove. I don't know how this will look on the standard textured plate. Assembly The assembly is straight forward, but it is difficult to separate the pins after the battle wheel is assembled. Insert one pin into the troop wheel and lay them onto a flat surface. Place the spice wheel onto the pin. Place the half slider between the spice wheel and the troop numbers. Place the top wheel on top. Make sure the half slider is oriented correctly. Insert the other pin and press tight.

What is a Kumiki Puzzle? Originating from traditional Japanese woodworking, Kumiki translates directly to "to join wood together." Unlike standard brainteasers or jigsaw puzzles, Kumiki puzzles are beautiful 3D structural challenges. They are meticulously designed so that every interlocking piece fits together securely without a single nail, screw, or drop of glue. The pieces simply lock together in satisfying locking joints. This cabin piece was inspired by Tsunetaro Yamanaka's work and the hundreds of puzzles he made in the early 20th century in Japan. This puzzle prints in pieces. Assembly is up to you! Why You’ll Love It The Ultimate "Aha!" Moment: Finding the secret master piece—the one key block that unlocks the entire structure—is an incredibly satisfying puzzle experience. No instructions included, you have to figure it out! A Beautiful Display Piece: When assembled, this Kumiki Cabin is a striking, minimalist work of art. It’s a puzzle you’ll want to prominently display on your desk, bookshelf, or coffee table, not hide away in a box. The Perfect Tactile Break: In a world dominated by screens, Kumiki puzzles offer a deeply tactile, hands-on escape. It’s a wonderful way to relax your mind, test your spatial awareness, and engage your hands. Why No Instructions Are Included The true magic of a Kumiki puzzle lies in the journey of discovery. By leaving out instructions, you're invited to fully immerse yourself in the challenge. Figuring out how the interlocking joints interact through touch, trial, and error is where the brain-boosting fun happens. Don't worry—the solution isn't impossible; it's waiting to be unlocked by your own intuition and spatial reasoning. There is no greater feeling than looking at the finished cabin and knowing you solved the riddle entirely on your own!

tags: p2|P2|p2s|P2S 3D打印机|x2|x2d|x2d 3d打印机|AMS|AMS 2|AMS2|ams2|ams2pro|AMS 2 Pro 保护器|reduce|filament|loading|time|buffer
description: The second iteration of the AMS Speeder is here ! Designed for the P2 and X2 series, and still compatible with the AMS, AMS 2 Pro, and the AMS Flipper by Jakob_K_Design , this advanced mod aims to reduce filament loading times by shortening the PTFE tubes behind the printer, while also providing neat and clean cable management. Features Faster Filament Changes: Used with shorter PTFE tubes, this holder cuts filament swap time by about 24 seconds, making your 3D printing process quicker and smoother. Strong and Reliable: Although PTFE wear is slightly higher than usual, the better performance makes filament handling more efficient. Printing and preparation You can use the provided 3MF, no supports required. For both main parts, I recommend using at least PETG to avoid deformation due to the chamber/AMS 2 Pro heat, and for the optional TPU seal, I recommend using TPU 95 HF. As for the assembly, you will need to cut PTFE tubes. For that, carefully use a sharp cutter and make sure to cut it straight. The PTFE tube lengths I recommend are : For X2D : ~118mm for the AMS output, 240mm for the buffer output, 400mm for the external spool holder output and 380mm for the auxiliary extruder input. For P2S : ~118mm for the AMS output and 240mm for the buffer output. For this mod to work, you will need an extension cable for the internal cable of the buffer . Don't worry, you will not have to open the back panel of the printer. You can order it here on Aliexpress : Buffer internal cable extension for AMS Speeder 2 , thanks to the WEPRO team for their help ! Please note that this cable was made specifically for this mod, so it will work without any issues as long as it's installed properly. Installation 1 - Turn off and unplug the printer. 2 - Unscrew and unplug the AMS Buffer. For this step, don't hesitate to refer to the official Bambu Lab Wiki : For P2S : Filament Buffer Replacement Guide for the P2S | Bambu Lab Wiki For X2D : Filament buffer Replacement Guide for the X2D | Bambu Lab Wiki 3 - Route the male side of the extension cable in the AMS Speeder and plug it into the buffer Make sure that the connector makes a “click” sound when you connect it ! 4 - Screw the buffer into place on the AMS Speeder 5 - Put the AMS Speeder in position on the AMS and route the AMS and External Exhaust Fan cables in the notches 6 - Install the cover and plug the female side of the extension cable in the printer cable Put the optional TPU Seal in the cover, and install the cover just as if it was the buffer, be careful to let the connector pass through ! Then use regular Bambu M3 machine screws to fix it in place. Connect the buffer cable and the external exhaust one, and manage the cables using the cover slots, make sure that the buffer connector makes a “click” sound when you connect it ! 7 - Cut and install the PTFE tubes Here are the ideal lengths for the tubes, feel free to experiment and make sure to cut them straight to avoid problems. 8 - Adjust Bambu Studio Settings To see faster print times, update the Filament Load/Unload durations in the slicer (Bambu Studio → “Prepare” tab → Printer Settings → “Basic Information” tab → Filament Load/Unload Time). You can adjust the load and unload times as needed, I personally use 8 seconds for each, which I’ve found to be optimal. Your AMS Speeder 2 is now ready to reduce your print times !

model_name: Noodle Nexus 2: Modular AMS Stacker Drawer
description: Introduction Another one? Yes. Clear up some desk space by stacking your AMS's! This version uses 45mm steel slides to slide out the lower AMS, making a super compact stacker. This is compatible with the original AMS and the AMS 2 Pro. The top AMS is positioned forward to ensure that the lid can open fully. Even so, with 350mm slide travel, the AMS lid will open enough to stay open without falling closed. The dimensions are: Height including an AMS 2 Pro on top: 475 mm Width: 443 mm Depth excluding handle and optional counterweight basket: 355 mm Handle adds 32mm of depth Counterweight basket adds 45mm of depth If this isn't exactly for you, check out this collection for alternatives. Modules Feet extensions to put this on top of your H-series printer 3rd/4th AMS Extension (link coming very soon!) Upcoming: AMS HT adapter Upcoming: Various Storage attachments, perhaps a tool drawer? Difficulty This project is designed for beginners . It is easy because: All parts print with minimal supports and all overhangs are easy to print. There is minimal post-processing required. There is only one type (and length!) of fastener needed with no heat-set inserts, no glue and no other specialty fasteners. You don't need "advanced" materials such as ABS. The challenging aspects are: Large parts, even PLA and PETG parts, can warp and your build plates need to be clean. You may even consider using some glue if you have had issues with your particular material and plate. You need to be able to print TPU, and to do this cleanly, you will need a filament dryer. Filament I recommend: PETG for the frame PETG or PLA for the drawer (if you plan on putting this on top of a printer though, do not use PLA) TPU 90A or similar for the feet If you use ABS or ASA, you must consider shrinkage compensation as the parts are large and the overall dimension can be affected by 2-3mm. Please feel free to post your print profile. Add lots of pictures and a detailed description please! It will help other people decide which one to use. Hardware for Assembly Only one type and length of screw is needed: BT3x14 BHCS Self Tapping Screw (AA223). This is a 3mm diameter, 14mm long screw designed for plastic with coarse deep threads that cut into and grip well onto holes in plastic. They are not expensive extremely easy to use as you don't need to embed heat set inserts or seat little M3 nuts. They also make the printed parts simpler and use far less material than using printed fasteners or bowtie joints. Alternatives: If you have 12mm screws or the socket head style of BT3 screws, they will be perfectly fine too. If Bambu doesn't ship to your country, the key words to search are “3mm self-tapping screw hex socket”. Try to get some without a pointy tip as they have a slightly longer usable thread length and a head height of 2mm or less. I found some products on AliExpress ( Listing 1 , Listing 2 , Listing 3 ) which look promising, but I have not tried them. Do NOT use countersunk screws as most holes in the design are parallel to the print bed plane and the screws can split your layers if you're not careful with tightening. You will need: 43 for the frame assembly 10 for the drawer assembly 16 to attach the steel slides to the frame and drawer assemblies 8 to attach the AMS's Optional: 4 to attach the counterweight basket 81 screws total (if I counted correctly…). If you ever wanted an excuse to buy an electric pencil screwdriver, here it is! In the bill of materials, I have put 5 packets of 20 screws but I suggest ordering extra if you are interested in making the future modules. You will also need 350mm or 14-inch nominal length, 45mm nominal width (can be a little wider as there is nothing below the slides), 12.7mm thick full extension slides. Here in Germany, I got Stahlia branded slides direct from their website , also available on Amazon.de . You do not need to get exactly the same one. I took specs from several different brands and accommodated for them all in the design and you just need 3-4 holes that line up. Worst case, you might need to make some new holes but I think that's unlikely as slide manufacturers just copy each other. IMPORTANT : If you are using soft-close slides, check that they are truly full extension and extend 400mm. Many 3-section slides that are labelled “full extension” are not really full extension, particularly some of the soft-close ones. Slide designers, when taking their regular slide and making a soft-close version, need to decide whether to reduce the load rating of their slide or reduce the extension to try to fit the extra mechanisms into the design. Some brands have lowered weight ratings (say, 35kg down from 45kg), some reduce their travel. Parts for Installation You will need a longer PTFE tube than typically supplied with printers (or a coupler to connect two shorter ones) as the AMS travels forward and back. The length needed depends on your particular setup. If the tube is brand new and tightly-wound for shipping, they will need to be relaxed to form gentle curves. Don't get the "star shaped" tubes, that's a gimmick. If you use a coupler, note that there is an entry side (tapered inlet) and an exit side (not tapered). You may also need longer 6-pin AMS connectors depending on your printer and AMS arrangement. Print Settings General Tips Flow rate calibration is highly recommended for every spool you use! Many clearances in the design are 0.1mm. For proper fit, the parts should not be under or over-extruded. Dry your filament (even PLA) to minimise risks with dimensional accuracy. Aux fan OFF if you've had issues with part warping. Don't worry, all of the overhangs are super easy. Specific Settings These are all set in the print profile. However, if you download it on PC and change the printer, some of these may get overwritten so I will list them here. These are the settings I use and are quite conservative and a little slow for a clean print with sharp corners, it's a balance between Bambu's “High Quality” and “Standard" profiles. Feel free to deviate as you see fit. Speeds Outer wall: 70 mm/s Inner wall: 150 mm/s Top Surface: 120 mm/s Everything else: default for your favourite profile Accelerations Normal printing: 4000 mm/s² Outer wall: 2000 mm/s² Inner wall: 0 (same as Normal) Top surface: 2000 mm/s² Sparse infill: 8000 mm/s² Everything else: default for your favourite profile Strength Parts are designed for a 0.4mm nozzle printing 0.2mm layer heights. Wall loops Top/bottom shell layers Infill Frame Parts 3 7/5 10-15%, your choice of pattern Slider Parts 3 7/5 10-15%, your choice of pattern TPU feet 6 5/3 Your choice All other parts 2 5/3 10-15%, your choice of pattern Bonus tip If you want the perfect 🧑🍳👌🏼fit between parts, make sure your beds are trammed! They're not always trammed out-of-factory; 3 of the printers I got in 2026 were not trammed. Manual Bed Leveling / Manual Bed Tramming | Bambu Lab Wiki P2S & X2D Heatbed Manual Bed Leveling | Bambu Lab Wiki Assembly and Installation As all screws are the same, this is quite straight forward. Just one thing to note: screws can get hot while tightening; tighten them most of the way and give them a minute before final tightening. Frame Assembly Assemble each half first. Use the screws to attach the 5 pieces of one side together. Insert the TPU feet - they are press-fit and should stay-in firmly without glue. Remove the inner part of the slide and attach to the frame using at least 3 screws. When tightening, push the slides up to the flat parts on the frame - this ensures that the left and right slides are parallel and level. Repeat for the other side and put the two halves together with more screws. Attach the top AMS with 4 screws. This will stiffen up the frame assembly considerably. For some versions of the original AMS, there are some small pieces of plastic that need to be trimmed. This is not necessary for the AMS 2 Pro and some original AMS variants. Drawer Assembly Assemble the drawer assembly with more screws. Attach the inner slides using at least 3 screws on each side. When tightening, try to get the two inner slides parallel. You can look at the unused holes to determine the positioning. If the holes are too big, you can use some washers (mine is OK without, this is just for illustration). Now slide this into the frame. Attach the lower AMS Put some filament inside the top AMS to provide some counterweight. Pull out the drawer and place the second AMS. Use 4 more screws to secure it in-place. And finally, post a picture here! Counterweight Options As you can guess, the whole assembly can tip forward when the drawer is opened fully. I have 3 options to reduce this risk. You can use one or more of the methods at the same time. Option 1 - Counterweight Basket Attach the counterweight basket using 4 screws (same screws as above!). The file for this is in a separate print profile, on this page. Fill an empty filament box with heavy stuff - try to get at least 2kg in there (a bag of sand, depleted uranium, a brick, whatever you have around the house). Put the box into the basket. You can make the box smaller too. Option 2 - Feet extensions These extensions extend the front by 95mm - if you have the table space these work great. Option 3 - Add another AMS Coming soon™! Support If you make one, please share a pic on social media! Facebook, Reddit, Twitter, whatever! It really helps me out. And of course: Changelog 25/06/2026 Original release

This spool weighs only 82 grams in total ( 41 grams per half ) while remaining strong where it matters most. Why this design is different The unique spoke pattern isn't just for looksit was designed to maximize strength while minimizing material use. Only 82g of filament for a complete spool Approximately 1.5 hours to print each half Spokes intersect in the center, creating high structural density where the spool experiences the greatest loads. The outer edge uses less material because it doesn't require the same level of reinforcement. This results in an elegant, lightweight, and efficient structure that uses filament only where it is needed. To my knowledge, I haven't seen another reusable filament spool using this type of spoke structure. Easy and familiar to use The locking mechanism is compatible with the same twist-lock concept used on Bambu Lab reusable spools, making assembly quick, secure, and intuitive. description: 🧩 COMPONENTS OF THE BENCHMARK – ACCURATE EXPLANATION 📍 THE SPIKES Vertical needles that test whether the printer can print VERY small details . ✔ If they remain straight and sharp = stable printer ❌ If they bend or become rounded = vibration or precision problem 📐 THE ANGLED OVERHANGS First overhang: 5°, 15°, 25°, 35°, 45°, 55°, 65°, 75° Second overhang: 10°, 20°, 30°, 40°, 50°, 60°, 70°, 80° They test how well the filament can hold its shape without supports at different angles. ➡ When an overhang starts to collapse or ripple = that is the limit of your printer ✨ If it stays perfect = the printer can go even further ⚙️ THE FOUR CALIBRATABLE FEET These are the parts you can rotate labeled 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1 . They test the printer’s tolerance . ✔ If a foot does NOT move = the printer is precise at that level ❌ If it moves easily = it cannot reach that level of precision 📏 THE SMALL CYLINDERS AND THE LABELS The labels ( 20.5, 15.5, 10.5, 5.5 ) indicate the intended size of the cylinders. ✔ If the cylinder matches the exact size = dimensional accuracy is correct ❌ If it is larger or smaller = calibration issue

Here we are again, 3D printing enthusiasts! It's mid-2026 and, after more than a year, I'm back with a new version of the "Great Calibrator," thanks to the success of previous versions. The model has undergone a redesign, losing some of the components that had been added to the main model over time and acquiring new ones (few, but effective). But the most impressive aspect is its compactness, precision, and ease of reading the tests, all while, of course, providing a good amount of stress to both your printer's steppers and nozzles, as well as the filament you're testing. Use is as simple and intuitive as ever: once printing is complete, let the print bed cool completely , then fold it and remove the main base. If your printer (or filament, or both) are already well calibrated, you'll notice that many parts will remain attached to the bed or will move away from it without remaining connected to the main base. This should (definitely) happen for the hinge and the bolt, as well as (probably) for the pins with the widest tolerance. Pins 3 and below may require a little pressure on the top. Caution: Don't use excessive force or tools to force a pin out. The goal is to read the tolerance allowed by the printer/filament combination under the conditions you printed under. An extreme unsuccessful print A successful print Let's review the model's components. Walls: The walls surrounding the main base should measure 0.8 mm , consisting of two 0.4 mm walls (the width of the standard nozzle). Turrets: As in previous versions, there are two turrets with a suspended sinusoidal upper part for support testing. You can therefore easily distinguish which method you prefer based on the results obtained. NOTE: There are two versions: the standard single-material version and the dual-material version that uses PETG and PLA for support separation. You'll notice some differences… Bridges: The bridge test is always present (the one on the far left with slopes of 45°, 60°, and the dreaded 75°) which, in theory, shouldn't pose any problems for your printers. I remind you that a "bridge" is a joint distance between two support points , and the different slopes are supported by two side walls. Half-bridges: Just like the bridges, to their right, at the center, you'll find the slopes for testing a half-bridge . What is it? Very simple, it's an overhang supported by a support on only one side , and the Great Calibrator gives you the ability to check the results for both sides. Overhang: A classic among classics, located to the right of the half-bridge, it has always been the biggest problem for a 3D printer: the "suspended" filament, meaning it's printed in "air" without any support. It depends on the extrusion capacity, filament cooling, rigidity, and the airflow system to your nozzle. The slopes don't change, but the 75° slope is more or less where the limit of what a filament printer can achieve stable overhanging ends. To verify them, it's not only important to note whether the lower part is aligned and not "spaghetti-like," but also to verify that the upper part can be completed with a good-looking top surface. Blades: The so-called "blades" have always been a distinctive feature of the Great Calibrator , as they allow for verification, and therefore adjustment, of the complexity of an extrusion balanced between thicknesses and spacing. These "blades" have a thickness that, from top to bottom, gradually decreases from 1.2 mm to a minimum of 0.4 mm (standard nozzle), with minimum distances that also decrease ( down to 0.05 ). The last distance may not be read at the slicer level, unless corrections are made or extrusion is somehow forced. This test (slicer stress) can therefore be verified already during the slicing phase without having to force printing in priority (the parameters provided with the model ensure that the last two blades are joined). Stringing stress cones : Here's another classic, placed in the center of the base, with the peculiarity that has always distinguished the Great Calibrator : the cones are not parallel to each other and not all perpendicular to the base. Obtaining a clean, smooth slin, complete cones, and no stringing will depend greatly on the quality of the filament, the extrusion temperatures, the quality of the nozzles, and so on. As you can see from the images, I managed to achieve excellent results with a simple A1 and a basic PLA filament from Bambulab . M-K-Nick : It's not the name of a rapper or a DJ, but the name of the "mechanical" innovation of the calibrator. Its shape and thickness are very unique and were specifically designed to be "easy" to print. The result should be a piece with properties that are elastic enough to be removed from the base without any effort (if your fingers aren't very fine, try using a simple tweezers, but don't force it. It should come out easily, despite the mechanical "block" caused by its particular shape). Bolt with its Nut: Here it is again, the essential bolt for testing the nut printed in the base circle. A well-calibrated printer should not cause any problems, so the nut should be easily screwed and unscrewed onto the bolt. The thread is standard, but the tolerance is approximately 0.2 mm between each wall, resulting in a total tolerance (circumference) of 0.4 mm. Som e problems may arise from the overhang required by creating the nut thread and/or the bolt itself . Parallelepiped dimensions : The block, as you can easily see, should measure 50 mm wide and 10 mm high and deep. Take the measurement, avoiding getting too close to the Base. Hinge: The other mechanical part of the Great Calibrator is this sort of "3-plate hinge" that can be used to test the possibility of performing some "on-plate direct printing" operations on mechanical parts. The plates that make up the hinge must be able to release with minimal effort and, once released, after a few bends to the left and right, they should have a fluid movement. Finally, don't forget the writing on the base, which must be perfectly legible: “ THE GREAT CALIBRATOR V1.0 BETA 04/2026" (yes... exactly, I started redesigning it in April lol)”. Try it, send me the print results and let's compare them. model_name: True Spring Filament Clip ⧸ Tangle Free Storage
description: A filament clip that solves the three most common problems of traditional filament clips. Plastic Fatigue Most filament clips rely on a printed flex geometry to generate clamping force. Repeated use and elevated drying temperatures gradually reduce the clamping force as the plastic permanently deforms. True Spring Solution The clamping force is generated by a real steel compression spring. The printed parts only guide the movement. No Plastic Fatigue. Constant tension. Filament Stress Many filament clips bend the filament sharply by securing it through spool holes or around the spool rim. Brittle materials may break after long term storage. True Spring Solution The filament is secured close to the spool core with a large bending radius, minimizing unnecessary stress while keeping the filament securely retained. Tangle Risk Some clips secure the filament directly to the wound filament. This can increase the risk of accidental tangles when the spool is handled carelessly. True Spring Solution The filament is retained independently of the wound filament. Nothing is attached to the filament winding itself. Hardware The clip uses two inexpensive compression springs. You can either use a compatible spring from the BOM or simply try the spring from an old ballpoint pen. Many common pen springs fit perfectly. No screws. No glue. No tools. Everything simply snaps together. Printer Tolerance Test Every printer and every filament behaves slightly differently. Since this model relies on precisely fitting moving parts, I strongly recommend printing the Printer Tolerance Test first. The test consists of one plunger and six labeled test sockets with clearances of 0.05 mm , 0.10 mm , 0.15 mm , 0.20 mm , 0.25 mm and 0.30 mm . The correct fit should move smoothly with minimal friction while having as little play as possible. Don't feel like running the calibration? Simply print Print Plate 1 (0.15 mm clearance) . It provides a good fit for most printers and materials. Temperature Testing Successfully tested after 24 hours of continuous filament drying: PETG - 45 °C ASA - 65 °C ASA - 80 °C PC - 85 °C For comparison, I tested a popular Flexi Filament Clip under identical print settings, using the same material and identical drying conditions. After 24 hours at the respective drying temperatures, the flex geometry had permanently deformed and the remaining clamping force was no longer sufficient for reliable reuse. If you have ever dried filament while using this type of clip, you probably know exactly what I mean. Recommended Materials PETG works perfectly for everyday use. For frequent filament drying or elevated temperatures I recommend ASA or PC . Assembly Printed parts and two compression springs. Insert the filament clamps. Insert the springs. Insert the Double Plunger and press firmly. Finished, enjoy.

description: AMS HT mount X2D/P2S - Standalone and AMS Flipper - V2 This is my brand new and completely (re)built and revamped mount for the AMS HT for X2D/P2S printer frames that can now be used either standalone with the printer by attaching it directly to the printer frame on the back, or with an AMS Flipper from @ Jakob_K_Design attached to the back and integrating with the AMS Flipper handle. Note: As the printer frame is shared between the X2D and the P2S, if printing using the P2S, you will have a few nozzle swaps for the interface layers, but they are minimized to just a few, so it shouldn't affect print time dramatically. NOTE: Please be careful with resetting settings, they have been carefully set to have repeatable successful prints and hold to the print bed. Optional Add-on : Designed to be compatible with my X2D Filament Track Switch mount by having a cutout reserved for the mount and utilizing triangles for chord organization. Optional Add-on: Cable organizer using the triangle brackets. Upon request by another user, I designed another add-on to make the cable organization of the 6-pin cable even neater using a figure-8 cable organizer loop that snap-fits into one of the triangle brackets and can be mounted either vertically or horizontally depending on your preference. Hardware required for assembly and installation You will need a few types of M3 Socket Head Screws and thin M3 square nuts: 7x Socket Head Screw M3x30mm (DIN 912) - Bambu Lab store part AA042 x2 3x Socket Head Screw M3x30mm for the mount assembly 4x Socket Head Screw M3x30mm for the installation to the X2D/P2S printer frame 2x Socket Head Screw M3x20mm (DIN 912) - Bambu Lab store part AA040 x1 5x Socket Head Screw M3x10mm (DIN 912) - Bambu Lab store part AA159 x1 10x thin M3 square nuts (DIN 562, ≤2mm height) - Bambu Lab store part AB015 x1 Optional: If you plan to install the Cable organizer you will also need 4x size 8x3mm round magnets (Bambu Lab store part CA008 x1) for the mount in the frame (and another 4x for the organizer itself ) Assembly The assembly is fairly simple and requires just a few standard hardware M3 screws and square nuts, providing a strong hold. You can follow the below step by step instructions, or follow the annotated images for location of screws, nuts and (optional) magnets. As the mount sits right next to the printer frame, for durability the model should be printed using PETG - so dry your filament prior to use! - you want to avoid stringing, warping or lifting off the bed. Print the four (4) parts - To help avoid any warping, you may want to reduce the Aux Fan speed to avoid spot cooling, which can contribute to lifting of large prints, or consider installing an Aux Fan deflector . Print the Main Bracket Pick either the Standalone Main Bracket if you want to install the mount directly to the printer frame or pick the AMS Flipper compatible Main Bracket if you are using the Flipper to mount the bracket to the Flipper Handle Print the Side Bracket for strong support of the mount and provide dampening to limit vibrations from the printer Print the Top Front Mount Bracket that holds the AMS HT and interfaces with the back and side brackets Print the Top Back Mount Bracket that holds the AMS HT and interfaces with the front and main brackets Print optional add-ons as desired: (Optional): Print the Filament Track Switch add-on to mount the Filament Track Switch to the frame over the AMS Flipper Handle and into the AMS HT side mount frame (Optional): Print the Cable Organizer add-on for extra neat organization of the 6-pin cable connecting to the AMS HT Annotated location of mounting hardware: Step by Step instructions: Connect the Top Front and Back brackets through their connecting interface Install two (2) thin M3 square nuts into the inside slots on both left and right side of the top arms Screw two (2 ) socket head screws M3x10mm length from the outside through each of the two arms to connect to the nuts to lock the front and back brackets together Slot the assembled Top Bracket into the Main Bracket through the four trapezoid interface arms note this is a precise interface with 0.15mm tolerances, so check that your printer printed the interfacing arms without any blobs or give them a light sand on the edges as needed Make sure the interface arms are aligned straight and push down using the back of your palm until the top and main brackets are flush - if things are tight and get stuck, a light sideways wiggle can help to loosen things Slot the Side Bracket into the Main Bracket through the two trapezoid interface arms using the same technique Install thin square nuts M3 in all remaining slots, sliding them to their embedded depths: One (1) - Inside of the Top Back bracket One (1) - Upper side of the Top Front bracket Two (2) - Inside of the Side bracket Two (2) - Sunk into the two slots on the back of the Main bracket - use a thin long screwdriver or pliers to push them into place Screw one (1) M3x10mm socket head screw from the bottom of the side bracket through the front bracket , watching until the screw surfaces through the square nut and locks the two parts together Screw two (2) M3x20mm socket head screws from the top of the Main Bracket through the interface arms, meeting the sunk square nuts Screw three (3) M3x30mm socket head screws from the back of the Main Bracket into the remaining holes connecting the Main and Top bracket with one (1) and the Main and Side bracket with two (2) screws (Optional) Install four (4) size 8x3mm round magnets into the holes on the back of the Main Bracket if you plan on installing the optional Cable Organizer. Installation Directly to the printer Remove the four (4) screws from the left backside of the X2D/P2S printer frame Remove the external spool holder mount if it is currently installed at the top and move it tothe bottom of the printer Attach two (2) M3x30mm socket head screws to the top of the mount and two to the bottom of the mounting holes aligning them with the four holes from which you removed the screws Using AMS Flipper Lift the left side (from the back) AMS Flipper Handle up and clip the mount into the handle - this should sit evenly almost flush on both sides -the mount will minimally protrude prior to tightening of the screws to create a counter clamping force to the AMS Flipper Handle to ensure a strong tight fit, but it will still allow the Flipper Handle to sit flush against the printer frame once aligned correctly as pictured below. Lower the Handle onto the printer and align the top and bottom evenly. A small gap before tightening the screws is ok but it should only be 1-2mm and be even between the top and bottom of the handle. If mount was correctly clicked into the handle and the handle sits even as shown above, screw the four (4) M3x30mm socket head screws onto the printer frame. I recommend starting with one of the bottom screws, but without fully tightening it, and then moving to the top and then finishing the rest of the screws and tightening things into place. Check that the flush fit hasn't shifted in case you tightened one screw before alignment was locked into place. The AMS HT mount and the top and bottom of the AMS Flipper handle should sit basically flush with the printer if the AMS HT side mount was clicked into place together correctly once everything is tightened as shown below: If things don't sit flush correctly, repeat Step 1-3, check the fit and try again until the mount is properly set in the center of the handle, resulting in a flush fit. If this is your initial installation of the AMS Flipper, follow the rest of the AMS Flipper installation instructions to finish installation of your AMS Flipper. Install optional add-ons Optional: Install the Filament Track Switch mount . Utilize the triangle cutout in the frame or use the cable organizer to store and tuck away the cords of the AMS HT: If you installed the External Spool holder on the bottom of the printer frame, you could route the power chord of the AMS HT through the triangle frame and down and using a cable tie (ideally a good quality Velcro one) attach the chord to the external spool holder for a clean installation. Optional: Install the Cable Organizer for AMS HT side-mount to organize the 6-pin cable using a neat figure-8 loop Done, enjoy easy access to your AMS HT on your X2D/P2S printer. So funny story. I love printing things. Therefore I have a lot of plastic waste from poop to supports etc…. A while ago my husband says “your going to need a dumpster for all that plastic”. Then my neighbor noticed the several bags of plastic “poop” I have and said the exact thing. And only when my nephew comes over and says the same thing once again I thought to myself, I need to make a little dumpster to catch all the poop my printer makes. I pictured the Home Alone 2 movie where the house Kevin rigs up has a chute outside the window going into a dumpster. So that's where the idea for project came from. There are tons of “poop” bins and baskets for the other printers but I wanted to make one for my new Bambu Lab A2L printer. She's a beast. Very detailed and prints well. I love it. It does shake the house though being a large sized bed slinger. I have been printing on silent mode to calm it down in most cases. This took me a week to create. A little longer than usual but I needed to get the tolerances perfecta. My main goal was to make it easy and reliable to print. That was the challenge. I tried several ways to get the chute to print as one piece but it never worked out. So clip or bracket that connects to the printer is separate and has to be glued to the chute. I did make a connection socket so the two fit together perfectly so all is needed is a drop of cyanoacrylate glue (Super Glue) or something similar on each edge of the connection opening and hold it in place for the appropriate time (depending on your glue). I have printed 19 sets of the chute and bracket and glued them together successfully with no problem. Supports were absolutely necessary to accomplish my goal. I tried to keep the settings simple but tweaked the settings like the top and bottom Z distance, speed etc… to get dumpster and chute to come out clean. Just be sure to keep my settings. You can add to them if you please but it wont be necessary as you can tell by my photos. I have had several people that don't have a printer me to print them one just because they wanted the cute little bin. I have even been changing the sizes per their requests. The dumpster itself is scalable and you can make a smaller or larger one depending on your needs. I am sure it will have many uses. If this becomes popular enough or I get a few requests I will consider making the bracket portion for the A1 and A1 Mini printers. Thank you ahead of time and please enjoy. Have a nice day.

Featuring a new split design, the back end of this bracket has specialized holes designed for a washer and screw and may be mounted directly into your studs or drywall, and features a channel running up the back for a set of skadis pins. Also introducing a new size ! In addition to the standard size mount, the new Wide bracket not only has the benefit of being able to be closely stacked with another mounted AMS to allow you to still lift the lid of the bottom unit, it has the added benefit of allowing you to mount each side of the mount directly into wood studs behind drywall for a super secure hold on the wall! MY AMS bracket is available in 2 sizes: STANDARD SIZE : Fits directly under the AMS and mounts across 19 skadis holes (will not fit the 14" IKEA Skadis boards) and does not have clearance to open another AMS lid underneath it. This is a great choice if you have limited space or are mounting these side by side with another bracket. When mounting the standard size in drywall, I recommend mounting one side into studs, and using strong anchors in the other side. A full AMS weighs roughly 50lbs, please use appropriate anchors. Each of these brackets have ample cable and ptfe tube clearance behind them. WIDE SIZE : Fits under and wide around the AMS and mounts across 21 skadis holes. and DOES have clearance to open another ams mounted underneath provided you are properly spacing the AMS units on your skadis board or wall. This is a great choice to “stack” your AMS units vertically to save space. Additionally, the screw holes on this unit are about 416mm across which if your house was built correctly, should center your screws almost perfectly on two studs ensuring a super secure hold on your wall. Each of these brackets have ample cable and ptfe tube clearance behind them. Each part and build plate in the design is labeled and color coded for ease of use, the skadis pins are compatible with each bracket, but need to be installed on the back ends, they will not provide proper cable clearance if you do not use the back end pieces. If you are wall mounting your bracket, you do not need to print the skadis pins. PARTS : I designed the holes on the bracket to be used with a #8 washer and #10 screws, the screws i recommend should be FLAT HEAD and 3" to 3-½" long. You want to make sure you have proper clearance to drill into your drywall and studs to have a secure fit. Washers MUST BE USED and please do not overtighten the screws, this is just plastic afterall. I have also included a template for your wall to mark out and level your ams. this is a two piece design, with minimal walls and infill, only to be used as a wall template to properly line up holes. please print this plate, and tape the two pieces together, and the inside holes line up with the standard bracket, and outside holes line up with the wide bracket. A word of note when choosing colors for this mount, if you are printing with a multicolor or gradient filament, since the parts do not all build at the same time or on the same plate, the lines or color shift will not line up on the final product and may look silly to you, I recommend using a solid color to print this. Please share your photos of your finished mounts, i would love to see what you create and how you mount these. I spent a lot of time designing this to get it just right, i would love to know how it works out for you!

description: A1 Vibration Damping Pods Inspired from the use of damping in the A2L. These mount to the brace that connects the X-axis to the Z-axis screws instead of the gantry. The mount is the point were any vibrations and or resonance would travel to the print head via the X-Axis – this way both X and Z axis have damping. Plus, space on my gantry is at a premium! French Riviera premium. I used Iron Sand (Iron Filings) - available on Amazon, or anywhere you buy your overpriced scientific supplies - as the damping material. This is better for high frequency vibrations than bearings or BB's and way better than marshmallows. Each bottom clip is secured with an M3x6 button head, coarse thread, screw. They are a tight slip fit by design but are removable if needed. They do not interfere with printer maintenance or your relationship with your mother-in-law. Disclaimer ~ Iron Sand is used in a wide variety of applications for this purpose. I don't have the equipment, nor interest to do a bunch of testing to say how effective these may be in this application on this device. I have seen varying guides of how to calculate damping material v’s object mass. This is just the direct application of theory. Feel free to test and comment with your results below. * Assembly- Fill each compartment to approximately ¾ full. I used a hobby syringe. Make sure to fill them equally so they weigh the same on each side! Use a scale to weigh each compartment as you fill them. Mine weighed 57grams each, once filled. Your results may vary. but, if they weigh the same as mine we can be twinzies. Seal each compartment by gluing a plug in the fill port. Or fill each port with a glue plug. Insert into X-axis brace from the top. Will be a snug fit by design. Grunting and cursing may ease the process. Make sure they sit all the way down. My brackets had some significant burrs, so you may need to de-burr or perform some fitment of the Pods. Insert clip from below. Or lower the printer onto the clip. Secure bottom and pod together with the M3x6 button head coarse thread screw. Tighten until something snaps! And of course -recalibrate… or don’t.. you do you. *These may give you buttery smooth prints, or bring about the end of times, or do absolutely nothing at all. Either way, I stand by option three. California Prop 67 warning - this print and its materials may cause dullness, averageness, and or mediocrity. If you develop feelings of apathy that last for more than 3 hours - who cares!

model_name: Stackable Filament Case with Clear Window
description: I designed this filament storage case to organize a large number of filament spools and make them quick and easy to access. The cases can be stacked vertically and arranged side by side. Because the lid opens from the front, you can remove the filament you need without moving the other cases. The case includes a large clear window, a hygrometer mount, a desiccant compartment, and a TPU gasket. These features make your filament easier to identify, access, and store. I hope this design helps you keep your 3D printing workspace organized and easy to use. I have uploaded a video explaining this model on YouTube: https://youtu.be/SJGec_SRGWo Main Features Access Your Spool Without Moving the Stack The lid opens from the front. Even when several cases are stacked vertically or placed side by side, you can open each case individually without removing the cases above it. This is especially useful when storing a large number of filament spools in a limited space. Large Clear Window The lid has a large clear window. By using a transparent acrylic or PVC sheet, you can check the filament color, remaining amount, and surface texture without opening the case. The lid locking nut can be printed with the same filament stored inside the case. This allows it to be used as a color sample. If you have a label printer, adding labels such as PLA, PETG, ABS, or TPU will make your filament collection even easier to organize. Spool Pull-Out Part In most cases, you can simply open the lid and remove the spool by hand. If the spool is difficult to reach, use the included filament pull-out part. Pulling this part forward makes it easier to bring the spool toward the front of the case. The rear section of the pull-out part also includes a compartment for silica gel or another desiccant. Check the Humidity Without Opening the Case A small hygrometer can be installed in the lid. This allows you to check the internal humidity at any time without opening the case. A TPU gasket is installed between the lid and the case body. Double-sided tape is also used around the clear window to help reduce air leakage and maintain a stable internal humidity. This case does not include an active heating or drying function. It is designed to store filament that has already been dried and to help protect it from moisture when used together with desiccant. Required Parts 3D-Printed Parts Case body Lid TPU gasket Spool pull-out part Lid-locking bolt Lid-locking nut Printing the lid-locking nut with the same filament stored inside the case allows it to be used as a color sample. Additional Parts Small Hygrometer ×1 A small rectangular hygrometer is recommended. Desiccant Silica gel or a similar desiccant can be used. Clear Sheet ×1 Acrylic, PVC, or another transparent sheet can be used. Size: 74 × 185 mm Thickness supported by the standard model: 0.5–0.6 mm The thickness of commonly available clear sheets may vary depending on your region or supplier. If you would like to use a different thickness, such as a 1 mm sheet, please leave a comment with the required thickness. Even if there is only one request, I plan to prepare a lid file that supports that thickness. M3 Socket Head Cap Screws ×2 Length: 25～30 mm These screws are used as hinge pins on the left and right sides of the lid. No nuts are used with these M4 screws. They are simply inserted from both sides. Double-Sided Tape Width: 5 mm This is used to attach the clear sheet and the hygrometer. Assembly Instructions 1. Install the Printed Lid-Locking Bolt Install the 3D-printed lid-locking bolt into the hook on the inside of the case body. Insert the part from inside the case, then slide it sideways along the hook until it is secured. Check the photos for the correct position and orientation. The part used in this step is the 3D-printed lid-locking bolt. It is not one of the metal M4 screws. 2. Install the TPU Gasket Fit the TPU gasket around the front opening of the case body. Make sure the gasket is installed evenly and is not twisted or lifted away from the surface. Any twisting or lifting may affect how well the lid seals against the case. 3. Attach the Clear Sheet to the Lid The rear side of the lid has a recessed area for attaching the clear sheet. Apply 5 mm-wide double-sided tape around this recessed area. The tape should form a continuous loop around the window without any gaps. Gaps may allow air to enter the case and reduce the effectiveness of the seal. Remove the protective backing from the tape and attach the clear sheet, cut to 74 × 185 mm. Align the clear sheet carefully. If the sheet is misaligned, it may interfere with the TPU gasket and reduce the effectiveness of the seal. Before permanently attaching it, confirm that the sheet fits correctly in the intended position. 4. Install the Hygrometer Attach the small hygrometer to the smaller window in the lid. Secure it directly with a small amount of double-sided tape. Use only the minimum amount of tape needed to hold the hygrometer in place. If it is attached too firmly, it may be difficult to remove when replacing the hygrometer or disposing of the case. 5. Attach the Lid to the Case Body Align the hinge sections on both sides of the lid with the holes in the case body. Insert one M4 socket head cap screw from each side. Do not tighten the M3 screws. Simply insert them from the left and right sides. No nuts are used in this step. Insert each screw only far enough that it does not significantly protrude from the side of the case. After installation, check that the lid opens and closes smoothly. 6. Insert the Spool Pull-Out Part If you are using desiccant, place it in the compartment at the rear of the filament pull-out part. Insert the pull-out part into the rear of the case body. Place the filament spool on top of it. 7. Install the Lid-Locking Nut Close the lid and attach the 3D-printed lid-locking nut from the front. Printing this nut with the same filament stored inside the case allows it to be used as a color sample for identifying the contents. You can also add a label showing the material type, such as PLA, PETG, ABS, or TPU. How to Use Remove the lid-locking nut and open the lid toward the front. Remove the filament spool directly by hand. If the spool is difficult to reach, pull the filament pull-out part toward the front of the case. Each case can be opened individually while the cases remain stacked vertically or arranged side by side. Important Notes This case is designed to store already-dried filament and help reduce moisture absorption during storage. It does not actively dry filament that has already absorbed a large amount of moisture. When necessary, dry the filament with a filament dryer before placing it in the case. The position of the clear sheet, gaps in the double-sided tape, and the condition of the TPU gasket will affect the quality of the seal. After assembly, check the following: The clear sheet is correctly aligned and is not lifting away from the lid. There are no gaps in the double-sided tape. The TPU gasket is not twisted or lifted. The lid opens and closes smoothly. The M3 screws do not significantly protrude from the sides of the case. The hygrometer is securely attached. Check the hygrometer regularly and replace or regenerate the desiccant when necessary.

This project intends to reduce the amount of harmful gases produced during the 3D printing process by creating a slight negative pressure in the chamber to reduce or eliminate them leaking out. It does this by automatically controlling a fume extractor fan based on what your Bambu printers are doing. It uses a 3D printed filter box with active charcoal and an ESP32 to poll one or two Bambu printers for status information and ramp a set of fans up and down based on the printer status. It also gives basic printer status information through a dashboard. Although this project was initially designed around two printers it can easily be used for one printer with no modifications other than printing a cap for the non-used intake. In fact I personally recommended using one printer per filter box for simplicity. Using more than two printers is also possible but is an advanced use case requiring some modifications to the code or possibly the 3D printed model and is not required for a standard one or two printer setup. This is a advanced build involving a printed filter box, a ESP32 micro controller, programming, wiring, and a read-only cloud connection between the ESP32 and your Bambu account. I tried to make it as simple as possible without requiring soldering, heat-sets, etc but it is still a involved project. I do not want to discourage anyone from attempting this but it does have multiple pieces that all need to come together for a successful working system. There are two print profiles with active carbon: One with a open bottom which makes it easier to mount the components but requires a longer print time due to supports and one with a solid bottom that prints quicker but might be a little harder to navigate inside. In my pictures I used the open bottom but the closed bottom is sturdier. You can also save some time by using a 0.6 nozzle @ 0.18 layer height or for the solid bottom model switching the “lid” color to match the box color. The lid for each version slides in so you have to be mindful of shrinkage. In my example, and in the print profiles, I'm using Bambu ABS for the box and Bambu ABS-GF for the lids as it has minimal shrinkage. The third print profile is for those of you that already vent to the outside but want to automate this process. It's a simple scaled down box with one input and one output and no filters but otherwise follows the same system and logic. The full read-me, Bill of Material, programming code, assembly instructions, and programming guide is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ADYDesigns/BambuAFE/ This project also relies on getting the fumes from your printer to this project. My recommendation is @Made.In.Meidling exhaust system: https://makerworld.com/en/models/1880330-slim-h2-quicklock-exhaust-system-updated . Instead of reinventing the wheel I used, with permission, the threaded connections from their system on my model so it is 100% compatible with theirs. NOTE : Bambu can, at any time, change the access to printer status through their cloud. If that does happen there is already code in place so you may manually turn on the fans using a single potentiometer. This way the main goal of this project can still be accomplished just in a less automatic way or if you want to use this with a non-Bambu printer. This is detailed on GitHub under the Manual Mode section.

Test Supporti PLA vs Interfaccia PETG In questo test ho confrontato due configurazioni di supporto per verificare la qualità della superficie e la facilità di rimozione: Configurazione 1 (sinistra) Modello: PLA Supporti principali: PLA Interfaccia di contatto: PETG Configurazione 2 (destra) Modello: PLA Supporti e interfaccia: PLA Risultati La combinazione PLA + PETG ha mostrato una separazione quasi perfetta tra pezzo e supporto. Grazie alla scarsa adesione tra i due materiali, l'interfaccia in PETG si stacca facilmente lasciando una superficie più pulita e definita. Con i supporti realizzati interamente in PLA, invece, l'adesione è maggiore: la rimozione richiede più forza e la superficie inferiore tende a non presentare molti segni lasciati dai supporti grazie ai test effettuati e profilo calibrato (alla fine ti metterò il link per il profilo calibrato). Vantaggi dell'interfaccia PETG ✅ Supporti più facili da rimuovere ✅ Migliore finitura delle superfici supportate ✅ Minore rischio di danneggiare il pezzo durante la rimozione ✅ Possibilità di ridurre il gap dell'interfaccia per ottenere dettagli migliori Nota Importante La tecnica funziona in entrambe le direzioni: Pezzo in PLA + interfaccia supporti in PETG Pezzo in PETG + interfaccia supporti in PLA Poiché PLA e PETG aderiscono poco tra loro, è possibile utilizzare uno dei due materiali come interfaccia di separazione per ottenere supporti facilmente removibili. Impostazioni consigliate Materiale modello: PLA o PETG Materiale interfaccia supporti: materiale opposto al modello Interfaccia supporti: 2-4 layer Distanza Z superiore: 0 mm (o molto ridotta) Torre di spurgo consigliata per evitare contaminazioni tra i materiali Conclusione Se disponi di una stampante con AMS o doppio estrusore, utilizzare un materiale diverso per l'interfaccia dei supporti è uno dei modi più efficaci per ottenere superfici migliori e supporti che si rimuovono quasi senza sforzo. In questo test la combinazione PLA/PETG ha dimostrato chiaramente il vantaggio rispetto ai supporti tradizionali realizzati con un solo materiale. description: 此模型是AMS HT的置顶支架，专为拓竹A1/A2L适配，可将AMS HT置顶与打印机顶部。 连接简单快速，稳定牢固，使用方便。 特点： 打印简单快速，无支撑打印，仅需198g耗材使用量。 连接简单牢固，采用一体打印卡扣+快拆卡扣固定。 加厚加强筋设计，承重力远超AMS HT的重量。 官方参数设计，不与打印机工具头干涉。 感谢官方的ams置顶方案，采用官方理线夹进行6PIN连接线进行理线。 依照AMS HT实际尺寸定制，尺寸贴合，稳定牢靠。 预留两个对称排气孔，左右朝向安装均可顺利排气。 如无经常拆装需求，或经常在晃动剧烈的桌面上打印，可选使用胶带将支架与AMS HT长期固定。 支架安装： 与置顶料盘支架相同，斜上方卡入，锁紧卡扣。 将燕尾卡扣卡入中间，即可完成支架安装。 AMS HT安装： 将AMS HT按照需要的方向放上支架，放入支架槽内。 连接好料管与6pin连接线。 线材整理： 使用官方卡扣（两个）安装至打印机支架上。 线材整理好并连接至打印机6pin接口上。 注意：请勿将AMS HT 的6pin连接线与打印机热床线缆进行缠绕，并前后移动热床，保证6pin连接线插头不被热床线缆挂到（ A2L打印机热床线缆有概率将6pin连接线插头给撤坏，一定要注意理线 ） 理线卡扣安装（官方版本）： 轻轻打开理线器，将其套到靠近线缆一侧的打印机斜撑上。 在斜撑上方的孔位中固定理线器。 将理线器沿斜撑滑动，对准内侧孔位后按压卡入。 将线缆卡入理线器。安装完成 安装后测试： 设计打印机与工具头完全无干涉。 安装后请进行干涉测试，以免支架安装反导致与工具头干涉导致影响打印进程。 支架拆卸： 拆除时，请先将卡扣移除，使用手指按压即可释放卡扣。 将两个卡扣拆除之后，整体斜向上旋转拆下。 A1安装方法： A1在安装后会紧贴打印机两侧立柱，安装时要尽量靠边。 卡扣会卡在打印机横梁的螺丝上，卡扣内留有此螺丝空间，可放心安装，锁紧卡扣时可能会相对紧一些。 安装后与A1打印机各运动部件互不干涉，即使X轴移动到最顶端，也与卡扣保留一定的间距。 工具头在最顶端移动也与支架留有一定间距，可完全放心使用。

description: Filament Storage Rack with Fix-Clips Description I am a teacher and normally I design educational models. This time, I wanted to challenge myself with something a bit more practical for my own workspace: a filament storage system. The goal was to create a storage rack that is simple, sturdy, and space-efficient, while still having a clean and modern look. I also wanted it to use a reasonable amount of filament, so the design went through several iterations before I landed on this version. The rack features what I call the Fix-Clip system . While the stacked pieces already have connectors to help align them, I did not want the whole structure to rely only on gravity. The Fix-Clips hold onto the sides of the rack and lock the stacked modules together, making the setup feel more secure and stable. There is also a small recess that allows you to remove the clips again, should you ever, for whatever diabolical reason, need to reduce your filament storage. Model Information The model consists of one main rack part and separate Fix-Clips. The main rack can be printed multiple times and stacked vertically to create the storage height you need. For extra stability, print and attach the Fix-Clips to the sides of each stacked section. This helps keep the modules fixed together while still allowing the system to be expanded, rearranged, or taken apart later. Important Note: For taller stacks, place the rack on a stable, flat surface. The Fix-Clips help secure the modules together, but overall stability will still depend on the height of the stack, the weight distribution, and where the rack is placed. description: 一板在手，测试无忧！ 这是一个集成了多种经典校准项目的3D打印综合测试模型，无需打印多个测试件，即可快速评估打印机的整体状态与参数设置。 模型尺寸小巧，耗材消耗少，适合： ✓ 新打印机验机 ✓ 更换耗材后校准 ✓ 调整切片参数验证 ✓ 打印机维护保养检查 ✓ 不同材料打印性能对比 测试项目说明 1. 收缩率测试（Shrinkage） 用于检测模型实际尺寸与设计尺寸的偏差。 重点观察： 长度尺寸是否准确 XY方向收缩情况 常见问题： 尺寸偏小 孔位缩小 装配件配合困难 可能原因： 材料收缩率较大 流量设置过高 冷却不足 解决方案： 调整XY补偿 校准Flow Ratio 优化打印温度 2. 悬垂测试（Overhang） 用于评估无需支撑时的打印能力。 测试角度： 10°~80° 重点观察： 边缘下垂 表面粗糙 层线变形 塌腰等 可能原因： 风扇风量不足 打印温度过高 打印速度过快 角度过大，超过打印极限 解决方案： 增大冷却风量 降低喷嘴温度 减小外壁速度 添加支撑 3. 搭桥测试（Bridging） 用于测试跨空打印能力。 重点观察： 中间是否下垂 是否出现拉丝 桥面是否平整 可能原因： 冷却不足 挤出量过小 速度设置不合理 解决方案： 提高桥接风扇速度 加大桥接流量 4. 球形效果测试（Sphere Quality） 用于检测曲面打印质量。 重点观察： 圆滑程度 层纹均匀性 接缝表现 可能原因： Z轴抖动 振纹（Ghosting） 机械间隙 解决方案： 检查皮带张力 校准Z轴 5. 拉丝测试（Stringing） 通过多个尖塔检测耗材拉丝情况。 重点观察： 塔之间是否出现细丝 丝线粗细程度 可能原因： 回抽不足 温度过高 耗材受潮 解决方案： 增大回抽距离 降低打印温度 烘干耗材 6. 尖锥测试（Spike Test） 用于测试尖端细节表现能力。 重点观察： 尖端是否完整 是否融化变钝 可能原因： 温度过高 冷却不足 解决方案： 降低温度 提高最小层时间 增加冷却风量 7. 色卡测试（Color Sample） 方便记录不同厚度耗材颜色效果。 用途： 耗材展示 配色参考 打印样品留档 8. 薄壁测试（Thin Wall） 测试打印机极限壁厚能力。 重点观察： 是否缺层 是否断裂 实际壁厚误差 可能原因： 流量不准 喷嘴磨损 挤出系统异常 解决方案： 校准流量 检查喷嘴状态 9. 表面质量测试（Surface Finish） 观察打印层纹与整体表面表现。 重点观察： 层纹均匀性 振纹 接缝质量 可能原因： 速度过快 机械共振 温度不匹配 解决方案： 调整加速度 优化打印温度 校准流量 10. 填充结构展示（Infill Pattern） 模型内置拓竹切片软件的全部填充结构： 可用于： 学习不同填充结构特点 对比强度与打印速度 如果这个模型对你有所帮助，欢迎点赞、助力、收藏并上传你的打印成果！ 祝大家打印顺利，层层完美！

## Device Description Circle Bambu Monitor is a compact desktop display for monitoring Bambu Lab 3D printer status in real time. It is built around an ESP32-C3 SuperMini development board and a 1.28 inch round TFT display with a GC9A01 driver . The electronics are housed in a snap-fit 3D printed enclosure designed for a clean front view and easy rear access. The device connects to Wi-Fi and reads printer data from Home Assistant entities. It does not connect directly to the printer. Instead, it uses Home Assistant as the data source, which makes it flexible and easy to adapt to different Bambu Lab printer setups. ## Main Components - TENSTAR ESP32-C3 SuperMini development board - 1.28 inch round 240x240 TFT LCD display - GC9A01 display driver - 7-wire for display connection - 3D printed main body - 3D printed rear cover - USB-C power supply - Home Assistant with Bambu Lab integrations ## What It Does Circle Bambu Monitor shows the current status of a Bambu Lab printer on a small round display. It can display print progress, printer state, current print phase, temperatures, filament information, layer progress, print weight, estimated finish time, and a clock when the printer is idle. The device also includes a built-in web configuration interface. On first startup it creates its own Wi-Fi setup network. After connecting to it, the user can configure Wi-Fi, Home Assistant URL, access token, timezone, and the Home Assistant entities used for printer data. Firmware updates can be installed through the browser using the web installer, so users do not need to use the Arduino IDE. ## Data Source The device uses Home Assistant as its data source. It reads configured Home Assistant entities for: - Print phase - Print status - Print progress - Active filament slot - Estimated finish time - Nozzle temperature - Bed temperature - Current layer - Total layers - Filament weight ## Installation and Setup Guide Connect the display to the ESP32-C3 using the wiring diagram from the project documentation . The display uses SPI communication. Make sure all wires are connected correctly before powering the device. Open the web installer in a supported browser, such as Chrome or Edge. 1. Connect the ESP32-C3 to your computer using USB-C. 2. Click `Connect`. 3. Select the ESP32-C3 serial device. 4. Click `Install`. 5. Wait until flashing is complete. 6. Disconnect and reconnect the device if needed. After flashing, power on the device. If the device is not configured yet, it will start in setup mode and create its own Wi-Fi network. The display will show: - Wi-Fi network name - Setup password - Setup IP address Connect your phone or computer to the setup Wi-Fi network shown on the display. Then open the displayed IP address in your browser. In the web configuration page, enter: - Your Wi-Fi network - Wi-Fi password - Home Assistant URL (example http://192.168.1.100:8123) - Long-lived Home Assistant token After saving, the device will restart and connect to your Wi-Fi network. After restart, the device will no longer use the setup Wi-Fi network. Find the new IP address in your router, DHCP client list, or network device list. Open the device IP address in your browser to continue configuration. After the device connects to Home Assistant, the configuration page allows you to select the required entities. Configure entities for: - Print phase - Print status - Print progress - Active filament slot - Estimated finish time - Nozzle temperature - Bed temperature - Current layer - Total layers - Filament weight You can use the searchable entity fields to find matching Home Assistant entities. For example, typing “nozzle”, will show matching nozzle temperature entities. Entity names depend on your Home Assistant setup and integration. Configure Timezone - Select your timezone in the configuration page. This is used for Idle clock screen and estimated finish time display. Choose the timezone that matches your location.

description: Ironing Calibration Plate System Find the perfect ironing settings for every filament This project is designed to help you quickly determine the best ironing settings for any filament without wasting time, material, or repeated trial prints. The calibration plate tests: Ironing Flow: 10% to 40% Ironing Speed: 10 mm/s to 40 mm/s 5 mm/s increments across the entire range Each square represents a unique combination of speed and flow, allowing you to instantly compare results and choose the smoothest finish for your specific filament. Custom filament labeling The text area on the plate is fully customizable, so you can print the manufacturer and filament type directly onto the model. Examples: Bambu PLA Basic - White SUNLU PLA Wood eSUN ePLA-ST Gray PETG HF Black The text can be printed in a different color, and the project is optimized to require only two AMS color changes , minimizing both print time and filament waste. Break-off reference system Once you find your ideal ironing settings, you can simply break off the corresponding square. The detached piece permanently stores: Ironing Flow Ironing Speed Your chosen calibration result No more screenshots, notes, or searching through old projects. If needed, the square can later be placed back into the calibration plate. Included storage stands This project includes two stand options: 1. Calibration Plate Stand For users who prefer to keep the calibration plate intact. Stores: One complete calibration plate. 2. Calibration Plate + Reference Tile Stand Designed for users who remove their favorite calibration square. Stores: One calibration plate. One detached reference tile. The selected tile remains visible and easily accessible, making it simple to reuse your preferred settings for future prints. Material-efficient design The entire system was designed with efficiency in mind: Minimal filament consumption. Only two AMS color transitions. Fast printing. Compact storage. Reusable for multiple filament brands and colors. You can create a complete personal library of calibrated ironing settings and keep everything organized in one place. Recommended workflow Customize the filament name before printing. Print the calibration plate. Compare all ironing combinations. Select the smoothest square. Break off the winning tile. Store both the plate and the tile in the matching stand. Reuse those settings whenever you print with the same filament. Recommended print settings Layer height: 0.20 mm Nozzle: 0.4 mm Material: PLA, PETG, or any material that supports ironing AMS: Optional but recommended for colored text Supports: Not required What's included Ironing Calibration Plate (customizable text) Plate Stand Plate + Reference Tile Stand Optimized AMS color setup Low-filament design If this project helped you Please consider leaving a like, rating, or posting your results with different filaments. description: AMS HT Side Mount für Bambu Lab H2 Serie Diese Halterung ermöglicht es, das AMS HT seitlich am oberen Rahmen eines Druckers der H2-Serie zu befestigen. Dadurch kann TPU direkt über die Bypass-Öffnung des AMS HT zum Druckkopf geführt werden. Der große Vorteil dieser Positionierung ist der extrem kurze und nahezu geradlinige Filamentweg. Das reduziert den Wiederstand beim fördern des Filaments auf ein Minimum und verbessert insbesondere den Druck mit sehr weichen TPU-Filamenten, die empfindlich auf lange oder stark gekrümmte Filamentwege reagieren. Zusätzlich kann das AMS HT während des Drucks weiterhin als Filamenttrockner genutzt werden. So bleibt das TPU während des gesamten Druckvorgangs trocken, was die Druckqualität zusätzlich verbessert. Einfache Konstruktion Die Halterung besteht aus drei Steckteilen, die ohne Schrauben oder weiteres Montagematerial zusammengesteckt werden. Diese Bauweise bietet mehrere Vorteile: Sehr einfacher und zuverlässiger Druck. Nur eines der drei Bauteile benötigt eine winzige Stützstruktur. Die Halterung lässt sich jederzeit wieder zerlegen und dadurch besonders platzsparend verstauen. Hinweis: Je nach verwendeten Material und Kalibrierung des Druckers und Filament, kann es sein, dass die Steckverbindung schwergängig ist. Versuche nicht die Teile mit Gewalt zusammen zu stecken! In diesen Fall ist es hilfreich die Steckverbinder mit etwas Schlafpapier nach zu arbeiten. Etwas Gleitmittel wie Balistol oder WD40 kann ebenfalls helfen. Einfache Montage Für die Montage muss lediglich der Glasdeckel des Druckers entfernt werden. Anschließend wird die Halterung einfach über den oberen Rand des Druckers gesteckt. Das AMS HT wird danach nur auf der Halterung abgestellt - ganz ohne zusätzliche Befestigung. Druckprofile Für dieses Modell stelle ich 2 Druckprofile zur Verfügung: Profil 1 - H2D / H2C Dieses Profil ist ausschliesslich für den H2D und H2C vorgesehen.
