model_name: The Ultimate Wall Mounted TPU Spool Holder!
tags: bambu|BAMBU LAB|TPU|tpu spool|tpu spool holder|tpu spool mount|wallmounted tpu|tpu wallmount|tpu holder|tpu bearing|tpu 608|spool|spool holder|spool holder bearings
description: This is the ultimate, fully customizable, wall mounted spool holder which should be suitable for the softest of filaments. It has been tested with: Bambu 95A Bambu 90A Bambu 85A Bambu TPU for AMS Siraya tech flex TPU Of course it should work with all standard filaments too. It features a total of six “tool” holders. The central two (one on each main arm) below the hub are designed to take the flap brake. The flap brake will only work with these two. The other holders are used for the friction brakes. This is the third version of my wall mount and based on the original one which was super smooth but had little control, could run backwards and overrun. I did update it with some brakes which helped but they weren’t very adjustable at all and adding a flap brake just wasn’t practical. I am still in a testing phase but even without adjusting between filaments this version has worked flawlessly so far. I hope it does for you too! Upgrading? For people who already have that old version, this version can re-use at least some parts you already have printed: The original wall brackets will work (although they will be tighter than the new ones). The PTFE tube holder is unchanged. The rear joining bracket is unchanged The wall template is unchanged, no need to redrill anything! Printing Suggestions. The 3MF file contains the settings and support methods I used for this print. Filament: Bambu PLA Metal Iridium Bambu PLA Metal Iron Grey Sparse infill 25% (15% will work just fne) Sparse infill pattern Gyroid Place brim ears on all four parts the two piece arms. In Bambu slicer the brim ears tool set to auto does a great job. You will need to set the brim type to “painted”. Materials you will need: Plugs and screws. Check the screw heads will sit in the countersunk hole and clear the dovetail on the arm. Plugs – if required – I used Fischer 4no. 6x30, 6mm drill bit Screws – 4no. 4x35 – make sure the head will sit within the recess A small amount of PTFE tube. (This is not essential, you can bypass the PTFE holder in use if you choose) Two 608 bearings – these are pretty good: https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B08ZN94S5L?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title but almost any 608 bearing should be fine. Fleece fabric Tessa tape,19- 20mm ideally 51608-00001-00 Or Cable tie Velcro with the soft side as the brake 10-20mm wide Super glue. Installation and assembly: This video should help you understand how it works when assembled, I’d recommend you have sound turned on whilst I’m fitting the brake. Sorry.. VERY boring video :( https://youtube.com/shorts/ZhJ1bJGjlVE?feature=share Choosing parts: Note that I have named all the parts in the 3MF file. I will refer to them here. There are two types of spool arms. One set is only printable on a large bed printer such as the H2D. The other set should be printable on most printer beds and offers a different aesthetic if you use two colours. Photos/videos are of the two part type. Choose how many tool arms to print and of which type (more on this later!). If in doubt just print one standard tool arm “ARM TYPE1 MEDIUM”, one flap brake arm “ARM TYPE 3 Flap Brake”. Note: Arms can be inserted upside down in the front arm holder. Choose which tool to print, again, if in doubt I would suggest “Brake Tool TYPE 1” which has the ridges around and no chamfer. Choose a cover plate type (you may not want cover plates at all!) Note that the large cover plate has a bambu logo which looks nice if printed in a different colour. Choose your axle cap design round or hex – photos are of the hex type. You can choose not to print the flanges. The hub does not require either of them but you won’t get the non-reverse function of course. There is a filament guide included “Flimanent Guide OPTIONAL”. This helped to stop filament loop drops in version 1. I still have it mounted in this version (in the photos) but I haven’t used it nor needed it so far. I would suggest you don’t print it unless you have problems and think it will help. Wall mounting: I would recommend printing the template and using that to position the drill holes. Accuracy IS important. Check that your screw heads will sit within the counter sunk holes. The wall brackets have a little vertical movement in them. Screw the brackets to the wall. Assembly: The two part version is very easy to put together but make sure you trim any access filament (the brim) off the joint on both sides! You can only push the two parts together from one side. Lay the main arm flat on a table and push the small arm on until the whole thing is flush. It may require some force, it’s designed to be tight. A light tap with a hammer can help. Join the parts of the PTFE tube holder together to match the photos. Attach the PTFE tube holder to one of the arms. Take the rear bracket and insert it, bevel edges forward onto the same arm. Now take the other arm and carefully seat it on both the rear bracket and the PTFE tube carrier. Now slide the whole assembly onto the wall brackets to check alignment. It should slide on easily. Assemble the hubs. Remove any support material, use snipe nose pliers to remove the support in the axel socket. Check the supported edge looks flat with no bits of support left and test fit the flanges (if you are using them) to make sure they are flat and flush when seated. Push an axel in each hub as far as it will go. Put a spacer sleeve on next, then your bearings which should be a fairly snug fit. Finally your choice of axel cap. The cap should take quite a bit of force to get on. If it is loose you might want to add some glue. Fitting the flanges Test fit the flanges again. They should be fairly loose fitting without glue. This is by design. Remove them, run a bead of superglue all the way around the edge of the hub, stick the flanges on and leave to dry. Check they are well stuck! Almost done! The hubs should fit together without any effort. Obviously they need to come apart to insert your spools so don’t glue them! Put them together and try dropping the hub into the wall mount. It should drop in and pull out with almost no effort. If it sticks or doesn’t seat correctly there may be some support materials in the arm sockets. If there isn’t try taking the hib in and our a few times. If it doesn’t and the arms didn’t slide into the the wall brackets with ease then you may have an alignment problem. Check your drilling template against the holes in the wall. How things work and Tuning: Flap Brake (s): The function of the flap brake is primarily to stop the spool from running backwards. You will need the smaller ARM TYPE3 (they aren’t handed) and one flap brake for the side you intend to use it on. Fit the brake to the arm (it should fit fairly tightly). When correctly aligned the outer ARM hex faces should line up with the Flap Brake male end hex faces but the most important part is that the flat end of the flap must line up perfectly with the deep flat edge of the scoops on the flange plate. Once fitted the arm can be adjusted by pulling it in and out. Insert it roughly into position so that the end just sits in a scoop The designed position is when it “ticks” fairly quietly in the forward direction and stops the spool turning in the reverse direction. Tuning the flap brake: “Turn” any other brakes off! Use your hand to manually turn the spool forwards and check that there is little to no resistance and you can hear the flap ticking on the disc. Then try to gently spin with spool in reverse. It should be stopped almost immediately as the flap connects with an edge. Note - If you want you can put flap brakes on both sides of the holder. Note – The flap brakes can actually be used as friction brakes too if you push the tool arm in further – it will just be more noisy! Main friction Brakes: Generally I would recommend installing just one or two but you can use up to four. NOTE: Why four? Partly – just in case and you might only have access to one side of the holder but you may like to have one on each side to keep the spool aligned or all four installed to keep everything aligned with a light pressure on all of them. There are two brake types, one is designed for Tessa tape or Velcro style cable ties to wrap around. The other can also take tape but can be used on it’s own – you can just angle the chamfered part against the spool. Tuning the main friction brakes: You can push and pull the arms and you can also angle the tool head on the arm which should allow to you to really fine tune the amount of friction you are applying perfectly to suit the filament type. My personal preference is to use Tessa tape, it sticks on and the surface is very smooth. Tool arms: The arms are handed for left and right There are three types. Short – This makes the tool easy to remove but doesn’t provide much resistance to stop the tool head from being moved when tilted. Medium – Recommended. Some give but plenty of resistance. However it is quite hard to pull the arm out without breaking it. Long – Loads of resistance, almost impossible to remove the arm. Basically a permanent position once you push the head all the way on. Happy Soft Filament printing!

description: Getting clean and consistent photos of your 3D prints can be surprisingly difficult. Large photo boxes are a common solution, but they also require valuable storage space. This parametric photo turntable is designed as a compact alternative. description: 〔Benchmark〕M·01 耗材收缩率校准均值测试 首次测试前请务必阅读指南 作为一个喜欢探索参数对打印件影响的3D打印玩家，在不少评论区见到新手甚至老玩家质疑作者的模型存在公差等方面的问题，但实际原因很可能是使用的耗材收缩率与作者差异较大或混用不同耗材导致的。因此，对所有需要装配的模型，我都建议先进行耗材收缩率校准测试。 一方面是我使用的耗材品牌众多自身需要，一方面是社区现有模型几乎都是单次取值误差较大，故而设计了本模型。根据常见的游标卡尺规格，尽可能缩短了打印时间（ < 40min），专为这一测试项目而设计，并提供了 快速 和 精确 两种测量方式，以满足不同需要。 同时，我还计划将其拓展为一个 基准测试模型系列〔Benchmark〕 ，保持省料省时的原则分享给更多 3D 打印爱好者，帮助大家获得更好的打印质量。如果你有兴趣， 请关注、助力以激励我发布更多实用模型 。 收缩率校准测试模型渲染图 测试准备 打开切片软件，在【项目耗材列表】中，选择需要测试的耗材 如系统中不存在测试所使用的耗材类型，请点击【项目耗材列表】中的齿轮图标打开设置，点击【自建材料】添加耗材类型（如下图），其中材料预设一般第三方厂商的 PETG 选择【Generic PETG】、PLA 选择【Generic PLA】 如未添加，请在【设备】页中设置好耗材对应再返回【项目耗材列表】添加 点击【项目耗材列表】中耗材名称后面的详情按钮，点击【编辑】，查看并确认选择耗材的【基础信息】-【收缩】选项值无误 如果你是首次对此耗材进行测试，应该为上图所示（100%），完成测试后填入取均值后的收缩率 K 即可 如果你是追求更精确的收缩率数值进行的多轮测试，则此选项应当已经填写了上一次测试的收缩率 K*，完成测试后使用本轮取均值后的收缩率 K 除以上一次测试的收缩率 K* 填入即可 快速测试 使用游标卡尺测量模型上半部分的 4 个圆柱体 根据圆柱体上标注的基准值（mm）分别计算收缩率 K1 K2 K3 K4 将 K1 K2 K3 K4 加总后除以 4 取均值得到快速模式下的收缩率 K 精确测试 使用游标卡尺测量模型下半部分的台阶，其中模型上每个台阶的 X、Y 轴基准值均为 10mm 根据测量的部分（建议为 10mm、20mm、30mm …… 100mm）分别计算收缩率 K1 K2 K3 …… Kn 将 K1 K2 K3 …… Kn 加总后除以 n 取均值得到精确模式下的收缩率 K（如有需要也可以与快速测量搭配测量取均值）

description: A2L and A1 Poop Bucket - Parametric Purge Waste Bin So, you can't find the ideal poop basket that fits your printer's exact spot on the desk ? You've come to the right place. This is a parametric waste bin generator - design your own poop chute to exactly your specifications, for either the A1 or the A2L. When customizing, don't forget to select the correct printer type in parameters. The A1 and A2L baskets are not fully interchangeable (especially if you opt for the lip), the printers have some differences even if they look similar. This design adds what a poop basket actually needs: A deflector that catches fast-ejected blobs and drops them straight down instead of letting them ricochet onto your desk A flared lip that widens the catch opening, so blobs landing low or wide still make it in. A floor baffle - a honeycomb base that traps purge blobs so they can't rattle every time the toolhead moves. A cable guide - a chamfer under the back edge for the power cable. No other poop basket has this, and on the A2L (often installed sideways against a wall due to its size - like in my case) a special opening for routing the power cable allows you to use all the available space between the printer and the wall. The notched corner wraps the printer's foot, and two ridges snap into its slits to keep the basket from sliding around. Fully Parametric Configure everything you need: Printer type - A1 or A2L (sets height and foot-notch automatically) Basket width and length Deflector - None, Essential, Half-Size or Full-Size Deflector height Lip , Baffle, Cable Guide - each on or off Preset files with ready-to-print configurations are included (standard and narrow versions), so if your setup is typical you can go straight to printing without touching a single parameter. Printing note Prints flat with no supports - every feature is self-supporting. Hook the notched corner over the printer's foot and press the ridges into the slits. Happy printing!

description: I am a big fan of star wars and the mandalorian.. description: Want a realistic life-size V40 Mini Grenade with a flying handle? This model is 100% brand new from the ground-up with stronger parts, easy screw-on assembly, and enhanced realism. What is the v40 Mini Grenade? The V40 Mini Grenade is an unusually compact fragmentation hand grenade developed in the Netherlands that is roughly the size of a golf ball. Weighing just 4.8 ounces, it allowed soldiers to carry the weapon in much greater quantities than standard fragmentation grenades. It gained historical fame for its utilization by U.S. special operations units during the Vietnam War. Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. It is designed to work with the Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring (linked lower on the page). If you use a pen spring, you can usually cut it in half and get two springs. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu Filaments used Metal Iron Gray black Matte Yellow Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Bambu Matte Dark Green is the closest Bambu filament Metal Spring Version Assembly 1. Insert the peg into the grenade topper as you see below. 2. Then insert a metal spring int the same way. 3. Lastly, screw the topper onto the body of the grenade – it helps to do this upside down or sideways so the spring doesn't fall out. Plastic Spring Version Assembly 1. Insert the printed plastic spring into the grenade topper as you see below. Make sure the peg at the top of the spring is sticking out the top, rotate it until it pops out if not. 2. Lastly, screw the topper onto the grenade body – its easiest if you do this upside down or sideways.

description: Star Wars Scout Trooper Wearable Full Armor Set 🚨 URGENT: WATCH THIS VIDEO BEFORE YOU SLICE OR PRINT! 🚨 STOP! Do not just click print. Armor needs to fit your body perfectly. Before you open these files in Bambu Studio, watch my complete walkthrough on exactly how to measure, scale, cut, pin, and orient your armor pieces for the best results. Only discrepancy is this video shows a 5'8 male on an old set of my armor, this Trooper armor is BETTER, and scaled TO ME (6'2 170 lb male), instead of the average dude you see in this video. See the attached images to see the scale visually: 👉 Watch Sizing, Scaling, and Cutting Guide in Bambu Studio 🟢 About the Model This is the ultimate, wearable Scout Trooper (Biker Scout) Armor Set from Star Wars, built completely from scratch for 3D printing. It features crisp geometric lines, optimized geometries for comfortable wear, and multi-part splitting to accommodate a wide variety of build volumes. Included in this file (.3mf): The Scout Trooper Helmet (Provided at full 1:1 wearable scale as a proof of concept! Pre-sliced and oriented if you want to jump straight in). Shoulder Pauldrons Bicep Covers & Elbow Covers Chest and Back Plate Armor Utility Belt (with detailed compartmental boxes) Knee Pads Ankle Boot Holster (designed to house your scout blaster weapon) Note: All armor parts (excluding the full-scale helmet proof-of-concept) are pre-loaded in the layout at a 20% display scale . This keeps the canvas clean and lets you easily test-scale components. 📐 Sizing & Fit Reference As shown in the display pictures, this set is currently modeled to fit my exact proportions: a 6'2" male weighing 170 lbs . Because everyone's proportions differ drastically, you must scale these to your body. To get your width, depth, and height tracking perfectly against your real-life proportions, you will need a reliable caliper setup. Print yourself a pair of my customized armor sizing tools here: 👉 Download my Free Cosplay Calipers Sizing Tool 🧵 Recommended Filament: SUNLU ASA / PETG (Sponsored) Cosplay armor needs to survive conventions, troopings, hot vehicles, and outside sunlight. Regular PLA can warp or sag under heavy heat. Because of this, I highly recommend using industrial-grade structural filaments from SUNLU . For ultimate outdoor durability and UV protection (crucial if you troop in sunny weather), use SUNLU ASA Filament . It resists yellowing, handles the heat, and leaves a gorgeous professional matte finish that hides layer lines beautifully. If you want high-toughness, impact resistance, and an easier overall print profile, go with SUNLU PETG Filament . Explore all options on the SUNLU Official Filament Store . 🛠️ Structural Assembly: Skip the Glue, Weld Your Prints! For multi-part prop builds like the helmet visor, utility belt, and large chest plates, conventional superglues are a weak point waiting to snap on the showroom floor. Instead, I highly recommend plastic welding your seams together. By using a hot stapler / plastic welder kit, you can melt metal reinforcing staples directly across the interior seams of your prints, followed by smoothing the plastic over with a hot iron attachment. This creates a permanent, structural plastic bond that will survive the stresses of walking and moving around in full kit. You can grab the go-to kit that I use for fusing large armor pieces directly on Amazon: 👉 Get the 100W Hot Stapler Plastic Welder Kit on Amazon 🎬 History of the Scout Trooper Armor First appearing on screen in Star Wars: Episode VI - Return of the Jedi (1983) during the iconic Endor speeder bike chase scene, the Imperial Scout Trooper armor represents a massive departure from standard Stormtrooper gear. Designed by legendary concept artists like Ralph McQuarrie and Joe Johnston, the armor was engineered to be lightweight, flexible, and heavily ventilated to support high-mobility reconnaissance missions. The Scout Trooper gear has since become a massive fan favorite, making notable modern returns in The Mandalorian , Jedi: Fallen Order / Survivor , and Star Wars Rebels . It's widely considered one of the most comfortable Star Wars armor sets to wear for long cosplay sessions due to its open-face visor design and flexible torso configuration. 🔄 Remix Potential & Creative Use-Cases While this is designed as a screen-accurate Star Wars build, this armor layout serves as an amazing template for total customization and remixes: Custom Mandalorian or Bounty Hunter Gear: The shoulder pauldrons, bicep covers, and knee pads can easily be cross-mapped into custom, battle-scarred mercenary cosplays. Post-Apocalyptic Scavenger: Paint it weathered rust colors, add mesh wiring, and combine the chest piece with cybernetic armor designs for a wasteland look. description: Want a replica of a US WW1 grenade? This is the original "pineapple" grenade from WW1 that was the predecessor to the Mk2 grenade we all know from WW2. This grenade has a spoon handle that flies off when you pull the pin, just like the real thing would. Background: Introduced in 1917, the US Mk1 Grenade was the first fragmentation hand grenade developed by the United States for use in World War I. It was notoriously complicated to operate in the field, often requiring the user to manually ignite the fuse before throwing. Due to soldiers struggling to arm it under pressure, the Mk 1 grenade was quickly recalled and replaced by the improved Mk 2 grenade fuze in 1918 (which this model depicts). Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. It is designed to work with the Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring (linked lower on the page). If you use a pen spring, you can usually cut it in half and get two springs. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu filaments used Basic Bronze Dark gray filaments are also period appropriate Silk+ Silver Assembly takes seconds Metal Spring Version 1. Insert the peg into the topper while its upside down. 2. Then insert the metal spring in the same way. 3. Then screw the grenade topper onto the body of the grenade. Doing so upside down is easiest. (this depicts a Mk2 grenade with the yellow stripe, but this Mk1 screws together in the same way) Plastic Spring Version 1. Insert the printed spring into the topper. description: "Why does that pirate have a ship's wheel attached to his belt?" "Arrr... it's driving me nuts!" Now you can finally tell one of the oldest pirate jokes... while being the punchline. Recommended Finish Print using a light brown filament . Apply a dark wood stain or dark brown varnish . Immediately wipe away most of the finish with a paper towel or soft cloth. description: Instant Ronin Double Tanto - Magnetic Knives Channel your inner samurai with the Instant Ronin - Double Tanto (Magnetic Edition) ! This isn't just a pair of sleek 3D-printable props—it's a fully mechanical, dual-sword ecosystem. By utilising a precise arrangement of 5-off 6mm x 3mm magnets per sword, these Tantos completely ditch traditional metal springs for solid-state physics. But here is the real kicker: One sword acts as the activator for the other. Mating the companion sword into the other triggers the magnetic mechanisms, releasing the internal locks and allowing for an instant, seamless locking - and the reverse when withdrawing. Absolutely zero glue required. Every magnet pocket has been engineered for a perfect, satisfying, push-fit. Print two, link them up, and prepare to lose hours of your life to the ultimate fidget experience. Features Triple-Action Magnetic Mechanics: Uses opposing and attracting magnetic fields to safely lock the blades closed, assist the deployment, and lock them open. 5-Magnet Precision Layout: Optimised specifically for standard, high-strength 6mm x 3mm cylinder magnets (5-off per sword). 100% Glue-Free Assembly: Meticulously tuned tolerances mean every magnet snaps tightly into place. Save the superglue for fixing the things you break with the Tanto. Zero Mechanical Springs: No metal springs to find, bend, fatigue, or lose tension over time—magnetism doesn't wear out! Dual-Tanto Blade Profile: A sleek, aggressive geometric aesthetic that looks as sharp as the mechanism feels. Maximum Fidget Factor Magnet Assembly Guide ⚠️ Crucial Tip: Because these are a push-fit, double-check your magnet orientation before you press them home. Getting a backward magnet out of a tight 3D-printed pocket is a special kind of pain you don't want to experience. Use a spare magnet as a reference tool! Follow this exact sequence to ensure the polarity works flawlessly, see my sectioned CAD image and assembly pictures to help with the below: The Master Slider Magnet [1]: Push a magnet into the bottom pocket of the Blade Slider . This can face any direction you like. Once it’s in, this magnet is the "Master" that dictates the rest of the build. The Extended Lock [2]: Press a magnet into the lower forward pocket of the Handle . This magnet must REPEL Magnet #1. (This repelling force is the secret sauce that lifts the slider up into the notch to lock the blade open!) The Retracted Lock [3]: Press a magnet into the bottom rear pocket of the Handle . This magnet must ATTRACT Magnet #1, snapping the blade securely closed so they doesn't slide apart when closed. The Kinetic "Spring" Caps [4]: Press one magnet into each of the two Circular Caps at the top hilt. Both of these magnets must REPEL each other, creating that crisp, snappy detent.

description: This is my biggest project so far and it was a really good way to use for the first time my new H2S, i know that no everybody has the bigger size printers so i made a 84% scale version that is compatible with 256x256mm bed sizes , the materials and the assembly is the same as the bigger variant and to be honest the bigger one might be a bit excesive. Other thing that im not really sure if the bigger variant is going to be compatible with all the H2 series and A2L since they all have slightly diferent print sices and its all very confusing. For assembly: Same materials for big and small variants. You are going to need some glue ( cyanoacrylate). A tube or stick that is 32mm in diameter and 160~180cm long, The lenght of the tube might vary depending of how tall you are and how big you want the model to be , i recomend having some lenght to spare and them cutting down if its to long with the top part of the model already assembled,i used a PVC pipe for this that was petty rigid. Some el ectric tape to wrap around the handle but that is opcional . And some 6mm max in diameter flexible tube or cable but that is also opcional . We are going to start ading the top part to the end of the tube and glue it in. Then we are going to start joining the two central parts, they have holes for pegs but you dont have to use all of them. Afther that we can add it to the tube trie to add glue so it glued to the top part but also to the tube. Now we can add the claws that also use pegs and the screw, is better to do this step now becuase later we are not going to have the angle to insert the screwand might get tricky. After that we can add the two lower parts. Now we can add the blades and box thingy , the blades also use some pegs. Now that we have all the top part conected we can cut the tube if its a bit too long if not we can add the final bits, you can mix and mach the rings and the colums if you want to get diferent combinations and have for example more rings, the model its designed so the lower part of the tube sticks out a bit so the printed part not gets damage when resting the axe on the ground. model_name: Mandalorian Grav Charge With Lightup Mod (Breach)
description: This is my version of the Grav Charge and holder from the show The Mandalorian. I designed it looking at pictures from the show to be as accurate as I could but also be a light up prop. To that end I designed it around these little magnet operated light up warning lights: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CMTJQRYX . The lights have a reed sensor in them that when the magnet is on the back they don't do anything but when you remove the magnet they light up. And the pattern is similar to the actual grav charge, close enough without needing expensive electronics or wiring anything. The back of the holder has some indents of 15mm magnets. Glue some magnets to the back and that will be strong enough to keep the light off. When you pull the grav charge off the holder the reed switch turns the unit on and the lights start to flash then after about 10 seconds go to the circular pattern. I added magnets on the bottom of the grav charges themselves also so you can still stick it to something like in the show but without affecting the light. Place it back on the holder and it turns back off. I went with these lights because they also turn themselves off after a couple minutes so they won't kill the battery if you leave them out. Print Details I printed the body and holder in Bambu ABS - Silver. The body has scarf seam turned on in its object settings which leaves less of a seam on the outside but does sometime affect the color slightly in that spot. If you are going to paint them leave scarf seam on, if you are going to leave them as is you may want to turn that off so the color is more consistent but the seam will be more noticeable. The cover is Bambu PETG Translucent Clear that I then used a red Sharpie oil based paint pen on because I couldn't find a good clear red filament. The combination ended up looking really good so that's what I would recommend or even possibly just a red marker. For printing the cover I have the speeds set to 20mm/s and a custom Bambu Transparent PETG setting that turns off cooling. It's the only way to get a mostly clear lens but you can of course use standard settings, the lens just might not be as clear and the LEDs won't be as distinguishable. Or you can buy a after market clear lens sized for about 28mm. I tried to optimize the print so no supports are required and the 2 x 4 magnets on the bottom should be press fit although I'd add a dab of glue behind them. The holder for the light also is press fit but you can also glue that in to be more secure. Since the lights turn themselves off the batteries should last for years so personally I glued them in.

description: Wax seals are fantastic at adding a level of class to letters, in sealing envelopes, or for attatching tags to brithday and christmas presents. Personally I plan on using them for creating immersive TTRPG props for my D&D game, so that I can hand them printed notices ( like these free ones ). Unfortunately, having a wax seal stamp design for every occasion, affiliation, or character can get expensive… so why not design and 3D print them? This is my first attempt at creating a design using one of my illustrations for Fantastical Geographic's debut . This design uses measurements taken from a proper wood and metal wax seal stamp so that the proportions of your seal will be similar, but also so that you can simply swap out the head and handle as you see fit as these are modeled separately. Or if you have a lot of metal stamp heads already you could simply want some fancy handles to accompany them instead of swapping things out. The head design and print profile have been optimized for 0.2mm nozzles as my experiments showed this yielded the best results. The head prints face up and uses ironing to create a smooth stamping surface for easy release, however, it is IMPORTANT to note that your ironing settings may need adjusting as this varies depending on printer, filament type, filament brand, and filament color! I've opted for PLA as it's the most accessible for many printers. If you are interested in reading my experiments I will be uploading a full write-up on my website of how I achieved the cleanest wax seal and release of the stamp (link to come). The TLDR is: 0.2 mm nozzle Head printed face up with ironing on 0.08mm layer height. 50% Infill 100% cooling Release Agent - A thin layer applied with an old brush Pre-cooling - Place the stamp in the freezer for 10-15 minutes (make sure to apply release agent first) Wait - Leave the stamp in the wax for about 1 minute before gently peeling off Additional Notes: I have included a 0.4mm nozzle profile, however, I was not able to get the ironing as smooth as the 0.2mm. It is there primarily for printing the handle, which doesn't require the high detail. These results were achieved with a tuned PLA filament profile for my machine. Your mileage may vary.

description: This one is for Squidward who relentlessly pushed for me to make the model, and then was so grateful when I got started! I hope you enjoy it! I designed this mask a bit different from my others and I am happy with the outcome. Essentially, I incorporated the mesh eyes directly into the mask so they don't need to be added or printed separately. If you would prefer to print it all in one color (to save time and money), you should be able to easily paint the mesh portion black with some black acrylic paint. I also experimented with how the horns are printed and attached to the head to make them more integrated into the design and also to avoid needing supports on them. My first version was a bit to tight to fit on my head, but it fit on everyone else's in my home. In this version I tweaked the hole size for the head and flattened the bottom of the print a bit to improve printability and eliminate some of the supports. I believe this should fit any head pretty easily now. One under appreciated part of my work is figuring out how to get a model absolutely maximize the space of a p1s sized printer. In this case of this print, lots of adjustments were made to get it just right. For this hobby (designing and 3d printing models) I certainly go through phases. After filling up all the wall space in a room with Hollow Knight masks, I prioritized new areas. This was a nice break from my current phase which has been pond fountains, I think I have one more of those left in me before switching again. I am experimenting with designing a toy for kids during long car rides, I am excited about it and hope to share it soon!

Fully assembled it is almost 24 inches long. Features: Working picatinny rail with attachments. Sights can be quick swapped with each other or a scope if you go with 8x2 magnets. 2 different threaded muzzle options 2 sight options 1 scope option 1 under barrel “flashlight / laser combo” (2 parts held together with magnets) 1 under barrel grip Most parts are separated out for easy color printing. I'll provide an AMS profile for some of the main parts & accessories if you want to go that route. (Grip, main sight, flashlight attachment & buttstock) Assembly: *Assembly is pretty straight forward but there are a lot of pieces. See images for the renders that show where everything goes. Yellow parts in the images are all the connecting / guide pins. You will want to assemble the 3 main sections first. Front, Mid, rear using the larger connecting pins. *Be sure to remember to put in the barrel insert into the mid section prior to any gluing (if you are doing that). Slide rear top (as I call it *on plate 4) into the mid section using connecting pin. Little holes on the top need to be towards the rear of the gun. Buttstock will hold the main rear and top rear sections together with connecting pins. Buttstock covers - There are small alignment holes for pins on the rear top. Add in pins to rear top (may be tight). Place covers onto pins. They only go on one way, see images for reference. Buttstock straps - These should fit snuggle into the openings on the covers. I'd start by inserting the strap on the right side of the gun fist, then push the left side up and in. Straps may need some filing. Mine fit in nice and required no gluing. Magazine connects to the bottom of the rear section using connecting pins. Magazine end cap and loop need to be glued on. Grips & trigger guard - There is an indent in the grip and the upper grip where the trigger guard sits. Due to the design you need to assemble these at the same time. Put 2 pins in the upper grip place it flat side down (in not already attached to mid section). Hold flat side of trigger guard in the grip with one hand while pushing the grip onto the pins guide the angle side of the trigger guard into the indent on the upper grip. Seems difficult when typing it out but its easy. Do test a test fit before gluing anything. I filled my trigger guard down a bit to get perfect fit before gluing. Top picatinny rail is held in my the screw pins. I added the screw pin down into the rails first, then aligned the pins above the holes & pushed them all the way into the main body of the gun. Mine were snug and required no glue. Bottom and side picatinny rails are all the same size & go in as descried above. Cover plates - These are glued on after everything is assembled. Under barrel plates hide some of the seam lines. Top 2 for the bolt area are aesthetic. If you want to use the top 2 be sure to glue them in before you glue in the bolt pin. Slide picatinny mount onto the rails. Add in magnets, make sure you get polarity right on the accessories for easy swapping. There are pins to secure the mount to the rails. Slide the pin in and place on the cap on the other side. You can glue them if you like, I chose not to since the mounts were snug on the rails for me. *Only 2 mounts are in the profile. Print more if you need them. Notes: Most larger flat pieces have 3 walls and 10% infill. I've also slowed the outer / inner wall speeds down to 60-80mm/s to try and negate seeing lines. Smaller items have brims and .16 layer heights to keep the details. Supports are enabled on individual objects where needed. Magazine & magazine end cap have a ton of triangles so you will see that warning. Simplify them at your own risk. Screw pins - I printed them facing up because I didn't want texture to show. Feel free to rotate them 180 if you have smooth plate. Magnets: if you use them for all accessories you will need 16 or 20 8x2 magnets. Be sure to get your polarity correct for easy swapping. If not using magnets you can print our 8mmx4mm plugs. I'm probably missing something but will update notes as needed. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HELLDIVERS SWAG o7

description: Disclosure Day Device - Movie Accurate Replica This is the most geometrically accurate 3D printable replica of the Disclosure Day Device available online. Screen-Accurate Details The Glyphs: The symbols engraved on the upper facet were fully recreated from scratch using high-resolution reference images, ensuring every line, dot, and proportion is completely true to the screen. Print-Optimized: Designed with structural durability in mind, guaranteeing a flawless print that captures the sharp edges and dramatic transitions of the prop. If you are looking for a true, movie-accurate replica born from genuine engineering and deep analysis rather than a rushed approximation, this is the model for you.

description: Membership Want to sell prints of my models? Join my commercial license membership today! A relic of ancient evil, lost to time. Until now. Last seen buying a Twix bar at the local Shop-N-Save. I kept seeing those 3D-printed "magic wand" card holders. You know, the ones where you wave a sparkly star at the register and tap to pay. CYBERPUNK OUTCAST FLINTLOCK MUSKET (DART BLASTER) "In a dark cyberpunk future, everything and everyone belongs to the corporations. Only the outcasts have never been owned. Corporations can lock your implants, freeze your bank account, and disable your smart rifle. But they cannot disable steel, black powder, and flint. Free people are forced to fight with the weapons of the past. A flintlock requires no firmware, no subscription, and answers to no one but its wielder." Inspired by this concept, the CYBERPUNK OUTCAST FLINTLOCK MUSKET is a fully 3D-printable elastic-powered toy dart blaster that combines the appearance of a cyberpunk firearm with the operation of a traditional flintlock musket. Rather than simply resembling a flintlock, it recreates the complete firing sequence with a functional cock, frizzen, powder pan, trigger, sear, and half-cock safety. The blaster is muzzle-loaded. Insert the dart into the barrel, seat it with the ramrod, cock the lock, aim, and fire. The entire loading and firing sequence is designed to resemble the operation of a historical flintlock while using a completely different internal propulsion system. The model features a compact folding design. Both the stock and the front assembly lock securely in their folded and deployed positions, allowing the blaster to be stored or transported in a much smaller package while remaining ready for use within seconds. Designed primarily for PETG printing, the model is almost entirely 3D printed. No metal springs, screws, glue, filament retaining pins, or other additional hardware are required. The only non-printed components are the elastic bands used for propulsion and mechanism operation. In addition to the original HEX 13 mm dart version, the project also includes a separate conversion profile for standard 0.5-inch foam darts. Features Fully functional flintlock-style firing mechanism Functional half-cock safety Muzzle-loaded operation with ramrod Folding stock with adjustable length of pull Folding front assembly for compact storage 99% PETG 3D printed No metal springs, screws, glue, or additional hardware. The only non-printed components are the elastic materials; the carriage guide rails also require lubrication during assembly. Includes a conversion profile for standard 0.5-inch foam darts Compatible with Bambu Lab P1 and A1 build volumes, as well as similar-sized printers (not compatible with the A1 Mini) Ammunition & Performance The primary configuration is designed to fire lightweight HEX 13 mm PETG or TPU printed darts weighing approximately 1–2 g. Typical performance: Muzzle velocity: approximately 40 ft/s (12 m/s) Effective range: approximately 3–10 m Shot dispersion at 3 m may reach approximately 0.25 m A separate conversion profile is included for users who prefer standard 0.5-inch foam darts. This project is intended primarily as an engineering and mechanical showcase that faithfully recreates the operation of a flintlock mechanism using almost entirely 3D-printed components. It prioritizes authenticity of operation and mechanical complexity over maximum performance. Before You Print Please review the listed performance characteristics before starting the project. If you expect significantly higher power, accuracy, or range, this model may not match your expectations.

tags: halo|halo energy sword|elite|elite energy sword|arbiter|master chief|halo cosplay|energy sword
description: Ever wanted a life-sized Halo energy sword? Me too! I was surprised that I couldn't find a print for this, so I made one myself. Coming in at just over a metre long, this is a faithful replica of the iconic Halo weapon. It looks great printed in either translucent blue or clear PETG, with light channels down the middle of each blade and compartments on both blades for electronics (batteries - sized for 18650 cells, control boards etc). Everything is designed to key together to allow for easy printing and assembly. This print takes up 5 full plates on my P2S and took a few days to print, with around 1.5kg of blade material. Each plate is as packed as it can reasonably be. It can of course be printed on smaller printers like the A1 and can be scaled down appropriately to suit this. Key assembly steps: Print and attach hilt sections together. I printed these in a grey PLA+, then stuck them together with CA glue. The fit is tight and may need a bit of force. There is a channel down the inside of the hilt to route wires for lights or switches. Optional - sand, prime, paint hilt. I painted with a base of black acrylic and then steel / silver acrylic on top, then sanded paint down in places to give a weathered look. Print blade base parts and attach to hilt. The fit between the hilt and blade base is a bit looser than any of the other joins, as this gives a bit more tolerance for any accumulated accuracy errors throughout the print. The intended attachment method is to use an M8 nut / insert / T-nuts heat-set into the handle, and an M8*40mm bolt through the blade into this nut / insert. You could however just use a suitable epoxy to bond the two parts well. Either way, this should be a secure connection once properly glued / torqued down. Attach blade pieces to blade base, finishing up with the optional reinforcing bar (secured using M3 heat inserts and M3*10mm bolts into the blade sections). You could use a suitable glue to attach these together, though the keyed fit is pretty tight. Optional finishing steps. I used a UV-set clear resin to fill the join lines between sections and make things look a bit more continuous. This certainly isn't a magic fix as it is obviously still printed in pieces, but it does help! You can then install electronics if desired. I found LED rope or LED-strips worked well (ideally with high density RGB COBs. If they're too far apart you get a less diffuse effect). The original energy sword sculpt was done by the extremely talented Sigil0fSaturn on the Sketchfab site, linked here ( Energy Sword - Halo Prop - Download Free 3D model by Sigil0fSaturn (@Sigil0fSaturn) [8dda2fc] )

description: One of the most mysterious objects in Steven Speilberg's Disclosure Day. Known simply as "The Device", it appears throughout the film as an object of immense but largely unexplained power. It is used to communicate, influence people, and later interact with technology, yet its true nature remains an enigma. 🎬 A recreation from memory I saw Disclosure Day and immediately wanted to model The Device. The challenge? At this time there are virtually no clear reference images available online, so this version is based primarily on my recollection of the film and the limited details I could find afterwards. Rather than waiting for reference material to appear, I wanted to see how close I could get while the movie was still fresh in my mind. 🛸 Accuracy and future updates From what I could determine: - The Device has a heptagonal-to-rectangular form - It features a series of unusual symbols - It has a metallic appearance I've recreated the symbols as I remember them from the film, but as better reference material becomes available I expect to refine and update the model. If future images reveal inaccuracies, I'll update the design where practical. 🖨️ Print notes - Single-colour print - No AMS required - Designed to print cleanly as a display piece For the most screen-accurate appearance, I recommend printing in a metallic or silk filament. I just used Matte PLA as it was all I had 👽 Why print it? - Movie prop replica - Sci-fi display piece - Conversation starter - Early fan recreation of an iconic object from the film 🚀 Getting in early I fully expect more versions of The Device to appear over the coming weeks as reference images become available. This is my attempt to recreate it before that happens. If you spotted details in the movie that I've missed, let me know in the comments. 🙌 If you print one - Share your make - Follow for future movie-inspired models - Boost if you'd like to support more fan recreations 😄

Rusting life support pipes hiss cold fog in the underground bunker of ruined Alpha-17 🌫️. Lynn, a former prosthetic mechanic of Interstellar Alliance special forces, brushes his fingertips over the gradient blade, catching fine dust from the 3D printing layers. Three years ago, only Lynn escaped from the excavation of an unknown ancient ruin on the edge of the Red Tide galaxy with this never-uploaded blueprint. Biochemical modified bounty hunters from the Federation have chased him across three star sectors, all convinced the blueprint hides the coordinate of the ruin's core star core. None of them know the coordinate is carved in the wing lines of this very dagger 🔑. The texture of the claw grip still retains fine burrs from prototype printing, which perfectly matches the feather texture of the giant eagle embedded in the crystal of the ruin's main chamber. Lynn extracted the whole design from this fallen feather fragment back then. Those hunters never guess that this dagger itself is the key to the ruin's defense system — only when it is placed in the palm of the giant eagle statue can the core be activated, and only when the blade is quenched by cold fusion plasma flame will the complete star map emerge from the gradient layer 🗺️. The dull thud of a bounty hunter's modified boot heel against steel plate has sounded at the bunker entrance. Lynn tucks the dagger into his prosthetic belt, his fingertips pressing the isotope detonator switch under the table. The pink-blue lines on the blade glow faintly cold under the dim emergency light. No one knows whether this dagger is the key to treasure or a curse that awakens the sleeping ancient civilization. No one notices that the remnant soul of the giant eagle has long dwelled in the blade along the printing layer, locking on the nape of the visitor's neck along with the bloody smell in the air 🦅.

description: This is a fan-made Lambent Light sword inspired by the anime series Sword Art Online, from the first season / Aincrad arc. The model is split into multiple parts to make it easier to print and assemble. A full sword STL is also included as a reference, but I recommend printing the separated parts for the best result. Files included: Sword_tip Sword_Blade_one Sword_blade_x2 Blade_trim Blade_deco_x2 Guard_upper Guard_lower Cross_bar Hilt Handle_Solid Handle1of2 Handle2of2 peg Handle_peg Full_sword reference file For assembly,you will need to print 5 peg included in the 3mf file btu incase your only using the stls and only 1 handle peg will be needed. i recommend that you also test the fit of the pegs before gluing so you can check the orientation of the blade, trim, etc… The peg file is used for the main alignment points, and the Handle_peg is used for the handle section. Depending on your printer tolerances, you may need to lightly sand the pegs or connector holes so everything fits cleanly. Once the blade is assembled, glue on the blade trim and decorative pieces. After that, attach the guard pieces, cross bar, hilt, and handle. You can either use the solid handle file or the split handle parts, depending on what is easier for your printer. I highly recommend using a strong glue for the pegs and connection points so the sword holds together properly and does not snap, especially if you plan on carrying it around or using it for cosplay/display. Dry-fit first, glue carefully, and take your time with the alignment. Good luck and enjoy printing ^^

tags: spear|bronze age spear|spear of king fuchai of wu|spearhead
description: This spearhead model is inspired by the famous Spear of King Fuchai of Wu (吴王夫差矛) . If you're interested in the history behind the original artifact, you can read about it on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spear_of_Fuchai The spearhead is modeled at approximately the same size as the original artifact and is just over 300 mm long. Since it exceeds the printable height of many printers, it is split into two pieces that are joined with the included connector. I recommend printing one spearhead piece per build plate, even though it may be tempting to place both pieces on the same plate. There are two reasons for this: Print stability – The spearhead is very thin and tall. When both pieces are printed side by side, the nozzle may strike one of them while traveling between parts, causing a print failure. (I learned this the hard way.) If you decide to print both at once, place them end-to-end (like - -) rather than side-by-side (like =) to reduce the chance of collisions. Surface finish – I found that the surface texture is noticeably smoother when only a single part is printed on the build plate. Printing multiple parts at once produced a slightly different finish. This may depend on your filament or printer, but for the best-looking result, I recommend printing the pieces individually. The spearhead shown in the photos was printed using ERYONE Gold Silk PLA at a 0.16 mm layer height. The gold color is intentional —newly cast bronze weapons had a golden appearance.The greenish appearance of the surviving artifact is due to the patina formed during more than two thousand years of corrosion. The pole is designed as 25 mm in diameter and is divided into 150 mm (approximately 6 in) sections. Each section uses M20 × 1.5 threads, allowing you to print as many sections as needed and screw them together to create a spear of your desired length. I printed the pole sections with Fuzzy Skin enabled to create a nice visual contrast with the smooth, polished spearhead. The pommel completes the assembly. To avoid support, a threaded connector was included and the pommel can be threaded onto the end of the pole using that connector. Printing Notes Supports is required for the lower spearhead section only. The upper spearhead section, pole sections, connector, and pommel print without supports. For maximum strength, glue the two spearhead halves together after inserting the connector. Note: The cover image was created using AI.

description: The faint hum of the short dagger vibrates through the cave, mixing with the low roar of alien wind that howls through the rock cracks 🪨. Koren, a veteran smuggler who has wandered the outer galactic rim for 12 years, never thought he would encounter something that cannot be explained by any existing astrophysics data 📡. His navigation system was struck by a sudden solar storm 72 hours ago, forcing him to crash land on this unmarked planet that does not appear in any galaxy public or black market star map. His three crew members all got wrapped by the growing root-like rock tissue when they tried to touch the glowing cave wall, turning into part of the cave in less than ten minutes. He ran all the way to this core cave, only to find this dagger half embedded in the central stone, with a dreamy pink-blue gradient, twisted branch handle wrapping a tiny round star core 🌟. When he got close, he could feel the tiny gravitational pull from the dagger, dragging his consciousness to connect with the remnant information left in the core. He saw the war that broke out a million years ago: the native civilization of this planet fought against the machine legion that came to plunder the planet's core energy, they chose to seal the dying star core into the dagger made of their own life tissue, dragged the whole legion into this cave, and buried everything here to stop the legion from spreading to other star systems 🛸. Now this dagger wakes up because of the new outsider, waiting for a new carrier to take the core out, or join the guardian of this cave forever. Koren tries to pull his hand back from the blade, but his boots have been firmly held by the growing branch, the same pink blue light is slowly climbing up his leg 🔹. The whispers of his old crew can be heard behind him, he cannot tell whether he is the chosen messenger or just the next prey for this ancient guardian. He tightens his grip on the dagger, waiting for what will happen next ✨.

description: 一、模型设计概述 本模型基于《我的世界》游戏内二维像素剑造型进行3D重构。区别于仅做平面拉伸的同类模型，该设计利用高低落差的阶梯式结构，塑造出三维立体的体素浮雕质感。在无需多色打印的条件下，依然可通过光影呈现丰富的层次感。 剑柄部分针对握持的人体工学进行了重新设计。参考游戏内官方3D化逻辑，将原二维扁平剑柄进行90度旋转并合并重组，消除冗余块面，使握把具备真实的立体体积和圆润的握持手感。剑柄底部设计有贯穿的镂空结构，可穿入挂绳，用于悬挂或作为背包挂饰。 二、打印与组装参数 文件拆分 ：剑身与剑柄已完成分体处理，默认分布在1-2两盘，可分开独立打印。 公差与组装 ：经多重精度测试，公差控制精准。装配预期为无胶水拼装（摩擦力卡合结构），无需额外使用粘合剂。 打印设置测试 ：内部已进行多组打印参数实测，以保障最佳打印质量。 三、耗材适配与操作提示 多色与单色适配 ：模型未预设固定配色，任何基础色彩耗材均可直接打印。纯色打印即可凸显像素浮雕质感；若配备多色打印系统（如AMS），或具备后期手涂上色能力，由于全模型皆为方块构造，表面涂装和分色操作非常简便，可根据游戏原作色彩自行调配。 耗材翘边预警 ：模型默认未在剑身部分添加辅助裙边（Brim）。若使用PETG或ABS等收缩率较高的材料，打印时 必须 在切片软件中手动开启裙边功能，否则极易发生翘边；若使用PLA材料，则无需额外处理。 打印尺寸限制 ：针对A1 mini 等较小打印平台的机器，无法直接打印原比例尺寸模型，可通过切片软件等比缩小后输出缩小版本。 四、文件开源与兼容性说明 本模型同步提供 STEP 格式开源文件，可在网页端下载。用户可将其导入任意CAD软件中进行结构修改，用于创作个人二次开发版本。 注意 ：此STEP文件暂无法在 Bambu Studio 切片软件中直接打开。如需在常见切片软件中预览和打印，请直接下载模型提供的 STL 格式文件。

description: Hufflepuff Harry Potter tap to Pay wand If you want a different wand handle please go check out any one of my harry potter wands and just print the wand stem part. They are all universal on the threads so they should all work together. Print both the heads , remove all of the supports . make sure you get all the little ones by the threads. For the back of the heads if it doesn't come off easy, use your bed scraper and make sure to push away from you. They usually peel off very easy but different filaments stick more or less together. Some filaments bond harder on the supports than others. Matte seems to work the best for easy removal. Glue the two heads together . On these larger ones you can screw the stem on then put a dab of superglue at the two top corners, let that kick, then unscrew and squirt a little more in between them at the bottom. Or just put glue around the head and stick it together and get it aligned before it kicks Then slide your card in and screw the stem on, Hold it right below the threaded part . The first few times it can be stiff to screw on, it will get easier with time.

description: A fully 3d printed Single-shot Cap-powered BB pistol! Fully 3d printed springs. Has 10 bodies to print, can fit on an a1 build plate at minimum. Semi-auto hammer and trigger system though it is single shot. hammer action works well. The larger spring is the hammer spring, simply slot into the holes in the hammer and the main body. The smaller spring is the Trigger spring, do the same. The two main halves of the pistol snap together, may need a spot of glue on the joints. To use, get a standard 8-shot ring cap, then cut off an individual cap using a utility knife, being careful with fingers. Break the barrel (shown in images) by pressing the barrel release latch (shown in images as well) on the left hand side of the pistol body, then lift the barrel, tilting it upwards from the end near the hammer. To lock the barrel, manually push the barrel release latch now protruding from the right hand side back into its original position. this can be fiddly ads the hole is quite precise. Load the singular cap into the recess at the end of the barrel, making sure it sits snug. This is a muzzle loader-so from the muzzle, cut out a small square of tissue. Place it on the muzzle and get a standard 6mm BB. place the BB on top of the tissue wad and using a blunt skewer, ram the BB and the wad into the barrel until you feel it stop (do not ram too hard as the cap holder will snap). Then you are ready to fire! *DISCLAIMER* I am not at fault for misuse of this toy causing damage to living beings and surroundings. Be responsible with this toy-never point at any living being , fire with Adult supervision and at a fixed target. Consider wearing Eye pro if necessary. Remember, this is a TOY ONLY and should be used extremely sensibly only in the right conditions.

model_name: Caine from The Amazing Digital Circus
description: Cosplay Caine the Ring Master from The Amazing Digital Circus (TADC) Printed in white PETG, with 2 walls, 2% lightning infill (basically hollow) to make it was light as possible. These files are for printing the teeth/jaws. They're split into 3 segments for each jaw; front, left, and right. And should fit on an Ender 3, or any 220 printbed or larger. The segments dovetail together, but I still recommend glue or plastic welding for the strongest attachment possible. It is designed to clip onto the brim of a baseball cap, and the aliceband isn't meant to sit it normally would on your head, but add better stability to the brim, because the center of gravity is farther forward than you would expect. I ultimately glued some nickels to the back to bring the center of gravity farther back for balance. However, if I were to do it again, I would add strategic infill to the farthest back section (in the slicer) for counterweight and to reinforce the clip connector holes, which I broke. I also recommend adding springs to the back of the jaws to space them apart, and keep them from hitting each other. I played around with various 3D printed springs, which I included. However, I ultimately broke the connectors while switching them, and just 3D printed a straight, flat rectangle piece that I plastic welded to them. Really, anything will work, as long as you attach something to them to keep them apart. I also recommend connecting the front of the jaws using fishing line. I included some small holes where fishing line may be attached, however they came out too small in my print, perhaps do to my printer settings in the slicer. I ultimately tied the fishing line around the seems where the segments meet, where it would be completely hidden. I would also recommend using a touch of hot glue on the knots, to absolutely make sure they stay. And of course you can adjust the length to choose how open the mouth hangs open, just make sure both lines are the same length. I choose to space them so that the bottom jaw doesn't rest on my shoulders, so it all turns with my head, but it also closes if I shrug my shoulders. For my cosplay, I used contact cement to glue a large stripe of red craft foam around the "gums" for texture and to hide the seams, and then I sealed it with Mod Podge for toughness and luster. A hair dryer can also be used to help shrink wrap the foam to the print, but be careful not to let the plastic get too hot or it could warp. I just painted the inside gums red, since they're less visible, and I was very concerned about weight since I was going to be wear it for long hours. Absolutely NO A.I. was used to make these models nor the images. Do not reupload my files somewhere else. I will upload them where I want. DO NOT SELL THEM! I made these models from scratch, and choose to upload them for free for the cosplay community for free. Remixes are welcome, especially as this can be improved, but please give attribution, and posted under the same CC BY-NC-SA license terms. Attribution shout-out to DexTech for their 3D Printable connector clips that I use in all of my large multi-piece prints. The tophat is here.

description: The cold stale wind of the abandoned spaceport vent brushes against the back of Linna’s cybernetic neck, the jagged bone handle of the dagger bites perfectly into his modified palm, the familiar tingle of the crystal veins crawling up his wrist hums in time with the blade’s pulse 🤚. Three standard days ago, he took a shady merc job to retrieve an “anomaly” from a derelict human research outpost that had been abandoned for three hundred years, drifting on the edge of the asteroid belt 🌑. He found the blade tucked into the hollow cavity of a fossilized alien spine, its gradient pink-blue color and twisted bone texture didn’t match any geological record of the asteroid, marking it as a visitor from the deeper void. He only thought it was a valuable oddity to sell to the rich collectors in the cyber city, enough money to replace his failing artificial heart, he never thought it would take root in him ✨. He killed three inquisitors at the spaceport port of entry yesterday, when the last one’s blood sprayed across the blade, it all soaked into the carved patterns instead of staining the surface, the cold blue base of the blade blushed soft pink, just like the veins that are now crawling up his own arm 🩸. His synthetic lung is leaking oxygen after taking a stray bullet, the inquisitors’ footsteps are getting louder, the crunch of their boots on metal debris echoing through the vent. The whisper in his skull is getting clearer now, he doesn’t recognize the language, but he understands every word: take me back to the star core, take me home. Linna tightens his grip on the clawed blade, grinning around the taste of blood in his mouth, he realizes now that he was never the one holding the dagger—he’s just a new bone for the void star skeleton, growing to carry it home 🗡️. The flashlight beam cuts into the end of the vent, and Linna presses the tip of the blade to the back of his own neck, waiting.🔦
